https://taz.de/Video-Clip-aus-Doku-Film/.title: Video-Clip aus Doku-Film: Thunberg lacht deutsche Fridays for Future aus
https://taz.de/Video-Clip-aus-Doku-Film/.author: Susanne Schwarz
https://taz.de/Video-Clip-aus-Doku-Film/.text:
Video-Clip aus Doku-Film: Thunberg lacht deutsche Fridays for Future aus
Die Begründerin der Bewegung übt jetzt lieber anderen Aktivismus aus. Deutsche Aktivistin Luisa Neubauer sieht das gelassen.
Greta Thunberg lacht. Darauf angesprochen, dass die von ihr begründete Bewegung Fridays for Future gerade in Berlin protestiere, bricht die Aktivistin in haltloses Gelächter aus. „Wirklich? Die machen das immer noch?“, fragt sie in einem Video ihren Interviewer Hubertus Koch, der sie für seinen Film „Auf Panzern in die Klimakrise“ in ihrer WG-Küche befragt.
Der kurze Clip macht die Runde. Er endet damit, dass die immer noch quietschende und prustende Thunberg die Hand in Richtung Kamera hält und „Schnitt!“ ruft. Wird ihr da gerade bewusst, dass ihre Reaktion wahrscheinlich als Verächtlichmachung ihrer alten Mitstreiter*innen und des Klimaschutzes gewertet wird?
Genau das geschieht: „Wenn sich Greta Thunberg darüber totlacht, dass noch immer Menschen fürs Klima auf die Straße gehen, warum genau noch mal soll dann Friedrich Merz zum Klimagipfel nach Ankara fliegen, statt beim Italiener seinen Geburtstag zu feiern?“, kommentierte etwa der konservative Autor Jan Fleischhauer auf X.
Thunberg protestiert mittlerweile nicht nur gegen mangelhafte Klimapolitik, sondern engagiert sich vor allem auch pro-palästinensisch und gegen Militarisierung. Ihr Gelächter war laut Filmemacher Koch aber nicht als Absage an das Klima-Thema gemeint gewesen. Er hat sich auf Instagram zu Wort gemeldet. Der Clip werde „komplett aus dem Kontext gezogen“.
Luisa Neubauer: „Nicht an irgendwelchen Clips abarbeiten“
Unmittelbar nach diesem Lachen gehe es weiter damit, „dass Greta eben sehr viel mehr macht als auf angemeldete Demos zu gehen, nämlich zivilen Ungehorsam übt, Staaten verklagt und so weiter“. Thunberg sei „aus dieser Fridays-for-Future-Nummer, die sie mit 15, 16, 17, 18 gemacht hat, rausgewachsen“, interpretiert Koch sein Gespräch mit der Aktivistin. Sie habe festgestellt, „dass das Appellieren auf angemeldeten Demos und das Abhängen auf Panel-Talks und Papst-Audienzen, und mit Merz und Obama klug daherzureden, strukturell gar nichts verändert hat, weil das bloße Appellieren wirkungslos bleibt“.
Sprich: Thunberg lacht Fridays for Future Deutschland nicht aus, weil die Bewegung immer noch auf Klimaschutz setzt – aber sie lacht sie trotzdem aus. Die deutschen Fridays sind auch aktuell wieder auf der Straße. Am Freitag finden anlässlich der Weltklimakonferenz im türkischen Antalya mal wieder in zahlreichen Städten Deutschlands parallel Fridays-Demonstrationen statt.
Luisa Neubauer, das bekannteste Gesicht von Fridays for Future in Deutschland, gibt sich gelassen. Dabei ist sie wohl diejenige, die ganz besonders gemeint ist. Sie ist häufiger Talkshow-Gast, war – übrigens noch zusammen mit Thunberg – eine von wenigen Fridays-Delegierten, die sich mit der damaligen Bundeskanzlerin Angela Merkel (CDU) trafen. Sie hat ein Programm für junge Führungspersönlichkeiten der Obama Foundation absolviert und gemeinsam mit dem damaligen Papst Franziskus dessen Apostolisches Schreiben Laudate Deum vorgestellt, das sich gegen die Leugnung der Klimakrise und für aktiven Klimaschutz ausspricht.
„Es geht in meinen Augen nicht darum, dass man sich überall einig ist – die eine Protestform oder den einen Aktivismus zu finden, der irgendwie richtiger ist als der andere“, sagte Neubauer der taz. „Ich wünsche uns allen in dieser verhärteten Welt ein bisschen mehr Gelassenheit und Sanftheit und Großzügigkeit miteinander.“ In der schon deutlich durch die Klimakrise erhitzten Welt gebe es kaum Zeit mehr. „Die sollten wir nicht damit verbringen, uns an irgendwelchen Video-Clips abzuarbeiten“. Aktuell hält sie sich auf der Weltklimakonferenz in Antalya auf – wie auch Greta Thunberg.
There is no planet B
Die Klimakatastrophe braucht unsere volle mediale Aufmerksamkeit. Dafür bündelt die taz seit Jahren ihre Kräfte und begleitet Konflikte und Fortschritte auf allen Kanälen. Und das schon lange: Die taz hat über radikale Klimaveränderungen berichtet, als andere Medien noch treu von unendlichem Wachstum sprachen. Und sie macht weiter, wenn andere ihre Berichterstattung zurückfahren. Unsere Artikel sind und bleiben frei zugänglich – ohne Paywall, dank über 52.000 freiwilliger Unterstützer*innen. Wir sind der Überzeugung, dass es kritische Informationen im Netz geben muss, die nicht kostenpflichtig sind. Gerade zum Thema Klimaschutz. Nur wenn unser Journalismus so viel wie möglich gelesen wird, kann er gesellschaftliche Veränderungen bewirken. Aber das geht nur, wenn sich unsere Leser*innen an dieser Idee beteiligen und den taz-Journalismus mittragen. Sind Sie schon dabei? Jetzt unterstützen

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Projeto cria rota cultural por ateliês artísticos no bairro da Boa Vista, no Recife
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Fátima Pereira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Quem circula pelo bairro da Boa Vista, no Centro do Recife, terá a oportunidade de conhecer uma dimensão menos conhecida da região: a produção artística que movimenta seus ateliês e espaços criativos. Nos dias 14 e 21 de novembro, a partir das 8h30, o projeto Tem Artista na Boa Vista realiza visitas guiadas gratuitas por espaços de criação do bairro. Os percursos começam na Livraria do Jardim/Celeste Café (Rua Manoel Borba, 292) e integram uma iniciativa que busca ampliar a visibilidade dos artistas locais e estabelecer uma nova rota turístico-cultural na cidade.
A proposta é conectar nove espaços criativos, entre ateliês coletivos, iniciativas de design, ilustração, serigrafia, produção editorial e artes visuais. Ao longo do trajeto, realizado inteiramente a pé, os participantes poderão conhecer os ambientes de trabalho, conversar com os artistas e descobrir diferentes processos de criação que fazem parte da dinâmica cultural da Boa Vista.
Além das visitas mediadas, o projeto investiu na identificação dos espaços por meio de placas instaladas nas fachadas. A sinalização apresenta informações sobre os ateliês, seus integrantes e áreas de atuação, além de QR Codes com audiodescrição, recurso voltado à acessibilidade de pessoas com deficiência visual. Também foram instaladas indicações para orientar a circulação pelo percurso.
As visitas guiadas fazem parte de uma programação com seis roteiros gratuitos. Cada saída contempla aproximadamente quatro ateliês, permitindo que os interessados conheçam outros espaços em visitas independentes, mediante agendamento direto com os responsáveis. A condução pelas ruas fica a cargo da equipe do projeto, enquanto os próprios artistas apresentam seus locais de trabalho e suas produções.
A experiência começa ainda com um lanche preparado com produtos da tradicional Padaria Santa Cruz, empreendimento que também integra a história e o cotidiano do bairro. A participação é aberta ao público infantojuvenil e adulto, mediante inscrição pela plataforma Sympla. As vagas para o sábado (14) estão esgotadas.
Entre os espaços que compõem a rota estão o coletivo ExLibris, que reúne iniciativas de design gráfico e editorial, serigrafia e autopublicação, como Livrinho de Papel Finíssimo, Titivillus Editora, Joana Pena Ilustradora e Grid Serigrafia. Também participam Ploeg, Rinaldo – Barco de Papel, Giu Calife, Ateliê Mont’Elberto, Arte Saraiva, Moita Cultural, Fogo Design e Novo Ateliê Coletivo.
A criação da rota também pretende estimular novas relações entre os espaços de produção artística e outros agentes que movimentam a Boa Vista, como moradores, comerciantes, escolas públicas, equipamentos culturais e visitantes. A escolha do bairro leva em consideração sua relevância histórica para o Recife e sua relação com diferentes movimentos culturais.
Segundo a curadora do projeto, Renata Gamelo, a iniciativa procura recuperar essa dimensão cultural do território e facilitar o acesso do público aos espaços de criação. “A escolha do território considera sua importância histórica e simbólica para o Recife. A Boa Vista reúne patrimônios materiais e imateriais e já foi cenário de encontros de artistas, intelectuais e coletivos culturais”, destaca.
Outro aspecto da iniciativa foi a construção colaborativa da identidade visual e dos elementos de sinalização. O trabalho contou com a participação de estudantes e professores de Design e áreas relacionadas, em diálogo com os artistas envolvidos, aproximando o ambiente acadêmico das práticas culturais desenvolvidas na cidade.
Com a circulação estimulada por ruas como Santa Cruz, da Glória e Visconde de Goiana, o projeto também aposta na movimentação cultural como estratégia de fortalecimento econômico e social do bairro.
A produção executiva é assinada por Clarisse Fraga, diretora da Bureau de Cultura. O projeto conta com incentivo do edital PNAB Pernambuco.

https://taz.de/Voelkerrechtler-zum-Exist.title: Völkerrechtler zum Existenzrecht Israels: Hat Vanessa Emde Recht?
https://taz.de/Voelkerrechtler-zum-Exist.author: Mitsuo Iwamoto und Judith Poppe
https://taz.de/Voelkerrechtler-zum-Exist.text:
Völkerrechtler zum Existenzrecht Israels: Hat Vanessa Emde Recht?
Haben Staaten ein Existenzrecht? Was heißt das für Israel? Haben Palästinenser ein Recht auf Widerstand? Der Völkerrechtler Kai Ambos ordnet ein.
taz: Herr Ambos, in Berlin droht derzeit eine Mitte-links-Koalition an einer Aussage der Linken-Abgeordneten Vanessa Emde zu scheitern. Sie sagte mit Bezug auf Israel: „Es gibt kein Existenzrecht für Staaten. Menschen haben ein Existenzrecht.“ Hat Vanessa Emde recht?
Kai Ambos: So einfach wie Frau Emde würde ich es mir nicht machen. Ein explizites Existenzrecht von Staaten gibt es im Völkerrecht zwar nicht. Aber das Völkerrecht schützt die territoriale Integrität von Staaten. Und der Staat Israel existiert. Er ist Mitglied der UN. Auch die Palästinensische Befreiungsorganisation hat ihn anerkannt. Und wenn ein Staat existiert, hat er auch das Recht, sich gegen Angriffe von außen zu verteidigen. So wie es beispielsweise die Ukraine derzeit tut. Israel hat also in diesem Sinne ein Existenzrecht, verstanden als negatives Abwehrrecht gegen Angriffe von außen. Wenn Israel etwa von Iran angegriffen wird, darf es natürlich seine Existenz verteidigen.
taz: Gleichzeitig gibt es bei Israel das Problem, dass das Land seine eigenen Grenzen nicht eindeutig definiert. Die Netanjahu-Regierung betrachtet das besetzte Westjordanland, Ostjerusalem und die Golanhöhen als Teile Israels. Derzeit kontrolliert Israel auch Teile Südlibanons. Für welches Israel gilt das Recht, weiterzuexistieren?
Ambos: Völkerrechtlich anerkannt sind am ehesten die Grenzen Israels nach dem UN-Teilungsplan von 1947 und die Grenzen der sogenannten Grünen Linie nach dem Waffenstillstandsabkommen mit den arabischen Kriegsparteien 1949. Die Anerkennung Israels in diesen Grenzen erlaubt aber nicht, das eigene Gebiet im Sinne eines Groß-Israels zu erweitern.
wochentaz
Dieser Text erschien zuerst in der wochentaz, unserer Wochenzeitung von links!
In der wochentaz geht es jede Woche um die Welt, wie sie ist – und wie sie sein könnte. Eine linke Wochenzeitung mit Stimme, Haltung und dem besonderen taz-Blick auf die Welt. Jeden Samstag neu am Kiosk und natürlich im Abo.
taz: Im Berliner Koalitionspapier steht: „Das Existenzrecht Israels ist unverhandelbar.“ Hätten Sie es genauso formuliert?
Ambos: Korrekt hätte man schreiben müssen: „Die Existenz Israels und seine territoriale Integrität sind unverhandelbar.“ Kein vernünftiger Mensch kann die Existenz Israels leugnen. Die Existenz eines Staates, der sieben Kriege parallel führen kann, der eine der besten Armeen der Welt unterhält, ist ein Fakt. Aber wer ein Staat ist, der muss sich auch an die Regeln des Völkerrechts halten, die gerade für Staaten gelten. Der Existenzrechtsdiskurs lenkt von diesem Kernproblem ab und führt zu einer mystisch-moralisierenden Überhöhung Israels.
taz: Spuren dieser Überhöhung finden sich derzeit auch auf Bundesebene. Der Bundesrat stimmte im Sommer einem Gesetzentwurf zu, der eine Person mit bis zu fünf Jahren Haft bestrafen soll, die „öffentlich oder in einer Versammlung das Existenzrecht des Staates Israel leugnet oder zur Beseitigung des Staates Israel aufruft“. Das Gesetz soll Antisemitismus bekämpfen. Ist es dafür ein gutes Mittel?
Ambos: Das Problem eines latenten oder codierten Antisemitismus kann nicht durchs Strafrecht gelöst werden. Ich werde nicht weniger Antisemitismus dadurch haben, dass ich Aussagen kriminalisiere, bei denen ich nicht weiß, was den Sprecher zu ihnen motiviert. Nehmen wir das Beispiel „From the River to the Sea“. Es kommt darauf an, wie der Slogan weitergeht und in welchem Kontext er geäußert wird. Ähnlich verhält es sich mit dem Satz „Staaten haben kein Existenzrecht.“ Das sind zunächst einmal von der Meinungsfreiheit geschützte Äußerungen. Natürlich können sie auch antisemitisch motiviert sein, aber das lässt sich nur schwer rechtssicher feststellen.
taz: Der inzwischen aus der Linkspartei ausgeschlossene Deutsch-Palästinenser Ramsis Kilani beruft sich immer wieder darauf, dass im Kontext gewaltsamer Besatzung und Unterdrückung den „Unterdrückten das Recht auf Widerstand“ zustehe. Inwieweit ist ein solches Recht im Völkerrecht verankert?
Ambos: Das ist eine schwierige Frage. Grundsätzlich lässt sich ein solches Recht aus einer Kombination von Menschenrechten und dem Selbstbestimmungsrecht der Völker ableiten. Wird einer Bevölkerung, wie es der Internationale Gerichtshof (IGH) in einem Gutachten 2024 für die Palästinenser festgestellt hat, das Selbstbestimmungsrecht durch eine rechtswidrige Besatzung permanent genommen, so muss sie sich dagegen wehren dürfen. Denn sonst ist das verletzte Recht ja praktisch wertlos. So verstanden ist das Widerstandsrecht ein Sekundärrecht zur Behebung der Primärrechtsverletzung. Etwas Ähnliches gibt es auch im privaten Bereich: Wenn bei Ihnen jemand ins Haus eindringt, dann ist das ein Hausfriedensbruch. Natürlich haben Sie dann das Recht, diese Person mit Gewalt aus Ihrem Haus zu werfen. Wenn die Person als Räuber mit einer Waffe eindringt und Sie bedroht, hätten Sie im Rahmen des Notwehrrechts in der Regel auch das Recht, diese Bedrohung gewaltsam abzuwehren.
taz: Einige Linke beziehen das palästinensische Recht auf Widerstand auch auf den 7. Oktober 2023, an dem die Hamas und andere Gruppen rund 1.200 Menschen töteten. Ist das legitim?
Ambos: Keinesfalls! Auch das Recht auf Widerstand unterliegt völkerrechtlichen Regeln. Es muss durch einen legitimen Repräsentanten der betroffenen Bevölkerung im Einklang mit dem humanitären Völkerrecht und den Menschenrechten ausgeübt werden. So sind insbesondere Zivilisten keine legitimen Ziele. Die Taten der Hamas habe ich deshalb schon kurz nach dem 7. Oktober gemeinsam mit einer Reihe von Kollegen als völkerrechtliches Verbrechen bewertet.
taz: Und wenn Menschen aus Gaza und dem Westjordanland sich mit Waffen gegen die israelische Besatzung wehren?
Ambos: Grundsätzlich haben Palästinenser das Recht auf Widerstand aufgrund der vom IGH festgestellten permanenten Vereitelung ihres Selbstbestimmungsrechts durch die israelische Besatzung. Ihre Widerstandshandlungen müssen sich aber selbst an die Regeln des Völkerrechts halten. Wenn Palästinenser direkt angegriffen werden, etwa von Siedlern, haben sie zudem ein Notwehrrecht nach nationalem Recht. Natürlich dürfen sie sich gegen solche Angriffe wehren.
Nahost-Debatten
Der Israel-Palästina-Konflikt wird vor allem in linken Kreisen kontrovers diskutiert. Auch in der taz existieren dazu teils grundverschiedene Positionen. In diesem Schwerpunkt finden Sie alle Kommentare und Debattenbeiträge zum Thema „Nahost“.
taz: In den letzten drei Jahren hat Israel das Völkerrecht wiederholt gebrochen. Die Armee tötete rund 20.000 Kinder in Gaza, rund 1,4 Millionen Palästinenser*innen leben derzeit in Zelten und temporären Behausungen. Welche völkerrechtliche Verantwortung hat Deutschland vor diesem Hintergrund als Verbündeter Israels?
Ambos: Jedes Land muss dazu beitragen, den völkerrechtswidrigen Zustand der Besatzung zu beenden. Kein Land darf einen solchen rechtswidrigen Zustand in irgendeiner Form unterstützen. Deswegen ist jegliche Unterstützung Israels im Westjordanland, zum Beispiel durch deutsche Waffenlieferungen, aber auch durch den Kauf von Produkten aus den israelischen Siedlungen, völkerrechtswidrig. Der Boykott solcher Produkte wird von zahlreichen engen Verbündeten Deutschlands gefordert und teilweise innerstaatlich durchgesetzt. Deutschland sollte entsprechende Bemühungen im Rahmen der EU nicht blockieren.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: Dossiê Guiné-Bissau: 53 anos de independência (Parte 2)
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: África & Diáspora
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Por Elisabete Vitorino*
Na primeira parte, vimos o que antecedeu à independência da Guiné-Bissau: a organização popular, a organização política e a Luta Armada de Libertação Nacional contra o domínio português. Nesta segunda parte, veremos a análise do professor Carlos Cardoso sobre o período pós-independência, as transformações ocorridas no país pós-independência e os avanços que o país precisa alcançar e quais ações necessárias para alcançar o desenvolvimento e os crescimentos político-econômicos e sociais.
Carlos Cardoso é formado em antropologia social e filosofia e doutor em Filosofia pela Universidade Friedrich Schiller, na Alemanha.
Confira a entrevista:
Elisabete Vitorino – Poderia falar um pouco sobre o período pós-independência e como impactou a sociedade guineense?
Carlos Cardoso – O período pós-independência é um período bastante conturbado. Desde logo porque pôs frente a frente duas concepções de sociedade diferentes; Uma concepção que vinha do processo da luta pela independência marcada pela dinâmica que essa mesma luta engendrou, mas também do outro lado uma concepção ligada a administração colonial com todos os seus vícios, com todas as suas características de uma sociedade dominada, de uma sociedade habituada a uma tutela. A uma tutela administrativa, a uma tutela política externa. Neste caso, na medida, se tratava de uma sociedade para todos os efeitos colonial.
Portanto, essas duas concepções, eu diria que de uma forma global entraram em choque e vários acontecimentos, vários episódios e várias movimentações revelaram essa concepção diferente de sociedade, daquilo que deveria ser a evolução social. Só para dar um exemplo, muitos dos comandos africanos aos quais nos referimos na publicação anterior recusaram-se a entregar as armas. As pessoas que pertenciam a tropa colonial recusaram a entregar as armas, provavelmente, pensando que era uma situação passageira que o PAIGC [Partido Africano para a Independência de Guiné-Bissau e Cabo Verde] não iria conseguir impor-se na nova sociedade, na nova Guiné-Bissau, que o poder não ia ser passado das mãos da administração colonial para a nova administração.
Houve vários episódios e vários acontecimentos que vão provar essa contradição. Foi também um período marcado por muita agitação política por conta dessa contradição, mas também por conta das expectativas que a independência estava a gerar ou gerou nos diferentes seguimentos da sociedade. Uma expectativa que foi de alguma maneira acompanhada de uma consciência revolucionária. Uma consciência que tinha presente aquilo que era os objetivos da revolução porque no fundo a independência e toda luta de libertação que se fez ao fim e ao cabo conduziu pelo menos na primeira fase uma autêntica revolução social. A conformação do PAIGC depois da independência foi uma conformação revolucionária que se distanciou radicalmente da forma de fazer, da forma de administrar colonial.
Desse ponto de vista, podemos dizer que entramos em um período de uma autêntica revolução social. E, nesse período, nós vimos que a sociedade por um lado tinha expectativas muito altas, por outro lado, nós vimos que progressivamente essas expectativas, essas esperanças começaram a ficar maiores. Na medida que o PAIGC não conseguiu ter força suficiente para fazer de fato prevalecer tudo aquilo que sonhava ainda nas matas da Guiné.
É um período de muitas expectativas é um período de muito engajamento. Os jovens andavam bastante entusiasmados para se engajarem no processo de transformação social que tinha iniciado nas matas da Guiné. Foi um período também em que o PAIGC começou a construir… Eu diria que deu continuidade a essa construção que se tinha iniciado nas matas, nas zonas libertadas de uma expansão das possibilidades, das oportunidades na área da educação, na área da saúde também. Foram feitos esforços tremendos no sentido de fazer com que a saúde chegasse em condições, não digo completamente gratuita, mas pelo menos em condições favoráveis as populações. Houve um esforço inicial, que hoje em dia ainda serve de referência no sentido de construir unidades industriais de transformação de produtos agrícolas. Começa a aparecer as primeiras fábricas de transformação, por exemplo, do caju, manga… Dos produtos em que a Guiné-Bissau tem vantagens comparativas relativamente a outros países. É um período de fato de muitas expectativas e das realizações efetivas nas diferentes áreas. Essas construções nessas diferentes áreas não tiveram uma continuidade e isso provocou algum desencanto por parte das populações
Quais foram as transformações ocorridas no país pós-independência?
Esses desencantos mencionados anteriormente foram se acumulando e a uma dada altura, podemos dizer que aquelas expectativas ficaram por cumprir porque essas transformações ocorridas no pós-independência começaram a fracassar e começaram cada vez mais a ficar menos imponentes. Então, podemos dizer que as obras sociais e econômicas começaram de alguma maneira a perder o ímpeto que tinham em 1974. É uma situação de desfalecimento do Estado. O Estado que começou por se afirmar como um Estado defensor dos mais pobres, dos menos privilegiados, pouco a pouco deixou de ser. A administração começou a ser povoada por indivíduos da elite, em parte burguesa… Essa pequena burguesia a que se referia [Amílcar] Cabral. Foi uma pequena burguesia que não se suicidou enquanto classe, enquanto defensora de seus próprios interesses. Não se suicidou e começou a revelar a sua verdadeira face. Tentando sobretudo enveredar por um emburguesamento da sociedade e isso obviamente começou a criar descontentes.
Provavelmente, o golpe de Estado em 1980 teria tentado de alguma maneira capitalizar esse descontentamento… Não estou a dizer com isso que só o descontentamento está na origem do golpe de Estado, mas o golpe tentou capitalizar esse descontentamento que já começava a sentir-se. O interessante é que esse descarrilamento no comportamento da pequena burguesia acentuou-se ainda mais depois de 1980, tendo conduzido inclusive à liberalização econômica. Começaram a aparecer alguns elementos da nova elite burguesa e isso agravou ainda mais o fosso e as clivagens sociais entre aqueles que tinham e aqueles que não tinham. Essa clivagem foi se agravando e com isso estou a falar já da terceira pergunta sobre quais foram as transformações ocorridas no pós-independência.
De fato, é um processo que teve suas origens já nos finais dos anos de 1970 e esse emburguesamento vai se agravar e vai criar clivagens cada vez mais fortes. Com isso podemos dizer que essas transformações, as conquistas que foram realizadas nos vários setores, nos vários domínios não foram sustentadas porque os objetivos já não eram aquilo que era a aspiração do povo da Guiné-Bissau. Nós estamos a falar da Guiné-Bissau porque em 1980 deixou de haver a unidade Guiné-Bissau/Cabo Verde. Os dois países separaram-se e cada um tomou o seu rumo. E podemos dizer que essas transformações no país em termos positivos foram sendo abandonadas, infelizmente para aqueles que depositavam alguma confiança no partido que liderava todo esse processo – o PAIGC. E a partir daí nós vamos ver uma série de ações que vão refletir essas contradições que começaram a surgir e sobre as quais Amílcar Cabral falava, afirmando que depois da independência, com a conquista da independência iriam começar a surgir novas contradições. E creio que essas contradições a que eu me referi estão um pouco ligadas a essas contradições devido a situação pós-independência.
Portanto, nós estamos a viver uma situação pós-colonial em que as esperanças começaram a desvanecer e entrou-se numa fase de clivagens, de lutas pelo poder. Porque o poder do Estado passou a ser um meio para salvaguardar os interesses de classe. Deixou de haver interesses unificados e começaram a surgir as contradições de classe e essas contradições que estão até hoje na origem da instabilidade na Guiné-Bissau.
Para você, quais os avanços o país precisa alcançar e quais ações necessárias para isso?
Há vários aspectos a serem considerados aqui. Primeiro é a questão política. Eu acho que o aspecto político é a primeira coisa a ser considerada, pois o país precisa de uma estabilidade. Certamente, vai depender da resolução de certos aspectos ligados às reformas institucionais que o país precisa. Reforma a nível da administração, uma reforma das forças armadas e da segurança. Esse aspecto é fundamental para que de fato se crie uma situação de normalidade institucional. Essa dimensão é extremamente importante. Depois tem a dimensão econômica. A Guiné-Bissau continua a ser um país dos mais pobres do mundo, com o rendimento per capita bastante baixo e com uma base de sustentação econômica bastante frágil. Portanto, um país cuja economia depende muito da agricultura e da exportação da monocultura do caju e por isso a nível econômico tem que haver uma transformação estrutural, devendo o país passar de produtor de matérias-primas para um país com capacidade de transformar essas matérias-primas a nível local, deixando o país de depender da flutuação dos preços do mercado a nível internacional. O mar da Guiné-Bissau é um mar bastante rico, mas o país não pode continuar a viver das receitas provenientes da licença de pescas.
Desse ponto de vista, há que fazer-se alguma coisa no sentido de transformar estruturalmente a economia do país. Do ponto de vista social, nós continuamos a assistir a algumas fissuras, algumas clivagens que inclusive outrora não existiam, como a clivagem da composição étnica do país. Começam a surgir pequenas contradições entre fulas de um lado e balantas de outro, outra entre mandingas de um lado e balantas do outro. Clivagens essas que se agudizam. A configuração do país, sobretudo a configuração política, apela à necessidade de alterar esse estado de coisas, caso contrário pode resvalar para situações muito mais complexas de gerir do ponto vista político e social. Tem que se atacar esse aspecto, e penso que os avanços que o país vai precisar, vai depender muito da gestão que se fizer deste assunto.
Nós assistimos a um país em que os militares continuam a ter uma voz bastante ativa na política, ou pelo menos em termos práticos de intervenção. Continuam a ter um peso bastante grande. Isso é uma situação que tem que ser resolvida. Há quem proponha um pacto entre civis e militares embora isso não seja consensual. Mas de alguma forma o país tem de resolver essa situação, para que os militares, por exemplo, passem a ter um caráter mais republicano e com funções republicanas de defesa da soberania. Eu acho que nessa direção tem que haver reformas estruturais a nível das forças armadas e da definição do tipo de forças armadas que nós queremos. A nível das reformas institucionais há que se pensar numa moldura governamental que faça prevalecer os princípios da democracia. O país fez uma transição democrática que não está completa e está longe de ser completa.
Portanto, essa afirmação e consolidação da democracia é um processo sobre o qual tem que se trabalhar nas próximas décadas para que de fato tenhamos um país democrático, um país onde o povo seja aquela franja da população que tem mais voz e cujo os interesses passem a representar um interesse do país, da nação e aí a consolidação democrática é um aspecto fundamental. Eu diria que provavelmente o país necessita de um pacto de cunho político, um pacto que traga os diferentes atores em desavenças hoje em dia para a mesma mesa e que se compenetrem todos de que o interesse do país está acima dos interesses dos grupos, dos interesses de elites, de classes. Portanto, esse é o caminho que o país tem que trilhar nos próximos anos.
Professor Carlos, eu agradeço sua disponibilidade em participar da entrevista e espero contar com sua colaboração em outras atividades
A experiência da Guiné-Bissau na luta por independência é algo indiscutível e única pois a mobilização e organização popular é retratada em livros e filmes nacionais sobre o tema. Vencer o domínio do invasor português com certeza marca a história do país e movimenta a história do país. Guiné-Bissau é hoje um país que busca crescer economicamente e no campo da educação superior. Hoje, o país é integrante da CPLP (Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa), o que o coloca em parceria com o Brasil no campo da formação superior com a vinda de estudantes guineenses para estudar no Brasil. Para além disso, a Guiné-Bissau tenta manter sua cultura, ancestralidade e modos de existir tão únicos, principalmente por meio da Língua Guineense idioma falado por mais de 90% da população.
*Elisabete Vitorino é paraibana, assistente social, mestra em Serviço Social e especialista em Saúde Mental pela UFPB. Atualmente é doutoranda em Estudos Étnicos e Africanos pela UFBA. Foi professora do curso de graduação de serviço social na Univerdidade Federal do Recôncavo da Bahia e professora formadora do curso de Aperfeiçoamento em Educação para as Relações Étnico-Raciais, promovido pela Universidade da Integração Internacional da Lusofonia Afro-Brasileira (Unilab) no Campus dos Malês. É autora do livro “Serviço Social e atuais tendências do exercício profissional na saúde mental em João Pessoa/PB”.
**Este texto integra um dossiê, no qual a colunista Elisabete Vitorino entrevista o professor Carlos Cardoso sobre a independência da Guiné-Bissau. Leia a primeira parte aqui.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: 5ª Feira Literária das Infâncias ocupa Academia Pernambucana de Letras com programação gratuita no Recife
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Fátima Pereira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Academia Pernambucana de Letras (APL), no bairro das Graças, no Recife, recebe, entre os dias 13 e 15 de novembro, das 9h às 17h, a quinta edição da Feira Literária das Infâncias (Flitin). Realizado pela Companhia Editora de Pernambuco (Cepe), o evento reúne atividades gratuitas voltadas ao público de zero a 14 anos, com lançamentos de livros, espetáculos teatrais, apresentações musicais, oficinas, contação de histórias e sessões de cinema. A edição deste ano tem como tema “Imaginar Futuros”, com propostas que aproximam literatura, ancestralidade, criatividade e questões ambientais.
Uma das novidades desta edição é a mudança no próprio nome do evento, que deixa de ser Feira da Literatura Infantil para se chamar Feira Literária das Infâncias. A alteração acompanha uma reformulação da proposta curatorial, que busca reconhecer a diversidade de experiências vividas pelas crianças, considerando diferentes contextos sociais, étnicos, culturais e de acessibilidade.
A curadoria é assinada pela editora de literatura infantojuvenil Gianni Gianni, que destaca a intenção de ampliar as representações das infâncias e aproximar a programação de questões contemporâneas. “Além de mudanças na linha curatorial, com uma direção artística mais alinhada a questões contemporâneas, a gente procurou se afastar de uma ideia um pouco estigmatizada sobre literatura infantil, procurando focar a pluralidade de infâncias e as formas de se viver essa fase da vida”, destaca.
A discussão sobre o futuro também atravessa temas como a crise climática, o isolamento social e a relação entre as pessoas e a natureza. Para Gianni, a feira pretende estimular reflexões sobre a construção coletiva de outros modos de viver, especialmente diante das preocupações que atingem crianças e jovens.
“Desde a pandemia de covid-19, muitas crianças e jovens enfrentam uma ansiedade relacionada à crise climática e ao isolamento social, seja ele causado por vírus, medo do outro ou excesso de tela. No meio dessa crise, como podemos restaurar o senso de comunidade e integração? Como repensar a organização do mundo, reaproximar natureza e cultura, humano e não humano, indivíduo e coletivo? Essas são questões que nos interessam na 5ª Flitin”, afirma.
A programação será distribuída pelos mais de três mil metros quadrados de área externa e pelos auditórios da APL. O espaço contará com praça de alimentação, cinema, palco principal, estandes da Cepe e de editoras convidadas, além de áreas destinadas a oficinas, lançamentos e atividades artísticas. Também haverá um espaço coletivo para designers e artistas gráficos apresentarem seus trabalhos.
Entre os destaques da feira estão os lançamentos de seis livros da Cepe. No sábado (14), às 10h10, serão apresentados os dois primeiros títulos da Coleção Samburá, iniciativa editorial que propõe revisitar a história de Pernambuco por meio da ficção, dando visibilidade a personagens e grupos historicamente marginalizados. Integram a coleção O resgate de Zambê, de Bell Puã, com ilustrações de Cal Santos, e Ayo, a menina do Porto, de Eron Villar, ilustrado por Bennê Oliveira.
A programação literária também inclui os títulos Assembleia dos bichos da cidade, de Isabelle Meunier; No canto da página, havia uma traça, de Rômulo Ramos; e Correria, primeiro livro-objeto da Cepe, criado pela artista visual Gabriela Amorim. No domingo (15), será lançado ainda O ratinho estrangeiro, de Samara Freitas.
O audiovisual terá espaço no Cine Flitin, instalado no auditório Mauro Mota. Durante os três dias, serão exibidos curtas-metragens que abordam temas como preservação ambiental, ancestralidade e identidade cultural. Entre as produções selecionadas estão Maré Braba, que trata dos impactos ambientais, e A menina e o pote, obra reconhecida internacionalmente e vencedora de mais de 20 prêmios.
As artes cênicas e a música também integram a programação. Na sexta-feira (13), às 9h30, o espetáculo Luanda Ruanda: histórias africanas, com Stephany Metódio, Alexandre Revoredo e Nino Alves, utiliza teatro e música para apresentar referências culturais do continente africano. No sábado (14), às 10h10, o público poderá acompanhar Evaristo, a Cutia, do Cutia Coletivo, que combina poesia de cordel e música para abordar os efeitos da urbanização sobre os animais.
Já no domingo (15), a programação reúne apresentações como Pantera rosa + Flores para que te quero?, com os malabaristas Ropix e Berniro Niro, o show Baju e Banda, da Cia da Baju, e o espetáculo Zé Tamanquinho, com Lucas dos Prazeres.
As nove oficinas previstas contemplam diferentes idades e linguagens artísticas, com atividades de dança, expressão corporal, música e criação. Entre elas está Orun para Erê, conduzida pelo artista e educador Orun Santana, que apresenta danças populares afro-brasileiras, como coco, ciranda, afoxé, samba, cavalo-marinho, maracatu e capoeira, por meio de brincadeiras. A atividade acontece na sexta e no domingo.
Para os bebês de zero a dois anos, a artista Gabriela Vasconcellos ministra, no sábado, a oficina Bebês-natureza, voltada à exploração sensorial e ao desenvolvimento da coordenação motora. A programação também inclui atividades de criação artística com materiais recicláveis, jogos e experiências de aproximação com a natureza.
A 5ª Flitin é realizada pela Cepe, com patrocínio do Banco do Nordeste e curadoria de Gianni Gianni. Todas as atividades têm entrada gratuita.

https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/no.title: Is it finally OK to be frank about 2000s pop culture? ‘It was profoundly, cheerfully horrible to women’
https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/no.author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/no.text:
In a 2008 episode of BBC Two’s comedy panel show Never Mind the Buzzcocks, the choreographer Arlene Phillips – the only woman on the programme – was told by the host Simon Amstell: “You look like you run a good whore house.” In reply, Phillips told a story with what appeared to be faux sincerity: while working with big stars, she explained, she would sometimes be asked to find dancers with “very special abilities” who might want to party after filming. Another panellist, the TV presenter Dermot O’Leary, mimed picking up a phone and said: “When you’re dancing tonight, do you mind having sex afterwards?” Everyone laughed.
Russell Brand’s imprisonment for rape and sexual assault this week, and allegations of sexual misconduct against the comedian and children’s author David Walliams have prompted scrutiny not only of the men involved, but of those who appeared to enable them. The chatshow host Jonathan Ross has apologised for a 2004 joke, in which he described the 15-year-old British comedy awards as being “like most 15-year-olds: drunk, unpredictable and probably going home with David Walliams”. The latter has denied the allegations made against him in reporting by the Guardian and ITV News, but is now the focus of an investigation by the Met police on separate sexual misconduct claims.
On the face of it, Phillips’s story had nothing to do with Brand or Walliams. But as clips like this have resurfaced they have been viewed in a different light. Were they simply jokes, or symptomatic of a wider culture in which women’s bodies and sexuality were routinely used as entertainment? Were they merely knockabout fun, or did they stand alongside the ubiquity of topless models on Page 3 of tabloid newspapers and so-called “lads’ mags”, which mixed lifestyle and often tasteless humour with overtly sexual images as a backdrop to something darker? Did the atmosphere of the time make more serious misconduct easier to overlook?
“The popular culture of the 2000s was profoundly, openly, cheerfully horrible to women,” said Sophie Gilbert, the author of Girl on Girl: How Pop Culture Turned a Generation of Women Against Themselves. “The shift from third-wave feminism to postfeminism during the 1990s enabled an environment where women were supposed to own their own objectification – to enjoy it and profit from it, and never complain.”
Gilbert cited Geri Halliwell and Kylie Minogue kissing on the chaotic entertainment show TFI Friday as a “surprise” for host Chris Evans, and Victoria Beckham being asked to step on a scale weeks after giving birth.
Throughout the late 90s and 00s, young female celebrities were relentlessly pursued by paparazzi, subjected to scrutiny over their weight and photographed in compromising situations. Upskirt pictures were published in magazines. In 2004, the highly successful celebrity magazine Heat devoted an entire special to celebrity cellulite, circling supposedly offending patches of skin on the legs of women including Beyoncé and former EastEnders star Martine McCutcheon.
When the singer Charlotte Church was 15, a website ran a countdown to her 16th birthday, when she would reach the age of consent – which was reported by the Sun. The Radio 1 presenter Chris Moyles, then 28, spoke on air about wanting to take Church’s virginity when she turned 16. Similar countdowns targeted other young celebrities, including Harry Potter star Emma Watson.
“I was made into this caricature: sexualised, patronised, ridiculed,” Church recently reflected. “I feel my character, the narrative of who I was in the world, was taken from me, and made into something salacious, or something to be ridiculed.”
Britney Spears faced similarly intrusive scrutiny as a teenager. In her memoir, The Woman in Me, she recalled reporters asking whether her breasts were real and “whether or not my hymen was intact”.
Ben Widdicombe, a former New York gossip columnist who examined the era in his memoir, Gatecrasher, recalled how the aftermath of 9/11 created an appetite for frivolous celebrity coverage; a phenomenon felt far beyond the US. “I saw an insatiable hunger for light, ‘sexy’ stories. This elevated a generation of young starlets into ‘pop icons’. However, the cruel logic of the tabloids is that they build you up only to knock you down,” he said.
The treatment of Spears particularly troubled him. “I genuinely feared that we were going to hound Britney to her death.” But, he said, audiences shared responsibility: “There’s no media without an audience – the public was baying for Britney to be humiliated, and the tabloids obliged.”
____
Of course, the era’s misogyny did not go completely unchallenged. Many women objected, but their voices were often drowned out by the all-powerful entertainment industry.
“It was only acceptable to the men who were being loud and dominating TV,” said the comedian Jo Caulfield. “As a woman who was around then, it wasn’t acceptable then or now. They did and still do protect the stars.”
Anna Tippett, an academic who specialises in the sexualisation of popular culture, said the idea that it was simply “a different time” overlooked the women who were actively challenging the culture. In a 2012 survey, Tippett found that 57.8% of respondents classified lads’ magazines as “soft pornography”, despite their mainstream acceptance. “Women who objected risked being labelled prudish, humourless or outdated,” she said. “There was considerable pressure either to appear ‘in on the joke’ or to remain silent.” Perhaps Phillips’s anecdote should be understood in that light.
Nowhere was that dynamic more visible than in comedy, an industry that blurred the line between provocation and intimidation. Brand’s public persona, and vast success, was built around sexual excess and outrageous stories about women.
“This was the nature of his appeal,” Gilbert said. “If TV and radio bosses didn’t want to call him out for his behaviour, it was because they knew his transgressions were what made him popular.”
In 2007, a 21-year-old Lily Allen appeared on Channel 4’s The Big Fat Quiz of the Year; again the only woman on the panel.
In another resurfaced clip, Ross suggested moving her away from Brand and the comedian and now Great British Bake Off presenter Noel Fielding so that she might “go home with her dress still on”. “How dare you? We’re not rapists,” Fielding said. “What if, horror of horrors, he ain’t even done a rape? You could ruin his reputation,” Brand quipped.
Even Allen laughed. But rewatching the footage years later made her uncomfortable, she said in 2023. “In retrospect, that’s really horrendous. I don’t think I felt that at the time, because it was the culture.”
During live performances of the TV sketch show Little Britain, Walliams played Des Kaye, a former children’s entertainer and sex offender who pulled down audience members’ trousers on stage and attempted to kiss them.
In 2008, the journalist Mary O’Hara described how comic Johnny Vegas had brought a young woman on stage at a London gig, where he groped her and repeatedly pulled up her skirt as she tried to cover herself. “Most disturbing, perhaps, was that around half the audience seemed to find this really funny,” she wrote. In a complaint about O’Hara’s article at the time, Vegas’s solicitors said that the young woman from the audience had told them she went along with the joke willingly and did not feel intimidated, scared or abused. His representatives have been contacted for comment for this article.
“I can’t tell you how toxic that culture was back then,” said the comedian Josie Long, who had her own backstage encounter with Brand.
“He would bite my face and I would tell him I didn’t like it and he would chase me around,” she recalled this week. “I would giggle because I was 22 and it was overwhelming.” Looking back, she said, she understood the behaviour as physical assault.
“Even at the smallest end of this spectrum, the culture was designed to tokenise and sexualise women,” Long said. It allowed “a kind of blokey camaraderie” that readily included “rape jokes and jokes about brutalising women”, while excluding different perspectives.
According to the TV writer Jack Searle, the rise of panel shows – at the expense of sitcoms – helped create a more adversarial form of comedy, dominated by “big, aggressive” male personalities. “Women – beware panel shows!” read the headline to an article by the comedian Jo Brand in the Guardian in 2009.
“Post-Britpop, post-Oasis, post-Cool Britannia, post-TFI Friday, you had the exuberance of the late 90s but with a nasty, lairy edge that certainly included misogyny,” Searle said. “Men on TV were like: ‘We know we shouldn’t be doing this, but we just have anyway.’”
Jessica Toomey, the director of the Live Comedy Association and the Women in Comedy festival, pointed to the lack of formal reporting procedures and the relatively small number of women in positions of power during the period. “The most frustrating sentence I keep hearing recently is: ‘Why didn’t they report it back then?’, when many victims just wouldn’t have felt empowered, informed or supported enough to know how to.”
___
So, how much has actually changed? Plenty, if you consider the rise of feminist blogging, an increase of women in positions of power in the industry and the ability to use social media to demand accountability.
“What has changed is not simply our recognition of misogyny, but the cultural willingness to confront it – and this is something to be celebrated,” Tippett said.
But other features remained, Tippett said, referring to the current era as “lad culture reimagined”: online abuse, “incel” culture and the prominence of figures such as self-professed misogynistic influencer Andrew Tate. Others point to the ubiquity of platforms such as OnlyFans as a contemporary successor to the influence of lads’ magazines such as Nuts and Zoo, and argue that widely available pornography, often seen by teenage boys, is more extreme than ever.
Meanwhile, some doubts remain as to whether greater awareness has translated into greater institutional accountability. This week, the comedian Lucy Beaumont, who revealed herself as a whistleblower in the investigation into Walliams, said she was struck by the lack of any obvious route for raising concerns. “There is no HR department in TV, there is no proper duty of care.”
She said she feared that speaking publicly about powerful figures could end her television career. “The reason high-profile people are not saying anything is because they lose work. No one wants to mess that up.”
In an article for the Guardian, she argued that the harmful actions of some men were seen and often ignored. “What happened to the women and girls wasn’t done in secret,” she wrote. “I think this is what the very national outcry is about – because it could have been called out, stopped, and women could have been prevented from being in dangerous situations with these men.”
Tara Joshi, a co-host of the 2000s pop-culture podcast Twenty Twenty, cautioned against treating the 2000s as a closed chapter. “Lad culture, tabloid culture, diet culture and misogyny all still exist, they’re just manifest in slightly different, perhaps more insidious ways,” she said.
Joshi acknowledged that conversations about abuse were now more open, and that more people may feel able to speak out. “But the reality is that Russell Brand was working in major film and television productions into the 2020s,” she said. “This conviction has only really been able to happen because there were an indisputable number of people coming forward with allegations.”
Searle said: “Celebrities behave that way when they feel untouchable, which comes from them recognising their own financial clout: everyone around them is earning their living from the star’s good reputation.
“Even now, unfortunately, it is still difficult to get someone to call out abusive behaviour if their salary depends on them not doing so.”

https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.title: How I survived being forced into pornography: ‘I died in that hotel room. I was a walking corpse’
https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.author: Anna Moore
https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.text:
When people ask Mariah Rief about her experience as a survivor of sex trafficking, they tend to start with the Craigslist ad which led the then 19-year-old to a “modelling shoot” at the Hilton hotel in San Diego. For others, the story starts when Rief enters the lobby and meets Theodore Gyi, the “photographer”. Or after they’ve taken the elevator up to a room, Rief standing at the threshold, Gyi behind her blocking her exit – and just inside the door, the silhouette of a second man waiting.
Whenever she talks about it, and whatever the questions, Rief always braces herself for blame, because, to some, it makes no sense. “You get, ‘But why did she answer that ad?’ ‘Why did she walk inside?’ and, my favourite, ‘Where were her parents?’” says Rief. “If you live in an idyllic world, it’s hard to imagine how this could happen.” The true starting point is years earlier. Rief’s beginnings, her childhood, layers of trauma and chaos, fast-tracked her to that hotel room in November 2016, believing that finally, life might be giving her a break. “It’s painful to say it but I was truly the perfect victim,” she says. “I saw that job as an opportunity. When I arrived at that hotel, I thought I was so lucky.”
Rief, 29, is in London to speak in parliament on behalf of UK Feminista. The campaigning organisation is launching a list of recommendations on how the government should use its new powers under the crime and policing act to force pornography sites to implement some fundamental protections. These include verifying that the people in the content they carry are adults, and have consented to its publication.
Until now, pornography sites have been able to act with almost total impunity, free to publish and profit from anything, no questions asked. Rief is one of the few whose case has resulted in criminal convictions. In 2022, Gyi, the cameraman who filmed her, was sentenced to four years for helping to coerce hundreds of women to appear in pornographic abuse videos. Ruben Andre Garcia, the performer who had been waiting for Rief in that hotel room, is now serving 20 years, while the ringleader of the operation, Michael Pratt, is serving 27 years. And yet, their videos and “brand” Girls Do Porn (GDP) couldn’t have been more “mainstream”. GDP, the subscription channel which operated between 2009 and 2020, released a new 45-minute video every week and also distributed content to sites like Pornhub. In 2014, Pornhub’s second most viewed video was made by GDP. Their videos were watched more than 1 billion times.
“They look polished, professional,” says Rief. Even now, some people doubt they could have involved sex-trafficked women, and on some level, Rief can see why. “Sex trafficking” means the use of someone for commercial sex acts by “force, fraud or coercion” – but for years, Rief blamed herself rather than believing she had been a victim of anything illegal. “My view of sex trafficking was the TV show Taken – you’re chased down, you’re hiding under the bed,” she says. “I thought I had done something to deserve it. I knew that I definitely didn’t sign up to do it but I guess I did it. Why didn’t I fight? Why didn’t I decide I’d rather die than do what they wanted? It’s almost 10 years to the day since I walked inside that hotel room and it’s taken so long to really understand it.”
Rief grew up in Missouri, the adopted child of a deeply religious family. “My biological mum was a drug addict who was selling her body to support her addiction,” she says. “To this day, I’m contacted by siblings I didn’t know I had.” At 18, she married a marine she barely knew and moved to his military base in San Diego. Within a year, that relationship was over and Rief was sleeping on someone’s sofa, working as a gym receptionist.
“I was just a teenager, but I was figuring it out,” she says. “I’d found a job, I’d got a car to get to work by putting the first payment on a credit card – and then I heard about this thing called ‘car insurance’. It cost more than I had in my bank account, and I just broke.” Rief called home in tears and asked for help. The response she got was, “Why aren’t you modelling?” She was advised to look on Craigslist.
“All my life, that had been the dream for me,” she says. “I’d been sent to modelling and etiquette classes. At 13, I’d been taught how to contour my face. We used to watch America’s Next Top Model and think, what an opportunity! When you grow up in Missouri, California seems like 1950s Hollywood. You just need to get over there and wait for that big break. Nobody, not even my mom, would have thought there were dangers in that world.”
When Rief went on Craigslist, “my mind was blown by how many modelling gigs there were,” she says. None mentioned nudity, although some were confusingly scant on detail. “I didn’t respond to those because I was raised in the church,” says Rief. After completing a stack of applications, Rief fell asleep in the early hours to be woken the next day by her ringing phone. A male voice, which she thought to be Australian, asked if she could get to the Hilton for a shoot that afternoon. For a few seconds, Rief wavered, so the man offered to put her in touch with someone who had worked with his company in the past.
“Within 10 minutes, I was called by a woman,” says Rief. “She said, ‘They’re safe, they’re legit, and it’s real money, you’ll get paid.’ I’m so stupid, it was happening so fast and I’d applied for so many jobs, I didn’t know which one this was, and I didn’t ask more questions. I just 100% trusted another woman. I don’t know why, but I would never expect a woman to deceive me in that capacity, knowing what I would be put through.” (Rief would later learn that women were paid $100 for making these reference calls.)
Arriving at the hotel was further reassurance. “It was really nice, right on the beach, close to the convention centre, full of businesspeople. I thought, ‘You don’t take a girl somewhere like this to do something bad.’” Gyi was friendly, but when he started to walk Rief towards the elevator, she hesitated. She’d expected the shoot to take place outside. “He told me that there was a lot of money involved. We needed to sign papers so, for my privacy and anonymity, they’d booked a room.” As they approached the room though, Gyi moved closer, and began to shepherd her. Standing at the threshold, the silhouette of a man inside and the smell of marijuana, Gyi said into her ear, “It’s going to be a lot better for you if you just walk in and let me tell you what we’re going to do here.”
“As soon as he did that, I had a very sobering thought,” says Rief. “‘I don’t have a choice. Walking into that room means they are going to get whatever they want and I don’t know what that entails.’ I didn’t know if they had guns. In that moment, I realised I needed to be what they needed. I needed to convince them that I’m not a liability if they let me leave at the end of it all. I wouldn’t be a problem for them. I walked inside and there were six studio lights pointing at the bed. I thought, ‘Oh God. Oh no.’”
Gyi explained that Rief would be performing in a “classy, well-made video” that would only be available on DVD for a select group of wealthy men in Australia. She could choose her wardrobe. A makeup artist arrived to make Rief up, and also cover her tattoos with foundation, supposedly to protect Rief’s anonymity. (“I later found out it was because they wanted us to look polished and adolescent,” says Rief.) When Rief told Gyi and Garcia that she was on her period, Garcia calmly presented her with a menstrual sponge. “I felt like I was 13,” she says. “He literally had to teach me how to use it.”
The shoot lasted eight hours. “The crazy thing is it felt like a blink of an eye,” she says. “Dissociation is really a hell of a drug. I died in that hotel room, I was a walking corpse. I was literally robotic, following every instruction.” At the end, though Rief hadn’t expected to be paid – she just hoped to leave alive – she was given an envelope stuffed with cash. It was $4,500. “I gathered all my stuff, I don’t even know if I put my shoes on, I just couldn’t believe it was over. It wasn’t until I got outside and it was pitch black that I realised how long I’d been there. For a while, I couldn’t even remember where I’d left the car.”
For about a month, nothing happened. Rief found a new job at a country club. She felt she was doing well. “I thought, ‘OK, maybe no one will ever know about this. Maybe I can move on,’” she says. “You try not to think about it. I didn’t tell one person.” Then, at work, a Facebook message arrived from someone she’d been at school with. It said: “How much did you get from it?” “I knew immediately,” she says. “By the end of that shift, my phone had just blown up.” GDP’s standard practice was to send screen shots and links to all the friends and family on a victim’s social media, partly to drive traffic and also to silence them, to beat them down. GDP also bought URLs in some of the victim’s names. That way, anyone Googling them went straight to a site with the videos and screenshots of her, creating the strong impression that it had all been consensual, and she was building a business in the adult industry.
For a while, Rief couldn’t see how life would ever be worth living again. The response from her community was too devastating. “There were memes about me. Elders in the church were saying, ‘we always knew she was no good.’ An aunt sent a message saying I was beautiful on the outside, but God knew I was ugly on the inside,” says Rief. “I had so many messages telling me I was a waste of life, I reached a point where I believed it. Maybe I deserved what happened to me.” Rief knows of 15 GDP victims who have since died by suicide or drug overdoses. She says that God and “spite” kept her alive. “People wanted me to die so bad, it lit a fire in me,” she says. “I decided I’m going to live. And I was going to turn this around.”
By 2021, Rief was a married stay-at-home mother of two young children when she was contacted by the FBI in connection with its case against GDP. Rief’s husband, whom she’d met at the country club, knew about the video – although it wasn’t something they discussed. “For years, I’d hardly talked about it at all,” she says. “When the letter came with this official FBI seal, I thought I’d done something wrong. It never crossed my mind that GDP had done anything wrong. I called the number, and told this FBI victim specialist that I wasn’t a victim of sex trafficking and not to contact me again.” The woman carefully explained their case and how GDP had operated. Then she said that the men were now in custody. “That was the best part,” says Rief. “That still gives me chills.” Rief was invited to attend the sentencing in a few weeks’ time at the San Diego federal building in order to give a victim impact statement.
Doing so changed her life. “I turned up and was shown into a conference room that was filled with young women,” she says. “I couldn’t believe how many there were. We were assigned a letter for anonymity and I was ‘U’. In the court, I got to hear all these girls before me, trembling, shaking, sobbing and describing the same experience in different variations. One had tried to jump out the window. One ran away and they dragged her back and assaulted her. For so long, I’d blamed myself and thought, ‘I should have done this’ or ‘why didn’t I do that?’ Now I had the opportunity to hear how that would have played out and it wouldn’t have gone well.”
Now Rief tells her story whenever she can, even though doing so makes her a target. Her phone is flooded with disbelieving messages, along with screenshots from the GDP video, showing her dead-eyed but smiling. “They’ll say, ‘you’re smiling, you’re not a victim, you’re a whore’,” says Rief, but adds that she doesn’t care. Rief runs her own consultancy to support other survivors and has authored a bill that is moving through the California senate, which would make content removal easier for survivors of online abuse. “My children are seven and four, they went with me to the capital building recently in Sacramento,” she says. “What they understand about my job is that ‘mommy changes the law.’”
“Sometimes I hate that the worst thing that’s happened to me has opened so many doors,” she continues. “It’ll never be worth it. I’ll never be able to say, ‘I’m glad this has happened.’ But I’ve been very intentional to make sure it’s not wasted.”

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Sophie Heawood
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.
I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.
I interviewed Brand in 2011 for a glossy magazine when he was promoting his remake of the film Arthur, with Helen Mirren. They were to be interviewed together, and an editor told me that if I accepted this freelance commission I would need to “muck about a bit and basically be into Russell Brand’s humour”.
When I played back the tape this week, I heard the me of 15 years ago asking Mirren if she had read his book (“No,” she hadn’t). Brand and I both pressed her. Had she really not read the chapter in Booky Wook 2 in which he outlines what he would like to do to her with her Oscar. “You have, I read it to you, the chapter’s called ‘Mummy Helen’,” he insisted. On the tape, he and I are both laughing while she is not. She was too dignified to play the game, saying she hadn’t been sure about joining his film project “because Russell is intimidating”. Yet we both ploughed on at her. I struggle now with how inappropriate this behaviour was – it’s mortifying. But it was what the job entailed.
Fast forward to Brand’s sentencing in court, where I listened intently to the victim impact statements from the women he was found guilty of attacking, each one stressing that recovering from his attacks had been rendered almost impossible by seeing him doing things such as joking about his sex drive every time they turned on the television or picked up a paper. I shuddered again. No, I’d had no idea what darkness he was capable of.
By 2014, when he turned to politics, I did at least write a piece about him in which I said he had, by now, “grabbed a thousand women as if they were lifeboats made of tits” and was trying to overthrow democracy “with a revolution fashioned from leftover bits of the internet and some string”, so at least my judgment had improved somewhat.
But he’s not the only interviewee whose darkness has been right there in front of me, hiding in plain sight. In 2007, I spent the day with Jared Leto, an actor who would go on to win an Oscar but who was then playing with his emo-rock band, 30 Seconds to Mars. I spent the day with him, his bandmates and various young women, some of them teenagers, who had flown into London from across Europe to see their hero play live. The girls who got to meet him seemed unworldly, wildly overexcited and close to fainting in his presence, and while I found his vibe intense to the point of weirdness, I never imagined he’d have any interest in these geeky fans. In 2026, he was accused by four women of criminal sexual conduct, with the alleged offences taking place when the women were teenagers. These are allegations he vigorously denies.
And now the spotlight is on David Walliams (who I’m relieved never to have worked with), after this week’s accounts from the women who had relationships with him as teenagers and now consider it grooming. He, too, denies any wrongdoing, beyond hurting their feelings. Walliams had sold £156m-worth of books in the UK alone, which is presumably why his industry protected him for so long.
Celebrities are surrounded by layers of people. When you interview one, people often imagine that you would have their phone number, but this is rarely the case, as that meeting will have been set up by a whole paper chain of intermediaries, which often include the star’s publicist, agent, manager and assistant. If there’s a photoshoot, you’ll be given a callsheet with numbers of the hair and makeup people, the styling department – and even drivers. Basically everyone apart from “the talent”, as their number is kept private every time. No wonder impressionable young fans were made to feel special by stars such as Walliams getting in touch directly from their own number.
I once interviewed a deeply charming celebrity at her home in West Hollywood, where we shared jokes about us both being chocoholics. As soon as I left, she called her agent to say I should be fired. I thought we’d got on well – but she was, as my editor subsequently reminded me, “a trained actress”. This is why the first rule of interviewing is to remember the maxim: “Why is this lying bastard lying to me?”, and that the star is never your friend. You are their conduit. And sometimes you are their cover.
- Sophie Heawood is a feature writer and commentator

https://www.humanite.fr/societe/manifest.text:
Avant un nouveau rendez-vous syndical le 17 novembre, avec une nouvelle journée de grève et de manifestations pour le secteur public, après le refus vendredi par le gouvernement de relever le point d’indice des fonctionnaires, différentes organisations syndicales et de défense des droits humains vont défiler ce samedi 14 novembre 2026.
Cette nouvelle journée de mobilisation agrège plusieurs revendications distinctes, mais qui convergent ce samedi : pour la hausse des salaires, pour davantage de moyens à l’éducation, contre la proposition de loi sur la présomption d’usage légitime des armes par les forces de sécurité, qui revient, selon elles, à “un permis de tuer” et contre laquelle près de 50.000 personnes avaient déjà manifesté le 20 septembre dans toute la France, selon les chiffres du ministère de l’Intérieur.
Les manifestations de ce week-end interviennent alors que le gouvernement a annoncé une revalorisation du Smic au 1er décembre estimée très insuffisante par les organisations syndicales, de l’ordre d’une vingtaine d’euros, indexation automatique comprise. D’abord appelée par la CGT, Solidaires et la FSU, la journée d’action intersyndicale du 17 novembre voit ses rangs gonflés par l’annonce de la CFDT, vendredi, qu’elle rejoignait les autres syndicats, après avoir fait part de sa déception des propositions salariales de l’exécutif à la sortie du dernier entretien avec Sébastien Lecornu.
Les mobilisations des lycéens se poursuivent elles aussi, les blocages affectant plus de mille établissements la semaine dernière selon les syndicats d’enseignants, de proviseurs et de lycéens, loin de l’estimation minimaliste de quelques dizaines avancée par le gouvernement.
Quant à la manifestation enfantiste de ce  14 novembre, elle agrège désormais autour d’elle des collectifs pour le climat, la justice sociale et des lycéens. Plus d’une centaine de rassemblements sont prévus dans plusieurs villes à l’appel du Collectif enfantiste et du Mouvement du 26 septembre.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: US air travel slowly recovers from nationwide flight ground stop as chaos continues
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Anna Betts
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Travel chaos continued across the US on Saturday morning as airlines scrambled to recover from a four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of the flights.
On Saturday morning, more than 3,000 flights within, into or out of the US had already been canceled, according to FlightAware.
The longest nationwide group stop in 25 years left passengers stranded at airports across the country, with no certainty about exactly when they may reach their intended destination.
The US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, on Friday blamed the ground stop on an ageing air control system, saying that the air traffic communications equipment became “overloaded with data and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers”.
“Because of that, we shut the system down,” the Trump administration official said.
The US homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, said on Friday that there was “no indication as of yet” that the communications failure had been caused by “a nefarious attack against us”.
Duffy warned that it would “take us time” to “resume normal operations”.
“Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” he said.
The rare flight grounding caused widespread disruptions, throwing travel plans into disarray as more than 8,000 flights across the country were canceled on Friday.
Among those affected by the fallout from the ground stop were sports teams traveling for games over the weekend. In college football, the Southeastern Conference announced that Mississippi’s game against Oklahoma had been rescheduled to Sunday – a day usually reserved for the National Football League (NFL).
Meanwhile, a men’s college basketball game between the University of North Carolina Greensboro and Cornell University, scheduled for Saturday, was postponed.
And although flights began resuming after the FAA’s decision to lift the ground stop, the aftermath still appears to be affecting passengers around the country. There were reported flight disruptions at airports in major cities including Boston, Washington DC, New York and Miami.
In a statement on Saturday, Duffy said that “operations are slowly returning to normal this morning” – but he added that “you will continue to see some delays and cancellations as carriers reschedule flights and reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most”.
“Our top priority right now is making sure travelers get home safely to their families as quickly as possible,” he said.
Duffy said he planned to hold a news briefing at 10.30am ET.
The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) also issued a statement on Saturday morning warning that “while US flights have resumed, there may be some follow-on disruption as airlines work to re-book affected passengers and get all services back to normal”.
The statement added: “Anyone due to travel on flights between the UK and USA should check with their airline for the latest information before heading to the airport.”
During the news briefing on Friday evening, Trump administration officials urged Congress – which until January is controlled by the White House’s Republican allies – to “fully fund a full build of a brand new air traffic control system”.
Friday marked the third nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA this century. The first occurred after the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. And the second took place in January 2023, after a pilot notification system went down.
