https://taz.de/Der-Hausbesuch/!6224387/.title: Der Hausbesuch: Das Gestrickte ist politisch
https://taz.de/Der-Hausbesuch/!6224387/.author: Waltraud Schwab
https://taz.de/Der-Hausbesuch/!6224387/.text:
Der Hausbesuch: Das Gestrickte ist politisch
Swetlana Nikitenko macht Stop-Motion-Filme mit gehäkelten Figuren. Es ist ihre Plattform, um gegen Rassismus und Ausgrenzung zu protestieren.
Von der Oma hatte Swetlana Nikitenko Stricken und Häkeln gelernt, weil sie für ihre Puppen neue Kleider machen wollte. Fragte damals jemand, was sie werden will, sagte sie: „Modedesignerin für Puppen.“ Aber so einfach ist das nicht.
Draußen: Wer von der vielbefahrenen Frankfurter Allee in Berlin-Friedrichshain in die Kreutzigerstraße will, muss den Durchgang unter einem Haus nehmen. Dahinter ist szenige Idylle. Bäume, ein Spielplatz, der Verkehrslärm gedimmt. An einer Wand steht: „Frauen, die kämpfen, leben!“ Viele der Häuser sind wild bemalt, als wäre hier Besetzerland. Und das war es nach der Wende ja. Auch das Haus, in dem Swetlana Nikitenko wohnt, rockt auf diese Weise.
Drinnen: Altbauten in Berlin haben oft ähnliche Grundrisse. Hier aber wurde die Wand zwischen dem gefangenen Zimmer, das zum Hinterhof geht, und der Küche herausgerissen und es wurde eine große Wohnküche daraus. Nikitenko hat aufgeräumt. In Kombination mit der dunkelgrün gestrichenen Wand wirkt die Ordnung kühl. Nur die gehäkelte Hirschtrophäe über der Tür zum Klo deutet versteckten Humor an. Mehr ist nicht zu erkennen von Nikitenkos Passion.
Aufregung: Swetlana Nikitenko findet es gewöhnungsbedürftig, Wildfremden ihre Wohnung zu zeigen. Und doch freut sie sich über Aufmerksamkeit. Vor allem über die für ihre Arbeiten. Sie führt ins Zimmer gegenüber, auch das ist aufgeräumt. Auf den Regalen stehen gehäkelte Objekte, darunter das Rote Rathaus, das Brandenburger Tor, ein Mann im Rollstuhl, ein gehäkeltes Coronavirus, eine Großstadttaube, die Skateboard fährt. Die Figuren sind niedlich und leicht zu übersehen bis auf das ballgroße Virus.
Groß im Kleinen: Nikitenko häkelt nicht einfach so Figuren; sie häkelt erkennbare Menschen. Der Mann im Rollstuhl ist mit seiner Brille und dem Bart als der Inklusionsaktivist Raúl Krauthausen zu identifizieren; die zwei Männer mit den Sternchenbrillen als die Magier Siegfried und Joy. Eine Figur mit hochgezogener Kapuze ist Nico Semsrott, Kabarettist und Politiker. Aus einem Hobby – Nikitenko häkelte etwa mal so nebenbei einen Hasen für das Kind einer Freundin oder eine Bohrmaschine für ein Portal, wo man Maschinen ausleihen kann – ist ihre Form des politischen Protestes geworden.
Protest: In den sozialen Medien lautet Nikitenkos Alias-Name „strickt dagegen“. Mittlerweile häkelt sie eher. Denn mit dieser Technik kann sie ihre fragilen und beweglichen Figuren besser konzipieren. Beweglich müssen sie sein, da Nikitenko mittlerweile kurze Stop-Motion-Animationsfilme mit ihnen macht, um etwa Demos für ein AfD-Verbot anzukündigen, um Inklusion zu fordern oder Obdachlosigkeit zu thematisieren. Auch queere Themen greift sie auf. So zaubern Siegfried und Joy in einem der Filme eine Regenbogenflagge auf den Reichstag, nachdem Julia Klöckner das untersagte. Nikitenkos Filme entstehen immer in Absprache mit Betroffenen. „Für mich sind Betroffene Expert*innen, die zu Wort kommen sollen“, sagt sie.
wochentaz
Dieser Text erschien zuerst in der wochentaz, unserer Wochenzeitung von links!
In der wochentaz geht es jede Woche um die Welt, wie sie ist – und wie sie sein könnte. Eine linke Wochenzeitung mit Stimme, Haltung und dem besonderen taz-Blick auf die Welt. Jeden Samstag neu am Kiosk und natürlich im Abo.
Gen Z: Das Unverständnis für die Jugendproteste treibt sie ebenfalls um. „Mir gefällt es nicht, dass die junge Generation nicht gehört wird. Schlimmer: Sie wird kriminalisiert.“ Einen Stop-Motion-Film zum Wehrdienst hat sie schon gemacht, er hat mit „Mehrzweckeiern“ zu tun. Junge Leute verstehen das. „Es ist gruselig, wie die alten weißen Männer dasitzen und eine gestrige Politik machen, die die Zukunft von Mensch und Erde so völlig verspielt.“
Kursk: Geboren ist Nikitenko in Eberswalde. Ihr Vater war Offizier in der sowjetischen Armee, ihre Mutter Deutsche. Als sie sieben Monate alt ist, wird der Vater nach Kursk versetzt; dort verbringt sie ihre Kindheit. Sie wächst nicht zweisprachig auf, der Vater sieht es nicht gerne, wenn die Mutter Deutsch spricht; aber ein bisschen versteht sie doch. Der Vater will auch nicht, dass sie in der Schule Deutsch als Fremdsprache wählt. „Er meinte, es sei unfair, weil ich einen Vorteil hätte durch die Mutter.“ Wie sie heute an Kursk denkt, die russische Stadt, in der inzwischen der Ukrainekrieg angekommen ist? „Gut, dass Sie danach fragen, die meisten denken, wenn sie Kursk hören, nur: Größte Panzerschlacht im Zweiten Weltkrieg“, sagt sie. Putins Angriff auf die Ukraine findet sie schlimm; zu Kursk an sich hat sie keinen Bezug mehr.
Vilnius: 1980, als Nikitenko zwölf ist, wird der Vater nach Litauen versetzt. Plötzlich lebt sie in einer Stadt, wo alles anders ist. „Die Litauer verstanden sich als Europäer in Kultur, Bildung, ihren Vorstellungen von Freiheit. Es gab diese Idee von der anderen Welt.“ Sie merkt jetzt, wie „verkrustet die Sowjetunion mit der vorgegaukelten Gleichheit“ war. „Auf alles Deckel drauf“, sagt sie. „Das System hat viel mit mir gemacht, nämlich dass ich funktionieren will, auch wenn ich nicht mehr kann. Und dann in Litauen diese Erfahrung, dass sich Leute was trauen.“ Litauisch kann sie ein bisschen, „die Sprache ist echt schwer“. Damals sprachen sowieso alle auch Russisch.
Chaos: In Litauen beginnt Nikitenko ein Studium der Philologie, wird schwanger, studiert weiter, bringt 1987 die Tochter zur Welt, lebt bei den Eltern. 1988 trennt sich die Mutter vom Vater und geht zurück in die DDR, nach Bernau bei Berlin. Auch Nikitenko stellt einen Ausreiseantrag und kommt im Februar 1989 nach. „Von Vilnus, der lebendigen Stadt, nach Bernau, das bieder wirkte und grau in braun.“ Ihre neue Realität fasst sie so zusammen: „Mittellos, alleinerziehend, ohne Deutsch.“ Dass sie in Litauen vier Semester studiert hatte, juckt hier niemanden. Man erkennt ihr nicht mal das Abitur an.
Bernau: Kaum angekommen, findet sie einen Job als technische Zeichnerin. Das Fach hatte sie in der Schule und war gut darin. Sie macht Reinzeichnungen im „Schichtpressstoffwerk“, so heißt die Fabrik. „‚Schichtpresstoffwerk‘ – ich liebe dieses Wort.“ Deutsch lernt sie jetzt sofort. In Bernau leben viele Russen und Russinnen. Schnell kriegt sie mit, dass nicht mehr viel von der deutsch-sowjetischen Freundschaft übrig ist. Sie hört, wie sich die Kolleg*innen in der Pause über die „Russenweiber“ auslassen; die hätten Zeitungen an den Fenstern statt Gardinen, könnten die Wäsche nicht richtig waschen, putzten die Treppen am Sonntag statt Samstag. „Hey, ich kann mein Mittagessen auch irgendwo anders essen“, sagt sie. „Das geht doch nicht gegen dich“, ist deren Antwort.
Die Wende: Mit der Wende wird das Schichtpressstoffwerk abgewickelt. Nikitenko nimmt daraufhin jeden Job an, den sie in der Nähe der Wohnung kriegen kann, solange ihr Kind klein ist. „Schlechte Bedingungen, wenig Geld, mit Ausländerstempel. Ich kann mich gar nicht erinnern, wovon ich gelebt habe.“ Dazu schlimme Erfahrungen mit Nazis. „Ich soll mich verpissen. Man würde meine Wohnung anstecken.“ Sie versuchte, sich nicht anmerken zu lassen, dass sie Angst hatte. „Das erste Jahr in Bernau hab ich nur geweint.“ Besser wird es, als sie zum ersten Mal in einem besetzten Haus im Prenzlauer Berg ist und sieht, dass es auch in Berlin Leute gibt, die alles miteinander teilen. Sie zieht dann ja auch nach Friedrichshain. „Aber auch in Bernau hab ich mit der Zeit tolle Menschen gefunden.“
Arbeitsamt: Die Jobsuche geht weiter. Ihr wird dann vom Arbeitsamt einzig eine Fortbildung als Hotelfachfrau angeboten. „Ausgerechnet mir; ich bin doch gar nicht der Typ, der auf wildfremde Menschen zugeht.“ Sie zieht es trotzdem durch, jobbt anschließend in Kneipen, einer Buchhandlung, einer Schildermalerfirma, bis sie, da sie sich im Jugendclub der Tochter engagiert, 2003 beim Landesjugendring Berlin eine Arbeit findet. „Endlich etwas Sinnvolles.“ Heute arbeitet sie beim Verein für demokratische Kultur, der mobile Beratung gegen Rechtsextremismus macht, Projekte gegen Rassismus und Antisemitismus. „Ich arbeite mit tollen Leuten.“
Zukunft: Nebenbei strickt und häkelt Swetlana Nikitenko. „Aber Handarbeit, das gilt vielen als wertlose Frauenbeschäftigung.“ Es war ihre Tochter, die sie ermutigte, ihre Sachen doch auf Instagram zu stellen. Plötzlich war da öffentliche Resonanz. Eins ihrer persönlichen Highlights: als ihr Film zu „Berlin autofrei“ 2025 beim Wettbewerb „Make it real“ von ARD Kultur nominiert ist. „Ich will noch so viel machen, habe so viele Ideen und so viel vor.“
Am 22. November 2026 feiert der taz Salon in Hamburg unter dem Motto „Anders machen“ sein 20-jähriges Jubiläum. Dort wird bei einem Strickzirkel ausgelotet, wie Stricken und Politik zusammenpassen.

https://taz.de/Schafkopfspiele/!6224449/.title: Schafkopfspiele: Und die Sau, die ist das Ass
https://taz.de/Schafkopfspiele/!6224449/.author: Jörn Kabisch
https://taz.de/Schafkopfspiele/!6224449/.text:
Schafkopfspiele: Und die Sau, die ist das Ass
In Bayern spielt man gerne Schafkopf, auch Ilse Aigner gehört zu den Koaddara. Eine Plakette am Wirtshaus braucht es dafür aber nicht.
D as schönste Kartenspiel, das man im Wirtshaus spielen kann, heißt Schafkopf. Ich habe mich dafür jahrelang in Berlin mit Kolleg:innen getroffen, die wie ich bayerischen Migrationshintergrund haben. Das ist wichtig, denn zu diesem Spiel gehört eine eigene Geheimsprache, die man umso leichter beherrscht, je mehr man des Bayerischen oder Fränkischen mächtig ist – interessanterweise spielt das Trennende der Dialekte in diesem Fall kaum eine Rolle.
Sitzen also vier Personen am Nebentisch und hält jede:r acht Karten in der Hand und es fallen Begriffe wie Gras, Eichel oder Schellen, ist oft von Luschen die Rede, von Unter oder Ober, am meisten aber von der Sau – dem Ass –, dann ist es eine Schafkopfrunde. Überhaupt: Es wäre eine Schande, ohne Worte zu spielen. Die Sprache ist derb, versierte Koaddara (Kartenspieler) haben für jede Karte, die auf den Tisch gelegt wird, einen kreativen Kommentar parat.
Wie beim Doppelkopf geht es darum, möglichst schnell herauszufinden, wer der eigene Partner ist, um dann gemeinsam möglichst hoch zu gewinnen oder nur knapp zu verlieren. Das Wortgeklingel dient dazu, geballte Potenz zu verbreiten, niemals aber (Achtung: Ironie), Wünsche an den vermeintlichen Partner zu richten. Das ist verboten. Als Anfänger sollte man trotzdem nach den ersten Partien gelernt haben, um was es beim „Schmieren“ und „Abspatzen“ geht und auch schon mal der „Oiden“ (die Alte: das Eichel-Ass) begegnet sein.
Aigner ist passionierte Schafkopfspielerin
In Bayern gehört das Spiel zum Wirtshaus wie die Halbe Helles. Oder auch nicht. Denn auch wenn mit Ilse Aigner eine passionierte Schafkopfspielerin bald das höchste Amt im Staate ausüben wird, hält der Bayerische Landesverein für Denkmalpflege das Spiel als Kulturgut für bedroht. Zur Rettung wurde die Kampagne „Schafkopffreundliches Wirtshaus“ gestartet. Zentrales Element ist eine gleichlautende „wetterfeste“ Plakette, die man sich als Wirt an den Eingang schrauben kann.
Als Koaddara habe ich dafür nur einen Kommentar: „Weiter“. Bei diesem Spiel bin ich raus. Denn am Gasthaus liegt es am wenigsten, falls die Leute tatsächlich nicht mehr schafkopfen. Bei uns darf einfach, weil draußen Gasthaus steht, drinnen auch gespielt werden. Vor allem an Tisch 3, da hat die selige Frau Deininger dem halben Ort das Karteln beigebracht.
Und mal ganz grundsätzlich: Es würde mich nicht wundern, wenn schon ein paar Wirte wegen der ganzen Plakettenschrauberei zusperren mussten. Ständig bekommt man irgendetwas mit Gastfreundlichkeit, Nachhaltigkeit oder Traditionsbewusstsein angeboten, das man sich an die Tür pappen soll. Nur die Plakette „Biertrinkerfreundliches Wirtshaus“, die fehlt noch.

https://taz.de/Gruene-in-Mecklenburg-Vor.title: Grüne in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Zustimmung trotz Bauchgrummeln
https://taz.de/Gruene-in-Mecklenburg-Vor.author: Rainer Rutz
https://taz.de/Gruene-in-Mecklenburg-Vor.text:
Grüne in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Zustimmung trotz Bauchgrummeln
Die Grünen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern stimmen auf ihrem Parteitag mit großer Mehrheit für Rot-Rot-Grün. Zugleich quält man sich mit einer alten Affäre.
Viel war bei den Grünen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern am Samstag von Kompromissen die Rede, die sie bei den Verhandlungen um eine künftige Landesregierung hätten eingehen müssen. Mal wurde kritisiert, der Koalitionsvertrag mit SPD und Linken sei zu unkonkret. Mal hieß es, er enthalte zu wenig zum Thema Inklusion. Schließlich das Festhalten an der Bezahlkarte für Geflüchtete – ein Armutszeugnis sei das.
Wie zuvor schon bei Linkspartei und SPD votierte am Ende aber auch der Landesparteitag der Grünen nahezu geschlossen für die Koalitionsvereinbarung und den Eintritt in eine rot-rot-grüne Regierung unter SPD-Ministerpräsidentin Manuela Schwesig. Also auch jene unter den rund 100 Delegierten, die in den Reden auf ihr „Bauchgrummeln“ hingewiesen oder erklärt hatten: „Die Grünen hätten hier stärker kämpfen müssen.“
Wenig verwunderlich sah Grünen-Chefverhandlerin Claudia Müller das etwas anders. „Ich bin wirklich stolz darauf, was wir als kleinster Partner herausgeholt haben“, warb die gewesene Spitzenkandidatin und designierte Umwelt- und Mobilitätsministerin von Mecklenburg-Vorpommern beim Parteitag in Stralsund um Zustimmung. Um dann hinzuzufügen: „Es ist ein Kompromiss, aber der richtige Kompromiss.“
Im Umwelt- und Klimaschutz sowieso, aber auch in allen anderen Bereichen des Koalitionsvertrags habe die Partei ihre Handschrift hinterlassen, so Müller. Sie betonte, dass die neue Regierung keine „Verlängerung“ der vorherigen rot-rot Regierung Schwesig mit grünem „Add-on“ sei, sondern eben etwas gänzlich Neues.
Unterstützung von der Bundesspitze
Unterstützung für Claudia Müller gab es von der Grünen-Bundesspitze. „Es freut mich so irre, dass es uns gelungen ist, dass ihr im neuen Landtag seid und jetzt Teil der Regierung werdet“, sagte Parteichefin Franziska Brantner. Sie lobte die „grüne Handschrift“ des Koalitionsvertrags, verlor dann aber nicht mehr viele Worte über das 130-seitige Papier.
Umso ausführlicher widmete sich Brantner gut gelaunt Tankrabatt, Stromsteuer, Übergewinnsteuer. Das große Ganze und darüber hinaus. Zum Beispiel: „Wir brauchen auch endlich eine müllfreie Welt.“ Oder: „Wir müssen unabhängig werden von den amerikanischen Tech-Bros.“ Die Delegierten applaudierten freundlich. Es wurde auch gelacht.
Dass die innerparteiliche Freundlichkeit der Nordost-Grünen gleichwohl ihre Grenzen hat, zeigte sich auf einem thematischen Nebenschauplatz des zweitägigen Parteitags: Vor einem Jahr hatten Vorwürfe von Machtmissbrauch und übergriffigem Verhalten die damalige grüne Landtagsfraktion in Schwerin erschüttert. Unmittelbar vor Beginn des Wahlkampfs lag der grüne Laden in Trümmern. Auch später kochte das Thema immer wieder hoch.
Es gilt nicht zuletzt als Verdienst von Claudia Müller, dass es die Grünen bei der Landtagswahl am 20. September mit knapp über 5 Prozent überhaupt erneut ins Parlament geschafft haben. Nachdem die ursprüngliche Spitzenkandidatin Constanze Oehlrich, die im Zentrum der Affäre stand, kurzerhand wieder abgesägt wurde, oblag es der resoluten Bundestagsabgeordneten Müller, den Landesverband im Wahlkampf wieder in die Spur zu bringen.
Warten auf die Aufarbeitungskommission
Und dennoch: Wer im vergangenen Jahr genau was gemacht hat, ist bis heute nicht geklärt. „Hier ist auch überhaupt nichts befriedet“, sagte eine Delegierte zur taz. „Schweigen und Besänftigen haben noch nie geholfen“, erklärte eine andere. Die alte Fraktion oder der alte Landesvorstand oder beide hätten eine richtig schlechte Figur gemacht und die Aufklärung behindert, heißt es immer wieder.
Ein pünktlich zum Parteitag veröffentlichter Beitrag zum Thema in der Welt – überschrieben mit „Moral ist, wenn man trotzdem mobbt“ – bietet zwar insgesamt wenig Neues und noch weniger Erhellendes. Dessen ungeachtet ist die grüne Aufregung groß.
Beim zweiten Teil des Parteitags am Sonntag könnte es daher noch einmal turbulent werden, wenn ein Antrag behandelt wird, in dem ein Teil der Basis fordert, dass eine versprochene Aufarbeitungskommission endlich ihre Arbeit aufnimmt. „Ich habe Redebedarf“, sagte eine Delegierte bereits zu Beginn des Parteitreffens. Sie war nicht die einzige.
Um das Problem dürfen sich dann aber bereits die am Samstag gewählten neuen Landesvorsitzenden Ines Balke und Pascal Hilker kümmern. Der 22-jährige Greifswalder Lehramtsstudent Hilker sagte der taz bereits im Vorfeld, es sei sein Ziel, den rund 1.700 Mitglieder kleinen Grünen-Verband in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern wieder zusammenführen.

https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6224397/.title: Die Wahrheit: Rote Daunenjacke trifft auf schöne Frisur
https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6224397/.author: Paul Amsel
https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6224397/.text:
Die Wahrheit: Rote Daunenjacke trifft auf schöne Frisur
Eine so wahre wie poetische Geschichte aus dem Reich Bremer Bürgersteige, wo gegenläufiges Personal aufeinanderprallen kann.
Jüngst ereignete sich in Bremen ein berichtenswerter Vorfall. An einem Freitag gegen 14.25 Uhr fuhr eine Frau in einer roten Daunenjacke auf ihrem Fahrrad die Hollerallee gen Südosten. Sie nutzte dabei den Radweg. Als sie ungefähr auf Höhe des Standesamtes war, bemerkte sie in rund 50 Metern Entfernung einen Mann, der ihr auf dem Fahrrad entgegenkam. Er fuhr auf dem Radweg Richtung Nordwesten entgegen der vorgesehenen Fahrtrichtung. Die Frau setzte ihre Fahrt ohne Bedenken fort. Sie rechnete damit, dass der Mann auf den angrenzenden Bürgersteig ausweichen würde.
Dies dachte auch der Mann über die Frau in der roten Daunenjacke. Beide Radfahrer waren noch etwa 25 Meter voneinander entfernt, als die Frau in der roten Daunenjacke entschied, doch auf den Bürgersteig auszuweichen. Im selben Moment traf der Mann die adäquate Entscheidung, sodass sie nun auf dem Bürgersteig aufeinander zufuhren.
Instinktiv verlangsamten beide die Geschwindigkeit. Der Mann entschied, auf dem Bürgersteig zu bleiben, bis die Frau ausweichen würde. Da dies aber auch die Frau dachte, blieben sie auf derselben Spur. Als sie nur noch zehn Meter voneinander entfernt waren, lenkten beide auf den Radweg zurück, sodann zurück auf den Bürgersteig und noch einmal auf den Radweg. Sie mussten bremsen und standen sich nun direkt gegenüber. In diesem Moment merkte die Frau mit der roten Daunenjacke, dass der Mann eine schöne Frisur hatte.
Die Frau entschied, schweigend zu warten, bis der Mann wieder auf sein Rad stiege und über den Bürgersteig an ihr vorbeiführe. Dazu aber entschied sich im selben Moment auch der Mann mit der schönen Frisur. Sie warteten. Schließlich sprach er: „Fahren Sie doch gerne seitlich an mir vorbei!“
Die Frau aber hatte sich im selben Moment dazu entschieden, den Mann zum Losfahren aufzufordern. „Fahren Sie doch gerne seitlich an mir vorbei!“, sagte sie. Infolge der gleichzeitig geäußerten Aufforderung mussten beide gleichzeitig lachen, wobei die Frau ein eher dunkles Lachen lachte, der Mann aber ein helles, beinahe schrilles.
Nach etwa elf Sekunden des Lachens, das langsam leiser wurde, sagten beide gleichzeitig: „Fahren Sie!“ Es folgte die folgende Abfolge von Aufforderungen, die von der Frau mit der roten Daunenjacke und von dem Mann mit der schönen Frisur gleichzeitig und im exakt selben Rhythmus ausgesprochen wurden, als redeten sie mit einer einzigen Stimme: „Bitte, fahren Sie! – Gut, dann bleiben Sie bitte stehen und ich fahre an Ihnen vorbei. – Ich? – Sie? – Ich meinte Sie. –Ich also. – Bitte, fahren Sie!“
Auch dieses Gespräch führte nun zu keinem Ergebnis. Beide stellten ihr Fahrrad ab und setzten sich auf den Boden. Jenes geschah ebenso im selben Moment. Nach einigem Nachdenken begann die Frau, ganz langsam an den abgestellten Rädern vorbeizurobben. Doch auch der Mann hatte sich dazu entschieden, und also robbten die beiden im selben Moment los und stießen schon bald mit ihrer Stirn zusammen.
Sie hatten nämlich beide damit gerechnet, dass der andere abbremsen oder ausweichen würde. Tatsächlich aber fassten sie im selben Moment den Entschluss, über die andere Person hinwegzurobben. Daher entstand eine beiderseitige Aufwärtsbewegung, die zu einem gleichzeitigen langsamen Aufrichten führte, bis sie sich Stirn an Stirn, Brust an Brust, Hüfte an Hüfte, Knie an Knie, Fuß an Fuß gegenüberstanden. Sie konnten den Atem voneinander spüren, was nicht das Schlimmste war, da beide kurz vorher die Zähne geputzt hatten.
Es folgten mehrere Ausweichversuche, erst Richtung Häuserfront, dann Richtung Straße, erst einen Seitschritt, dann gleich drei schnelle Seitschritte hintereinander. Da die Frau mit der roten Daunenjacke und der Mann mit der schönen Frisur alle Schritte aber im selben Moment taten, blieben sie im selben Abstand voneinander stehen.
Noch einmal entschied sich die Frau, das Problem kommunikativ zu lösen. Der Mann traf dieselbe Entscheidung im selben Moment. So sagten sie beide im Chor: „Es kann doch nicht sein, dass wir nicht aneinander vorbei…“ Als sie merkten, dass sie dasselbe sagten, hörten beide gleichzeitig auf zu reden, und warteten genau 27 Sekunden.
Reden, reden, reden
Sie holten dann gleichzeitig Luft und merkten daran, dass auch die andere Person wieder zu reden anfangen wollte. Beide entschieden sich aber, nun so lange zu reden, bis die andere Person zu reden aufgehört haben würde. „Es kann doch nicht sein, dass wir nicht aneinander vorbeikommen“, sagten sie abermals und redeten dann mindestens eine halbe Stunde weiter. Sie redeten über das Wetter, über das Radfahren, später auch über die Umsatzsteuer und den Krieg in der Ukraine. Sie verwendeten dabei exakt dieselben Worte und holten an denselben Stellen Luft. Schließlich sagte die Frau: „Gut, wenn wir keine Lösung finden, hole ich meine große Schwester.“
Der Mann kündigte im selben Moment an, seinen großen Bruder zu holen. Beide setzten sich auf den Boden und riefen ihre Geschwister an. Sie bewegten sich nicht mehr, bis sein Bruder und ihre Schwester am vereinbarten Ort eintrafen, was gleichzeitig geschah. Als die Schwester der Frau in der roten Jacke und der Bruder des Mannes mit der schönen Frisur sich sahen, merkten sie, dass sie sich kannten. Sie hatten in den späten Neunzigerjahren in demselben Unternehmen gearbeitet, das Folienbeschriftungen für Tankstellen herstellte.
Sie hatten sich viel zu erzählen, da sie sich schon lange nicht mehr gesehen hatten. Nach einigen Stunden verabschiedeten sie sich. Der Bruder nahm seinen Bruder, die Schwester ihre Schwester an die Hand, die beide während der gesamten Zeit schweigend auf dem Boden gesessen hatten. Mit der freien Hand griffen sie jeweils das Fahrrad.
Sodann gingen die Geschwisterpaare aneinander vorbei, wobei die Frauen an der Häuserwand entlanggingen und die Männer an der Straße, worauf sich die Geschwister vorher kurzerhand verständigt hatten. Die Frau mit der roten Daunenjacke und der Mann mit der schönen Frisur haben sich seither nicht mehr gesehen.

https://www.humanite.fr/societe/college-.title: À Paris, les proviseurs entre amertume et interrogation sur l’avenir
https://www.humanite.fr/societe/college-.author: Caroline Constant
https://www.humanite.fr/societe/college-.text:
À l’appel du syndicat SNPDEN-Unsa, les personnels de direction des lycées ont manifesté ce vendredi 13 novembre. Un peu perdus par l’ampleur du mouvement, ils affirment leur fatigue et refusent de régler le conflit à la place du gouvernement.
Un trousseau de clés tendu du bout des doigts, avec un slogan sur une pancarte : « Les chefs d’établissement ne sont pas des cibles ». Tel était le mot d’ordre des rassemblements, un peu partout en France, et devant le Collège de France à Paris, de personnels de direction des lycées, à l’appel de l’un de leurs syndicats, le SNPDEN-Unsa. Leurs revendications tiennent en peu de mots : ils veulent que les blocus s’arrêtent, que les agressions de personnels stoppent et que les lycéens reprennent le chemin des cours, ce qui risque de ne pas être immédiat, compte tenu de la colère de la jeunesse et de l’absence de réponse à leurs revendications, hors le tout sécuritaire de la police.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Pulisic double leads US to 6-0 rout of Haiti in Pochettino’s farewell tour
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Jeff Rueter
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
When Mauricio Pochettino named his US roster for the November window, few could have expected that the games would double as his brief lame-duck era. A week of camp instead brought constant media coverage, efficient negotiations and questions about the future of the national team. Come Wednesday, his day job will take him far from the federation’s headquarters in Fayetteville, Georgia, as he hopes to make sense of Manchester United.
Saturday finally allowed Pochettino and his players to get on with the intended purpose of this window, and they took to the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals with aplomb. The US opened their two-leg series against Haiti with a dominant 6-0 victory in front of a considerably pro-Haitian crowd in Miami. Auston Trusty provided the first half’s only goal before Julian Hall, Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun contributed to the eventual rout.
Concacaf allowed Haiti to host the match in Miami under an “exceptional hosting arrangement” because of the ongoing political unrest and gang violence in Port-au-Prince.
Pochettino’s penultimate lineup as US manager built on the momentum fostered during the previous international window. Tyler Adams retained the captain’s armband after being named permanent skipper in September, a decision on which Pochettino’s successor would be foolish to renege.
Trusty partnered Chris Richards between the first-choice full-back tandem of Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman. Pulisic and McKennie made their first international appearances since the World Cup. Diego Kochen and Hall started in goal and at striker, respectively, as two members of a rising generation who debuted en masse in the previous window.
One major evolution under Pochettino led to the game’s opening goal. Midway through his tenure, Pochettino cut into Pulisic’s ownership of dead-ball duties, opening the door to alternatives after the Milan winger had too routinely sent his deliveries into the first defender. Malik Tillman made the most of the change, scoring a pair of direct free-kick goals in the World Cup knockout rounds. It also helped Sebastian Berhalter establish himself in a prominent role, transforming from an uncapped outsider when Pochettino arrived into an every-game option capable of filling multiple roles in midfield.
In the ninth minute, Freeman drew a free kick on the right flank roughly 30 yards from goal. Berhalter stood over it as players congregated in the penalty area, curling his delivery around the crowd and beyond the far post. Trusty arrived without a defender in tow, steering the ball back toward the right post for his second international goal.
VAR took some time to confirm that Trusty had stayed onside for such an unobstructed run, and the Celtic defender had plenty to reflect on in the interim. It was his first on-field action in nearly a month, having last played on 15 October following the death of his father, Walt. The decision was met with a series of emphatic claps from Trusty as his teammates returned to celebrate with him for a second time.
Still, Les Grenadiers threatened the US with greater attacking ambition than Mexico or Canada had shown in the previous window. Backed by raucous support, Haiti sustained an intense, swarming press whenever the Americans had possession in their defensive third. In the 16th minute, Danley Jean Jacques fashioned a powerful effort after a quick Haitian break, but Kochen parried the shot away from any would-be follow-up. Lenny Joseph found another opening shortly after the half-hour mark, only for Richards to time his sliding block expertly.
The teams converged near midfield around the 40th minute after an exchange between Adams and Josué Casimir, with the Haiti attacker appearing to attempt to slap Berhalter in the face after the US midfielder intervened on his captain’s behalf. Guatemalan referee Walter López ultimately showed yellow cards to Casimir and Berhalter, and the remainder of the half unfolded in disjointed fashion as neither side looked willing to back down.
The second half sustained that intensity, with both teams leaving a little extra in their challenges. Haiti felt they had earned an attacking free kick in the 52nd minute after Tillman brought down Casimir from behind. As the home-away-from-home faithful booed, the US broke down the flank with a decisive sequence of passes, Pulisic carrying into the final third before slipping the ball left to Robinson.
The left back sent it back into the box for the onrushing Hall, whose movement had afforded him time to pick his spot. The 18-year-old comfortably dispatched his effort into the net. Despite making his debut only in September, Hall already has four goals from five appearances for the US, a tally he looks poised to build on for years to come. Only two other American men have scored four international goals before turning 20: Pulisic and Gio Reyna.
Hall’s appearance on Saturday also officially cap-tied him to the United States, ending any possibility of a one-time switch to Poland, who had courted the teenager.
Hall continued to torment Haiti’s center-backs. Five minutes after his goal, he drew defenders toward him before playing a clever backheel into Pulisic’s path. Carlens Arcus tripped the Milan attacker as he tried in vain to reach the bouncing ball. It was a straightforward penalty decision for López.
Pulisic made no mistake from the spot, opting for power as he drove his effort straight down the middle while goalkeeper Alexandre Pierre dived helplessly away. The American star peeled toward the corner flag for a smiling celebration with a group of young fans before exchanging high-fives with his teammates.
It was his 34th international goal, drawing him level with Eric Wynalda for fourth on the program’s all-time scoring chart. Their shared position lasted just 32 seconds.
Haiti squandered possession from the ensuing kickoff, handing the Americans the ball inside their own half. Freeman swept a pass into the middle, where Pulisic collected possession and fashioned a shooting opportunity from more than 20 yards out. Pierre could do little to stop it, and suddenly the US were four goals to the good with more than two hours still to play across the two legs.
Much of Pochettino’s tenure has been spent imploring his players never to let up regardless of the scoreline, and the US took that message to heart. McKennie separated himself from Joseph at a 68th-minute free kick, heading home his 13th international goal and his first since 28 March.
Haiti still tried to claw back some of the deficit, catching the young Kochen in no man’s land a few minutes later with a lofted ball over the high US defensive line. The nominal home support erupted as Casimir collected the long ball and found Joseph in the box for a comfortable finish. But VAR determined that Casimir had strayed offside by the narrowest of margins, his big toe enough to negate the consolation goal.
In truth, there was little left to be decided. Balogun appeared to score his first US goal since his ill-fated last-16 appearance against Belgium, only for VAR to controversially rule it out for an apparent infraction. Balogun needed no contact with defenders to make amends five minutes later, gliding between two opponents before strolling into the box and nutmegging Pierre.
Both the disallowed first effort and the legitimate second prompted the same celebration from a smiling Balogun: a pantomime tap of his watch, “it’s about damn time” in so many words.
The rest of the year will likely feel similarly free of stakes. US Soccer is not expected to appoint Pochettino’s successor until the new year, with Olympic team coach Steve Cherundolo poised to handle December’s friendly window on an interim basis. There is something of a somber party atmosphere around the team at present, attacking with fearlessness and showing considerable fight when games get thorny. All that remains for Pochettino before taking over at Manchester United is to see out a 6-0 advantage in Tuesday’s second leg in Cincinnati.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: US judge blocks Trump’s plan to renovate historic DC golf course
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Guardian staff and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
A federal judge has ordered a temporary suspension of any work at a historic Washington public golf course, in the latest setback for US president Donald Trump’s plan to turn it into a championship-level course.
In a 30-page decision, US district judge Ana Reyes temporarily blocked the federal government from moving forward with a plan that would have closed East Potomac Park on Sunday. Trump said in an 18 October social media post that the closure would last 15 months and transform the park’s golf offerings into “one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World”.
Reyes ruled that the Trump administration’s stated reasons for closing the park were “pretextual” and that the government violated at least two federal laws “to meet an arbitrary deadline”.
“The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely,” Reyes wrote.
The plaintiffs argue that Trump’s plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something the president denies.
Although Reyes ordered that the park – near the Jefferson Memorial, 2 miles (3km) south of the White House – remain open, the Trump administration does not have to maintain golf operations at the site, the judge wrote. But the government “cannot use the absence of golf operations as a reason to exclude the public,” she added.
The ruling by Reyes, who was appointed by Joe Biden and whom Trump has called a “lunatic”, is the latest instance of the federal judiciary pushing back against Trump’s sweeping efforts to redesign the nation’s capital through major construction projects.
Many of his projects, including plans for a huge ballroom at the White House, the installation of his own name on the Kennedy Center and construction of a massive arch, have been challenged in courts.
The ruling came in a lawsuit brought by the DC Preservation League, a historic preservation group that says Trump’s plan to redevelop the park violates various federal regulations and statutes.
The group’s lawyers earlier won a ruling from Reyes that blocked the National Park Service, part of the Interior Department, from cutting down trees at the park or making other irreversible modifications without advance notice.
Democracy Forward, which is representing the preservation league and two local residents in the case, said in a statement it was grateful that Reyes stopped “another one of the president’s vanity projects”.
The group’s senior legal adviser, Catherine Carroll, said: “The administration’s inexplicable drive to destroy East Potomac Park would have taken away a treasured park that could never be replaced.”
The Interior Department, Justice Department and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The lawsuit has produced several heated confrontations between Reyes and Justice Department lawyers. The judge said last month that the government’s removal of hundreds of trees from the course and failure to tell the preservation group about the work “has cost the government all of its credibility” in the case.
Reyes has ordered an ethics investigation into whether government lawyers have repeatedly misled her about the timeline for the park’s closure.
The Justice Department has accused Reyes of overstepping her authority and inappropriately belittling government lawyers. It demanded her recusal from the case, a request she denied.
Trump, who owns golf courses globally, has focused on the East Potomac Park renovations as part of his larger ambition to leave an architectural legacy across Washington.
The park has three golf courses totalling 36 holes, a miniature golf course and a paved loop popular with cyclists and runners. The proposed redesign would turn the area into a single 18-hole championship course that Trump has said could hold world-class events, such as the US Open and the Ryder Cup, while remaining open to the public.
With Reuters and Associated Press

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: World leaders head to Asia for back-to-back diplomatic summits
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Oliver Holmes and Rebecca Bailey
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
The global political centre of gravity will be firmly in Asia this week as world leaders fly in for back-to-back high-level summits against the backdrop of the tussle for influence between the superpowers China and the US.
Beijing will have the home advantage when it welcomes Donald Trump to its southern technology hub of Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting. It starts two weeks after the US leader lost midterm elections.
The summit also comes after an awkward-at-best revelation that the head of Nvidia, the US chipmaker that for a long time was the world’s most valuable company, was having an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects was a Chinese spy.
Apec represents more than 60% of global GDP and has primarily promoted free trade and multilateralism. This year’s meeting could be defined, however, by the confirmed trilateral meeting between Trump, the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.
The three-way meeting has been likened to a modern-day Yalta, when in 1945 then US president, Franklin D Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Crimea to carve up Europe after the second world war. However, analysts say a “Yalta 2.0” that issues edicts on Ukraine and Taiwan without their involvement is unlikely.
Xiaoyu Pu, an associate professor at the University of Nevada’s department of political science, said a three-way meeting “might be more symbolic than substantive, although symbolism itself matters in great-power diplomacy.
“Trump appears interested in nuclear arms control and denuclearisation. Xi’s priority is likely to maintain a stable relationship with Washington while preserving China’s strategic partnership with Russia. Putin, meanwhile, wants to maintain his bargaining leverage over Ukraine.”
Apec begins on Wednesday and follows a flurry of other diplomatic gatherings, chief among them the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) meeting in the Philippines, starting on Sunday, which Trump will attend.
While he is in Manila, US officials will hold a sidelines meeting of the so-called Quad – Australia, India, Japan and the US. In addition, a Francophone summit, which includes the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, is happening concurrently in Cambodia.
Critical global issues at all these summits will include AI supply chains and governance, tariff reductions and the green energy transition. Trump’s focus has been on denuclearisation. A key regional focus will be on the South China Sea, where Beijing has built massive military outposts in disputed waters, as well as the gigantic Indonesian forest fire haze blanketing the region.
The humanitarian and security crisis in Myanmar has become a perennial issue, as is status of Taiwan, which China does not recognise. The self-ruled island is sending the founder of the tech hardware company Acer as its envoy to Apec.
Global pivots towards Asia
For well over a decade, Washington’s engagement in the region has been coloured by concern over the rise of China, with the then president Barack Obama telling Australia’s parliament in 2011 that the US was “a Pacific power, and we are here to stay” – a policy known as the “pivot to Asia”.
The strategy of intense diplomacy and trade deals was adopted by Joe Biden, who hoped to gather allies on the continent who wanted to balance their relationships with both superpowers.
Some analysts see Trump’s transactional style in Asia as a continuation of the pivot policy. Still, the president’s volatility and unpredictability have spooked smaller nations, who regard China as a more predictable partner.
Jayant Menon, an economist at Singapore’s Iseas-Yusof Ishak Institute, said that countries in south-east Asia had been “laying the groundwork for a future with reduced dependence on the United States” by seeking deals elsewhere, including with each other and the EU.
“Amid persistent uncertainty and an administration determined to levy tariffs by any legal means, south-east Asia’s ability to ride out another round of tariffs depends on deeper regional integration and diversification beyond the US market,” he wrote this month in the East Asia Forum.
Beijing’s more predictable policies do not necessarily make it any more palatable for its regional neighbours, however, and the Chinese premier, Li Qiang, could have tough talks when he goes to Manila for the Asean summit, especially on the South China Sea.
China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, recently urged Manila to rein in Filipino politicians who he said had repeatedly “smeared” Beijing, after public outcries in the country over the disputed waters.
Brunei, China, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan and Vietnam have been locked in decades-long territorial standoffs in the busy waterway, which could sit on deposits of oil and gas. Washington has sent military ships on “freedom of navigation operations”, despite Chinese outcries, although US-linked crises in Iran, Ukraine, Venezuela, and Palestine and Israel have sucked up Washington’s focus under Trump’s second term.
A decades-long attempt to sign a South China Sea pact is not expected to happen at this year’s Asean summit, as previously hoped. Despite monthly meetings, negotiations will have to continue next year, when Asean’s leadership rotates to Singapore.
Diplomats at the Asean summit will also be focusing on Myanmar, which is seeking reintegration. Each country in the group is assessing how to deal with their isolated neighbour. The timing of summits this week coincides with a judgment in the international court of justice on Thursday that could find Myanmar responsible for genocide. The coup leader, Min Aung Hlaing, remains barred from Asean but is allowed to send a representative.
Asia’s week of diplomacy will be followed next month by the G20 summit in Miami, Florida, which Xi is expected to attend if US and Chinese relations continue to hold steady.
Additional research by Yu-chen Li

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.title: Italy fines Meta $887m for accessing Android users’ photos and videos
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.author: Agence France-Presse
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text:
Italy’s data protection agency has fined Facebook parent company Meta €805m ($887m) for accessing users’ photos without their specific consent.
Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement.
Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”.
In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn for misleading the state’s residents for more than a decade about the use of their data – a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression.
Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has imposed on a tech company.
In 2021, Amazon received a more than €1.1bn fine for breaching competition law.
That sum was subsequently reduced to €752m on appeal.
The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing.
According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery.
The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it.
In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” – about 20 million Android users in Italy – and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”.
The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”.
It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4% of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201bn in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5bn.

https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov.title: UK government to consider changing age of consent after allegations against Russell Brand
https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov.author: Raphael Boyd and Press Association
https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov.text:
The government has said it will consider calls to change the age of consent after a woman waived her right to anonymity to publicly claim she was raped by Russell Brand as a 16-year-old schoolgirl.
Mia Latter, now 37, alleged she had been orally raped by the jailed comedian when she was a teenager and he was 30 years old.
In an interview with the Sunday Times, she called for the introduction of a staggered age of consent – which would make relationships between adults and teenagers aged 16 and 17 illegal.
Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, told the newspaper that Latter’s “heart-breaking story” meant a law change deserved consideration.
She said: “We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it’s really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.
“It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it.”
Under UK law, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds.
Latter said: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.
“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”
Latter was referred to under the pseudonym of Alice in previous reporting by the Sunday Times, the Times, and Channel 4’s Dispatches documentary.
She was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.
He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.
She told the newspaper that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.
Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.
Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.
She spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court.
He was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.
Earlier this week, it was announced that a series of “serious” sex offence allegations against comedian David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as “sexual assault”.
Walliams denies any wrongdoing.
Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams’s accusers was asked to sign a non disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should also look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: “When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn’t come under the current consultation.
“I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced.”
It is believed MPs outside Labour may support a bill to change the age of consent laws, with Jess Brown-Fuller, the Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson, coming out in favour of reviewing them.
Commending Latter for the “extraordinary bravery” it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: “I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.
“We already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It’s time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls.”
Latter’s decision to come forward was also praised by Bridget Phillipson, the minister for women and equalities, who said she “and thousands of others across the country will be in awe of her courage and determination”. She added that it is “up to all of us to send a message to women and girls who experience sexual violence: the shame is not yours. Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change.”
Latter’s allegation was reported to the Met police, who said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.
A Met Police spokesperson said: “Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
“Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
“This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence.”
The CPS said: “The Crown Prosecution Service will continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible.”

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: ATP Finals tennis: Alexander Zverev v Rafael Jódar and more – live
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Tom Bassam
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
The contrast between how hard Jódar is working on his serve to Zverev is huge. There’s a double digit rally just to make it 15-15 and then a tough volley to go up 30-15. The next point is dominated by Zverev and when Jódar misses down the line at 30-30 he coughs up more break points. This time Zverev turns the screw in the rally and finally makes the pass to take charge of the first set.
Zverez goes up 0-15 when Jódar goes wayward with a forehand but the Spaniard battles back gamely to make 30-15. A piercing early backhand from Zverev makes it 30-30 and we have our first sniff of danger for Jódar. An unforced error from Jódar gives Zverev his first break point but a loose forehand, loopy and long, from the German is a gift to get back to deuce. Zverev gets another break chance when Jódar goes long with a cross court backhand, but a steely second serve and follow-up backhand see off the danger. Zverev can only find the net with his return on the next point and Jódar escapes with hold after wicked approach pins his opponent on the baseline.
Jódar hits a lovely forehand winner to take control of the game at 15-0 and looks pretty nerveless as Zverev tries to get on the front foot. A backhand winner down the line from the 20-year-old at 40-15 seals it.
Zverev is aggressive from the off, coming into the net on the very first point but his approach isn’t the best and Jódar finds the pass. After getting out to 30-0 lead, Jódar dumps a forehand into the net and suddenly we’re at 30-30. A couple of sloppy errors from Zverev to release the pressure and the Spaniard has the first game on the board.
Ok, let’s get into it. Alexander Zverev gets the first chance to state his credentials at this year’s ATP Finals. Zverev has thrived in the absence of the top men’s players, winning the French and US Opens but with Carlos Alcaraz back and lurking on the side of the draw in Turin, we will see how the 29-year-old handles the gaze of coming into this glitzy event with the added weight of being world No 1.
On the other side of the court we Rafael Jódar, a player who has rapidly ascended the rankings. The 287 days between his ATP Tour-level debut and Jódar reaching the top 10, a run which featured his first title in Morocco, obliterated the previous record held by Gustavo Kuerten. Zverev is favourite but Jódar is coming. Play begins shortly.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Kayla ⁠⁠Harrison defeats Amanda Nunes to retain UFC bantamweight belt
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Kayla Harrison defeats Amanda Nunes to retain UFC bantamweight belt
Harrison won the fight by a fourth-round submission against MMA legend Nunes, who made a comeback after a three-year absence.
Kayla Harrison has retained her Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) bantamweight title with a fourth-round submission win over one of the mixed martial arts (MMA) all-time greats, Amanda Nunes, in the United States.
The American fighter leveraged her tremendous grappling skills and thwarted her opponent’s attempt to take the belt back in the main event of UFC 334 at New York’s Madison Square Garden on Saturday.
A two-time Olympic judo champion, the 36-year-old Harrison was facing arguably the greatest female fighter of all time in Nunes, a dominant two-weight champion at bantamweight and featherweight before she stepped away from the sport in June 2023. But the Brazilian could not shake off the rust from her long absence as she let the fight slip away from her.
Nunes did well initially, looking crisp in her striking and avoiding some early takedown attempts, but she eventually succumbed to Harrison’s grappling attack, spending much of the latter part of the opening two rounds on the bottom in a scarf-hold position from which she struggled to escape.
Emboldened by her success, Harrison displayed the full range of her judo skills with perfectly timed trips and tosses and vice-like ground control. In the fourth round, she chased Nunes down to the mat, jumping on her back and quickly sinking in a rear-naked choke that forced the 38-year-old to submit.
“I think I’m still in shock,” said Harrison, who had surgery on herniated disks in her neck in January.
“It feels surreal. Sometimes I can’t believe my life. I’m just really grateful, I’m humbled, it’s an honour and a privilege to stand before you,” she said, addressing her opponent.
Harrison (20 wins, one defeat) admitted she was not sure what was next for her but took a moment to acknowledge the audience.
“New York City, I love you,” she exclaimed after the fight.
Nunes (23 wins, six defeats) took her gloves off but did not make herself available for a post-fight interview.
Meanwhile, Ciryl Gane of France defeated American Josh Hokit by unanimous decision to retain the heavyweight title after a bruising five-round battle fought at a frenetic pace.
Gane successfully defended his title for the first time, sweeping the scorecards 48-47, 48-47, 48-47 against Hokit.
The first round saw Gane (15 wins, two defeats) get up quickly from an early takedown by Hokit (10 wins, one defeat), then land a few sharp jabs, uppercuts and an overhand right as he countered Hokit’s forward pressure. Hokit did, however, close the round with a slam with about 30 seconds remaining.
Hokit came back in the second round. After Gane stuffed an early single-leg attempt, Hokit pushed forward with determination, trading heavy right hands and clinching along the fence in a very physical exchange.
Hokit carried that momentum into the third round with a scramble takedown, then worked Gane over with several clinch elbows and foot stamps before flashing him the middle finger at the bell. As Hokit’s punches began to fade in the fourth round, Gane took control, countering the challenger’s fence clinches with several body kicks, knees to the midsection and short, dirty-boxing uppercuts.
With the result still in the balance in the fifth round, Gane stuffed Hokit’s takedown attempts and opened a cut just above his left eye, then dominated the striking with jabs, body shots and multi-punch combinations through the end of the round.
Gane kept things simple after the fight, as did the typically brash Hokit.
“It was an amazing fight,” Gane said.
Hokit said he would enjoy the moment, even if he was on the receiving end.
“Resilience builds character,” Hokit said.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.title: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain - Middle East crisis live

Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain
The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.
Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.
The statements are very similar, I’ve pulled out a few below:
Saudi Arabia’sMinistry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement published by the Saudi Press Agency:
The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.
Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on the Qatar news agency (QNA):
The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.
In light of Iran’s latest strike attempts on US allies in the Gulf, it’s useful to look at what the US commander-in-chief has been saying in recent days, as my colleague Patrick Wintour reports.
Donald Trump has said in a series of media interviews since Thursday that he will attack Iran only if necessary, claiming that Gulf countries, such as Saudi Arabia, have urged him to hold back from planned large-scale military strikes.
Vance had been seen by the Iranians as the most trustworthy figure close to Trump, but they had rejected his request for a personal meeting with their negotiators to discuss the terms of a peace deal.
Vance has been at the forefront of Republicans saying the war was the cause of the widespread Republican losses in the midterms. Trump said he had been disappointed in the American public because higher diesel prices were a small price to pay for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.
Five killed in Houthi attack near Yemeni government capital
I reported earlier that Yemeni government forces are falling back to Aden to try and secure their interim capital which is coming under pressure from Houthi forces.
A Houthi attack on a checkpoint near Aden has killed five people and injured eight others near Aden, AFP is reporting.
The missile targeted a checkpoint in Khor Omeira, Lahj province, AFP says, citing three unnamed military sources and a government source.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain
The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.
Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.
The statements are very similar, I’ve pulled out a few below:
Saudi Arabia’sMinistry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement published by the Saudi Press Agency:
The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.
Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on the Qatar news agency (QNA):
The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.
Below is the full statement from Bahrain’s foreign ministry on the Iranian drone strikes today, which were intercepted and shot down. This has been published in Bahrain’s various state-controlled media outlets.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.
This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.
The Kingdom views them as a blatant attack on its sovereignty and territorial integrity, a flagrant violation of Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks on the Kingdom of Bahrain and neighboring countries and demanded their immediate cessation, a targeting of innocent citizens and residents, a sabotage of de-escalation efforts, and a serious threat to the region’s security and stability.
The Ministry affirmed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s categorical rejection of the flimsy pretexts and baseless claims put forward by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, emphasizing that no pretext justifies aggression against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states.
It stressed that freedom of navigation and passage, by sea and air, in straits used for international navigation is a right guaranteed by the rules of international law and is not subject to the will or conditions of any state.
The Kingdom also rejects the transformation of its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences.
The Ministry also affirmed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s inherent right, both individually and collectively, to self-defense in accordance with Article (51) of the Charter, and to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents, in close coordination with its brothers in the Gulf Cooperation Council, based on the Joint Defense Agreement, which considers an attack on any member state an attack on all, as well as with its allies and partners. The Ministry noted that the Kingdom of Bahrain, as a member of the UN Security Council, calls upon the Council to condemn these repeated attacks and demands that it assume its responsibilities and take decisive measures to ensure Iran’s full compliance with Resolution 2817, and to halt its attacks, threats, and support for proxy groups in the region. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs added that the Kingdom of Bahrain affirms that its security is a red line, that its sovereignty is non-negotiable, and that it will remain, as it has always been, a proponent of good neighborliness, respect for the sovereignty of states, and non-interference in their affairs, and is committed to the security and stability of the Arabian Gulf.
Iranian media are reporting that their foreign minister Abbas Araqchi will be in Oman on Tuesday for talks with his Omani counterpart.
Oman, along with Qatar, has been one of the key negotiators in ceasefire and peace talks between Tehran and Washington.
As both sides have settled into a strategy of exerting continued economic pain on the other, we’re yet to see any movement on a deal though.
The US is maintaining a highly expensive military operation in the Gulf, with a naval blockade that aims to stop Iranian oil ships leaving the Persian Gulf, thereby hurting the Iranian economy, and through a missile and drone operation targeting Iran’s southern coastline aimed at protecting and helping commercial ships get out. Oil flows are said to be back near their prewar level.
But Iran hasn’t strayed from its demands, and the conditions it wants to end the war: a measure of control over Hormuz, removal of the blockade and economic sanctions, having its assets unfrozen, and reparations.
Yemen government forces dropping back from Bab el-Mandeb to shore up Aden capital
I mentioned earlier the withdrawal of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces from the areas around Bab el-Mandeb where they’ve been attempting to stave off the Houthis.
A lightning-strike offensive back in September saw the Houthis sweep almost the entire Red Sea coast and almost seize control of the critical Red Sea strait, which has become another chokepoint in the flow of oil and and energy supplies from Gulf producers.
Here’s the full statement from the Yemeni forces, who are now redeploying towards Aden, where their government is based.
The Houthis are gathering steam in the south, where most areas remain under government control.
The Souther Yemeni forces said:
The Southern Armed Forces announce the implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate.
This step is taken based on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats.
The Houthis’ stronghold currently remains most of northern Yemen, where they control the capital Sanaa and other populous areas. Since the civil war erupted in 2014, the Houthis have pushed the internationally-recognised Yemeni government south and stunned the Saudi-backed administration with their push south in September.
That prompted a military fight back operation, and Saudi Arabia striking Houthi areas in Yemen as the Houthis targeted airports and oil supplies in the Gulf kingdom.
The US thinks Iran still has between 1,500-2,500 missiles in its arsenal despite the US-Israeli damage done this year to its production facilities, reports the Wall St Journal.
They noted difficulties with tracking Iran’s stockpile, and assessing whether they’re ready for launch or remain in storage.
But they noted that Iran has appeared to manage to slowly rebuild its arsenal during the long lulls in fighting and mostly from stockpiled weapons components. Tehran has also kept up a ready supply of drones and short-range missiles.
The assessment would go against what Trump and his Secretary of Defence/War, Peter Hegseth, have been claiming repeatedly throughout the nearly-nine months of war so far; that the US has “decimated” Iran’s long-range fighting capability.
Both the US and Israel had also stated the goal of destroying Iran’s ballistic-missile capabilities when they launched war on 28 February.
Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza refugee camp
Hamas has confirmed the killing of Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, commander of the group’s Rafah Brigade, in an Israeli airstrike on a Gaza refugee camp on Saturday night.
The Israeli military said it had taken steps to “mitigate harm to civilians” in the strike. It said it had also targeted other Hamas militants in the strike but gave no further detail.
Israel’s military first announced the killing on Sunday, saying they had targeted Younis who they said had been working on restoring Hamas and getting members to “advance and carry out terror attacks”.
Younis had been one of the senior Hamas figures who helped plan and oversee the October 7 attacks. He had only been the Rafah brigade leader role for two months, after Israel killed his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid.
In their statement announcing his death, Hamas said Younis was “one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack”.
Earlier this week, an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital, the largest operational hospital in southern Gaza, killed at least six people, including a surgeon and patients, and injured 30, local officials said. The IDF said it had been targeting a commander of Hamas’s armed wing.
Israel is still striking Gaza on a near daily basis despite the the US-brokered ceasefire having come into action since October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire, and more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza since the war began.
Here’s a recap of what the various sides have said this morning regarding the latest Iranian strikes targeting a US air base in Bahrain.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards:
The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force.
The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response.
Bahrain’s foreign ministry
Iran continues its systematic hostile approach through its sinful attacks targeting the Kingdom of Bahrain.
[Bahrain] rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks.
I’m yet to see a response from the US, but can expect Centcomm (which oversees all American military operations in the Middle East) to comment at some stage, like it did for Friday’s attack. Those strikes also targeted a radar site.
Bahrain locals: 'I was hoping this period was behind us'
After two months of calm, the explosions have started again for Bahrain citizens.
Locals reported hearing blasts about 4am local time, and then a second round at 6.30am.
It’s exactly what I was hoping wouldn’t happen: Iranian attacks starting again, with all the worry and uncertainty that go with them”, Hayat Ibrahim, 65, told AFP news agency.
Another resident, Mohammed Abdallah, a shopkeeper in the capital Manama, which is just north of the air base targeted said:
I was hoping this period was behind us and wouldn’t happen again.
Bahrain’s Interior Ministry posted public warnings on X, telling “residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location, and follow news through official channels”.
Iran had last launched strikes in the first week of September, when the regime targeted US military assets in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base on Sunday morning, reported Iranian media.
They said they had attacked the air base in retaliation for “hostile US actions”. The base is about a 30-minute drive south of Manama.
US forces have been quietly carrying out a series of strikes on Iranian sites in recent weeks, including on the key Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, where there’s a major IRGC presence. Trump has called them minor strikes.
Bahrain officials this morning have accused Tehran of continuing a “systematic hostile approach” to the kingdom.
The drone flurry this morning comes just 48 hours after Iran launched drones on Friday, the first escalations targeting Bahrain in two months.
That attack targeted an American radar facility. US Central Command said it had shot down the two drones without any injury or damage.
Bahrain officials hadn’t issued any warnings for that attack, but were forced to send out public alerts this morning telling residents to seek shelter. The Interior Ministry told locals to remain calm but proceed to to the nearest safe location.
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the fighting in the Middle East.
Iran has targeted an airbase inBahrainin the latest resumption of strikes since September, prompting public warnings and sirens to ring out in the Gulf kingdom this morning.
According to Iranian media, the IRGC said it had sent six drones to attack a US radar system hosted in the US-allied island state.
Explosions were heard around the capital, Manama, but Bahrain authorities say their air defences intercepted the attacks before they reached their targets.
Bahrain, which lies directly across the Persian Gulf from Iran, is home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, and has been repeatedly attacked by Tehran during the course of the war, which has seen flare-ups in strikes amid long bouts of inaction.
There are fears Iran’s attacks this morning might signal a resumption of the war while US President Donald Trump has threatened but refrained from returning to major combat. Negotiations to end the war remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz.
Developments in the Red Sea this morning will add to further concerns for Gulf oil flows.
The Yemeni government forces supported by Saudi Arabia, fighting the Houthis, have retreated from the Bab el-Mandeb area, giving the Iran-aligned rebels even greater control over the critical shipping lane, which Saudi Arabia and other Gulf oil producers had been relying on to get their supplies out.
Elsewhere, Hamas has confirmed that a senior commander involved in planning the 7 October attacks was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Saturday.

https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.text:
À l’Odéon, à Paris, Romeo Castellucci adapte « Faust » sans mots. Il met en scène l’échec du langage mais aussi la vivification obstinée du théâtre.
Au commencement était le verbe. Non, l’esprit. Ou bien la force. En fait : l’action. Les chemins pris chez Goethe par le docteur Faust pour interpréter le logos, alors qu’il entreprend de traduire en allemand le Nouveau Testament, ont semble-t-il servi de guide à Castellucci pour cette adaptation du grand classique germanique dont le sous-titre résume ce départ du verbe à l’action : Fait, non dit.
Au commencement le geste, donc, celui du comédien Gérard Bayle, quasiment nu, qui lève ses mains au ciel comme en prière, mais pour finir par les porter à son visage et pleurer. Le poids des années sur les côtes que dévoile sa peau maigre, le vieillard s’allonge, à l’article de la mort, et un bip d’électrocardiogramme se fait entendre, bientôt entrecoupé d’une liste des grands noms du canon de la philosophie et de la science : Confucius, Kant, Arendt, Locke. Y est glissé Charlie Brown, le personnage de Charles M. Schulz, philosophe miniature....
