https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: De la Fuente denies racism in Spain despite Yamal, Vinicius avowals
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
De la Fuente denies racism in Spain despite Yamal, Vinicius avowals
La Liga stars Lamine Yamal and Vinicius Jr have publicly said they face racist abuse in Spain, which has faced FIFA punishment over the issue.
Weeks after FIFA punished Spain over Islamophobic chants by their supporters and their star Lamine Yamal admitted having repeatedly experienced racism in the country, the Spanish team’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has claimed the country does not have a racism problem.
De la Fuente appeared to quash any concerns about racism as he addressed the media on Saturday before his team’s UEFA Nations League match against England.
“In Spain, there is no racism,” the 65-year-old said in response to a question about his England counterpart Thomas Tuchel, who revealed he would speak to his players about the antiracism protocol in place before Sunday’s match in Madrid.
“You can tell this to Thomas. As clear as that. There is no racism. Exactly the same as in England, in Spain, there is no racism. We’re not racists, none of us.”
While a capacity crowd is expected for the top-of-the-table Group C clash at the Metropolitano Stadium, the world champions will have to play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for Spanish supporters singing an Islamophobic chant during a fixture against Egypt in March.
Several high-profile players have been targeted by racist abuse in recent years, including Yamal and Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr, who has been moved to tears in news conferences while talking about the issue.
England players faced racist abuse during a game in the Spanish capital in a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were targeted.
Tuchel said he did not expect racist abuse on Sunday but his players would be reminded of antiracism protocols.
“I think the referee and the officials know about that [racist chanting].”
He later clarified his comments as not being specifically about Spain and criticised reporters for creating “a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing”.
“I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens,” he said.
England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.
“In the past, I’ve experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria, and there was a protocol in place we followed,” Rice told reporters. “We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
“I’m not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium. The players we’re playing against we have a lot of respect for. It’s set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one.”
Yamal has faced racism ‘a thousand times’
In September, Barcelona and Spain star Yamal said he had experienced racism “a thousand times” with many people unaware that their comments or behaviour is racist.
Asked by former Argentina international Jorge Valdano in an interview with Spanish broadcaster Movistar whether he had directly experienced racism, Lamine said: “A thousand times.”
“People are indirectly racist towards you but maybe don’t realise it. There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist, and they don’t even notice.
“If someone calls me Black, it’s not going to bother me at all. Ultimately I’m Black. I’m not any other colour. Another thing is whether it’s good or bad, whether they’re saying it to offend me.
“But if I’m playing a match. and they paid for a ticket to see me, I’m not going to get angry just because they disrespected me.”
Yamal criticised the anti-Muslim chants by fans in what should have been a friendly match against Egypt.
A section of supporters had chanted: “Whoever doesn’t jump is Muslim.”
Egypt’s national anthem also received a barrage of whistles before the friendly.
Yamal, a Muslim whose father moved from Morocco to Spain, issued a damning statement on Instagram in the wake of the row.
“I am a Muslim. Yesterday at the stadium the chant ‘the one who doesn’t jump is the Muslim’ was heard,” he posted.
“I know I was playing for the rival team and it wasn’t something personal against me but as a Muslim person it doesn’t stop being disrespectful and something intolerable.”
Yamal added: “I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people.”
Years of racist abuse aimed at Vinicius
Real Madrid’s Vinicius has been the most notable target of racism and has openly addressed the issue, often in tearful news conferences.
On May 22, 2023, Vinicius said the Spanish league “now belongs to racists”, and two days later, Spanish police arrested four men suspected of hanging an effigy of him four months earlier from a bridge in Madrid in front of the club’s training centre in advance of a Madrid derby.
The arrests came amid an international outcry after racist abuse was hurled at Vinicius during another league match.
A year later, Vinicius broke down in tears and said he was struggling to stay motivated and enjoy playing football due to the recurring racist abuse he was subjected to in Spain.
During an emotional news conference before Brazil’s friendly against Spain, he expressed frustration that fans kept getting away with hurling racist abuse towards him.
This year, Vinicius praised Yamal for his public condemnation of Islamophobic chants, saying players need to stick together in the fight against discrimination.
“Hopefully, we can continue with this fight,” he said.
“It’s important that Lamine speaks about it. It could help others. We are famous. We have money. We can balance these things better, but the poor people and the Black people who are everywhere, they surely struggle more than we do. So we have to stick together, those who have a stronger voice, the players.”
“I’m not saying that Spain or Germany or Portugal are racist countries, but there are racists in these countries and in Brazil and other countries as well,” Vinicius said. “But if we keep fighting together, I think future players and people in general won’t have to go through this again.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Jordan sentences three men to death by hanging after deadly church attack
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Jordan sentences three men to death by hanging after deadly church attack
Three men have been convicted of carrying out an attack on a church in the Karak governorate that killed nine people.
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out last month’s deadly gun attack on a church in the kingdom’s south.
Armed men killed nine people and wounded 25 others, storming a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, in the Karak governorate on October 23.
Authorities said three men, two Jordanian brothers and their relative by marriage, had fled after the attack and were arrested three days later.
In a statement on Sunday, the Jordanian military said the “State Security Court issued its ruling sentencing to death the three criminals who carried out the terrorist attack” at the church.
Crimes listed
The court found them guilty of “committing terrorist attacks” resulting in death, as well as weapons offences, “conspiracy to commit terrorist acts” and “promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation”.
“One of the perpetrators of the terrorist operation was also convicted of providing funds with the intention of using them to finance the commission of terrorist acts,” it added.
In late October, Jordanian security forces arrested the three suspects in the attack on St George’s Greek Orthodox church after clashing with them.
The governorate is home to many members of Jordan’s Christian minority, which makes up about 300,000 of the country’s 11.5 million people.
King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the “harshest penalties” as he offered his condolences to the victims’ families. He has ordered a review of the country’s security procedures for responding to attacks after the incident.

https://gothamist.com/news/death-toll-fr.title: Mamdani: Brooklyn building collapse kills 6 adults, 2 children with rescue work still underway
https://gothamist.com/news/death-toll-fr.author: Brittany Kriegstein, Verónica Del Valle
https://gothamist.com/news/death-toll-fr.text:
Eight people, including two children, are dead, and 18 others are injured after a three-story apartment building collapsed in Flatbush on Wednesday afternoon, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday. More than 250 firefighters and emergency service workers responded to the scene; they continue to search the rubble for survivors.
The building, located near Bedford and Flatbush Avenues, collapsed around 4 p.m. Wednesday into a lot where construction workers had been excavating earlier in the day for a new building, officials said. Six people died at the scene, and two others succumbed to their injuries at nearby hospitals, the mayor said. Two of those who died were construction workers. At least seven of the injured are children. Most of those still hospitalized are in stable condition, though one person is in critical condition, Mamdani said.
Though rain threatened to complicate the rescue effort, FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said it would not “stop our operations.”
“ This type of an emergency is something our members train extensively for, and we will be here until we are one hundred percent sure there are no more people trapped,” she said.
The devastation puts the collapse among the worst such disasters in recent city history. The Department of Buildings and law enforcement have begun an investigation into what caused the building to collapse. The developer of the new construction appears to have flouted orders from the buildings department in the past.
Mamdani said five entities were involved in the construction site and are associated with about 100 other projects across the city. The Department of Buildings began a sweep of those sites Thursday, he said.
“If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable,” Mamdani said.
The scene was chaotic Thursday morning as firefighters, emergency service workers and police officers moved around the site. A demolition excavator worked through the rubble, piling the debris on one end of the lot — a mattress, a refrigerator, wood floor panels — while bricks, clothing and dozens of music records lay scattered across the site.
Families who had spent the night on the sidewalk wrapped in blankets waited for any information about the fate of their loved ones.
One woman collapsed to the ground after learning her husband was among the dead.
“My husband, he died,” she yelled in Spanish.
Segundo Iza stood at the site of the collapse. He said he knew one of the construction workers who had died. They’d grown up together in Ambato, Ecuador. They’d met playing soccer.
Iza said his friend had moved to the U.S. four or five years ago. He had one son and another child on the way.
“He was someone who came here to achieve many dreams, to find better days for our children and our parents,” Iza said. “So it’s sad that our friend died here in New York.”
Assiah Bah, 23, said she and her family were waiting outside all night for news of their two cousins who lived in the collapsed building and were cooking dinner at the time of the disaster.
“We don't know what is going on, if they're still alive or if they passed, we don't know,” Bah said Thursday morning, saying her family immigrated from Guinea.
The extent of injuries and location of those who were caught in the wreckage has been changing throughout the rescue operation.
“We've seen infants, toddlers being pulled out of the rubble on stretchers into ambulances to be rushed to the hospital,” Councilmember Farah Louis said from the scene Wednesday night.
Katie Stevens, a teacher who lives down the block, said she was home, doing her laundry when she heard what sounded almost like a car crash. A few minutes later, she heard sirens and helicopters overhead. She said she found a family with a young boy standing on the sidewalk next to the rubble, crying. “ Can I do anything for you right now?”
“We need everything right now,” Stevens recalled them telling her. She took the young boy to a nearby clothing store to use the restroom. He kept asking her when he could go back home.
“I don't know, love,” Stevens told him. “I don't know. I don't know, but you are safe. Your family is safe. You're gonna be okay.”
The building collapsed into a hole where construction workers had been excavating for a new building on an adjacent lot earlier in the day, according to the city's buildings commissioner Ahmed Tigani.
“I actually watched it. I was in my room when the building fell down. You could hear it.” Antione Vines said, Wednesday night from the scene. “ Before they build a new building and you're connecting it to another building that’s been up since the 1700s, you gotta look at the structure of the building. You can't just build a new building and connect it.”
Nearly all of the building had caved into the adjacent construction site, shearing off the side of the neighboring residential building, exposing a stairway, a closet full of clothes and a bedroom set.
“We’ve been waiting here all night. We went to four hospitals, and they haven’t given us any information,” Luis Siguencia said of his son, 22-year-old construction worker Gabriel Siguencia, as he anxiously waited at the scene Thursday morning.
“He wanted to get ahead. Because we all come here with the dream of getting ahead. He had his papers and everything.”
Gabriel, who recently arrived from Ecuador, had been working on the foundation at the site for the last two weeks.
New York City's Office of Emergency Management said it has coordinated with the Red Cross to open a reception center for impacted residents at the Flatbush YMCA at 1401 Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn.
As of 6 a.m., the Red Cross has registered seven households (14 adults and five children) for emergency assistance, including temporary lodging.
Mamdani said anyone searching for a loved one should call 311 or 212-639-9675.
Liam Quigley, Ryan Kost and Catalina Gonella contributed reporting.
This is a developing story and has been updated.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: PF apura suspeitas de fraude em contratos emergenciais na enchente em Canoas e Cachoeirinha
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Polícia Federal (PF) deflagrou, nesta sexta-feira (13), a Operação Deságue para investigar possíveis fraudes em contratos emergenciais de locação e operação de motobombas durante as enchentes de 2024 em Canoas e Cachoeirinha, na região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre. Segundo a corporação, o sobrepreço estimado nos contratos de Canoas é de pelo menos R$ 7 milhões.
Foram cumpridos 13 mandados de busca e apreensão em sete municípios gaúchos — Pelotas, Porto Alegre, São Leopoldo, Cachoeirinha, Gravataí, Capão da Canoa e Canoas — e em Itapema, em Santa Catarina. A operação resultou no bloqueio de mais de R$ 10 milhões em ativos financeiros e na apreensão de três veículos.
Os contratos investigados foram custeados com recursos federais destinados à resposta ao desastre climático. As motobombas utilizadas para retirar a água das áreas inundadas teriam sido contratadas de uma empresa sem estrutura operacional compatível, que, segundo a PF, teria sido favorecida e repassado a execução dos serviços a empresas especializadas por valores inferiores aos cobrados das prefeituras.
Em Canoas, a investigação aponta cobranças entre nove e dez vezes superiores aos custos reais em determinados serviços. Em Cachoeirinha, o serviço investigado envolveu duas motobombas entre 13 de maio e 13 de junho de 2024. Segundo a PF, também foram identificados orçamentos fraudulentos, elaborados ou assinados após o início ou mesmo depois do encerramento dos serviços.
A corporação informou ainda ter identificado saques em espécie e transferências para pessoas físicas e jurídicas sem vínculo aparente com a operação dos equipamentos. Os investigados poderão ser indiciados por crimes como fraude em licitação ou contrato, corrupção ativa e passiva, associação criminosa e lavagem de dinheiro.
A Prefeitura de Canoas confirmou nesta sexta-feira (13) a exoneração do secretário-geral de Governo, João Batista Portella Pereira. A administração informou que a decisão ocorreu após tomar conhecimento de que Pereira, secretário da Fazenda à época das contratações, é um dos alvos da operação.
Em nota enviada ao Brasil de Fato RS, a Prefeitura de Cachoeirinha afirmou que os fatos investigados ocorreram durante as enchentes de 2024, na gestão anterior, “não possuindo qualquer vínculo com a atual Administração Municipal”. Informou ainda que não houve buscas nas dependências da prefeitura, mas exclusivamente em residências de investigados da gestão anterior, e se colocou à disposição para colaborar com as autoridades.
Procurada pela redação, a Prefeitura de Canoas não enviou resposta até o fechamento desta matéria.
Confira a nota da Prefeitura de Cachoeirinha na íntegra
A Prefeitura de Cachoeirinha esclarece que a operação deflagrada pela Polícia Federal nesta sexta-feira (13) refere-se a fatos ocorridos em 2024, durante a gestão anterior, não possuindo qualquer vínculo com a atual Administração Municipal.
Ressaltamos que não houve nenhuma ação ou busca da Polícia Federal nas dependências da Prefeitura, tendo os mandados sido cumpridos exclusivamente nas residências de investigados da gestão anterior.
Pautada pela lisura, transparência e responsabilidade, a atual gestão reforça que está totalmente à disposição para colaborar com as autoridades competentes para o completo esclarecimento dos fatos.
Prefeitura Municipal de Cachoeirinha

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Milton Leite se torna réu por suspeita de ligação com o PCC
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Odair Braz
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Justiça de São Paulo acatou denúncia do Ministério Público e tornou Milton Leite e mais 13 pessoas réus por suspeita de ligação com a facção criminosa Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC). Leite é ex-vereador e ex-presidente da Câmara Municipal de São Paulo e está preso.
O político filiado ao partido União Brasil foi para a cadeia em setembro, após uma operação da Polícia Civil junto com o Ministério Público que investigava a atuação do PCC no transporte coletivo paulistano.
Com a decisão da Justiça tornada pública na quinta-feira (12), Leite teve a prisão temporária convertida em preventiva. Outros 11 denunciados também tiveram prisões preventivas decretadas.
No documento que torna Leite réu, a denúncia informa que ele e todo o grupo de investigados “agiram sob a orientação de lideranças da organização criminosa, como Antônio José Muller Junior, vulgo ‘Granada’, e Marlon José de Souza Rosa, vulgo ‘MR’ e ‘Murilo’, denunciado em fase anterior desta investigação. Os denunciados atuaram para infiltrar e perpetuar a facção na exploração do transporte público, em procedimentos licitatórios e no poder público, bem como para movimentar e ocultar recursos da organização criminosa”.
Influência
Sobre Milton Leite, especificamente, o documento diz que o ex-presidente da Câmara Municipal de SP “promoveu interesses da organização criminosa, valendo-se de sua expressiva influência política e da condição de proprietário de fato da concessionária Transwolff Transportes e Turismo Ltda., empresa sabidamente vinculada à facção criminosa e destinatária de aportes ilícitos, exercendo atos de gestão, controle e ingerência em favor da permanência e favorecimento do grupo criminoso no sistema de transporte coletivo urbano da capital paulista”.
A decisão ainda aponta que Leite era informado sobre a rotina e os negócios da concessionária Transwolff Transportes por meio de “vídeos e informações sobre a implantação dos ônibus elétricos, o fornecimento de carregadores pela Enel, o treinamento de técnicos e o Projeto Aquático, explorado pelo grupo econômico na região do Bororé”.
Após a decisão da Justiça, os réus têm agora o prazo de dez dias para apresentar a defesa às acusações. Milton Leite está preso no Centro de Detenção Provisória II de Guarulhos, na Grande São Paulo.
A Agência Brasil tentou contato com a defesa de Milton Leite e não obteve retorno até a publicação deste texto.

An NFL official will work two games on the same day Sunday after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide for several hours Friday, disrupting travel plans for professional and college teams across the country.
Don Willard will officiate the Miami Dolphins’ game against the Indianapolis Colts at 1pm ET before traveling 112 miles east to work the Pittsburgh Steelers’ Sunday Night Football matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The NFL benefited from its Sunday schedule, with teams typically traveling the day before their games. But Friday’s flight stoppage forced adjustments across the league’s officiating crews and elsewhere in American sports.
The NBA also made changes to its officiating assignments as travel disruptions continued into Saturday.
Brian Forte was added to the officiating crew for the Chicago-Minnesota game, replacing Jason Goldenberg. Jenna Schroeder, meanwhile, replaced Forte for the Dallas-Cleveland game. The Brooklyn-Memphis game brought Michael Smith into the three-person crew late in the afternoon after another referee could not get there in time.
Brent Barnaky and CJ Washington were added to the Denver-New Orleans game on Saturday night after officiating a game in New Orleans on Friday night. Two other referees had been assigned earlier Saturday.
Major sporting events slowly returned to normal Saturday after the nationwide ground stop, although teams across the country continued to grapple with its effects.
Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before kickoff, and a number of games were delayed by hours to give visiting programs more time to arrive and prepare. No 2 Utah’s game at No 22 Arizona was pushed back three hours, as was Arizona State’s game at Central Florida. Other teams, like Auburn, opted for charter buses. One way or another, most teams found a solution.
There was, however, one major exception: the No 19 Mississippi game at Oklahoma was moved to Sunday, with kickoff scheduled for 1pm ET.
JuJu Watkins and her third-ranked Southern California teammates had just boarded their flight to face top-ranked South Carolina when the ground stop was issued. The Trojans women’s basketball team stayed in Los Angeles for the night after being deplaned, and their departure for Greenville was pushed to Saturday afternoon.
Fairleigh Dickinson women’s basketball coach Stephanie Gaitley found out late Friday night that her team’s flight to Ohio State had been canceled. There was discussion about leaving immediately by bus and making a stop halfway, but Gaitley preferred to let her team get a better night’s sleep before setting out on a 10-hour bus ride on Saturday morning.
In women’s soccer, the Utah Royals were already in the Washington DC area ahead of their National Women’s Soccer League semi-final against the Washington Spirit on Saturday. The Kansas City Current were supposed to depart Friday for their semi-final against Gotham FC on Sunday in New York.
The Current told ESPN they were “collaborating with key stakeholders, including the NWSL and our charter partner, to identify next steps in order to arrive safely ahead of our match against Gotham FC on Sunday”.
There were 14 scheduled NHL games on Saturday, and the majority of teams made it to their destinations before the flight stoppage began. The San Jose Sharks, who were left waiting to see whether they would be able to travel, arrived late Friday in Utah.
In the NBA, most teams were, at worst, mildly affected by Friday’s events. Cleveland were the outlier.
The Cavaliers started their Saturday much earlier than usual, leaving Miami at 8.54am on a plane taking them to Cleveland, where they were set to play the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday night.
The Cavs couldn’t get out of Miami on Friday night as planned after a game against the Heat that capped a three-game road trip, then scrambled to rebook some hotel rooms. NBA teams typically don’t fly on the morning of a game, but exceptions have been made for unusual situations.
Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell said he would have preferred Saturday’s game to be rescheduled, but noted the team would “make adjustments, figure it out and go from there.”
“Back-to-back, three-hour flight, it was already a tough one,” Mitchell said. “But hey, they say we’ve got to play, we’ve got to play.”
Rescheduling the game against the Mavericks wasn’t an ideal option. Cleveland have a busy arena with a minor league hockey team, college games and other events scheduled; Saturday’s game falls in a stretch where the arena is playing host to events on 11 consecutive days.
“It’s part of it,” Cleveland coach Kenny Atkinson said. “You just adapt.”
The Cavaliers listed Mitchell, James Harden, Peyton Watson and Jarrett Allen as questionable on Saturday night’s injury report shortly after their flight landed in Cleveland. All four started Friday’s game in Miami.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: NFL week 10: Lions thrash Patriots, Vikings v Packers and more – live
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Graham Searles
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
The boo birds are out at Lambeau, furious with a shocking 2.2 yards per play from their Green Bay offense. Nothing Jordan Love can do at present against a horribly good Vikings defense. Five sacks for the purple people eaters at the break.
Andrew van Ginkel comes in off the edge and doubles up with Kyle van Noy to punish Jordan Love again. That is the fourth sack of the day of the Vikings. 3rd and 14 on the way.
This game is just awesome. Quality players all over the field are making plays non-stop. Who else but Xavier McKinney who intercepts Kirk Cousins on 3rd and 9. Three picks in his last two games. Impressive.
Ouch. Atlanta get a stop and force a field goal try only for a defensive offside to hand a fresh set of downs to Patrick Mahomes. He needs one play to make it count. Josh Downs scores his first touchdown as a Chief on debut.
Short, but tasty gains keep the Vikings rolling to midfield. Then Cousins lays in a nice 17-yard throw to Justin Jefferson. Watch out! Packers get some pressure but Cousins throws it away in time. 43 yards to go at 2nd and 10 at the two-minute warning.
That completion to Matthew Golden was overturned so no redemption in the end for him. Just more misery for the Packers. They punt it and Kirk Cousins is control at his 25-yard line. A decent Jordan Mason dash for seven yards and the Vikings are smiling with loads of clock for this drive.
Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is questionable to return with an ankle injury.
After making a 23-yard reception on Kansas City’s second offensive play just 89 seconds into the game, Kelce was chased down by Atlanta safety DeMarcco Hellams and tackled around the ankles. Kelce limped off the field and walked gingerly to the locker room.
Drops have been a problem all season for Green Bay and they continue as Matthew Golden misses a ball that would have moved the sticks. Then a delay of game forces the Packers to 3ed and long but Jordan Love converts to … Matthew Golden for 12 yards. Redemption. The Packers on their 40-yard line now.
Oh that has got to hurt!!! The former Packer running back Aaron Jones spills out to the left edge and finds the pylon to put the Vikings up three scores at Lambeau Field.
Kirk Cousins is actually intercepted after the near miss earlier in the drive … or is he?! He is sacked by Karl Brooks but the quarterback’s knee was down as he flopped the ball up to Lukas van Ness. Lucky escape for the Vikings.
Cousins then unleashes hell with a 24-yard strike to Tai Felton. Again bunching the receivers works a treat for the Vikings. One yard to go for the score!!!
Ooooh Kirk Cousins is almost picked off as he tries to find Justin Jefferson out on the left sideline. Carrington Valentine makes the play jumping the route. On 2nd and 10 do-it-all offensive weapon Myles Price dashes for 12 yards to move the chains. Cousins then lumbers for eight to push Minnesota to the edge of the red zone.
Another Vikings sack of Jordan Love. The linebackers crash into the interior of the line and Levi Drake Rodriguez storms through for the sack. Then Eric Wilson slashes through an open lane and brings down Love again. On eight of nine plays the Vikings have got to Love. Complete domination!!! Punt puts the Vikings at midfield.
Hold on! Miami go for the trick play as Kyle McCord throws laterals it to receiver Malick Washington who goes for the home run throw to Justin Tolbert and Tolbert hangs on for the 34 yard score. Tie game.
Cousins is cooking now at least he would be if his tight end could hold on to the ball on 3rd down. Before that he hit the touchdown scorer Myles Price for 11 yards but the punt team is on the field after the incompletion. Your move, Jordan Love!
The NFL’s best red zone defense are playing up to that billing as Jordan Love tries to find his tight end Tucker Kraft in the end zone only for Harrison Smith to intercept the pass. Smith goes on way to draw the pass from Love then sprints back across to the middle of the end zone to grab the overthrown ball. What a play. This is immense from the Vikings defense.
Another week, another heartbreak for Jonathan Taylor fantasy owners. Indy aiming to snap a run of five successive defeats against a Miami team starting Kyle McCord at quarterback with one win all season.
Green Bay send the heat at Kirk Cousins but he gets rid of it to bring up 3rd and 8. Second prize still very good for the Packers who shut him down again … but wait … the yellow flags fly. Face mask against the offense! 3rd and 23 then … good luck. They bunch the receivers to the right, Cousins goes left to the rookie Myles Price who streaks across the field diagonally and makes the catch. The receiver bounces off a defender and races into the end zone off to the right again for his first career touchdown! WOW!!! Welcome back Kirk Cousins … you like that?!
This offense needs to back up its defense now. Kirk Cousins tosses it to Gavin Bartholomew from under center for 10 yards to move the chains then scrambles for four. A third 3rd down up quickly but can they convert this one? YES! Cousins hooks up with old pal Justin Jefferson for 13 yards. That’s the way to do it.
Dallas Turner gets to Jordan Love with a straightline dart at the quarterback. He goes through the blocker and whacks Love for his eighth sack of the season. To add insult to injury rookie kicker misses the field goal attempt wide right. Minnesota’s defense does it again.
A bone-headed roughness penalty puts the Packers at midfield. Jordan Love gets tricksy on the QB sneak on 3rd down as he rolls out to the right then hits Tucker Kraft for 15 yards rather than trying to dive over. About 30 yards to go for the touchdown.
The Vikings defense is on top form though. Andrew van Ginkel hits Mark Redman then strips the ball from the tight end’s grasp. Kirk Cousins is back on the field just like that with 10 yards to go for the score!!
Kirk Cousins is a Viking again and takes over on offense at the 30-yard line. The 38-year-old has a trusty weapon in Justin Jefferson to find though on 3rd and 7 he goes way short of the sticks for a screen pass and the blocking is abysmal. Three and out and a punt. Nothing new for the Vikings offense then.
A quick reminder of the upcoming action in 15 minutes …
(6-2) Kansas City Chiefs v Atlanta Falcons (3-6)
(3-5) Houston Texans v Cleveland Browns (5-4)
(6-2) Minnesota Vikings v Green Bay Packers (6-3)
(1-7) Miami Dolphins v Indianapolis Colts (2-7)
(3-5) Carolina Panthers v New Orleans Saints (3-5)
(7-1) Buffalo Bills v New York Jets (2-7)
(6-2) Jacksonville Jaguars v Tennessee Titans (1-7)
Lots of playoff contenders in action with the Bills, Jags and Chiefs looking to go full steam ahead for January. Unlikely any of that trio will fall today but ya never know, do ya!
Also speaking of playoff contenders the blissfully weird NFC South pits the Panthers and Saints in a “winner goes top” match as both sit with three wins and five losses. The Bucs and Falcons are both one game back at 3-6 so maybe it could be Atlanta that grab some initiative against a Chiefs team who are without star running back Kenneth Walker.
(5-5) New England Patriots 10-35 Detroit Lions (7-2)
Well that is about as comfortable as it gets. Detroit enjoy a large slice of luck with Drake Maye exiting the game with an ankle injury and pile on the pain through a Jahmyr Gibbs onslaught. No shame for New England in being bowled over by the NFL’s best offensive player but still will smart being knocked back to 5-5. The Pats will hope Maye returns quickly otherwise their playoff hopes could be kaput. The Lions meanwhile go joint-top of the NFC North. Ausgezeichnet!!
The backups are in for Detroit as they look forward to an exciting run to the playoffs in the ultra competitive NFC North. Next up for the Lions are the Buccaneers. Gibbs will have a trickier day against a stout run defense but Detroit will still be confident of getting it done at home.
Gibbs is having an unforgettable night on his holidays in Germany. The NFL’s leader in total touchdowns this season and yards from scrimmage has 153 yards rushing on 22 carries and two scores with another 99 yards on seven receptions.
Meanwhile, AJ Brown is out of the game for New England with a hamstring injury. That trade has not worked out and then some.
Jahmyr Gibbs races out to the right and big blocker Penei Sewell beats back the onrushing Patriots to carve a lane for the running back. Gibbs then races past him and dances round a couple for defenders and in up the sideline. He now has the most touchdowns of any player in the first four seasons of a career with 62. Amazing.
Injury news from the big one in the NFC North in a little while … Kirk Cousins won’t get the opportunity to throw to Jordan Addison when the veteran quarterback begins his second stint with the Vikings.
Addison was ruled out for the Vikings’ game with the Green Bay Packers because of a thumb injury. Addison has 18 catches for 277 yards and one touchdown this season.
Green Bay’s inactive players are running backs Josh Jacobs and Pierre Strong, linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive lineman Donovan Jennings, guard Kevin Zeitler and center Sean Rhyan.
But the Lions cough up a flag of their own for pass interference on the next play putting the Patriots on the 15-yard line. DeVito fires one into Mack Hollins for five yards. Next a play action bootleg comes to nothing and it’s 3rd and 5.
The Lions rush four, they almost collapse on DeVito but he flings it out to rookie Lan Larison for the 10-yard score. Nice. DeVito’s first touchdown throw as a Patriot and the first score of Larison’s career.
Quick stop for New England and the cat may start thinking about a stroll among the pigeons.
DeVito has another 3rd down to contend with but before that the moustachioed Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has his hands on his knees and shakes his head in disappointment. Bit harsh considering the backup is definitely doing his best. Maybe he was predicting future pain … New England score on a short pass but a flag cancels it out for offensive pass interference. When it rains it pours.
Here we go, Tommy! The Patriots backup scrambles for 11 yards to move the chains and he hits Mack Hollins for six. New England are 30 yards away from a much-needed touchdown as the third quarter closes.
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has tied HoF’er Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns (61) by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history
Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes needs one touchdown pass against the Falcons to overtake Peyton Manning (327) for the most touchdown passes by a quarterback in his first 10 seasons, including the playoffs
With a win at the New York Jets, Josh Allen can surpass Patrick Mahomes (95) for the second-most regular season wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine seasons
Later, on the other side of the ball from Kirk Cousins for the Vikings will be Jordan Love at quarterback for the Packers. He is enjoying an excellent season with Green Bay aiming for the playoffs. A win today would be a big step to making it happen.
Love now leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 for 19 touchdowns to six interceptions as the league’s best at explosive plays. He ranks first in intended air yards (3,251), intended air yards per attempt (9.5) and completed air yards (1,553) at the heart of the league’s second-best passing attack.
They have two No 1 receivers emerging in Christian Watson - third in the league with 879 yards - and Matthew Golden - fourth with 783 yards.
And the Packers have needed an effective passing game. They have the worst rushing attack in the NFL.
Another 3rd down, another DeVito throw and another slight let down from his receiver. This time the ball cannons off the fingertips of Efton Chism. They punt it back to Detroit. Hard luck for New England fans.
As we look forward, there has been another score in Munich … the Lions extending their lead to 28-3. The game has reached the point where Detroit are flexing their creative muscles. Amon-Ra St Brown collects the short pass from Jared Goff and the offensive line collapse and shuttle ahead through the centre of the Patriots defense allowing St Brown to barrel through for a 28-yard touchdown. Your move, DeVito.
So with the Lions well set for a victory that would put them tied for top in the NFC North with the Bears at 7-2 … we can look ahead to another NFC North clash on the way with six other matches to savour coming at 12pm CST/1pm EST/6pm GMT (home teams listed second):
(6-2) Kansas City Chiefs v Atlanta Falcons (3-6)
(3-5) Houston Texans v Cleveland Browns (5-4)
(6-2) Minnesota Vikings v Green Bay Packers (6-3)
(1-7) Miami Dolphins v Indianapolis Colts (2-7)
(3-5) Carolina Panthers v New Orleans Saints (3-5)
(7-1) Buffalo Bills v New York Jets (2-7)
(6-2) Jacksonville Jaguars v Tennessee Titans (1-7)
The Vikings face down the Packers at Lambeau Field bidding to end a run of two defeats with a familiar face coming in at quarterback. Kirk Cousins is back for Minnesota. The veteran has 10 appearances as a Viking against Green Bay. His record: 5-4-1 with two of those five wins coming on the road.
The Pats defense has done their job with a quick three and out. DeVito went 4/19 for 16 yards and an interception before the break. New England dutifully run the ball a couple of times with little success. DeVito gets the call, drops back, completes the pass but a false start puts them back to 3rd & 11. D’oh.
The players are back out on the field with the Lions taking over on offense.
Jahmyr Gibbs had a monster first half recording 171 yards of total offense, the most of any Detroit player in a half since Barry Sanders 32 years ago. Decent company to keep.
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye injured his right ankle on a sack by Aidan Hutchinson in the first quarter and won’t return to the game.
Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down at the Detroit 15-yard line on New England’s first drive. Andy Borregales then kicked a 33-yard field goal. Since then the Patriots have failed to score a point.
Hutchinson himself grabbed his right knee after jumping and landing while celebrating. He went to the locker room for evaluation.
Guten tag, football fans! Week 10 is in full swing in Münich with the final international game of the season pitting the (6-2) Detroit Lions against the (5-4) New England Patriots. It is a bit of a one-sided affair thus far as Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has exited the game with an ankle injury putting Tommy DeVito under center for Mike Vrabel’s team.
The Lions lead 21-3 and have had some struggles on offense with Jared Goff throwing two interceptions but Jahmyr Gibbs has run one touchdown in while Amon-Ra St Brown and Isaac TeSlaa have caught one each. Wünderbar!
Let’s see if the Patriots can bounce back in the second half.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.author: Daniel Harris
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.text:
Our teams are tunnelled … and here they come!
- Updates from 7.45pm (GMT) kick-off in Madrid
- Get in touch: email Daniel and follow us on BlueSky
Sun 15 Nov 2026 14.41 EST
First published on Sun 15 Nov 2026 13.15 EST
Sun 15 Nov 2026 14.41 EST
First published on Sun 15 Nov 2026 13.15 EST
Ah, I forgot to note that James Trafford has been given the start in net. Maybe it’s to keep Jordan Pickford on his toes, but it won’t have escaped Tuchel’s attention that his no 1 got nowhere near Enzo Fernandes’ equaliser in Atlanta – not did it escape Bellingham’s, caught on camera saying “It was in the middle of the goal”, perhaps with added expletive. Pickford has been decent for England, but that doesn’t mean better isn’t possible.
I’m really looking forward to seeing how Hall does against Lamine. He’s an excellent builder of play and a pretty good defender too, but does he have the explosion and recovery pace to get close?
When did Vogue become Shoot become Mizz? The December edition not only features Jude Bellingham as its cover star – I can’t say my wife was impressed when it arrived through the letterbox – but with a gatefold poster, signed “Jude X”. And of course the “Hey Jude” headline is stone-cold genius; how do they think of these things?!
Pre-match controversy:
I daresay Lamine Yamal, for one, disagrees with his manager.
Spain, meanwhile, will want to circulate the ball, pulling England’s midfielders out wide to open that space in the middle Tuchel knows they mustn’t vacate; easier said than done. Ruiz will look to attack the box, Merino too – with both adding set-piece threat – while Lamine and Baena will both fancy themselves to have the better of their full-back, both inside and out.
Oyarzabal will, I think, play off Quansah, fancying his nous to create space, while I’d not be surprised if Rice is the pressing trigger, the front players looking to jump when the ball goes into him.
So, where is the game? I actually think Spain’s XI gives England a good chance. I’d not be at all surprised if Anthony Gordon is under orders to get about Martin Zubimendi – the way Alex Ferguson once did with Park Ji-Sung and Andrea Pirlo – a lovely passer but, by the standard a little weak. Mikel Arteta signed him because Declan Rice isn’t a first receiver, able to turn on the ball and punch into midfield, only to find the physicality of the Premier League was too much, hence the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, so Gordon – and Morgan Rogers – can worry him, allowing England to take possession high up the pitch.
I also think they’ll use Kane dropping deep to thread passes in behind Spain’s high line, Gordon and Rogers looking to attack the space with Bellingham also joining the last line. Meantime, Anderson and Rice will seek to carry the ball forward, with the former also seeking to unfurl long passes and get the home defence turned to face their own goal.
I should add that, while England could have won that Wembley game –they’d have been close to impregnable at 3-1 – they might easily have been 3-0 down before they scored.
Tuchel speaks, telling ITV that “it’s a beautiful match”. They’ve qualified, done their homework and now can try and top the group.
Quansah keeps his place for doing well, while he wants to see White under pressure and cites his club partnership with Konsa as a reason for picking him, just as last game, he went for the Newcastle understanding between Burn, Hall and Gordon down the left side.
Otherwise, he wants to see “patient defending” when in a 4-4-2 or deep block, adding that, “under no circumstance” can they “open the middle” as, if you do, Spain will “go right through you” as they did to score their third when winning 3-2 at Wembley – a game in which Harry Kane missed a penalty to put England 3-1 up. Finally, they must avoid ball-losses in their own half.
Taking a closer look at the England side, there’s no getting away from it: the defence isn’t up to standard. Lewis Hall, mind-bogglingly omitted from the World Cup squad, is in – Tuchel’s problems were not just reflective of a panic at a crucial moment, but that he picked a group able to play one way only, without difference-making options. Otherwise, though, Konsa is now an automatic choice, but Quansah callow and lacking elite potential, while White is a decent Premier-League player and nothing more.
Email! “Thanks for putting up the squad list,” says Edan Tal. “Delighted that Clint Hill finally managed his long awaited call up.”
Shaun Derry next. Or Dan Burn.
Back to the teams, the thing that strikes me about Spain’s – the thing that always strikes me about Spain’s – is the absence from it of Pedri. I’m not sure there’s another midfielder in the world I’d prefer to have, but De la Fuente likes the balance without him, even with Rodri absent. I do wonder, though, if they’ll be able to exert their usual midfield control, given he’s gone for Merino, who offers goal-power but not loads else.
What’s on the line? Er, not much. Both sides are into the last eight, but the group-topper – England if they win tonight, Spain if they don’t – will play an unseeded team in the quarters, with the second leg at home, when the competition resumes at the end of March. In contention from the other A-groups are Italy, France, Belgium; Netherlands, Greece, Germany; Portugal, Denmark, Norway.
As for England, Thomas Tuchel plumps for the joy of a Konsa/Quansah centre-back pairing, with Dan Burn dropping out. Otherwise, Ben White is in at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, and the now-settled front six remains the same.
Spain are still without Rodri, but Lamine Yamal, rested for the 2-0 win away to Czechia, returns in place of Yeremy Pino. Otherwise, Pedro Porro, so important at the World Cup, loses out to Marc Pubill; Dean Huijsen is replaced by Aymeric Laporte; Mikel Merino is in for Fermin Lopez; and Mikel Oyarzabal is at centre-forward, not Ferran Torres.
We’ll go into those shortly, but in the meantime, also going on:
Teams!
Spain (4-3-3): Unai Simon; Pubill, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Fabian Ruiz, Merino; Lamine Yamal, Oyarzabal, Alex Baena. Subs: Raya, Joan Garcia, Marc Roca, Huijsen, Ferran Torres, Fermin Lopez, Pino, Pedro Porro, Barrios, Williams, Munoz, Pedri.
England (4-2-3-1): Trafford; White, Konsa, Quansah, Hall; Rice, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham Jude, Gordon; Kane. Subs: Pickford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Hill, Burn, Spence, Lewis-Skelly, Gibbs-White, Bellingham Jobe, Eze, Ngumoha, Calvert-Lewin.
Preamble
The scandal of England’s World Cup semi-final capitulation is already enshrined in the extensive annals of mythological failure; failure so gloriously tepid and inept it’s barely failure at all, rather a perfectly pitched lyrical paean to the sacred, desperate art of getting in your own way as wimpishly as possible. It is beautiful.
The truth, though – and part of the beauty – is it remains an ultimately futile act. Let’s say England see out the win, setting up a final meeting with Spain: Emlyn, what happened next?
Spanish football stye is, without doubt, the hardest there’s ever been to beat. We saw it with Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona, Vicente del Bosque’s national team – and now with Luis de la Fuente’s European and World champions. None of those sides were or are without obvious, glaring flaws, and yet their ability to look after the ball; their command of angles, most particularly of movement and first touch; their commitment to their principles; leave all opponents with an impossible dilemma: try to beat them by being more like them, or try to beat them by playing in a way they are expert at neutralising. Good luck, chaps.
Which is to say that, had England eliminated Argentina in Atlanta, they’d almost certainly have lost the final in the same predictable way they lost the Euro final. However – football being a perfectly balanced sport in which to cover one hole you necessarily leave another open – there’s always a however. So, however: that embarrassment of England’s defeat might, finally, have forced home the bitter reality that teams who cower and hope time runs out quickly enough to save them are not teams who win tournaments.
Tonight’s match will take a decent barometer of how deeply they believe an axiom proved infallible over many, many decades. The game being the game, a result that would once have been the difference between progress and not barely matters, given both sides are already through to the next stage. But this contest is not about that, rather about whether England can find a way of imposing themselves – on Spain, but also on themselves, for there is beauty in that too
Kick-off: 8.45pm local, 7.45pm GMT

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Five red cards issued for mass brawl in New York Red Bulls v Club América friendly
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Jeff Rueter
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
One hallmark of Mauricio Pochettino’s time in international management was been his refusal to embrace the term “friendly.” His preferred branding is “unofficial games”.
His spin gained a bit of validity on Saturday, in the New York Red Bulls’ “friendly” against Club América, marred by a mass brawl between the sides that resulted in five red cards and a bevy of beverages thrown from the stands.
The game itself was odd for a few reasons. First, the Red Bulls have already been eliminated from MLS’s comically forgiving postseason, which means players (aside from veterans like Emil Forsberg) delayed vacations for a glorified scrimmage. Second, the match was announced on 1 October, at which point it was abundantly clear that the NWSL’s Gotham FC, a tenant of the Red Bulls’ Sports Illustrated Stadium, could host a playoff semi-final on the same weekend.
That scheduling snafu, combined with the comically poor state of the pitch, became a serious problem for the NWSL club, who settled for 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium for Sunday’s semi-final.
For the Red Bulls, the show must go on – and boy, did they, also finding a way to entertain the fans who showed up for the low-stakes affair.
Not with their soccer exploits, mind you. Playing without the aforementioned veterans and US internationals Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti, the remaining Red Bulls came ready for a scrap. At one point in the second half, América goalkeeper Rodolfo Cota required treatment for taking a boot above his knee while closing a shooting angle, putting the visitors on alert.
Roughly 40 minutes into the second half, this unofficial game abandoned any attempt to be friendly. Mijahir Jiménez dribbled toward the right corner flag, only to be taken down by a defender. He took great umbrage to the nature of the challenge, kicking off a maelstrom of shoves, punches, thrown drinks from the crowd, and men pressing their chests and foreheads together like bighorn rams in the throes of the rutting season.
The full sequence lives on thanks to a live watch-along streamed on YouTube, where former Mexico defender Miguel Layún comes to life in his gamer chair and begs his compatriots to keep the fracas alive. The fracas lasted 65 seconds, while the ensuing corner kick came a full seven minutes after Jimenez’s dribble.
The only final scoreline from the night that matters: two Red Bulls sent off against three players from América. And, hopefully, a cautionary tale to put an end to meaningless exhibitions like these.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: WTA Finals final: Elina Svitolina v Mirra Andreeva – live
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Beau Dure
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
If you like off-court drama, this is the tournament for you.
Coco Gauff expressed but then clarified some reservations about the format, a round-robin leading to knockout play.
Jessica Pegula was caught on a hot mic griping that Mirra Andreeva was a “diva” who “needs to be humbled.”
Pegula apologized, then did not deliver said humbling, losing to Andreeva 6-3, 6-4 in the semi-finals.
And now our final pits Andreeva, the latest teen phenom in a sport that seems to produce a new one every few months, against Elina Svitolina. Important note: Svitolina is from Ukraine. Andreeva is from … well, you can probably guess, even if you didn’t read the note below about Andreeva’s compatriot Aryna Sabalenka and her apology to Svitolina.
Who will win this season-closer? Who will apologize to whom? Will Andreeva add to her trophy case after her breakthrough major at Roland Garros earlier this year? Follow along to find out.
The rise of Mirra Andreeva has seemed inevitable ever since she burst on to the tour as a precocious 15-year-old more than three years ago, but this week, six months after her maiden grand slam triumph at Roland Garros, she has taken another massive step forward in her career. The 19-year-old will attempt to close out the most impressive week of her career by winning one of her most significant titles after thoroughly outplaying Jessica Pegula, the fifth seed, 6-3, 6-4 to reach the championship match of the WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.
A year ago, Andreeva surprisingly failed to qualify for the WTA Finals, missing out by a paltry six points after bizarrely deciding not to compete in the final tournament week before the event. The world No 3 has been utterly supreme in her long-awaited debut appearance, bulldozing through elite opposition to reach the final without dropping a set. She has conceded just 18 games in four matches this week, including a 6-4, 6-0 demolition of the No 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka, winning 11 games in succession from 1-4 down.
Andreeva will rise to No 2 in the WTA rankings for the first time in her career on Monday regardless of the outcome here. The world No 1, Elena Rybakina, and Sabalenka, who drops to No 3, will both be defending a large number of points at the Australian Open after Rybakina defeated Sabalenka in this year’s final. This means the No 1 ranking will almost certainly be a realistic target for Andreeva at the start of the 2027 season, particularly if she closes out this imperious week with a title.
The Russian will face Elina Svitolina after the Ukrainian dominated the Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the second semi-final, rolling to a 6-2, 6-1 win. Svitolina, who also beat Sabalenka this week, will be attempting to win the WTA Finals for a second time after first lifting the trophy in 2018. This will be a rematch of their encounter earlier this week during the group stage, which Andreeva easily won 6-4, 6-0.
Elsewhere, Sabalenka issued a public apology on Saturday after being accused of making offensive remarks towards Svitolina during Friday’s match. An angry Sabalenka was caught on camera making a comment between points, which some social media users interpreted as an offensive insult against her Ukrainian opponent.
“My comment was not directed at Elina,” Sabalenka said in a social media post.
“I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Record number of migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Record number of migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands
New European Union migration and asylum laws have largely failed to stem the flow of migrants to Spain and its territories.
Spain has declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands after the arrival of more than 9,000 people in its Atlantic Ocean territory since the start of November.
Spain’s Maritime Rescue Service said it had rescued 1,488 migrants aboard 14 dinghies, also known as pirogues, most of whom arrived on El Hierro in the Canary Islands from West Africa on Saturday.
That’s broken the record of 1,461 people rescued six years earlier in November 2020.
Spain’s Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres is visiting El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals.
Al Jazeera’s Bernard Smith, reporting from El Hierro, said the arrival this year has set a record in the 32 years since statistics have been collected.
“There’s been even more arrivals by Sunday afternoon”, Smith said, adding that the new arrivals are processed at the port in El Hierro and taken to a reception centre and sent on to other Canary Islands or to the Spanish mainland.
The European Union’s new Pact on Migration and Asylum officially came into force on June 12, 2026, introducing “firm and fair rules” for accepting asylum requests, marking the most sweeping overhaul of EU asylum and border laws in decades.
“EU states are under pressure to do more to control migration from Africa and from outside the European Union,” Smith said, adding that the new rules haven’t stopped the flow of migrants to Spain and its enclaves.
Spain’s Ceuta enclave
Last month, Spain deported more than a dozen of the 80,000 people who had entered its North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco over a 48-hour period in late July.
At least 100 people died during the mass crossing into the autonomous city, which covers just 18.5 square kilometres (7.1sq miles) and has a population of about 80,000.
Most of the migrants arriving in El Hierro depart from West Africa, many leaving from Senegal, with hopes of reaching mainland Europe.
But to get there, they risk their lives in small, often overcrowded boats at sea.
One boat on Saturday was carrying 240 people, including 12 women and 36 children, authorities said.
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded at least 450 deaths on the Western African Atlantic route in the first 10 months of 2026.
“It is a treacherous journey,” said Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque, reporting from Dakar in Senegal, from where some of the boats depart, adding that favourable weather conditions in the Atlantic Ocean have made departures from the coastlines in Africa much easier in recent years.
“So when the weather conditions allow it, the boats go out there,” he said, noting that migrants use “wooden fishing vessels called pirogues” in which up to 100 people are packed in for “a journey that can last one week”.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/looki.title: ‘Looking away was never a choice for me’: How Hollywood’s love affair with Israel turned sour
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/looki.author: Fleur Hargreaves
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/looki.text:
‘Looking away was never a choice for me’: How Hollywood’s love affair with Israel turned sour
Once Israel could rely on Hollywood to have its reputation laundered, performing the role of a benign ally which shared the values and interests of the West.
However, a growing number of actors and prominent figures in film and TV are confronting the industry’s ongoing complicity with Israel's occupation and its actions in Gaza, which a consensus of experts and human rights groups have called a genocide.
More and more artists are using their platforms to speak about the plight of the Palestinians and have contributed to Israel’s cratering approval among western audiences.
In 2025, US-based organisation Film Workers for Palestine (FWP), established by a group of filmmakers the previous year, released a pledge to end complicity with the genocide in Gaza.
It garnered the signatures of more than 5,500 people in the industry, including A-list actors like Josh O’Connor, Olivia Colman, Andrew Garfield, Emma Stone and many more.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Inspired by Filmmakers United Against Apartheid, a group of artists who refused to screen their work in apartheid South Africa, signatories pledged not to screen films, appear at or work alongside Israeli film institutions implicated in genocide and apartheid.
“People were ready to publicly put their name to a commitment of refusal... to not be complicit in Israel’s genocide,” an FWP spokesperson told Middle East Eye, adding that there is “power in numbers”.
A major element of Israel’s “normalisation” is through allowing western films to be shown in Israeli cinemas and festivals, they added, but filmmakers can challenge this by specifying consultation requirements for particular territories in their contracts.
“I do think there is a sea-change happening,” the spokesperson told MEE, where “people are thinking about their labour and how it is related, how their art is being used".
Many actors wore ceasefire and Palestine pins on the red carpet, using award ceremony speeches and publicity to draw attention to the conflict.
One of the pledge’s signatories, British actor and prominent human rights activist Juliet Stevenson, told MEE that “it was a no-brainer for me to speak up”.
The actor, who is an Amnesty Ambassador, has supported refugee rights throughout her career and last year spoke out in favour of proscribed organisation Palestine Action.
She explained: “I felt I had no option really, looking away was never a choice for me. I don’t know who I would’ve been if I had looked away.”
She added that the potential impact on her career “did not cross my mind”.
Regarding why more artists and institutions had not spoken out, she said it was “hard to find an answer that isn’t connected to fear, or not wanting to rock the boat”, but as consciousness shifts, more people are emboldened to take a stance, she said.
The recent success of NAZA, an Israeli film featuring soldiers' testimonies of their crimes in Gaza, which received a 25-minute standing ovation at Venice Film Festival, demonstrated for Stevenson that “people in Hollywood who can't seem to operate alone, can seem to stand up with others”.
Corporate consolidation
US film and distribution company Paramount, which was recently acquired by pro-Israel billionaire Larry Ellison, criticised FWP’s pledge as “an effort to boycott Israeli film-makers”.
Since the Ellison family took over the studio, there were reports of Paramount blacklisting talent because of their stance on Palestine, however the company denies this.
Other sources clarified that, while no itemised list exists, senior management “shares a set of values” and will not work with anyone expressing “hate”.
Mark Ruffalo, star of Marvel’s The Hulk and a vocal pro-Palestine supporter, faced accusations of antisemitism from Ellison after criticising Paramount Skydance's controversial $111bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery.
In a social media post, Ruffalo highlighted links between Paramount, run by CEO David Ellison, and Oracle, the firm owned by his father Larry, whose surveillance technology maintains Israeli apartheid and occupation.
Ruffalo shared a video of former Oracle CEO Safra Catz stating that “we have some really profoundly scary technology at Oracle, and we wanted to make sure it was available for the effort”, referring to the Israeli military’s response to the 7 October 2023 attacks.
“Look how [Catz] revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle,” he commented.
“These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day be used on you,” Ruffalo warned, urging opposition to the merger, which he said would be “catastrophic” for the entertainment industry.
The media giant accused Ruffalo of using “antisemitic tropes” in criticising a deal which would put one family in control of much of American media, including news channels CNN and CBS, and streaming platform HBO.
In response, over 180 prominent Jewish figures signed a letter defending Ruffalo against the “false and dangerous weaponisation of charges of antisemitism”.
Union failures
Ruffalo is not the only actor to face institutional backlash for supporting Palestine.
In November 2023, Susan Sarandon was dropped by her talent agency after speaking at a pro-Palestine rally, while Melissa Barrera was fired from the Scream franchise for resharing a post accusing Israel of “genocide and ethnic cleansing”.
While the US actors’ union SAG-AFTRA rallied against talkshow host Jimmy Kimmel's suspension by ABC for criticising US President Donald Trump, it remained silent on the repression of actors opposing Israel.
“The tide has changed,” Amin El Gamal, chair of SAG-AFTRA’s National Middle Eastern and North African Committee, told MEE, referring to the climate after 2023.
But Hollywood’s “gatekeepers have largely not caught up to public opinion”, remaining unresponsive to union members’ demands to end their “deep complicity” in Israel’s crimes.
He cited the union’s pro-Israel statement issued six days after 7 October, when the death toll in Gaza had already surpassed the number killed in the Hamas-led attack, describing it as “helping justify ongoing genocide”.
"Go birds, fuck ICE and free Palestine." Hannah Einbinder turned her Emmy win for best supporting actress in a comedy into a platform for activism, wearing a red Artists4Ceasefire pin and joining fellow actors on the red carpet calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. In a follow-up interview, Einbinder said the cause was deeply personal, citing friends working as doctors and teachers in Gaza. She added that as a Jewish person she feels a responsibility to distinguish Judaism from the state of Israel, and voiced support for the Film Workers for Palestine boycott, saying it “does not boycott individuals, it only boycotts institutions that are directly complicit in the genocide.”
— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) September 15, 2025
Gamal said he repeatedly reached out to the union asking to discuss the statement, but was ignored.
It took almost a year for senior staff to agree to a meeting after an open letter was published in The Hollywood Reporter, only to reject his committee’s proposal for a ceasefire statement.
Although SAG-AFTRA, which also represents broadcasters, condemned Trump and Russia for targeting journalists, it failed to comment on Israel’s systematic targeting of Palestinian journalists.
On the Warner Bros merger, the union released a weak statement, calling for “enforceable safeguards” before the deal proceeds, despite its implications for the labour interests that it is supposed to represent.
BDS success
Meanwhile, Norway’s actors union, Norsk Skuespillerforbund (NSF), recommended its members refuse to work with complicit Israeli institutions in line with Boycott, Divestment and Sanction (BDS) guidelines.
It also joined other artists’ unions in an appeal urging Norwegian authorities to review their cooperation with Israel and protect Palestinian culture from erasure.
The Netherlands’ International Documentary Film Festival, the world’s largest documentary film festival, also recently signed the Dutch and Belgian cultural boycott against Israel.
Ireland’s Cork Film Festival updated its policy to reject funding from governments “found by the International Court of Justice to violate international humanitarian law” or involved in measures “relating to genocide, war crimes, or crimes against humanity”.
FWP launched a campaign targeting Germany’s Berlinale film festival over its crackdown on filmmakers and workers using their platforms to draw attention to Palestine.
Often these institutions claim to be apolitical, yet after Russia’s invasion, Berlinale made Ukrainian flag pins, and funded a group of Ukrainian film-makers: a blatant double standard.
Berlinale receives government funding and is broadcast across Germany, where obsessive crackdowns on pro-Palestinian expression have led to artists being cancelled and deplatformed.
When Israeli-Palestinian film No Other Land won the Documentary Film Award at the Berlinale in February 2024, German politicians accused Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham of antisemitism for criticising his country’s apartheid in his acceptance speech.
No Other Land was also awarded last year’s Oscar for best documentary feature, indicating Academy voters were keen to signal a position on the conflict they were otherwise reluctant to express.
Yet when the Palestinian director Hamdan Ballal was violently attacked by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank shortly after winning the Oscar, the Academy faced criticism for its lack of response.
'A small number of people have disproportionate amounts of power… and a lot of them are still very aligned with Israel’s interests'
- Amin El Gamal, chair of SAG-AFTRA Middle East committee
Another FWP campaign targeted Mubi, which accepted $100m in funding from Sequoia Capital, a venture firm deeply invested in Israeli military technology.
Although FWP did not call for a boycott, its campaign prompted a drop in Mubi’s subscriber base and staff revolts, leading the arthouse streaming platform to concede to some of the group’s demands, albeit in diluted form.
“On the one hand, it’s very hopeful… that we have the hearts of the masses in the US,” El Gamal stated, "but at the same time, increasingly, a small number of people have disproportionate amounts of power… and a lot of them are still very aligned with Israel’s interests.”
He explained that celebrities hold “large cultural capital and actual capital” which they can lend to amplifying Palestinian voices and solidifying Israel’s status as a “toxic rogue state”.
Israel is “so used to getting their way and evading any kind of accountability, they don’t understand what it means to confront this palpable change of attitude”, resorting to silencing critics and vilifying boycotts, which are non-violent, he continued.
But when it comes to “a few billionaires against the masses”, he said, through cultural boycotts and collective action, “people power will always win”.

Morning update
Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,
If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:
*Two Houthi ballistic missiles and three drones, aimed at Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region and Riyadh, were intercepted and destroyed, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
*Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said their forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a base in Bahrain.
*Bahraini air defence systems intercepted and neutralised several Iran aerial attacks on Sunday, Bahrain Defence Force said in a statement, accusing Iran of continuing its "systematic hostile approach through its malicious attacks" on the kingdom.
*Hamas' armed wing said on Sunday that a senior commander, Samir Abu Younis, 53, who commanded its Rafah brigade, was killed in an Israeli airstrike.
*Two oil tankers struck naval mines as they tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz “secretly”, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy says.
*Israeli settlers stormed the al-Harayeq area of the town of Beita, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, and attacked the home of Palestinian citizen Mutie Salim Qutish.
*Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine officials on Saturday, following an investigation into allegations of oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hezbollah group.
*American intelligence believes that Iran has some 1,500-2,500 missiles, and the apparent size of the arsenal has impacted Trump administration's decision on whether to resume strikes on the Islamic Republic, The Wall Street Journal reported.
*A car bomb killed two people, including a child, and wounded another, in a suburb of Damascus on Saturday, Syrian Arab News Agency (Sana) said.
*President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, Reuters reported.
