https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.title: DOJ warns Elizabeth Warren over Trump investigations – US politics live
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.author: Tom Ambrose
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.
Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.
On CNN’s State of the Union, he reaffirmed that he believes he has a path to victory, citing support and a widespread openness to change within the Senate Democratic caucus.
“This really is a response to the call of the voters, who clearly rejected Donald Trump and his awful policies, but they haven’t fully hired the Democrats,” Van Hollen said, alluding to how the US president’s Republican party lost control of Congress during the 3 November midterm elections.
“They’ve given us a chance, and I think we need to earn their trust. And I think that begins by not going back to business as usual.”
Van Hollen criticized reports that Schumer’s team may move the Senate caucus leadership election date earlier than 1 December. He contended that the caucus should have a debate about the group’s direction as the Democrats assume control of Congress in January for the second half of Trump’s second presidency.
Senator Elizabeth Warren, the likely incoming chair of the Senate Banking Committee, was warned by he US Department of Justice of potential “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into president Donald Trump.
It is the latest warning sent by the justice department to congressional Democrats about their potential plans to investigate the administration or Trump associates, Reuters reported.
Trump last week ordered the department to look into Democratic lawmakers for “threatening” people, and US attorney-general Todd Blanche subsequently indicated that his agency was prepared to battle congressional Democrats.
In a letter to Warren, US attorney Aaron Reitz in Houston told the Massachusetts Democrat she appeared “eager to wield your future gavel like a tomahawk, hunting for the scalps of president Trump’s private associates”.
Reitz told her to preserve materials “relevant to your intent to weaponize congressional investigations and deprive citizens of their core constitutional rights”.
Notices to preserve records can presage investigations. Warren’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Reitz shared the letter on social media and Trump reposted it to his Truth Social account several hours later.
Warren and other Democrats have signaled that when their party takes control of Congress in January, they plan to investigate large corporations, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, among others.
In other developments:
Donald Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington. Trump’s departure comes after the often-omnipresent president had remained largely out of public sight for the past several days.
Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances. Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.
US air travel disruptions continued for a third day with more than 10,000 flights affected on Sunday, but transportation secretary Sean Duffy predicted a return to normal by Monday even as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule following a systemwide ground stop.
After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024. Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Why Silicon Valley is backing Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang after his ouster
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Why Silicon Valley is backing Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang after his ouster
Huang’s peers, including Elon Musk, have praised his business acumen and potential risks to the US’s AI goals.
Some of the biggest names in the United States tech sector have launched a campaign to back former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down last week after reports of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
Billionaire Elon Musk and several others praised Huang on social media and urged the Nvidia board to consider reinstating him. Failing to do that, they warned, could hurt US aspirations and business deals within the burgeoning artificial intelligence (AI) sector.
Huang founded Nvidia, which manufactures advanced chips used to power AI, in 1993. The company has since become one of the most valuable in the world and is a cornerstone of the US push to secure AI dominance over China.
After Huang’s resignation, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO. Since last week, Nvidia’s shares and those of some of its partners have suffered significant losses.
An online petition, meanwhile, gathered tens of thousands of signatures from Huang’s peers, former and current Nvidia employees, the company’s stakeholders and other supporters.
Here’s what we know:
Who said what?
Elon Musk, the world’s richest man and CEO of SpaceX, has been a vocal supporter. He praised Huang’s business acumen in a post on his X platform on Saturday, arguing that Nvidia could lose business without him.
“Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract,” he wrote. “Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.”
In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker, the CEOs of investment firms Altimeter Capital Management and Atreides Management, said Huang was an “incredible leader” and deserved a measured investigation. The firms are shareholders in Nvidia.
“Given the extraordinary success of Jensen Huang’s leadership over a long period of time and given the massive uncertainty associated with recent events surrounding his departure, we believe it is in the best interest of all stakeholders and certainly the shareholders of Nvidia for the Board to pursue a slow, measured and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang,” they wrote.
What is the ‘Stand with Jensen’ campaign?
Dozens of major tech leaders also signed an open letter titled “Stand With Jensen” calling for Huang’s return. They included Musk, Garry Tan, CEO of venture capital firm Y Combinator, and Steve Chen, cofounder of YouTube.
The letter, which has garnered more than 172,000 signatures, said Huang was “forced out without due process and without even a few days to make his case”. It asked the board to reinstate the CEO, investigate the allegations and then publicise its findings and decisions, including how it will weigh employees’ and shareholders’ interests when taking further action.
“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the letter read. “We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the centre of this controversy was a spy.”
“Thirty-three years of leadership do not place anyone above accountability. But accountability requires evidence, a fair hearing, and a reasoned decision. Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the letter said.
Some Nvidia employees also showed solidarity with Huang who they said fostered a supportive company culture.
Darrell Dai, who identified himself as a robotics engineer, said in a LinkedIn post that he resigned in support, saying he was struggling to understand Huang’s departure “before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it”.
What has Huang done?
Huang is discussing a possible return with close confidants, according to the Financial Times.
But he faces hurdles. The US restricts Nvidia from selling chips to China, but lawmakers are now looking into whether Huang’s alleged affair may have affected the US’s own AI goals, and more seriously, whether the issue has national security implications.
At least two Congressional committees have asked Huang and senior White House officials to attend hearings in the coming weeks.
US President Donald Trump’s administration has faced criticism for allegedly failing to scrutinise Nvidia’s deals strongly enough, amid the AI race with China, with some pointing to a $25m Nvidia donation to Trump’s White House ballroom project.
The Financial Times newspaper reported that the board has already reached out to Rene Haas, CEO of British chipmaker Arm Holdings, as a potential successor. However, one of Huang’s supporters told the paper that his allies were nonetheless putting together a “war room” of tech executives to lobby for his return and were trying to gain support from the White House.
What does the scandal mean for tech founders?
The matter has rekindled a longstanding argument in Silicon Valley that founders are often unfairly treated by the very companies they founded.
Angel investor Elad Gil, who worked for Google and Twitter, said this was a good time for “founders to revisit their board” to avoid what he called a “coup”.
He cited the removal of OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman in 2023 over allegations that he was pushing profit over AI safety. Altman was reinstated a few days later after major figures such as Microsoft’s Satya Nadella offered him a position.
“Reset your board during good times to avoid sudden action during bad times,” Gil said.
Among those supporting Huang is Travis Kalanick, Uber’s cofounder and former CEO. The board asked him to resign in 2017 after allegations that he did not act on sexual harassment cases in the company. He has not returned.
Pavel Durov, founder of Telegram, warned founders not to have boards at all. In 2014, Durov was kicked off by the board of VK, his first platform, after several run-ins with Russian authorities, including for its refusal to submit protesters’ personal data to the government or to block late opposition leader Alexey Navalny from the site.
But Anthony Scaramucci, a former White House communications director and founder of investment firm SkyBridge Capital, dismissed the calls for Huang’s return.
“A suspected Chinese intelligence operative got close to the man running the most strategically important company in America,” he posted on X.
“Until every one of those probes closes, no director with a fiduciary duty can vote to bring him back. Genius doesn’t buy you an exemption from national security.”

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120389.title: Gefährliche Fluchtroute | Rund 1500 Migranten erreichen die Kanaren
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120389.text:
- Politik
- Gefährliche Fluchtroute
Rund 1500 Migranten erreichen die Kanaren
Besonders betroffen ist die kleine Insel El Hierro. Die Hilfseinrichtungen stoßen dort an ihre Grenzen.
Madrid. Mehr als 1500 Menschen auf der Flucht sind am Wochenende auf den Kanarischen Inseln angekommen. Der Großteil der Migranten erreichte die kleine Insel El Hierro. Dort kamen allein am Samstag 13 Boote an. Am Sonntag erreichten mindestens vier weitere Boote die Insel; die Zahl ihrer Insassen war zunächst noch unklar.
Je ein weiteres Boot gelangte nach Gran Canaria und Teneriffa. Unter den rund 1500 Neuankömmlingen waren am Samstag mindestens 120 Minderjährige, berichtete der staatliche spanische TV-Sender RTVE unter Berufung auf die Behörden. Die Migranten stammen vor allem aus Senegal, Gambia, Mauretanien und Guinea. Die Überfahrt über den Atlantik kann – wenn alles gut geht – bis zu einer Woche dauern.
Derzeit ist die Lage vor allem auf El Hierro, einer Insel mit nur gut 12.000 Einwohnern, besonders angespannt. Seit Monatsanfang hatte El Hierro mehr als 9000 Migranten in 91 Booten empfangen. Die spanische Regierung hatte deshalb für die Kanaren bereits einen migrationspolitischen Notstand ausgerufen.
Der Präsident der Kanaren, Fernando Clavijo, forderte am Sonntag eine sofortige Umsetzung der mit Madrid vereinbarten Hilfszusagen. Dazu gehören zusätzliche Unterbringungsplätze, eine bessere medizinische Versorgung und schnellere Verlegungen von Migranten auf andere Inseln und das spanische Festland. Der Minister für Territorialpolitik, Ángel Víctor Torres, reiste unterdessen nach El Hierro, um sich ein Bild von der Lage zu machen.
Die Kanarenroute zählt zu den gefährlichsten Migrationswegen nach Europa. Nach Angaben der renommierten, in Afrika gut vernetzten spanischen Hilfsorganisation »Caminando Fronteras« kamen in den ersten fünf Monaten dieses Jahres mindestens 635 Menschen bei dem Versuch ums Leben, die Inselgruppe rund 100 Kilometer vor der Nordwestküste Afrikas zu erreichen.
Die Kanaren verzeichnen unter allen spanischen Regionen die meisten Ankünfte von Migranten. Allerdings war ihre Zahl zwischen Januar und Ende Oktober im Vergleich zum Vorjahreszeitraum um gut fünf Prozent auf 13.327 zurückgegangen, wie aus Zahlen des Innenministeriums hervorgeht. Den starken Anstieg der vergangenen Wochen führen spanische Medien auf die Verschärfung der sozialen und wirtschaftlichen Krise im Senegal zurück. dpa/nd
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.

Grève du 17 novembre, rentrée sociale et convergence des luttes | Entretien avec T. Vacheron (CGT)
Publié le 16 novembre 2026
Le printemps social va-t-il se poursuivre durant l'hiver ? Ce 17 novembre, l’ensemble des organisations syndicales de la fonction publique appellent à la grève pour dénoncer le gel de leurs rémunérations et exiger des moyens supplémentaires pour leurs missions, en plein débat budgétaire. Dans le privé, ils sont rejoints par l’UNSA, Solidaires et la CGT, alors que le coup de pouce du SMIC de 8 euros ne satisfait aucune des organisations syndicales.
Aux côtés de celles et ceux qui luttent !
L’urgence sociale, c’est chaque jour la priorité de l’Humanité.
- En exposant la violence patronale.
- En montrant ce que vivent celles et ceux qui travaillent et ceux qui aspirent à le faire.
- En donnant des clés de compréhension et des outils aux salarié.es pour se défendre contre les politiques ultralibérales qui dégradent leur qualité de vie.
Vous connaissez d’autres médias qui font ça ?  
Je veux en savoir plus !

https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.title: The hill I will die on: There is only one acceptable occasion on which to ghost someone – when you die | Temi Wilkey
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.author: Temi Wilkey
https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text:
Digitising our dating lives has conditioned us all away from human connection. I spend weeks of my life huffing and puffing to keep the balloon of flirty banter in the air – with a stranger I only find vaguely attractive. I go on dates with people who are “my type on paper” but upon meeting, find the paper much better than the person. I meet a woman with a devastating mouth and an even more devastating wit, only for her to ghost. The only acceptable reason to ghost someone is if you have, in fact, died.
Long ago, when Margaret Thatcher proclaimed “There is no such thing as society”, she wasn’t heralding an era of Tory rule that destroyed all public services that kept true community alive. No – she was prophesying 40 years into the future about the digital-age phenomenon of ghosting. The fact that this practice is widespread enough for there to be a word for it is proof of the long since disintegrated fabric of our society.
I think if you share any time or spit with someone, you should have the courage and common courtesy to let them know if you don’t fancy doing it again.
Back in the day – when you would meet potential partners through friends or extended community circles – dumping someone with neither word nor explanation would be unthinkable. You’d be shunned for barbarism. But so much of dating now is at a remove from our would-be communities, siloed away into these apps, so there is no one to hold us accountable. Late-stage capitalism has us all working so hard that it’s rare we make it out of the house or office to socialise. When we do, we’re less primed for chance encounters with new people because we’re busy focusing on the people we barely get to see.
Couple that with an app culture that filters out those who don’t meet our expected criteria and, of course, modern dating becomes less connected and more prejudiced (OkCupid stats show a majority of straight men exclude the option to date black women). We swipe and we judge. We lean into our biases and lean out of romantic risk.
A friend of mine swiped left to reject the man who is now her husband. On an app, his 2D profile fell flat. But when she later bumped into him in real life, she fell for the strange wonder of how his face moved. In the flesh, she saw his unique personal magic.
So, set your single friend up with another friend. Send them out on a date. Or go out dancing. Book a hall. Throw a party! If it isn’t affordable, let’s fight to make it affordable.
We need a renaissance of hall parties. Thrown for no reason. Other than our need to gather – in community, in our chosen villages – to satiate our desperate hunger for connection. Or, at least, to give us singletons a chance at the unsanitised magic of human partnership.
- Temi Wilkey is a writer, performer and star of the one-woman shows Main Character Energy and Lover Girl

Hamburger Bauruine : Neue Runde im Poker um den Elbtower
Die Verhandlungen über einen Einstieg der Stadt bei dem Prestigeprojekt ziehen sich seit Monaten hin. Jetzt droht die Baufirma ihre Kräne abzubauen.
D er Elbtower soll als eines der höchsten Häuser Deutschlands einmal weithin sichtbar das Entrée zur Hamburger Innenstadt markieren. Doch die Baustelle ruht, und vor wenigen Tagen hat die ausführende Baufirma Lupp dem Hamburger Senat die Pistole auf die Brust gesetzt. Sollten die Verhandlungen mit dem Hamburger Senat über eine Fertigstellung des Wolkenkratzers nicht vorankommen, würde der erste von mehreren Hochbaukränen abgebaut, die dort seit drei Jahren unproduktiv herumstehen und nur Geld kosten. „Stadt Hamburg, beweg dich! Sonst sind wir hier weg“, sagte Lupp-Geschäftsführer Thilo Moser der FAZ.
Die Baustelle an den Elbbrücken verdankt sich noch dem Immobilienzauberer René Benko, der sich im Zusammenhang mit seiner Insolvenz mehreren Gerichtsverfahren gegenüber sieht. Knapp 250 Meter hoch sollte der Elbtower werden. Inzwischen hat man sich mit dem Architekten David Chipperfield verständigt, das 200 Meter auch okay wären. 100 Meter stehen schon als Betongerippe.
Dieser Zustand ist natürlich etwas peinlich, weshalb der rot-grüne Senat vor gut einem Jahr angeboten hat, einem Investorenkonsortium um den Hamburger Immobilienunternehmer Dieter Becken unter die Arme zu greifen, das angeboten hat, das Hochhaus fertig zu bauen. Die Baufirma Lupp gehört zu dem Konsortium ebenso wie die Stiftung des verstorbenen Unternehmers Klaus-Michael Kühne, die Versicherung Signal-Iduna und der Unternehmer Dirk Rossmann.
wochentaz
Dieser Text erschien zuerst in der wochentaz, unserer Wochenzeitung von links!
In der wochentaz geht es jede Woche um die Welt, wie sie ist – und wie sie sein könnte. Eine linke Wochenzeitung mit Stimme, Haltung und dem besonderen taz-Blick auf die Welt. Jeden Samstag neu am Kiosk und natürlich im Abo.
Obwohl schon 350 Millionen Euro in den Rohbau geflossen sind, tut sich das Konsortium schwer, den Turm zu finanzieren. Die Stadt hat deshalb angeboten, die unteren zwölf Stockwerke für 595 Millionen Euro zu kaufen – allerdings erst nach Fertigstellung des Gebäudes. Auf keinen Fall will sie dafür ins Risiko gehen.
Nicht nochmal auf die Nase fallen
Letzteres ist ein Politikum, hatte der damalige Hamburger Bürgermeister Olaf Scholz (SPD) doch versprochen, kein Cent öffentlichen Geldes werde in das Projekt fließen. Der rot-grüne Senat rechtfertigt sein Angebot damit, dass er sich dem Land Nordrhein-Westfalen verpflichtet habe, ein Naturkundemuseum für das gemeinsame Leibniz-Institut zu errichten. Das sei im Elbtower machbar und 230 Millionen Euro billiger als ein eigener Neubau.
Finanzsenator Dressel sagte, die 595 Millionen Euro wären ein „Global-Pauschal-Festpreis“. Damit ist die Stadt bei der Elbphilharmonie schon einmal auf die Nase gefallen, weshalb sie jetzt alle möglichen Sicherungen einzubauen versucht: Rechtsanwälte, die die Transaktion prüfen, eine Risikobewertung sowie einen detaillierten Leistungskatalog.
Die Verhandlungen mit den Investoren macht das schwierig. Zuletzt hatten Vertreter der Regierungskoalition den Druck erhöht, indem sie die Beteiligung der Stadt infrage stellten, und ein Hamburger Immobilienunternehmen hat das Angebot gemacht, ein Museum für 100 Millionen Euro weniger in einem seiner Objekte unterzubringen.
„Wir wollen vermeiden, dass der Elbtower scheitert“, versicherte Lupp-Geschäftsführer Matthias Kaufmann der FAZ. Allerdings kosteten zwei Monate Stillstand auf der Baustelle fast eine halbe Million Euro. Und ohne die Lupp’sche Spezialtechnik könne das Haus nicht weitergebaut werden.
Hamburgs Bürgermeister Peter Tschentscher (SPD) sagte dem Fernsehsender RTL Nord, die Stadt lasse sich nicht unter Druck setzen: „Die privaten Investoren haben die Erwartungen der Stadt nicht so richtig ernst genommen, und das können wir nicht akzeptieren.“ Es gebe ja eine klare Kalkulation: „Wir wollen ein sehr gutes Naturkundemuseum, aber wir wollen es eben auch zu einem günstigen Preis, und dabei bleibt es.“

Lebanon’s second airport could provide economic and political benefits
The establishment of a second airport in Lebanon gives the war-devastated country more options for air travel.
Beirut, Lebanon – Lebanon’s second airport is scheduled to begin operating test flights on Independence Day, November 22, in what experts and analysts say could prove to be a boon to the country after years of war and an economic collapse.
In June, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and other officials took a test flight from Beirut to Rene Mouawad airport, located in the northern town of Qlayaat. Lebanese officials hope a new airport will stimulate growth in one of Lebanon’s poorest and most underserved regions.
Qlayaat airport was originally set to open mid-2026, but Israel’s war on Lebanon delayed it.
The beginning of commercial flights was deferred to November 22, but it was pushed further to mid-December, when many in the Lebanese diaspora return home for the winter holiday, due to construction delays. Commercial flights are now expected to start on December 14.
Chokepoint
Rafik Hariri international airport, Lebanon’s only functioning airport, located just south of the capital, Beirut, has been sensitive to political and regional disputes.
Supporters of Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed Shia armed group, have at times weaponised the vulnerabilities of Rafik Hariri airport’s location by blocking the road connecting it to the capital. In February 2025, Hezbollah supporters blocked the road when two Iranian planes were prohibited from landing in Beirut.
A new airport in the north, outside Hezbollah’s traditional zone of influence, could potentially weaken this logistical chokepoint, said Bassel Doueik, a Lebanese political analyst.
“Whenever tensions rise between them and the government, they [Hezbollah] tend to block the inbound and outbound [traffic] on the Beirut airport road through protests, and this is a strategic advantage for the group,” Doueik, a Lebanese political analyst, told Al Jazeera.
“I don’t think the new airport will remove this strategic advantage, but it will actually decrease it to a certain extent because the [Qlayaat] airport is small and it cannot substitute for the current airport.”
Hezbollah has been the strongest military and political actor in Lebanon in recent decades, but its role has come into open debate in the country following the 2024 ceasefire with Israel and the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in Syria, the group’s key regional ally.
The opening of a new airport is not expected to change internal political calculations, but analysts say it gives the state alternatives in the event of future conflicts.
“The state gains manoeuvrability and alternatives by opening a second airport. But in terms of Hezbollah’s arms or anything else, it doesn’t change much for the state,” Marcel Baloukji, a Lebanese political and security analyst, told Al Jazeera.
“This airport becomes a factor in any potential future war. Beirut airport could be shut down, but alternatives [to fly in and out] would still exist, especially for foreign nationals and diplomatic missions present in Lebanon.”
Economic troubles
But officials say the reason for opening a second airport is economic rather than political.
Lebanon’s economy has struggled to recover from the 2019 economic crash due to Israel’s ongoing assault on the country and the US-Israel war on Iran.
Inflation is expected to hit 17.5 percent this year, and the World Bank predicts Lebanon’s economy to contract by 6.4 percent in 2026. Previous estimates suggest Lebanon has suffered damage estimated at more than $14bn since 2023.
Still, Dania Arayssi, assistant director of the New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy, told Al Jazeera that she believes there is a legislative angle for the establishment of a new airport as well.
“Successfully managing a facility that can generate significant public revenue could help rebuild citizens’ trust in state institutions,” Arayssi said.
“It would show that the government can enforce its authority, protect public assets from Hezbollah’s interference, and lead on delivering services that benefit the country as a whole.”
South Lebanon, where an Israeli invasion has turned into an occupation that analysts believe could last years, has been the worst-affected part of the country as a result of Israel’s war. But other parts of Lebanon are also struggling and have a history of state neglect.
Qlayaat, on the other hand, is located in the northern Akkar region, just 6km (3.7 miles) from the Syrian border. Officials believe the new facility would serve much of Lebanon’s north, as well as important Syrian cities like Homs, Latakia and Tartous, with the northern neighbour struggling to modernise its dilapidated airports.
Experts told Al Jazeera that the fall of President al-Assad in December 2024 partially paved the way for the airport project, as Syria’s former government had been opposed to the idea.
After Salam formed the government in early 2025, plans for the new airport became a priority.
Officials said Qlayaat airport is likely to receive low-cost airlines. In June, Turkiye’s Istanbul and Mersin airports and Dubai in the UAE had been confirmed as destinations for flights from Qlayaat, with new locations likely to be announced in the coming days. Officials said the airport could serve 115,000 passengers in the first year, reaching about 600,000 by the fourth year.
Baloukji said the airport would also have domestic benefits and be a more reassuring route for foreign tourists.
“From the perspective of employing workers, it keeps people in that area and enhances tourism because many people are avoiding Beirut airport due to Hezbollah’s influence,” he said.

Industrie macht mehr Umsatz und baut dennoch Jobs ab
Die Wirtschaft in Deutschland erholt sich, etliche Branchen stehen wieder besser da. Der Arbeitsmarkt profitiert bisher nicht davon.
Hamburg. Die Industrie in Deutschland ist einer Untersuchung von EY zufolge wieder im Aufwind, baut aber dennoch weiter Stellen ab. »Im dritten Quartal setzten die Industrieunternehmen 546,3 Milliarden Euro um, 4,6 Prozent mehr als im Vorjahreszeitraum«, erklärte das Beratungsunternehmen am Montag. Das war der dritte Anstieg in Folge nach zuvor zehn negativen Quartalen. Doch: »Auf dem Arbeitsmarkt kommt von der Erholung nichts an – im Gegenteil.«
EY zufolge arbeiteten Ende September noch 5,3 Millionen Menschen in der deutschen Industrie – 2,6 Prozent weniger als ein Jahr zuvor. Seit 2019 gingen demnach 405.800 Arbeitsplätze verloren, ein Minus von 7,1 Prozent. »Etwa jeder vierzehnte Industriejob ist damit verschwunden.«
Bei der Umsatzentwicklung gibt es deutliche Unterschiede zwischen den Branchen. Während sich insbesondere der Bereich Metallerzeugung und -bearbeitung zuletzt stark im Aufwind befand (plus 19,5 Prozent) und auch die Elektroindustrie im dritten Quartal um 12,5 Prozent zulegte, stagnierten Maschinenbau und Papierindustrie. Chemie- und Pharmaunternehmen setzten 5,6 Prozent mehr um, Textil- und Autoindustrie jeweils etwas weniger als im Vorjahr.
Den Zuwachs bestimmter Branchen führen die Experten vor allem auf den Rechenzentrumsboom und die militärische Aufrüstung zurück. »Der Bau von Rechenzentren für Künstliche Intelligenz sorgt weltweit für eine enorme Nachfrage nach Stromtechnik, Kühlsystemen, Kabeln und Metall«, erklärte Jan Brorhilker von EY. »Hinzu kommen die milliardenschweren Investitionsprogramme der Bundesregierung, allen voran für die Verteidigung.«
»Bei der Beschäftigung ist das Bild dagegen einheitlich: In allen untersuchten Branchen arbeiten weniger Menschen als vor einem Jahr«, erklärte EY. »Am geringsten fiel der Stellenabbau mit einem Rückgang um 1,8 Prozent in der Elektroindustrie aus.«
»Die Industrie hat beim Umsatz wieder etwas Boden unter den Füßen«, resümierte Brorhilker. »Aber wir reden über eine leichte Erholung von niedrigem Niveau aus, nicht über einen breiten Aufschwung.« Deshalb gebe es bei der Beschäftigung keine Trendwende. AFP/nd
Kein Milliardär im Rücken
Andere Medien haben Konzerne oder Milliardäre im Rücken. Wir haben die nd.Genossenschaft und Leser*innen wie dich. Das macht uns unabhängig und genau das wollen wir bleiben. Aber es heißt auch: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.

Jordan bans Telegram, accusing it of promoting 'extremism'
16 November 2026 10:04 GMT
Jordan announced a ban on the Telegram network on Monday, accusing it of contributing to the spread of "extremism" within the kingdom.
"We are announcing the blocking of the Telegram application as part of efforts to strengthen digital security and protect users," the Public Security Directorate stated in a press release.
The move is intended to prevent "cybercrimes, threats, blackmail, and the dissemination of illegal content", as well as to counter "any attempt to spread radicalisation and extremism".

https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.title: Cop31 live: diplomats divided as climate crisis talks enter second week
https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.author: Ajit Niranjan
https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text:
Deep divides as second week of talks begin
It is a measure of how difficult a battle the Australian presidency of negotiations and the Turkish hosts of the conference face at Cop31 that, as the second week of talks begins, there are still deep divides not only as to what the outcome of this Cop should be, but even over what form it should take.
Deep into Saturday night, ahead of the official rest day on Sunday, negotiators from around the world were still slugging it out over whether this Cop should have a “cover decision”.
As regular readers of this blog will know, cover decisions are a standard feature of Cops, and have been for more than two decades. They function as a useful negotiating device to capture progress made in the talks that does not fall neatly into the other negotiating strands, such as those on the mitigation work programme (on reductions in greenhouse gas emissions) or on finance.
This has rarely been controversial – cover decisions have included a wide variety of issues that are important without fitting neatly within the other “work programmes”, and have included the state of the oceans, the impact of the climate crisis on food security and health, new science, and clarifications of the outcome of Cop discussions.
One long time Cop participant told the Guardian: “Optimally all items would find a space in the negotiated decisions. If that is not possible, then there has to be enough political goodwill and diplomacy to carry off an ambitious cover decision.”
But after Cop28 in 2023 in Dubai produced a cover decision whose 28th paragraph included the key pledge to “transition away from fossil fuels”, some countries took a harder line. At Cop29 in Baku, the Azerbaijani hosts complied with the wishes of regional allies and announced there would be no cover decision. This stifled further discussion of the “transition away from fossil fuels”, as it could not be incorporated easily into other negotiating strands.
The following year, in Belem, the Brazilian hosts reinstated a cover decision, which allowed for a reference to the Dubai decision (the “UAE consensus”) to be included.
This year, the best way to take forward issues including Brazil’s global roadmap on the transition away from fossil fuels, the global electrification target, and the controversy over whether the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change should be delayed, would be a cover decision.
But the Arab Group, Russia, and the Like-Minded Developing Countries (a loose grouping that sometimes includes China and India, but also Saudi Arabia and allies among fossil fuel producers such as Bolivia and Venezuela) are opposed to having any form of cover decision at this year’s Cop. They are claiming there is no legal basis within the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change for having a cover decision, which is an odd stance for countries that have signed up to so many of them over the years.
The row is likely to continue, and could hold up progress in the talks. It is seen by some as a sign of how the absence of the US has affected the talks, as under Joe Biden and Barack Obama, US negotiating teams were known to some as the “Saudi whisperers”.
With the world leaders gone, the negotiations will now hinge on whether countries can find common ground. Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the UNFCCC, called for flexibility in their positions: “There is no collective success without compromise from every party.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?
The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command area of responsibility.
The United States has deployed a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East as diplomatic efforts to permanently stop the US-Israel war on Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled.
On Monday, a US official told Al Jazeera that the USS Theodore Roosevelt had arrived in the Middle East. The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility.
The United States and Iran entered into a two-week ceasefire in April and later announced a broader memorandum of understanding in June, which collapsed in early July.
Since then, mediators from Pakistan and Qatar have been trying to prevent a return to the full-scale exchange of attacks between the US and Iran that also badly affected the broader Gulf region in March.
Last week, US President Donald Trump stated that further military strikes against Iran are “quite unlikely” and said the military component of the war was “effectively over” following discussions with Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani. But he noted the US military remains “locked and loaded” if conditions change.
Does the deployment of another aircraft carrier to the region mean the US-Israel war on Iran is going to resume?
Here’s what we know:
What is the USS Theodore Roosevelt?
Named after the 26th US president, Theodore Roosevelt, the vessel is a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.
Commissioned by the US Navy in 1986, the ship carries more than 5,000 personnel and a full air wing of more than 60 aircraft, including F-18s, the twin-engine, supersonic, all-weather multirole fighter planes.
According to the US Navy, the warship is tasked with “conducting carrier air warfare operations and assisting in the planning, control, coordination and integration of air wing squadrons in support of carrier air warfare”.
Besides combat operations, the carrier also replenishes ships at sea and rescues people, including refugees, at sea.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt has performed combat and humanitarian missions since its commissioning. During the 1990-91 Gulf War, it was deployed to the Mediterranean and the Red Sea for combat operations. In 2003, it also supported US strikes during the Iraq War.
It was also deployed in the Asia Pacific region during 2020-21 for military exercises with India, Japan, Australia, South Korea and Malaysia.
In October, a US official told Al Jazeera that the USS Theodore Roosevelt left its San Diego base in September, bound for the Middle East. According to another official, it arrived in the Middle East on November 15.
But the Pentagon and CENTCOM, which oversees military operations in the Middle East, have not formally confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region.
What is the state of US deployment in the region?
The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East brings the total number of US aircraft carrier strike groups operating in the region to three. The USS George Washington and the USS George HW Bush are the other two aircraft carriers currently deployed in the region.
Last month, a US official told Al Jazeera that the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group (ARG), carrying more than 2,000 Marines, has also followed the USS Theodore Roosevelt to the Middle East. The Wall Street Journal reported that the strike group and naval deployments could involve an additional 9,000 to 10,000 US soldiers in total, including sailors and Marines assigned to the carrier strike group and other ships. However, the US military is yet to confirm these deployments.
The US has had troops and military assets stationed at bases in the Middle East for decades. Of these, eight are permanent bases, located in Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. As of mid-2025, there were 40,000 to 50,000 US soldiers stationed in and around the Middle East, including personnel at large, permanent bases and smaller forward sites across the region.
According to open-source intelligence analysts and military flight-tracking data, the US has deployed more than 120 aircraft to the region since early February, before the war on Iran began. This is the biggest surge in US airpower in the Middle East since the Iraq War.
Reported deployments include E-3 Sentry Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft, F-35 stealth strike fighters and F-22 air superiority jets alongside F-15s and F-16s. In March, the Pentagon also ordered additional US forces to the Gulf.
The reinforcements consisted of three distinct formations.
The first was the Tripoli ARG, centred around the America-class assault ship USS Tripoli and the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit (MEU).
The second was the Boxer ARG, built around the Wasp-class assault ship USS Boxer and the 11th MEU, based in southern California in the US.
Together, these two Marine groups have added 4,500 Marines and sailors in the region.
The third was a contingent of about 2,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division’s Immediate Response Force, based at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The airborne infantry division is focused on parachute assaults.
In total, nearly 7,000 additional soldiers have already been deployed to the Middle East since the US-Israel war on Iran began.
How has Iran responded?
Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, has said the country “will not wait for the US to attack first”. He said, “The US may be seeking to buy time by abusing diplomacy, in order to prepare the ground for another attack.”
Speaking to state TV in a video released by Iran’s Fars news agency, Gharibabadi warned, “Iran is not Cuba that you can blockade, nor is it Venezuela that you can force to surrender.”
He said US forces “have had no success with either an air blockade or a land blockade” in Iran so far, while the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) is currently producing missiles with “new ranges”.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has called for stronger regional energy cooperation, warning US attacks threaten stability across the Middle East.
“Given the increasing impact of US and Israeli aggression on the region’s energy security, strengthening energy cooperation has become an urgent and strategic necessity,” Araghchi said at a meeting of foreign ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization in Islamabad, Pakistan, on Monday.
“Our region needs not only an independent security framework but also a regional, reliable and sustainable energy mechanism to safeguard energy flows, ensure stable energy supplies, reduce vulnerabilities from external factors, and increase our collective resilience to geopolitical shocks and disruptions,” the IRNA news agency quoted him as saying.
What has the US government said on resuming the war?
The Trump administration has appeared increasingly divided on how to proceed with Iran, since the Republican Party suffered heavy losses in this month’s US midterm elections.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said Washington’s economic pressure campaign against Iran was proving effective, so a resumption of large-scale military operations was likely unnecessary. “The economic pressure on Iran is going to get even worse,” he added.
But Trump has given mixed messages about his plans for the war.
Last week, after a meeting at the White House’s Oval Office with Qatar’s prime minister, Trump stated on Truth Social and in a surprise briefing that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict and that a resumption of strikes was “quite unlikely”, declaring the US-Israel war on Iran militarily “effectively over”.
Still, Trump insisted that the US economic pressure campaign against Iran would stay in place, including a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and a more recent task force aimed at cutting off Iran’s trade by land and through the Caspian Sea.
Meanwhile, Iran’s conditions to end the war include an end to the US naval blockade of Iran’s ports, the lifting of economic sanctions, the release of Iranian frozen funds, ending fighting on all fronts and an explicit announcement of an end to the war.
Iranian officials have in recent days underlined that Tehran will not accept the current status quo of “no war, no peace”.
Trump, on his part, has indicated that he is running out of patience with Iran as diplomacy stutters. Last week, Trump said he had told his country’s lead negotiator, Vice President JD Vance, “We don’t need a deal with Iran.”
“Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” he wrote on his Truth Social platform.
So can diplomacy work, or is the region on edge?
Ali Vaez, Crisis Group’s Deputy Program Director for the Middle East and North Africa told Al Jazeera that both sides are caught in a perilous game of chicken, convinced that striking first may be safer than waiting to be struck.
“The danger is that their efforts to deter another war could inadvertently ignite one that neither can win, contain or easily end,” he said.
Diplomatic efforts to stop attacks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz also remain stalled.
In an interview with Al Jazeera last week, Iran’s parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, highlighted that Tehran wanted to move beyond a state of “no war, no peace”.
Ghalibaf said Iran has conveyed seven conditions for a deal through a Qatari mediator and was awaiting an official US response. The conditions he outlined included lifting the US naval blockade and sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian funds, ending hostilities on all fronts and formally declaring the war over.
Trump’s administration, meanwhile, has tightened sanctions and maintained the blockade on Iranian ports.
“Diplomacy still has a pulse, but it is suffocating under the weight of mutual mistrust and maximalist demands. Unless both sides find a face-saving exit, negotiations risk becoming little more than an intermission between successive rounds of warfare,” Vaez said.
The main issues in the US-Israel war on Iran now are those of sequencing and leverage, according to Rashid al-Mohanadi, vice president at the Center for International Policy Research. “Who does what, when, and how for a potential end of the conflict,” he told Al Jazeera on Sunday.
Al-Mohanadi added that it is clear that the region is against going back to full-scale war, which is obvious as “the whole region is leading on the mediation”.
However, he warned, the principal protagonists in the war appear to have divergent perceptions over their leverage.
“The Iranians perceive they have more leverage. The Americans perceive they have more,” al-Mohanadi said. “When you have a situation like that, reaching a diplomatic end is quite difficult.”

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120389.title: Vor Parteitag | Gründungsmitglieder des BSW fordern Distanz zur AfD
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120389.text:
- Politik
- Vor Parteitag
Gründungsmitglieder des BSW fordern Distanz zur AfD
Nach der Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt hat das BSW mehrfach mit der AfD gestimmt. In den Reihen der Partei wächst die Sorge vor einem Ruck nach rechts.
Berlin. Führende BSW-Politiker fordern von ihrer Partei klare Distanz zur AfD. Das BSW solle nicht nur Koalitionen mit der AfD ausschließen, sondern auch »eine formelle oder faktische Tolerierung, eine Stützung einer AfD-geführten Regierung und auf Dauer angelegte Absprachen zur Zusammenarbeit«, heißt es in einem Papier mehrerer Vorstandsmitglieder zum Dresdner Parteitag Ende November.
Hintergrund ist die parlamentarische Zusammenarbeit von BSW und AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt. Das BSW will zwar keine Koalition und will den AfD-Kandidaten Ulrich Siegmund auch nicht zum Ministerpräsidenten wählen, stimmte aber unter anderem mit der AfD gegen weitere Ukraine-Hilfen. Es laufen Gespräche über Inhalte, die eine AfD-geführte Minderheitsregierung umsetzen müsste. Die AfD hat vorgeschlagen, dies schriftlich zu regeln.
Kommission für »Magdeburger Weg«
Die BSW-Grundwertekommission unter dem Vorsitz von Parteigründerin Sahra Wagenknecht stellt sich hinter den sogenannten »Magdeburger Weg«. Mehrheiten sollten bei Sachthemen auch durch gemeinsame Anträge genutzt werden, heißt es in einem Positionspapier. Der gemeinsame Ukraine-Antrag sei »ein gelungenes Vorbild«. Und: »Eine punktuelle Übereinstimmung bedeutet weder eine gemeinsame politische Grundlage noch eine politische Annäherung.«
Die BSW-Spitze hält auch im Leitantrag zum Dresdner Parteitag fest: »Wenn es eine Mehrheit für Frieden in der Ukraine, die Wiederinbetriebnahme von Nord Stream oder für kostenloses Mittagessen in Kitas und Schulen gibt, werden wir sie durchsetzen, unabhängig davon, wer Teil dieser Mehrheit ist.« Koalitionen mit der AfD schließt diese offizielle Vorlage jedoch abermals aus.
Trotzdem wollen nun führende Köpfe der Partei eine Klarstellung per Änderungsantrag. »Die AfD ist ebenso der politische Gegner des BSW wie die regierenden Parteien der ›Mitte‹«, heißt es darin. Beide Lager stünden für Aufrüstung, Sozialabbau, die »Begünstigung der Superreichen« und einen Rechtskurs. »Die AfD, die diesen Kurs noch verstärken wird, kann kein Partner für das BSW sein.« Insbesondere sei die AfD keine Friedenspartei. Wagenknecht selbst habe 2023 angekündigt, keine »gemeinsame Sache mit der AfD« zu machen.
Millionenspender unterstützt Bedenken
Hinter dem Änderungsantrag stehen die stellvertretenden BSW-Vorsitzenden Christian Leye, Amid Rabieh, Ralph Suikat und Jessica Tatti sowie die Vorstandsmitglieder Sevim Dağdelen , Klaus Ernst und Ralf Krämer. Darunter stehen Dutzende Unterstützer. Die meisten Initiatoren waren früher in der Linken. In ihren Reihen gibt es Bedenken, dass das BSW nach rechts driften könnte. Zu den Unterzeichnern des Antrags zählt auch der Unternehmer Thomas Stanger, der dem BSW mehrfach Millionenbeträge gespendet hat.
Die Partei war Anfang 2024 als Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht gegründet worden. Inzwischen hat sich Wagenknecht vom Parteivorsitz zurückgezogen, das Kürzel BSW steht nun für Bündnis soziale Gerechtigkeit und wirtschaftliche Vernunft. Anders als in Sachsen-Anhalt hat die Partei in Berlin und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Wahlniederlagen eingesteckt. In mehreren Landesverbänden gab es Streit, in Thüringen eine Spaltung.
Wichtig für die Zukunft der Partei wird der für Mittwoch erwartete Spruch des Bundesverfassungsgerichts im Streit über das BSW-Ergebnis bei der Bundestagswahl. Das BSW war mit 4,981 Prozent der Zweitstimmen haarscharf an der Fünf-Prozent-Hürde gescheitert. Die Partei geht von Zählfehlern aus und nimmt an, dass sie eigentlich mit 35 Abgeordneten im Parlament sitzen müsste. In dem Fall hätte die jetzige schwarz-rote Koalition allein keine Mehrheit. dpa/nd
Kein Milliardär im Rücken
Andere Medien haben Konzerne oder Milliardäre im Rücken. Wir haben die nd.Genossenschaft und Leser*innen wie dich. Das macht uns unabhängig und genau das wollen wir bleiben. Aber es heißt auch: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.

Un agent de la police municipale de Choisy-le-Roi a été interpellé, samedi 14 novembre, après avoir menacé de tuer des personnes en raison de leur couleur de peau. Le mis en cause a depuis été placé en garde à vue. De quoi mettre en alerte les élus d’opposition, trois semaines après l’attentat raciste de Trappes, qui comptent demander une enquête approfondie au maire.
Près de trois semaines après l’attentat raciste qui a endeuillé Trappes, un policier municipal a assumé vouloir tuer « des gens de couleur ». L’agent a été interpellé samedi 14 novembre, en fin de matinée, au sein de son appartement situé dans le 16e arrondissement de Paris.
Les autorités ont été prévenues, vers 9 heures, qu’un individu « très agressif » déambulait dans la cour de sa résidence, située rue...

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Robert Tait in Washington
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.
The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand, push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.
He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
White House officials said the president would be accompanied to Apec by Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX entrepreneur who spent almost $500m (£380m) unsuccessfully supporting Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.
The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from the Nvidia spying scandal, which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.
The US president has said he does not plan to bring up the subject; administration officials insist he will not do so and that the meeting will be dedicated to implementing a trade agreement between the two superpowers.
Huang persuaded the Trump administration to lift restrictions on the sale of Nvidia’s AI chips to China that had been imposed during Joe Biden’s presidency.
Mao Ning, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, told reporters on Monday that at the trilateral summit, Xi, Trump and Putin “will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance”.
Some analysts have characterised the meeting as a “big three” gathering echoing the 1945 Yalta meeting of Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin that in effect carved up postwar Europe, between a communist-ruled east and a democratic, capitalist west.
Such a prospect has alarmed Ukraine, which fears that Putin – who initially suggested the trilateral meeting – will use it to persuade Trump and Xi to agree to a settlement of the war with Russia on Moscow’s terms.
However, Trump has said Ukraine will not be up for debate at the meeting and that its main purpose will be to discuss ending the US’s war with Iran and “denuclearisation” – shorthand for a deal among the three powers to limit nuclear arms.
That is believed to be unpalatable to China, which has been increasing its nuclear arsenal, and has signalled an unwillingness to enter into reduction agreements until it is closer to parity with the US and Russia.
Analysts say the main beneficiary of the three-way meeting is likely to be Putin, whose standing will be boosted by being treated on an equal footing by two other leaders whose countries are, in reality, much more powerful.
Expectations of a substantial agreement are low.
Lyle Goldstein, an international affairs fellow and China specialist at Brown University in the US, said the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting would not have a substantive result. “There will be no ‘Yalta’, as many have feared,” he said.
Jonathan Czin, the Michael Armacost chair in foreign policy studies at the Brookings Institution, said Trump’s lame duck status would deter Xi and Putin from trying to reach long-term arrangements with the US.
“Both men know Trump’s time is expiring even more quickly than his leverage – and that he will be irrelevant in a mere 26 months [when his term expires],” Czin told an online Brookings forum. “Why would either man make a deal with a leader whose time and leverage are waning? They will only do it if they think they can pilfer more from Trump diplomatically than they will be able to gain from the next American president.”
Nevertheless, Goldstein – who took soundings on Chinese expectations for the summit in a visit to Shenzhen last week – predicted Trump would follow the pattern of previous presidents by turning increasingly to global affairs while he faces the prospect of his influence on the domestic front being curtailed after the Democrats’ victories in the House of Representatives and the Senate.
“The president has been badly damaged by the election and will have limited prospects for the next two years,” he said. “That may cause him to be more active in foreign policy since he can act in that domain with fewer constraints. It would not surprise me if Trump is ready to go all-out to make some further splash in foreign policy.”
With the risks of reigniting the war with Iran high and the Russia-Ukraine war still resistant to a diplomatic resolution despite White House efforts, Goldstein suggested Trump could attempt “a dramatic foreign policy flourish in Asia”, such as an agreement with Kim Jong-un, the North Korean dictator with whom he has frequently boasted of having a close relationship. Kim is not expected to attend the Apec gathering, although there have been rumours he may appear.

https://taz.de/Depardieu-nimmt-Berufung-.title: Französische Filmlegende: Depardieu nimmt Berufung im Belästigungsprozess zurück
https://taz.de/Depardieu-nimmt-Berufung-.text:
Französische Filmlegende: Depardieu nimmt Berufung im Belästigungsprozess zurück
Eigentlich wollte Schauspieler Gérard Depardieu gegen eine Verurteilung wegen sexueller Übergriffe kämpfen. Nun macht er überraschend einen Rückzieher.
dpa | Der französische Schauspielstar Gérard Depardieu will überraschend nicht mehr gegen seine Verurteilung wegen sexueller Übergriffe ankämpfen. Die Anwälte des 77-Jährigen bestätigten zu Beginn des Verfahrens vor dem Pariser Berufungsgericht, dass der Darsteller von der Berufung zurücktrete. Auch die Staatsanwaltschaft zog daraufhin ihre Berufung zurück. Das Urteil aus erster Instanz – 18 Monate Haft auf Bewährung wegen Übergriffen auf zwei Frauen bei Dreharbeiten – wird damit rechtskräftig. Depardieu selbst war vor Gericht nicht anwesend.
In einer durch seine Anwälte verbreiteten Mitteilung entschuldigte sich Depardieu für von ihm begangene Verletzungen. „Ich wurde für schuldig befunden. Ich verstehe dies und akzeptiere diese Verurteilung“, teilte der 77-Jährige mit. „Ich entschuldige mich daher tiefsinnig und aufrichtig bei all jenen, die darunter haben leiden können.“ Er habe sich am Set oft hinter Provokation und Anzüglichkeit versteckt. Er habe geglaubt, dass seine Worte und einige seiner Gesten ohne Konsequenzen seien. „Sie waren es nicht, besonders von einer machtvollen Person kommend, wie ich sie gewesen sein mag.“
„Ich verstehe fortan, dass es eine Grenze zwischen Unverschämtheit und Verletzung gibt“, führte der Schauspieler fort. „Ich hatte nie, nie die Intention, die Frauen, die mir begegnet sind, zu verletzen. Aber ich verstehe, dass die Intention nichts an der Verletzung ändert.“ Und weiter: „Prozesse vor den Gerichten strapazieren uns“, schrieb Depardieu. Ihm sei alles entgleitet, vor allem seine Verteidigung. Der Vorfall habe viel Leid angerichtet. Er könne die Zeit nicht zurückdrehen, aber trete von seiner Berufung zurück.
Depardieu hatte Belästigung vor Gericht zuvor bestritten
Eine Dekorateurin und eine Regieassistentin hatten Depardieu beschuldigt, sie bei Arbeiten zum Film „Les volets verts“ (Die grünen Fensterläden) von Regisseur Jean Becker 2021 an den Brüsten und am Po begrapscht zu haben. Auch soll der berühmte Darsteller sie obszön angesprochen haben.
In erster Instanz hatte Depardieu vor Gericht bestritten, die beiden Frauen sexuell belästigt zu haben. Im Fall der Ausstatterin räumte er ein, sie an den Hüften berührt zu haben – betonte jedoch, dies sei nicht sexuell motiviert gewesen.
Die Staatsanwaltschaft hatte die Übergriffe in erster Instanz als vorsätzlich eingestuft. Das Gericht verurteilte Depardieu neben der Bewährungsstrafe zu Geldzahlungen an die beiden Frauen. Auch solle er in ein Register mit Sexualstraftätern aufgenommen werden.
Vorwürfe gegen Depardieu mehren sich seit Jahren
Bereits seit Jahren häufen sich Anschuldigungen sexueller Übergriffe gegen die französische Filmikone. Erst vergangene Woche hatten Medien neue Details zu Vorwürfen publik gemacht. Depardieu hatte bisher die Vorwürfe abgestritten.
Der preisgekrönte Schauspieler hat in mehr als 200 Filmen gespielt, viele sind zu Klassikern des Kinos geworden, wie „Cyrano von Bergerac“, „Asterix und Obelix“ und „Die letzte Metro“. Wegen der Vielzahl an Anschuldigungen sowie missbilligender Äußerungen ist er in Frankreich mittlerweile zur äußerst umstrittenen Figur geworden.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Jordan bans Telegram over national security concerns
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Jordan bans Telegram over national security concerns
Authorities say measure is part of ongoing efforts to reduce cybercrime and strengthen digital security.
Jordanian authorities have banned the Telegram messaging app, saying the move aims to curb the dissemination of illegal content and what they describe as “extremist material”.
The Public Security Directorate (PSD) announced the measure in a statement published on Monday amid a security crackdown after nine people were killed in an attack on a Greek Orthodox church last month.
The PSD urged citizens to “exercise caution when using social media applications, to avoid interacting with accounts, links, or entities of unknown origin, and to report any unlawful practices or content through official channels”.
The church shooting took place in the village of Hammoud in the west-central governorate of Karak. On Sunday, three men were sentenced to death by hanging over the attack.
The incident prompted Jordan to carry out air strikes on neighbouring Syria that Amman said killed 20 members of the ISIL (ISIS) armed group linked to the church attack.
Meanwhile, a security officer was killed and another wounded this month in Amman in what authorities described as another “terrorist attack”.
Telegram, founded by Russian entrepreneur Pavel Durov in 2013, is believed to be used by groups such as ISIL. In July, Russia issued an arrest warrant for Durov, accusing him of aiding “terrorism”.
The 42-year-old is currently believed to be in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates and faces up to life in a Russian prison if found guilty. He is also being investigated in several other countries.
Telegram supports end-to-end encrypted chats, but not all conversations are encrypted. The messaging app is popular in the Middle East and North Africa. The region accounts for about 8 percent of global users.
