https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: FBI raids and a recycling firm: how a promising US mayor wound up at the center of a bribery scandal
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Robin Buller in Oakland
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Two years ago, residents of Oakland, California, woke up to a shocking scene: their mayor’s home was being raided by the FBI. Agents were seen carrying dozens of boxes from the hilltop home of Sheng Thao, the city’s 38-year-old leader, as part of an investigation constituents would later learn alleged her participation in a pay-to-play scheme with the city’s recycling contractor.
It was a stunning moment for Thao, who was elected to lead the Bay Area city in 2022 and was once seen as a promising young mayor in a city that has long grappled with economic inequality and a reputation for violent crime. Her story of growing up in a refugee family and overcoming domestic violence and homelessness to become the first person of Hmong descent to run a major US city resonated with readers confronting questions about equity and representation that came to the fore during the Covid-19 pandemic, and made her the subject of glowing media profiles.
As mayor, Thao revived the city’s Ceasefire violence-reduction strategy and brought in a much-needed infusion of revenue through the sale of the Oakland Coliseum sports complex. But her tenure was far from smooth. At the time of the raid she was already facing a heated recall campaign grounded in her perceived failure to address the city’s mounting public safety and homelessness crises – one that would see her ousted from office in November 2024. Two months later, Thao was indicted on federal corruption charges, and eventually replaced by longtime progressive congresswoman Barbara Lee in a special election.
Now, Oakland is anxiously watching the final chapter in this political drama unfold as Thao and three co-defendents stand trial over the alleged bribery scheme. Having just concluded its fifth week of hearings, the case is rich with soap-opera-esque plot points, from an alleged beating at a recycling company’s headquarters to text threads in which co-defendants celebrated the plot that would make them “$100 million dollars richer” and touted that “money buys everything”.
Proceedings are expected to conclude later this month, with Thao facing six federal counts in total. If found guilty, she could face up to 20 years in prison. To the frustration of other witnesses, Thao, who has a constitutional right not to testify, has yet to take the stand.
The saga has left residents disappointed and reopened longstanding frustrations about a city that has everything it needs to thrive – a prime location on the bay, a diverse population, a burgeoning arts and culture scene, and a growing economy – but a government that struggles to deliver basic services or answer for its shortcomings.
“When the news [of the FBI raids] broke, there was a wide range of feelings from the community,” said Stephanie Tran, president of the Oakland Chinatown chamber of commerce, of the fall from grace of a mayor who offered representation to Oakland’s sizeable Asian-American community. “Many were, quite honestly, just disappointed, even sad,” she said, that an Asian woman in such a high position of power was now associated with this controversy.
‘People moved on’
The bribery, conspiracy and fraud charges against Thao rest on claims that during her 2022 campaign, David and Andy Duong – a father and son whose family runs California Waste Solutions, the company that provides Oakland’s recycling services – paid for negative mailers attacking her rivals and promised her romantic partner, Andre Jones, a $300,000 no-show job. In exchange, prosecutors allege, Thao promised to extend the company’s multi-million-dollar city contract, appoint the Duongs’ preferred people to important municipal positions, and buy shipping containers converted into homes for unhoused people from a company the Duongs ran with a business partner.
All four defendants have pleaded not guilty, with their lawyers denying the existence of any bribery scheme. Thao’s legal team did not respond to the Guardian’s request for comment.
Darwin BondGraham, news editor at local non-profit media outlet The Oaklandside, said the courthouse has been frequented by members of Oakland’s political class. But when it comes to everyday Oaklanders, many just want the mess behind them. “The trial is accounting for things that happened when Oakland bottomed out during the first few years of the pandemic,” BondGraham said. “I think people moved on.”
What many want is simple: a City Hall that fixes the potholes, answers 911 calls and acts with accountability. But in Oakland – which has faced recurring budget deficits for decades, leading to substantial staffing shortages and hundreds of millions in deferred maintenance – these basic services are not a given.
Those are the sorts of core concerns that pushed Emily Wasserman, a mother of two living in the city’s Laurel neighborhood, toward local advocacy. In 2024, Wasserman was ready for change. Thao had been her councilperson for several years, and Wasserman found her ineffective. So she started volunteering with a voter education group, Empower Oakland, founded by Thao’s main rival in the 2022 election, Loren Taylor.
Part of the alleged bribery scheme involves the co-conspirators sending out campaign mailers critical of Taylor in exchange for favors from Thao.
While Oakland’s problems didn’t start with Thao, the failures of successive governments to address them came to a head during her post-Covid leadership. A recent report found that illegal dumping cost the city $10m more than it did a decade ago. Police responses to the most urgent calls averaged 23 minutes in 2022 and at times stretched past an hour in 2023, yet a city audit last year found Oakland has no targets for how quickly officers should respond.
To Wasserman, the city’s shortcomings – and the allegations against Thao – speak to structural problems with how Oakland is governed. “One of the things that bothers me the most in our government is that there is not a lot of accountability to the general public,” she said.
It isn’t for a lack of ideas, said Lakisha Young, founder and CEO of education non-profit The Oakland Reach. “Our city is inundated with initiatives,” she said, pointing to the many literacy, violence prevention, and affordable housing programs Oakland has approved in recent years – but that lack any formal infrastructure for tracking results. “It makes you feel like things are happening, but there is never any follow-through.”
She says that if the city is serious about tackling some of its most intractable problems, like public school testing scores and children’s literacy rates, it needs to ensure that earmarked funds are used meaningfully and with oversight.
“Every year our kids are behind in the same way they were behind when we had 60% less resources because we are not building an ecosystem that is accountable to measuring its results,” Young said. “When people are held accountable, different things happen.”
Oakland’s challenges ‘don’t begin and end with this trial’
In recent days, the trial has centered on testimonies from Mario Juarez, an alleged co-conspirator in both the bribery and mailer scandals who is cooperating with government prosecutors.
Juarez claimed that shady dealings between the Duongs and city government predate Thao’s term. He alleged that in 2014, after securing Oakland’s $300m recycling contract, the Duongs gave gym bags full of cash to a revolving door of city officials, including a “sitting” councilmember.
The defense has raised questions about Juarez’s credibility, suggesting that he artificially inflated expense reports and travel receipts submitted to the Duongs, and it is unclear whether Juarez will name any officials alleged to have accepted bribes. Nonetheless, his claims echo a sentiment held by many Oaklanders and articulated by Chinatown’s Tran: “The challenges that Oakland has, quite candidly, didn’t begin with this trial, and they won’t end when it’s over.”
On 3 November, voters passed a charter reform that takes aim at some of those challenges. Known as the “strong mayor” reform, Measure EE amends the city’s governance structure – which has historically been ambiguous about whether ownership for key decisions lies with the city council or the mayor – by placing clear accountability on the leader’s shoulders. Going forward, the mayor will function as the city’s chief executive, with hiring and firing privileges as well as legislative and budgetary veto power.
Supporters see it as an important step toward building accountability back into the city’s governance structure.
“This will help to set the stage to address some of the longstanding challenges of how we can govern and work as a city,” echoed Wasserman.
Others, like district 4 councilperson Janani Ramachandran, are less exuberant about the measure, especially in the aftermath of Thao’s indictment. “I think that the unpredictability of who Oakland might vote in as mayor is a little scary,” she said. “You can swing from someone as wildly incompetent as Sheng Thao to someone as professional and experienced as [current mayor] Barbara Lee.”
For Tash Nguyen, executive director of economic equity non-profit Restore Oakland, the city’s future success rests more with the hands of its people than its politicians. To her, the political scandals matter less than the solidarity she has seen among Oakland’s residents in the past year, from forming ICE patrols to combat the federal immigration crackdown, to creating tenant unions to defend their homes against profit-driven rent surges.
“Folks are showing up for each other. That’s what makes Oakland so special,” she said. “People outside of Oakland don’t know about that.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Israel mata comandante do Hamas em ataque aéreo no sul de Gaza
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Renato Santana
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
As Forças de Defesa de Israel (IDF) anunciaram, neste domingo (15), a morte de Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, comandante da Brigada de Rafah, um dos braços militares do Hamas, em um ataque aéreo realizado na noite de sábado (14), na região de Al-Mawasi, a oeste de Khan Yunis, no sul da Faixa de Gaza.
A operação foi conduzida conjuntamente pelo Exército israelense e pelo serviço de inteligência interna Shin Bet. Em comunicado, as duas instituições afirmaram que Abu Younis era uma das principais lideranças militares do Hamas e que havia assumido o comando da Brigada de Rafah aproximadamente dois meses antes, depois da morte de seu antecessor, Nael Abu Obeid, em um ataque israelense em 15 de setembro.
Segundo o Exército israelense, Abu Younis também havia ocupado os cargos de vice-comandante da Brigada de Rafah e comandante do batalhão de Tel Sultan. Israel o acusa de orientar operações contra soldados e civis israelenses e de trabalhar para reconstruir a capacidade militar do Hamas na região.
As autoridades israelenses divulgaram imagens do momento em que o comandante foi atingido enquanto caminhava por uma rua. Conforme o diário The Times of Israel, citando um comunicado público, a morte foi confirmada pelo próprio Hamas.
Ataque atingiu área com barracas de deslocados
O ataque contra Abu Younis ocorreu em Al-Mawasi, faixa costeira próxima a Khan Yunis que abriga milhares de palestinos deslocados pela guerra e que vivem em barracas e estruturas improvisadas.
Segundo a agência palestina Wafa, uma barraca de deslocados acabou atingida deixando um morto e dois feridos. Profissionais de saúde ouvidos pela Al Jazeera relataram que as vítimas foram levadas ao Complexo Médico Nasser, em Khan Yunis.
O correspondente da Wafa informou ainda que não há identificação nominal das vítimas ou mais detalhes que permitam determinar se o ataque à barraca correspondeu exatamente ao ponto em que Abu Younis foi atingido.
A região de Al-Mawasi havia sido designada por Israel como zona humanitária durante a guerra, mas vem sendo atingida por operações militares israelenses. Grande parte da população palestina foi deslocada de suas casas e depende de abrigos improvisados para sobreviver.
Hamas confirma morte e divulga trajetória do comandante
As Brigadas Izz ad-Din al-Qassam, braço militar do Hamas, divulgaram um comunicado neste domingo (15) confirmando a morte de Abu Younis.
O grupo afirmou que o comandante, também conhecido como Abu Mahmoud, integrava o Conselho Militar Geral das Brigadas Al-Qassam e havia ingressado na estrutura militar do Hamas em 1991. Ao longo de sua trajetória, ocupou diferentes posições de comando na região de Rafah.
Em sua manifestação, o Hamas classificou a operação israelense como um assassinato covarde. O grupo anunciou que o funeral do comandante seria realizado na tarde deste domingo (15), em Khan Yunis. A confirmação foi divulgada pelas agências Reuters, Associated Press e Anadolu, além de veículos de imprensa israelenses e árabes.
Ataques continuam apesar do cessar-fogo
A morte do comandante ocorreu durante a vigência do cessar-fogo anunciado em outubro de 2025, que interrompeu parte das operações militares de grande escala, mas não encerrou os ataques israelenses à Faixa de Gaza.
Israel e Hamas continuam trocando acusações sobre violações do acordo. O governo israelense condiciona a retirada de suas forças e o avanço das negociações ao desarmamento do Hamas, enquanto o movimento palestino rejeita as exigências israelenses.
Segundo o Ministério da Saúde de Gaza, os ataques israelenses desde o início do cessar-fogo provocaram pelo menos 1.643 mortes e deixaram 5.964 feridos até o balanço divulgado no sábado (14).
Desde o início da ofensiva israelense, em outubro de 2023, o número de palestinos mortos chegou a 74.695, enquanto 176.093 pessoas ficaram feridas, segundo os dados divulgados pelo Ministério da Saúde palestino.
A escalada de ataques também atingiu instalações médicas. Na quinta-feira (12), um bombardeio israelense contra o Complexo Médico Nasser, em Khan Yunis, matou seis pessoas, entre elas um médico e uma criança de 13 anos, segundo autoridades sanitárias palestinas. Outras 28 pessoas ficaram feridas.
Israel afirmou que o ataque ao hospital tinha como alvo integrantes do Hamas, incluindo um comandante militar. A ofensiva provocou a interrupção de serviços médicos e cirúrgicos no complexo.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: No Peru, papa Leão 14 critica cultura que associa dignidade humana à produtividade
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O papa Leão 14 afirmou, neste domingo (15), que a doença não diminui a dignidade humana e criticou a lógica de uma sociedade que mede o valor das pessoas pela capacidade de produzir. A declaração foi feita durante a oração do Angelus, na cidade de Cusco, no Peru, onde o pontífice dedicou uma mensagem especial às pessoas que enfrentam enfermidades físicas e emocionais.
“Aos olhos de um mundo condicionado por uma ‘cultura do descarte’ e pela produtividade material, a doença é vista como um infortúnio que diminui o valor de uma pessoa. Que grande mentira!”, declarou.
Segundo Leão 14, a experiência do sofrimento, quando vivida com fé, pode se transformar em um caminho de crescimento no amor, solidariedade e aproximação com Deus.
“Vocês estão no coração pulsante da Igreja”, afirmou, dirigindo-se aos enfermos.
Na mensagem, o papa recordou dom Richard Daniel Alarcón Urrutia, antigo arcebispo de Cusco, que morreu em 30 de outubro, após um longo período de enfermidade, poucas semanas antes da chegada do pontífice à cidade. Leão 14 destacou a trajetória religiosa do religioso e afirmou que ele havia trabalhado intensamente para a realização da visita.
A visita a Cusco também representou um desafio pessoal para Leão 14, tendo em vista que ele retirou um tumor do pulmão em outubro. A antiga capital inca fica a mais de 3,4 mil metros acima do nível do mar – uma altitude suficiente para deixar muitos visitantes sem fôlego. O papa, com 71 anos, foi diagnosticado com um adenocarcinoma pulmonar, tipo mais comum de câncer no pulmão. Ele retirou o nódulo em uma cirurgia considerada bem-sucedida.
Religiosidade popular e memória
Ainda neste domingo, Leão 14 se encontrou com representantes da piedade popular no Parque Arqueológico Nacional de Saqsaywaman, em Cusco. Diante de fiéis e representantes de manifestações religiosas tradicionais, o pontífice destacou a importância das festas, procissões, peregrinações, músicas e danças na preservação da identidade cultural e da fé dos povos.
“Uma festa religiosa, uma peregrinação, uma procissão não são apenas uma manifestação cultural: por trás de cada imagem, cântico, promessa e sinal há uma comunidade de corações que procuram Deus e uma voz amiga que responde e se aproxima desde o céu”, afirmou.
O papa defendeu que essas tradições sejam também oportunidades de encontro, evangelização e compromisso comunitário. Para ele, a religiosidade popular representa uma expressão da fé construída coletivamente, que reúne a memória dos antepassados, a devoção familiar e a confiança em Jesus Cristo e nos santos.
Durante a passagem por Cusco, o pontífice prestou ainda uma homenagem ao Senhor dos Terremotos, imagem de Cristo crucificado venerada na Catedral da cidade. A devoção remonta a 1650, quando, segundo a tradição religiosa local, a imagem foi levada em procissão durante um terremoto, e os tremores cessaram.
Como demonstração de proximidade com a população, Leão 14 ofereceu um manto para ser colocado sobre a imagem. O gesto foi apresentado como sinal de comunhão e solidariedade com a comunidade peruana.
Viagem pela América do Sul
A passagem pelo Peru integra uma viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul, iniciada em 6 de novembro, que também incluiu compromissos no Uruguai e na Argentina. A sexta missão internacional do pontificado de Leão 14 contempla dez cidades nos três países e se encerra em 16 de novembro.
A visita ao Peru tem significado particular para o pontífice, que viveu no país por mais de duas décadas, onde atuou como missionário e bispo. Na Argentina, as mensagens do papa sobre justiça social e proteção dos trabalhadores ganharam repercussão em meio às políticas de austeridade adotadas pelo presidente Javier Milei.
Já no Peru, o discurso de Leão 14 também incorporou reivindicações históricas das comunidades camponesas. Durante uma missa celebrada no sábado (14), em Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, o pontífice abordou o desafio da distribuição equitativa dos benefícios gerados pelos recursos naturais.
“A oração e a piedade são vazias se não conduzirem a um compromisso transformador com o bem comum”, afirmou. Na mesma homilia, ressaltou a importância do trabalho de agricultores, comerciantes e pequenos empreendedores.
Ainda neste domingo, ele segue para Pucallpa, uma das maiores cidades da Amazônia peruana, onde se encontrará com líderes indígenas. Situada às margens do rio Ucayali, Pucallpa está no coração de uma região que se tornou um dos principais focos de desmatamento do Peru. Dados do governo peruano apontam que o país perdeu 3,2 milhões de hectares de floresta entre 2001 e 2024 – uma área equivalente ao tamanho da Bélgica.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Huge waves pummel California coast, forcing closure of popular piers
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
The California coast was pummeled again on Sunday by huge waves that inundated beaches, flooded local streets and forced the closure of popular piers.
The National Weather Service office for the San Francisco Bay Area warned that surf up to 35ft (11 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves.
“Stay out of the water, stay off rocks and jetties, and never turn your back on the ocean!” the weather service said on social media.
On Saturday, waves above 50ft were recorded in San Mateo county, just south of San Francisco.
Surfers weren’t deterred, taking advantage of giant waves at the famous Mavericks beach near Half Moon Bay.
Farther south, the Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office issued an evacuation warning near the coastal town of Capitola that took the brunt of the powerful surf.
In southern California, several piers, including ones in Ventura, Manhattan Beach, Huntington Beach and San Diego’s Pacific Beach, were closed during the weekend as they were slammed by waves.
At La Jolla Cove near San Diego, known for its lounging sea lions, water overflowed the beach and crashed up a staircase leading to the sand.
Conditions were calming by Sunday afternoon, but large waves were expected all week, forecasters warned.
The ongoing super El Niño has warmed the ocean, leading to an increased volume of seawater.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Superlotação, fome e sede: o que está por trás da camiseta de preso pedindo por direitos humanos em presídio de SP
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Kaique Dalapola
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Um protesto no topo de uma caixa d’água no início de novembro expôs a dimensão da crise humanitária enfrentada pelas pessoas presas no Complexo Prisional de Pinheiros, na zona oeste da capital paulista. No dia 5 de novembro, dois detentos subiram na estrutura do Centro de Detenção Provisória (CDP) 2 de Pinheiros durante uma movimentação interna. Um deles vestia uma camiseta branca escrita “direitos humanos urgente”, enquanto o outro exibia a mensagem “Raquel, te amo”.
A manifestação, transmitida com imagens do helicóptero da TV Globo, é uma manifestação que reflete a rotina de violações diárias relatada por familiares de custodiados e documentada em relatórios oficiais de inspeção penal. Os dois que subiram na caixa d’água foram encaminhados para sanção disciplinar,
A mãe de um jovem de 23 anos preso em uma das unidades do complexo, que falou com Brasil de Fato sob anonimato por temer represálias contra o filho, relata um cotidiano marcado pelo desabastecimento e pela deterioração física acelerada dentro das celas.
De acordo com o depoimento da mãe, os presos são despertados logo no início da manhã para receberem uma alimentação insuficiente, composta apenas por “um dedo de café puro e pão velho sem manteiga”.
Ela afirma que, com frequência, os detentos passam o dia inteiro sem ter acesso à água potável, situação que se agrava de forma drástica durante os períodos de calor intenso na cidade. “Desde quando entrou nesse inferno, meu filho claramente é outra pessoa, está perdendo peso, está ficando depressivo e com vários sinais de adoecimento, mas nem dipirona eles tomam”, disse.
“Conheço mães que perderam o filho dentro da cadeia por pura negligência, e eu temo acontecer o mesmo comigo ou com qualquer outra mãe, porque o que acontece dentro desses presídios é desumano, é o completo desprezo pelo ser humano. Se fizessem isso com qualquer outro grupo da sociedade, o mundo já estaria denunciando, mas como são apenas os nossos presos, ninguém quer nem olhar”, pontua a mãe de um preso.
População carcerária é mais que o dobro da capacidade oficial
Dados da Secretaria da Administração Penitenciária (SAP) mostram que o Complexo de Pinheiros operava, nesta semana, com 5.007 homens encarcerados em uma estrutura física projetada para abrigar 2.485 pessoas, ou seja, há o dobro de presos que previa a capacidade arquitetônica da unidade.
O excedente populacional atinge níveis extremos em três das quatro unidades prisionais que compõem o complexo. O caso mais agudo é o do CDP 3 de Pinheiros: com capacidade oficial dimensionada para 605 detentos, o local mantinha 1.522 presos sob custódia, 2,5 vezes o total de vagas disponíveis.
Situação semelhante ocorre no CDP 1, que abriga 1.280 pessoas em um espaço arquitetônico planejado para 521 vagas. Já no CDP 2, unidade onde os presos subiram na caixa d’água em protesto, a ocupação era de 1.745 homens para um teto projetado de 793 vagas, um contingente excedente de 952 pessoas amontoadas.
A única exceção no complexo é o CDP 4, destinado a custodiados em regimes diferenciados ou perfis específicos de prisão, que contava com 460 homens para 566 vagas abertas.
As consequências da superlotação crônica foram detalhadas em artigo publicado na última quarta-feira (11) no jornal Folha de S.Paulo, assinado por Rodrigo Sérvulo da Cunha Vieira Rios e André Ferreira, respectivamente, presidente e conselheiro do Conselho da Comunidade da Comarca de São Paulo. O órgão, previsto no artigo 80 da Lei de Execução Penal (LEP), tem como atribuição legal visitar presídios e encaminhar relatórios circunstanciados à Justiça.
No artigo, intitulado “Direitos humanos urgentemente”, os dirigentes do Conselho da Comunidade afirmam que as inspeções recentes realizadas nas unidades de Pinheiros revelam que a subida na caixa d’água representou “um grito de desespero saído diretamente de um calabouço”. As vistorias do conselho ocorreram no CDP 1 em agosto, no CDP 2 em setembro e no CDP 3 no fim de outubro.
Nas três unidades visitadas, o conselho identificou uma população total de 4.364 homens para apenas 1.924 vagas oficiais — um excedente direto de 2.440 detentos. O texto alerta que a superlotação atua como catalisador de um quadro sanitário alarmante: o CDP 2 informou a existência de 105 pessoas vivendo com HIV e 36 casos confirmados de tuberculose em celas sem ventilação adequada e com atendimento médico precário.
Outro dado ressaltado pelos integrantes do órgão na Folha de S.Paulo refere-se à mortalidade sob custódia estatal. Somadas, as três unidades fiscalizadas contabilizaram 33 mortes nos últimos doze meses: quatro no CDP 1; dez no CDP 2; e 19 no CDP 3.
“A lei diz que o Estado pode restringir a liberdade de alguém por decisão judicial, mas não o autoriza a suprimir sua dignidade. A pena prevista em lei é a privação da liberdade, não a fome, a doença, a ausência de tratamento médico ou a exposição a condições degradantes”, sustentam os dirigentes no artigo.
Relatórios desmentem versão oficial da SAP
Em nota enviada ao Brasil de Fato, a Polícia Penal e a Secretaria da Administração Penitenciária (SAP) afirmaram que o Complexo de Pinheiros “opera dentro dos padrões de segurança e disciplina” e que há investimentos contínuos na capacitação e recomposição de pessoal, com concurso em andamento para a contratação de 1,1 mil agentes.
A pasta afirmou que o abastecimento de água é regular, com bebedouros dotados de filtragem e instalações com manutenção preventiva, citando laudo emitido pela Sabesp em junho que atesta a potabilidade.
Sobre a alimentação, a SAP afirmou que segue cardápio padrão supervisionado por nutricionistas, com quatro refeições diárias produzidas na Penitenciária José Parada Neto e na Penitenciária da Capital, a P1 de Guarulhos. Em relação à saúde, disse que os presos dispõem de assistência médica e odontológica conforme a demanda e consultas por meio do sistema TeleSAP.
No campo da saúde, o Relatório Final da Audiência Pública sobre o Sistema Prisional Paulista, organizado em conjunto pelo Conselho Estadual de Defesa dos Direitos da Pessoa Humana (Condepe) e outros órgãos, aponta que o sistema TeleSAP de telemedicina atua apenas como mecanismo paliativo e complementar, incapaz de suprir a falta estrutural de médicos presenciais.
Dados apresentados pela própria SAP em abril indicam que 78 unidades prisionais paulistas operavam sem equipes vinculadas ao SUS e sem médicos regulares.
Vistorias da comissão de direitos humanos da OAB-SP registraram ainda que a chefia do setor de saúde de diversos presídios é exercida por técnicos de enfermagem e que a medicação fornecida a presos com doenças graves costuma se resumir a analgésicos básicos.
Quanto à alimentação, levantamentos anteriores da Defensoria Pública já haviam identificado que os detentos do CDP 2 enfrentavam até 15 horas consecutivas de jejum entre o jantar e o café da manhã, em desconformidade com a Resolução 3 de 2017 do Conselho Nacional de Política Criminal e Penitenciária (CNPCP), que estabelece a oferta mínima de cinco refeições balanceadas por dia.
Mortes sob custódia crescem no estado
O cenário observado em Pinheiros reflete a escalada da mortalidade em todo o sistema penitenciário de São Paulo. Dados oficiais divulgados pela própria SAP mostram que o número de pessoas mortas sob custódia estatal subiu de 280 óbitos no primeiro semestre de 2025 para 353 no segundo semestre daquele ano, mantendo-se em patamar elevado no primeiro semestre de 2026, quando foram registradas 354 mortes.
O diagnóstico elaborado pelo Núcleo de Estudos da Violência da Universidade de São Paulo (NEV-USP) em parceria com o Condepe aponta uma estimativa anual de aproximadamente 500 mortes nas prisões de São Paulo. Em termos proporcionais, o número equivale a uma morte a cada 19 horas sob responsabilidade do Estado.
Para o advogado criminalista Antonio Gonçalves, pós-doutor pela Pontifícia Universidade Católica de São Paulo (PUC-SP), a degradação nas prisões provisórias desvirtua a própria finalidade legal do encarceramento prévio.
“A prisão provisória tem natureza estritamente cautelar e visa assegurar a instrução criminal ou a aplicação da lei penal, não podendo funcionar como execução antecipada de pena nem como imposição de sofrimento físico”, avalia o advogado.
Gonçalves ressalta que o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), no julgamento da Arguição de Descumprimento de Preceito Fundamental (ADPF) 347, declarou o sistema prisional brasileiro em “estado de coisas inconstitucional” devido à violação massiva e sistêmica de garantias fundamentais.
“O Estado tem o dever de custódia e responde objetivamente por danos morais e materiais causados a quem está sob sua tutela direta. A submissão de pessoas não condenadas a celas superlotadas, sem água potável, sem atendimento médico e com proliferação de doenças infectocontagiosas enseja a responsabilidade civil do poder público perante os familiares e os próprios custodiados”, afirma o advogado.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: United States 6-2 Canada: women’s ice hockey world championship 2026 final – live reaction
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Bryan Armen Graham
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
The United States are world champions again! Hilary Knight and Kelly Pannek score twice each as the Americans complete a historic golden double, adding the world championship to the Olympic title they won in Milan in February.
Canada struck first through Sarah Fillier, but the US roared back with five unanswered goals before cruising to their 12th world title. The Americans finish the tournament unbeaten, having trailed for just five minutes and 14 seconds across seven games, all during tonight’s opening period. A commanding performance from start to finish and a definitive closing statement in this team’s annus mirabilis.
Hayley Scamurra has made a little history of her own. The 31-year-old forward from suburban Buffalo has become the first player to win Olympic gold, world championship gold and the PWHL’s Walter Cup in the same calendar year.
Scamurra won the Walter Cup with the Montreal Victoire in May, added Olympic gold with the United States in Milan in February and completed the treble with Monday’s 6-2 victory over Canada in Herning.
And she put her own finishing touch on the achievement, scoring into an empty net with 3.27 remaining to seal the Americans’ 12th world title.
The US have swept the three individual awards handed out by the tournament directorate, putting another exclamation point on their charmed run to world championship gold.
Caroline Harvey was named the tournament’s most valuable player and best defender, while Aerin Frankel took best goalkeeper honors and captain Hilary Knight was named best forward.
Harvey and Knight also made the media-voted All-Star Team, alongside Canadian forwards Jessie Eldridge and Sarah Fillier, Sweden defender Mira Jungaker and Austria goaltender Selma Luggin.
Luggin’s selection is particularly noteworthy: the Austrian helped her country win its relegation game to retain a place in the top division, earning All-Star recognition despite playing for a team at the opposite end of the standings from the champions.
The Star-Spangled Banner rings out inside Herning Hockey Arena as the American players stand arm in arm, singing along beneath the rafters. Gold medals draped from around their necks, the world champions are basking in the moment after their 6-2 victory over Canada.
Kelly Pannek, who scored twice, credited the Americans’ collective drive for their remarkable run of success, which has now delivered Olympic and world championship gold in the same calendar year.
“I just think it’s the way everyone keeps trying to push each other to get better,” Pannek said afterward. “Everyone trusts that we’re pushing ourselves, and then we come together as a group. It’s just so natural.”
Pannek, who was named the team’s player of the game, pointed to the blend of established stars and emerging talent as a key ingredient.
“You have players that have stayed at the top, like Hilary, and players that have made their way to the top, like Caroline Harvey, and everyone in between. It’s just such a team effort. We play gritty at times, we play skilled at times, and it’s just super fun to be a part of.”
Sarah Fillier, to no one’s surprise, took player of the game honors for Canada after scoring both of her team’s goals.
The United States are world champions again! Hilary Knight and Kelly Pannek score twice each as the Americans complete a historic golden double, adding the world championship to the Olympic title they won in Milan in February.
Canada struck first through Sarah Fillier, but the US roared back with five unanswered goals before cruising to their 12th world title. The Americans finish the tournament unbeaten, having trailed for just five minutes and 14 seconds across seven games, all during tonight’s opening period. A commanding performance from start to finish and a definitive closing statement in this team’s annus mirabilis.
That should settle it! Hayley Scamurra slides the puck into the empty net after Canada pull Desbiens for an extra attacker. Hilary Knight picks up the assist, her third point of the night.
And what a 2026 it’s been for Scamurra, who is now minutes away from completing a remarkable personal treble: Olympic gold, the PWHL’s Walter Cup and world championship gold, all in the same calendar year. The Americans are closing in on a historic double of their own.
Emma Bowling crashes into Aerin Frankel just before the TV timeout, but the US goaltender is OK after the collision. Canada have pulled Desbiens for an extra attacker as play resumes, throwing everything forward in a desperate attempt to erase the three-goal deficit.
Renata Fast returns to the ice after Canada kill off a penalty they could scarcely afford to concede on. The Americans still lead by three, but Canada have survived another dangerous two minutes and kept their flickering hopes alive.
Renata Fast is sent to the box for boarding, but only after an extended delayed penalty during which the Americans keep possession for nearly a full minute.
Well, Canada aren’t going quietly. A scant 40 seconds after Eden put the Americans four goals to the good, Sarah Fillier races clear on a breakaway and rifles a gorgeous shot over Aerin Frankel’s shoulder to pull one back.
It’s the second goal of the night for the Georgetown, Ontario, native, with Kristin O’Neill and Renata Fast collecting the assists. Three goals in less than two minutes to start the third period. So much for a quiet finish.
The floodgates have opened in Herning! Lacey Eden is left all alone to finish a gorgeous cross-ice pass from Joy Dunne, ripping a shot past Desbiens to give the Americans a four-goal lead.
Caroline Harvey picks up the secondary assist as the US score twice in the opening three minutes of the final period. What was a tense gold-medal encounter has suddenly become a rout and the Americans are closing in on a historic double.
The Americans have struck again! Just 89 seconds into the third period, Kelly Pannek gets her second goal of the night, redirecting Cayla Barnes’ shot from the point past Ann-Renée Desbiens to stretch the US lead to three.
Lee Stecklein picks up the secondary assist on Pannek’s fifth goal of the tournament. After breaking a 1-1 tie midway through the second period, Pannek has now supplied two of the biggest goals of the night. The United States have tacked on a crucial insurance goal early in the final period with the gold medal in sight.
The Americans are one period away from completing an unprecedented calendar-year sweep of the two biggest prizes in international women’s hockey. Having won Olympic gold in Milan in February, the Americans can become the first US team to add the world championship in the same year.
And despite the parade of penalties in that frenetic second period, the stat sheet suggests the Americans have earned their two-goal cushion. They’ve outshot Canada 19-13 through 40 minutes, converted one of three power plays and – crucially – killed off all five Canadian advantages.
The US have spent 12 minutes in the penalty box to Canada’s six, yet somehow emerged from the middle frame with a 3-1 lead. Twenty more minutes of that defensive resilience and the John Wroblewski’s side will have made history.
US forward Hayley Scamurra praised her team’s composure during a penalty-filled second period that saw the Americans turn a 1-1 deadlock into a 3-1 lead.
“I was really proud of us, how we handled all that adversity,” Scamurra told TSN during the second intermission. “A few times we were maybe on our heels a little bit with the penalties, but I was really proud of our penalty kill and the way we attacked after those. I think we got a lot of momentum for ourselves.”
The 31-year-old from Williamsville, just outside Buffalo, is also chasing a remarkable personal milestone: completing hockey’s Triple Gold Club in a single year, having already won Olympic gold and the PWHL’s Walter Cup with Montreal.
“It’s just been unbelievable,” she said. “I’m just so honored to be with the teams that I’ve been with. Some amazing players and leaders that I’ve been able to be a part of.”
Asked about protecting the two-goal lead over the final 20 minutes, Scamurra is to the point. “It’s just sticking to our game plan, sticking to what we’re really good at. As long as we keep attacking and playing forward, I think we’re going to do a really great job here.”
The “U-S-A!” chants are gathering in volume inside Kvik Hockey Arena as the Americans head into the second intermission with a two-goal lead.
Kelly Pannek put the defending champions ahead midway through the period before Hilary Knight struck her second of the night on a four-on-three power play, capping a chaotic sequence of penalties.
Canada have 20 minutes to find a way back into this one, or the Americans will be celebrating their 12th world championship.
Hilary Knight strikes again! The American captain hammers home a one-timer on the four-on-three power play to give the United States a two-goal cushion late in the second period.
Megan Keller and Taylor Fox pick up the assists, with Fox’s 13th of the tournament setting a new single-edition world championship record.
It’s Knight’s second goal of the night and ninth of the competition, a personal best at the age of 37. After trailing for the first time all tournament, the defending champions have overturned the deficit with three unanswered goals and are suddenly in command.
Another penalty! Canada’s Danielle Serdachny is sent off for tripping, just 34 seconds after the Americans were penalized for too many players on the ice.
That makes three penalties in the space of 90 seconds. The US now have a four-on-three advantage in a suddenly chaotic finish to the second period.
And now the Americans are penalized for having too many players on the ice! Hannah Bilka heads to the box to serve the two-minute bench minor, cutting short the US power play.
We’ll have four-on-four hockey for the next 64 seconds before Canada get a brief advantage of their own.
Moments after killing off their fourth – and dodgiest – penalty of the night, the Americans get a power play of their own as Canada’s Renata Fast is sent to the box for tripping.
Well, here’s something you don’t see every day. The United States have been assessed a two-minute bench minor for abuse of officials, with Abbey Murphy sent to the penalty box to serve it.
A rare call at any level, let alone in a world championship final. Canada have a chance to draw level on the power play.
The Americans take the lead! Hayley Scamurra delivers a superb cross-crease pass to Kelly Pannek, who hammers home a first-time shot past Ann-Renée Desbiens.
It’s the Minnesota Frost forward’s fourth goal of the tournament, with Scamurra and Grace Zumwinkle credited with the assists.
After trailing for the first time at this world championship, the United States have turned the game around midway through the second period.
The Canadians kill off the penalty, thanks in no small part to Ann-Renée Desbiens, who produces a spectacular save to deny Abbey Murphy from point-blank range.
Now the United States will go on the power play for the first time after the Canadian goalscorer Fillier heads to the box for two minutes on a tripping penalty.
And it’s another tidy penalty kill for the United States, who deny the Canadians a single shot on goal during the power play.
The Americans cleared the puck repeatedly as Canada struggled to establish themselves in the attacking zone. Hayley Scamurra even creates a shorthanded chance at the other end, but her effort was turned back.
The teams are back to even strength as the American penalty kill remains 100% for the tournament. A smattering of “U-S-A! U-S-A!” chants can be heard in the crowd.
Canada’s Jessie Eldridge sounded pleased with her team’s opening period after setting up Sarah Fillier’s goal.
“I think I know if I can get Filly the puck, she’s going to put it in the net,” Eldridge told a TSN reporter during the first intermission. “It’s been working so far. We’re hoping to get a couple more.”
Eldridge was part of the Canadian team who won gold in this same building four years ago, but played down the significance of that experience.
“I think we’re a completely different roster here. Both sides, too,” the Montreal Victoire forward said. “We’re just going to keep playing our way.”
And her assessment of the opening 20 minutes? “It’s great hockey. I think it’s going to be a lot of fun in the next 40.”
We’re all square after 20 minutes in Herning, with Sarah Fillier’s opener for Canada canceled out by Hilary Knight’s eighth goal of the tournament. The Americans have outshot the Canadians 11-8.
Canada will begin the second period with just under a minute remaining on the power play.
A second penalty on the United States. It’s going to be two minutes for holding on Pannek as Wroblewski throws his arms up in disbelief after having a look at the replay. It’s another chance for Canada’s tournament-best power play, a unit that entered today’s game converting at 43%.
Hilary Knight pounces on a rebound in front of goal to draw the Americans level, sending chants of “U-S-A!” ringing around the arena in Herning.
Laila Edwards makes a lovely move at the point to create the opening, with Tessa Janecke also picking up an assist as Knight buries the loose puck past Ann-Renée Desbiens.
It’s Knight’s eighth goal and 11th point of the tournament, and the United States are back on level terms with less than four minutes remaining in the opening period.
Canada have the lead through Sarah Fillier – the second coming of Marie-Philip Poulin? – but the Americans are beginning to turn the screw in the attacking zone.
Kelly Pannek tests Desbiens with a sharp-angle effort from close range, only for the Canadian goaltender to turn it away.
The shots are level at 6-6 with just over five minutes remaining in the opening period.
Canada strike first! Sarah Fillier redirects the puck past Aerin Frankel with a deft backhand finish to give the Canadians the lead midway through the opening period. Jessie Eldridge and Rosalie Tremblay pick up the assists.
That’s five goals in five games for Fillier, who missed Canada’s first two matches through injury but has scored in every appearance since.
And for the first time at this world championship, the United States find themselves trailing.
Canada are enjoying more time in the attacking zone as we reach the first media timeout. Jessie Eldridge goes down under pressure in the American zone, while Caroline Harvey loses her stick in the scramble, but there’s no penalty.
Canada have their first good look at goal as Jessie Eldridge carries the puck into the American zone and sends a backhander toward the net. Frankel corrals it comfortably.
At the other end, Laila Edwards unleashes a blistering shot from the point through traffic, but Desbiens tracks the puck all the way and makes the save.
Both goaltenders have been called into action in a lively opening four minutes.
The lineups are confirmed for tonight’s gold-medal game, with Aerin Frankel in goal for the United States and Ann-Renée Desbiens between the pipes for Canada.
US captain Hilary Knight starts alongside forwards Tessa Janecke and Alex Carpenter, with Megan Keller and Laila Edwards the starting defensive pair. Frankel enters the final having set American records for career wins and shutouts at the women’s world championship.
Canada captain Laura Stacey starts up front with Caitlin Kraemer and Daryl Watts, while Renata Fast and Nicole Gosling form the starting defensive pair. Desbiens has been similarly impressive throughout the tournament, conceding just one goal in three starts.
Today’s gold-medal game will be the 201st meeting between the US and Canada in women’s international hockey, a rivalry stretching back to the inaugural world championship final in 1990.
Canada hold the historical advantage, with 109 victories to the Americans’ 90, plus one tie across the first 200 encounters. But the US have enjoyed the upper hand recently, winning the 2025 world championship final and February’s Olympic gold-medal game, both in overtime.
There is another historical wrinkle to today’s showdown: the last time the women’s worlds were staged in Herning, in 2022, Canada beat the US 2-1 in the final. Brianne Jenner scored twice in just 83 seconds during the second period to secure Canada’s 12th world title.
Four years later, the Canadians return to the same city chasing their 14th. The Americans, meanwhile, are looking to close the gap with a 12th championship of their own.
A fit and firing Sarah Fillier is a welcome sight for Canadian fans. The 26-year-old forward missed the first two games of this world championship with an upper-body injury. Since returning, the forward has wasted little time making her presence felt.
Fillier has scored in all four games she has played, including Sunday’s semi-final against Sweden, when she broke a scoreless deadlock with a power-play goal midway through the second period. Sarah Wozniewicz and Emma Maltais added further goals as Canada completed a 3-0 victory.
The 2022 Beijing Olympic champion, who plays for the PWHL’s New York Sirens, has emerged as one of Canada’s most important attacking players. Her scoring touch could prove crucial against a US defense that has conceded only twice in six games.
US goaltender Aerin Frankel has been quietly making history of her own at this world championship, for all the attention lavished on Americans’ headline-grabbing attack,
Frankel recorded her eighth career shutout at the women’s worlds with a 17-save performance in Sunday’s 5-0 semi-final victory over Finland, breaking the American record previously held by Nicole Hensley.
The Boston Fleet goaltender also became the United States’ all-time leader in world championship victories earlier in the tournament, taking her career tally to 19.
With the Americans having conceded just two goals in six games on their way to tonight’s final, Frankel will face a considerably sterner examination against Canada as the US pursue a 12th world title.
Sweden won the third-place game earlier today, beating Finland 2-1 in a shootout to claim their first medal at the tournament in nearly two decades.
Lina Ljungblom, a forward with the PWHL’s Montreal Victoire, forced overtime with a power-play goal six minutes from the end of regulation after Vancouver Goldeneyes forward Michelle Karvinen had put Finland ahead late in the second period. Hilda Svensson, a 20-year-old Ohio State sophomore, assisted on the equalizer before scoring the decisive shootout goal.
Swedish goaltender Ebba Svensson Traff turned back 29 shots through overtime and stopped four of five shootout attempts. Finland’s Sanni Ahola, of the Ottawa Charge, finished with 35 saves.
It is Sweden’s third world championship bronze, following medals in 2005 and 2007.
If Canada are to halt the Americans’ winning streak, Ann-Renée Desbiens may have to be at her very best. The 32-year-old goaltender has been close to unbeatable in Denmark, allowing just one goal in three starts while posting a tournament-leading .981 save percentage.
Sunday’s 13-save shutout against Sweden was her second in succession and the 10th of her world championship career, leaving her three behind compatriot Kim St-Pierre’s all-time record. It was also her 25th victory at the worlds, extending her own Canadian record.
Desbiens arrives on the back of an outstanding professional season with the Montréal Victoire, whom she helped to their first Walter Cup championship after leading the PWHL with 19 wins and a 1.11 goals-against average.
Against an American attack averaging more than eight goals per game, Canada will need every bit of that form.
Hej, Guardian-læsere and welcome to our live coverage of the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship final between the US and Canada. The fiercest rivalry in women’s hockey is renewed tonight in Herning, Denmark, with another world title on the line, less than nine months after the Americans broke Canadian hearts in the Olympic final at Milano Cortina.
The neighboring countries that share the world’s longest international border have exercised an extraordinary duopoly over this competition since its inception in 1990, combining to win all 24 previous editions. Canada lead the all-time count with 13 titles to the US’s 11, but the balance of power has shifted south of the border in recent years. The Americans are defending world champions after a dramatic 4-3 overtime victory in last year’s final in the Czech Republic, and followed that with a 2-1 overtime win over Canada for Olympic gold in February, sealed by Megan Keller’s winner.
The US arrive in flying form. John Wroblewski’s team have won 20 consecutive games in international competition since their defeat to Canada in the 2024 world championship final, including six straight victories at this tournament by a combined score of 50-2. Sunday’s 5-0 semi-final demolition of Finland followed an even more emphatic 14-0 quarter-final rout of hosts Denmark. Canada, meanwhile, booked their place with a 3-0 shutout of Sweden, behind goals from Sarah Fillier, Sarah Wozniewicz and Emma Maltais.
There have been individual milestones aplenty for the Americans. Caroline Harvey, the 24-year-old defender, has racked up 15 points in six games, a single-tournament record for a player at her position. Taylor Fox has equaled the tournament record with 12 assists, while captain Hilary Knight, now 37 and the US team’s north star for so many years, continues to extend her extraordinary world championship records: 74 goals and 130 points in 93 appearances. Between the pipes, Aerin Frankel recorded her eighth career shutout at the worlds against Finland, another American record.
Yet for all their dominance against the rest of the field, the Americans know Canada represent an altogether different challenge. These familiar opponents have met in 23 of the previous 24 world championship finals, and their last two major title encounters have required overtime to separate them.
Puck drop is scheduled for 1pm ET (7pm local time), with live television coverage on NHL Network in the United States and TSN and RDS in Canada. Canadian viewers can also stream the game on TSN’s digital platforms. We’ll have all the buildup, team news and live updates from Herning right here.
Bryan will be here shortly to marshal our coverage of the women’s ice hockey world championship final between the United States and Canada. In the meantime, here’s the Associated Press report on Sunday’s semi-final twin bill:
The United States and Canada will renew their rivalry in the final of the women’s ice hockey world championship on Monday.
In the semi-finals on Sunday, defending champions the US blanked Finland 5-0 before Canada shut out Sweden 3-0.
US captain Hilary Knight had a goal and an assist, with Kelly Pannek, Alex Carpenter, Caroline Harvey and Lacey Eden also scoring.
Aerin Rankel stopped 17 shots for her eighth career world championship shutout and 19th victory.
The Americans jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the opening period after Pannek netted the opener from the low slot 6:36 in and Knight fed Carpenter with a backhand pass from behind the net to double the advantage with 3:26 remaining.
Harvey, Eden and Knight extended the lead to 5-0 in the span of 1min 35sec in the second period.
Tournament leading scorer Harvey moved to 15 points from six games. Knight extended her record points tally to 130, with 74 goals and 56 assists in 93 games at the worlds.
Finland pulled goalie Sanni Ahola, who made 20 saves, after the second period, with Emilia Kyrkko taking over and finishing with nine saves.
Sarah Fillier, Sarah Wozniewicz and Emma Maltais scored a goal each and goalie Ann-Renée Desbiens made 13 saves for Canada’s shutout.
Fillier skated to the left circle before breaking the deadlock with a snap shot high into the net 7:15 into the middle period.
The forward extended her goal streak to four games. She missed the first two games of the tournament with an upper-body injury.
Wozniewicz made it 2-0 on a breakaway and Maltais added the third in the final period.
Finland will face Sweden in the bronze-medal game after finishing third last year.
Canada have won 13 world titles, followed by the US with 11.
The Americans won the 2025 title in the Czech Republic and Olympic gold at the Milan-Cortina Games in February, beating Canada in overtime in both finals.

https://www.theguardian.com/business/202.title: Customers report difficulty accessing online services at major US banks
https://www.theguardian.com/business/202.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/business/202.text:
Customers reported difficulty accessing their online accounts at some major US banks on Monday.
The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began Friday and lasted for hours, which affected services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot and had serious repercussions all around the world. Also on Friday, ageing equipment led to a temporary grounding of all commercial airplanes in the US, sparking travel havoc.
Bank of America, Chase, US Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users as down or experiencing issues on Monday, according to the website downdetector.com.
Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said on Monday.
“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete, but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”
A spokesperson from US Bank said its systems are not directly affected; however, “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”
Zelle’s network operator is a company called Early Warning Services, which is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.
Some Chase customers received a message that said: “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

https://www.middleeasteye.net/trending/s.title: Somali-American Uber driver left in coma after alleged hate crime in Minnesota
https://www.middleeasteye.net/trending/s.author: MEE staff
https://www.middleeasteye.net/trending/s.text:
Somali-American Uber driver left in coma after alleged hate crime in Minnesota
A Somali-American Uber driver is fighting for his life after being strangled and repeatedly run over with his own vehicle, allegedly by a passenger in Minnesota, in an attack his family believes was motivated by anti-Muslim hatred.
Mohamed Yusuf was working in Hopkins, a suburb of Minneapolis, early on Saturday when a passenger allegedly asked him his name before telling him he did not like the name "Mohamed".
According to Yusuf's relatives, the passenger then allegedly choked him from behind, seized control of his vehicle and ran him over multiple times.
"He was run over multiple times with his own vehicle," Yusuf's son, Mustafa Osman, told The Somali Brief.
Yusuf was reportedly found in a ditch nearly a mile away, suffering from broken legs and ribs, two collapsed lungs, a spinal injury and internal bleeding.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
He remains hospitalised in a coma, according to his family.
Hopkins police confirmed that officers responding to a report of a suspicious vehicle at around 1.20am on Saturday discovered a seriously injured man and subsequently took a male suspect into custody.
According to the Times of India, arrest records show that a man identified as Samit Apurva Patel was taken into custody by Hopkins Police on 14 November on a first-degree assault charge.
However, authorities have not confirmed whether Patel's arrest is connected to Yusuf's assault or publicly identified the suspect in the case.
Police have also not established a motive or confirmed whether the incident is being investigated as a hate crime.
The attack has sparked outrage among Somali and Muslim Americans, with community members demanding that authorities investigate it as a possible hate crime.
US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar condemned the attack, warning that the continued dehumanisation of Somali Americans has real-world consequences.
"This horrific act of racial violence is unacceptable," Omar wrote on X, adding that no one should live in fear because of their identity, while calling for an end to the hatred dividing communities.
My heart is with Mohamed and his family. I am praying for his full recovery. This horrific act of racial violence is unacceptable. No one should live in fear because of who they are. The relentless dehumanization of the Somali community has real consequences. We must unequivocally condemn this violence and reject the hatred that divides our communities.
— Ilhan Omar (@IlhanMN) November 15, 2026
Prominent Muslim-American scholar Omar Suleiman also responded, warning that attacks targeting the Somali community were becoming increasingly frequent.
Suleiman said Yusuf had simply gone to work to provide for his family and was now fighting for his life, praying for his recovery and calling for accountability for those who spread hatred and those who act upon it.
Attacks on our Somali community are more and more frequent. Mohamed Yusuf went to work to provide for his family and is now fighting for his life after a horrific attack. May Allah grant him a full recovery and hold accountable those who spread and act upon such hatred.
— Dr. Omar Suleiman (@omarsuleiman) November 15, 2026
The case triggered widespread anger online about the atmosphere that allowed such attacks to happen across the United States.
One of Yusuf’s family members took to X and said, “The passenger said he hated people named Mohamed. I'm angry at our government for feeding that hatred with its anti-Muslim and anti-Somali rhetoric.”
My in law is in a coma after being strangled, run over with his own car and left in a ditch by an Uber passenger. I don't understand how anyone can do something so horrific to another person. He's one of the kindest people I know and has made me feel welcome in this family. He was just doing his job. The passenger said he hated people named Mohamed. I'm angry at our government for feeding that hatred with its anti Muslim and anti Somali rhetoric. I'm praying he makes a full recovery and comes home to his family. He and his family deserve justice for what was done to him.
— atikh 🇸🇴 (@tikhbana) November 15, 2026
A GoFundMe created for Yusuf and his family has already raised over $140,000.
'Our politicians created this hostile environment'
The attack comes amid heightened concerns over anti-Somali rhetoric in the United States, particularly in Minnesota, which is home to one of the country's largest Somali-American communities.
President Donald Trump has repeatedly targeted Somali immigrants in his political rhetoric, while Republican politicians in Minnesota have also made inflammatory remarks about the community.
House Majority Whip Tom Emmer recently claimed on a conservative podcast that Minnesota had effectively inherited Somalia's civil war.
"Our politicians created this hostile environment," one of Yusuf's relatives told The Somali Brief, describing the assault as a hate crime.
Speaking at a news conference outside Hennepin County Medical Center on Monday, Jaylani Hussein, executive director of the Council on American-Islamic Relations' Minnesota chapter, blamed the attack on what he described as a sustained campaign of hatred and dehumanisation against Somali Americans.
"For more than a year and a half, Muslims across this country, and specifically Somali Americans here in Minnesota nationwide, have lived in [an] unwritten climate of fear, hatred, bigotry and dehumanisation," Hussein said.
He accused Trump, local politicians and online agitators of contributing to an increasingly hostile environment for Somali Americans, including Congresswoman Ilhan Omar.
"This rhetoric has built an environment that we are living in today, an environment which is what we believe has created this heinous attack that took place on Saturday night here in Minnesota," he said.
Hussein acknowledged that police were still gathering evidence and urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Hopkins Police Department.
“At this time, we know that Yusuf was on the phone with a family member the entire time the incident was taking place. I do not know what the officials are ready to share yet. We know that they are working hard and we recognise that this case requires additional information,” he added.
"This is one of the most heinous attacks that we have ever seen, and it has shocked the conscience of all of us. We know it did not happen in [a] vacuum. We know it happened in an environment that has been created, festered and driven,” Hussein said.
Minnesota state Senator Omar Fateh also condemned the attack, calling for an immediate and transparent investigation.
"Mohamed Yusuf should be home safe with his family, not fighting for his life after an attack fueled by hatred towards his Somali identity," Fateh wrote on social media.
The news conference brought together community leaders, elected officials, including Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey, and rideshare drivers demanding that authorities investigate the assault as a possible hate crime.
Uber said it was "shocked and horrified" by the incident, adding that it had banned the rider from its platform and would cooperate with law enforcement.
A fundraising campaign established to support Yusuf and his family had raised more than $140,000 by Sunday, as supporters rallied around the injured driver.
Yusuf's family described him as a devoted father and hardworking man who was simply trying to earn a living and return home safely.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Cornell announces full review of Greek life after scrutiny over sexual assault case
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Sam Levine
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Cornell University is set to announce a “full review” of fraternities and sororities determining their future on campus after an alleged sexual assault there has brought scrutiny to the system at the Ivy League school.
University president Michael Kotlikoff announced the review on Monday in an update outlining several steps the institution has taken after a woman said she was gang raped at an on-campus fraternity’s house.
Cornell had already banned fraternity parties for the rest of the academic year after the gang-rape was alleged in a civil lawsuit that captured international attention.
“I know many in our community have lost confidence in the Cornell administration’s ability to prevent and respond to sexual violence,” Kotlikoff wrote in a letter published on Monday. “You have raised necessary questions about what the administration is doing to keep our students safe and where we have fallen short.
“You have called for greater transparency and better communication about what we are doing so that nothing like this can ever happen at Cornell again. I am committed to doing the necessary work to rebuild that confidence: regularly communicating and engaging about the work we have been doing and will do to build a culture of care and responsibility.”
The changes include re-evaluating policies towards drugs and alcohol on campus, programming changes in sexual assault and bystander intervention trainings, and hiring a new victim advocate to work in the school’s Sexual Harassment and Assault Response & Education (Share) office.
Kotlikoff’s letter came months after a woman named Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against several members of an on-campus fraternity who she said raped her after she was drugged in November of 2024. She filed a complaint with Cornell and the university police, but no criminal charges were filed.
Two members of the Chi Phi fraternity were expelled in connection with the case. The others were made to write essays, attend workshops or serve short suspensions.
All deny wrongdoing, while Jane Doe has expressed feeling unsupported and disbelieved by Kotlikoff.
New York attorney general Letitia James is now conducting an investigation into the case.
Cornell was also scheduled to hold a community meeting on Monday evening, followed by two follow-up “listening sessions” for campus community members and staff in the coming weeks.
“These will be opportunities for open, frank, face-to-face conversations – and for advancing the work we can only do together,” Kotlikoff wrote in a note.
In early October, Cornell tapped Sally Yates, a former high-ranking US justice department official, to review the school’s policies around sexual assault.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Saudi Arabia strategy challenged by anti-Houthi forces in Yemen
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Saudi Arabia has been accused by anti-Houthi forces over its military strategy after its Yemeni allies withdrew troops from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and pulled back forces from parts of Marib in the central part of the country.
The Saudi-backed government explained the repositioning by saying the strategic priority was to break the attritional siege on Taiz, Yemen’s third city, and to protect Aden, the southern port city in which the Saudi-backed and UN-recognised government is now based.
Many blame the Houthi advance on the absence of a consolidated military command and control among the disparate forces backing the Aden-based government. Saudi Arabia responded to the setback by sidelining the commander of its Yemen coalition, Lt Gen Fahd bin Abdulaziz al-Salman, and replacing him with the chief of staff, Gen Fayyad bin Hamed bin Ruqad al-Ruwaili.
The Houthis’ steady advance towards the areas surrounding Bab al-Mandab, the narrow strait linking the Red Sea with the Indian Ocean on Yemen’s west coast, culminated on Sunday with a formal withdrawal of Yemen government forces, including some in the Southern Giants Brigades that had always been reluctant to defend territory outside the old southern Yemen. In 1990 Yemen had been divided in two, and many in the south want to return to a separated state.
The Saudi-backed government launched a fresh military campaign 42 days ago to drive the Houthis from Yemen but so far it has backfired.
The forces redeployed on Sunday have moved along the coast to al-Suqyah, 95 miles west of Aden, and inside the old Southern Yemen.
The retreat seems to be acknowledgment of Houthi resilience and is all the more remarkable given the Saudi air superiority. More than 300,000 Yemeni civilians have been displaced.
Amr al-Bidh, special representative of the exiled Southern Transitional Council (STC) leader, Aidarous al-Zubaidi, a separatist anti-Houthi force that is opposed by Saudi Arabia, accused the Saudis of incompetence – and in effect warned Riyadh that unless it became more open to a southern state it would lack the cohesive forces required to prevent the Houthis becoming a permanent security threat.
He said: “When there is no strategy and no plan, it is inevitable the Houthis would take advantage. The STC will defend the south to the last man but we are fighting with one hand behind our backs since January after Saudi Arabia attacks on the STC.
“The STC forces retain a credible capability on the ground. But we need practical and political support from the region to counter the Houthis and create the basis for a negotiated settlement, one in which the pathway towards southern independence is fully recognised. We cannot continue like this or else the Houthis will keep expanding.”
The breadth of support for the STC, backed by the United Arab Emirates, however, remains disputed. The movement suffered a near fatal setback in January and since then some of the Giants Brigades have switched to backing Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia continues in effect to keep as many as 10 STC leaders hostage in Riyadh, and has refused to let al-Zubaidi to return from exile in Abu Dhabi. Al-Bidh argued the priority should be defensive, avoiding counteroffensives that backfire, improving command and control, and widening the coalition.
Al-Bidh said reconciliation would require Riyadh to acknowledge the political declaration al-Zubaidi made about a timetable for a southern state in January, and that al-Zubaidi’s return would boost morale and help unify chaotic southern military factions.
He said a recent Yemeni government cabinet reshuffle, including a new information minister, was designed primarily to try draw southerners into fighting the Houthis and not to change policy toward the south.
He also urged the UK to use its diplomacy to bring in other actors rather than simply backing Riyadh. A group of southern Yemenis have written to the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, seeking a review of UK policy. “We recognise that the longstanding advice from your office is to continue following the Saudi line while calling for unity among the anti-Houthi forces,” the letter said. “But you must surely recognise that every time Britain calls for ‘the unity and territorial integrity of Yemen’, it is asking the southern people and their armed forces to fight for a political outcome in which they do not believe”.
The former US special envoy to Yemen Tim Lenderking said the US administration was treating Yemen like a sideshow adding “world powers do not understand the gravity of what it is at stake here”. He warned “the problem is only going to get bigger through apathy and lack of attention”.
