https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.title: What Is ‘Affordable Housing’ in New York, and What Are My Options?
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.author: Samantha Maldonado
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.text:
New Yorkers know the struggle is real to secure housing that doesn’t eat up most of a paycheck — let alone is safe, comfortable and convenient.
According to the city’s 2023 Housing and Vacancy Survey, 18% of renters put between 30% and 50% of their income towards housing costs, and 25% spend more than half their income. And there is a 1.4% vacancy rate across the city, with even less availability for apartments with rents at the low end of the spectrum.
All that means what you already knew: the housing market is brutal. So while finding a cheap place to live requires as much luck as finding a needle in a haystack, there are options — and it’s important to know what those are and where to look for them.
What Is Affordable Housing, Anyway?
Typically, “affordable housing” means housing structured so tenants pay about one-third of their income toward rent. That threshold is determined by federal housing policy, which sets the tone and rules for the vast majority of affordable housing in New York.
“Affordable housing” is also a term often used for housing that is income-restricted — that is, set aside for people whose income falls within certain limits.
But there are many other things that are called “affordable housing.” It can also refer to housing that has lower-cost mortgage or leasing terms, or that receives some form of funding from taxpayers. With that comes regulations about how the buildings are governed — including how much rent can increase — and how people may qualify to live there.
There are many kinds of affordable housing options available in New York City — and many government programs that run them — and they can be hard to navigate.
“The way that it’s organized is driven by the programs, as opposed to, ‘I am a person looking for an apartment. What are the options?’” said Oksana Mironova, a housing policy analyst with the Community Service Society.
Let’s get into some of the big types of affordable housing available in New York City:
Rent-Stabilized Apartments
When you have a rent-stabilized apartment, rent is set and enforced by the government. These are privately-owned and operated apartments in all kinds of buildings.
Unlike rent-controlled apartments (more on those below), rent-stabilized apartments are pretty common. About one million apartments are rent-stabilized, which means they make up about a third of all rental apartments in the city.
The rent in these apartments is what the name implies: regulated. They are subject to rent increases not by the whim of the landlord, but through a vote by the Rent Guidelines Board once a year.
For the most part, you find these apartments like any other — through online listings, brokers or by word of mouth.
There are no income eligibility requirements for rent-stabilized apartments on the market — you apply like any other apartment. Some apartments that are rent-stabilized are not advertised as such.
In general, buildings of at least six apartments built before 1974 probably contain rent-stabilized apartments. The only way to know for sure is to request the rent history of your apartment from the state.
If you’re apartment-hunting, you can make a solid guess using this tool, or by looking at a compiled list of rent-stabilized buildings. But remember, rent-stabilization applies to the apartment, not the building.
Rent-Controlled Apartments
You may have also heard of apartments that are rent-controlled, which is different from rent-stabilization. Rent-controlled apartments are vanishingly rare. There are fewer than 20,000 rent-controlled apartments in the city, according to the Rent Guidelines Board.
Rent control generally applies to tenants in buildings constructed before 1947 who have lived in them since 1971. Unless you take over a rent-controlled apartment through succession rights — specific rules that allow a person to stay after the tenant on the lease dies — you’re unlikely to get one. That’s because when the tenant vacates the apartment, the rent may increase to the market-rate price. It may still be rent-stabilized, depending on the size and age of the building.
Affordable Rentals Through the NYC Housing Lottery
This is affordable housing you might get through the city-run housing lottery system, Housing Connect, and is often in newly constructed buildings where most of the apartments have market rate prices. Developers creating those new buildings build according to regulations that require them to build a certain number of affordable units within a for-profit complex.
To win a lottery apartment, you have to qualify based on your household size and income. These apartments are typically rent-stabilized.
You can also find affordable re-rentals without having to apply for the lottery. These are apartments that someone won through the lottery, but later vacated. Through April 2027, these apartments can be filled by qualified applicants on a first-come, first-served basis. You can apply to these like you would to any other apartment on the market, but you need to show you qualify based on your income and household size.
In addition, Housing Connect has lotteries for affordable homeownership opportunities — in other words, chances to buy a condo or co-op at a specific price for those whose income and household size allow them to qualify.
Affordable Rentals Through the New York State Housing Lottery
This is affordable housing you get through the state-run Housing Search. Eligibility is also determined by household size and income. Nabbing this state-financed housing is similar to the process of city-financed housing, and the offerings are similar, too.
HDFC Co-ops
HDFCs, or Housing Development Fund Corporation cooperatives, are apartment buildings where the owners — or shareholders — must make a certain amount of money. The requirements vary by individual building.
Once you get an apartment in an HDFC co-op, you may sell it at an appreciated value, but only up to a limited maximum. The seller won’t make a big profit, but that way, the affordability passes onto the next buyer. Plus, most HDFCs impose a flip tax, which means a percentage of profits from a sale go directly to the HDFC, to be invested in the building maintenance or for reserves.
For that reason, HDFCs are known as limited-equity or limited-profit cooperatives.
“The idea is, you purchase something relatively affordable to you and when you sell the apartment, you also sell for something that is affordable within the building’s guidelines,” said Arielle Hersh, director of policy at the Urban Homesteading Assistance Board. “It is not meant to be an investment.”
There are more than 1,200 HDFC co-ops across the city, according to UHAB.
You can find some HDFCs through Housing Connect, though others are listed like any other apartment, such as on Streeteasy. The Urban Homesteading Assistance Board, which works with HDFCs, posts available apartments on its website.
Mitchell-Lama Cooperatives
Mitchell-Lamas are apartment buildings that, like HDFCs, require income limitations for interested applicants. But the sale prices tend to be even cheaper than HDFCs, since sellers can only sell for the price they originally paid plus capital assessments (and possibly mortgage amortization).
“When the shareholder leaves the apartment, for whatever reason, and they give up the shares back to the co-op, the way it usually works, there is no profit,” said Adele Niederman, president of Cooperators United for Mitchell-Lama. “They only get back what they invested when they purchased it.”
The state oversees some Mitchell-Lamas, while the city oversees others.
Interested applicants for city-supervised Mitchell-Lama co-ops must enter a lottery to get on a waiting list. Once on the waiting list, it could take many years to be chosen to purchase an apartment.
Cooperators United hosts workshops and informational events for those interested in learning more about Mitchell-Lamas, which you can find here.
NYCHA
The New York City Housing Authority oversees public housing where tenants pay 30% of their income for rent. More than 350,000 New Yorkers live in public housing.
You can apply to be considered for an apartment here.
NYCHA may reach out to applicants for an interview. It’s hard to know when or if applicants might get an interview “because of of the extremely large size of the waitlist and low vacancy rate,” NYCHA warns. Over 10,800 families are on the wait list for public housing, according to NYCHA data.
Vouchers
Vouchers provide help in paying for an apartment, and there are many different types, funded by many levels of government. A significant share are for those facing specific challenges or in certain situations, such as for people who are living with HIV or AIDS.
Barika Williams, executive director of the Association for Neighborhood and Housing Development, offered advice for those who need to find housing they can afford.
“If you’re already getting some sort of services, support, aid, consultation from somebody in the city or state government, ask them,” she said. “They’re going to start by giving you the program you’re eligible for based on an issue you have.”
Here are some of the largest voucher programs.
Housing Choice Vouchers – Section 8
Section 8, which is also known as the Housing Choice Voucher Program, is a federally funded rental-assistance program for low-income New Yorkers administered by NYCHA. Over 109,000 families receive a Housing Choice Voucher through NYCHA, which allow tenants to rent an apartment on the private market. Tenants typically pay a third of their income for rent, with the voucher covering the rest.
To be eligible for Section 8 vouchers, you must have a household income below a certain threshold.
NYCHA re-opened the waitlist to get a Section 8 voucher briefly in July. After being selected from the waitlist, applicants must complete an interview before they get vouchers. Nearly 194,000 applicants are on the waiting list for Section 8 housing.
Housing Choice Vouchers are on pause — meaning those on the waiting list can’t be pulled off it — in the wake of federal funding cuts.
Another type of Section 8 voucher is a Project-Based Voucher. The subsidy is tied to an apartment, not a tenant, though the eligible tenant will still pay a third of their income in rent.
Freeze Your Rent
Senior citizens and people with disabilities who live in rent-regulated housing can freeze their rents through programs known as the Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption and Disabled Rent Increase Exemption. Through this program, eligible tenants can keep their rents at the current amount and their landlords receive a tax abatement credit.
Find out more here about the programs, including eligibility requirements and how to apply.
CityFHEPS
The City Fighting Homelessness and Eviction Prevention Supplement is a city-funded voucher program that provides rental assistance anywhere in New York state for up to five years. Typically tenants pay 30% of their monthly income towards rent, with the voucher covering the remaining costs.
The maximum rent depends on the household size, number of bedrooms and the county where the apartment is located — for instance, about $3,058 for a two-bedroom for a family of four in New York City.
CityFHEPS is for individuals and families facing eviction and have previously been in the shelter system, or are living in a homeless shelter.
Here’s a guide on how to find housing with a CityFHEPS voucher.
The city created another form of vouchers through the City Housing Assistance Program, which will begin next year. The vouchers are for a slightly more expansive set of New Yorkers than those who qualify for CityFHEPS, including tenants living in rent-stabilized apartments and facing eviction, and those in a wider variety of shelters.
FHEPS — not to be confused with CityFHEPS — is another voucher program, but run by the state. It’s designed for families with children who receive cash assistance who are facing eviction or have been evicted, or lost housing because of a health or safety issue like domestic violence.
Other Programs
There are many other programs to keep rent affordable for senior citizens and people with disabilities.
For example, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development provides funding to build and subsidize rental housing where rent is capped at 30% of income for qualifying residents through its Section 202 and Section 811 programs. Eligible New Yorkers can apply for these programs through the service providers that manage the housing developments, like New York Foundation for Senior Citizens or the Met Council.

https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.title: What is Area Median Income? The Magic Number Behind Affordable Housing Math in NYC
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.author: Samantha Maldonado
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.text:
A Murray Hill two-bedroom for $4,518. A Marble Hill one-bedroom for $3,180. A Flatbush studio for $2,022.
These were some recent affordable housing offerings in the city’s lottery system.
But those rents aren’t exactly cheap. You might ask, affordable for whom?
In New York City, affordable housing — at least what’s in the housing lottery — is housing where the rent is set at about one-third of household income and receives some sort of government subsidy. The affordable housing in the lottery is rent-stabilized, meaning its price can increase only in increments as approved by the Rent Guidelines Board.
But affordable housing is not necessarily housing only for low-income people.
“Affordable housing is for all income levels and sizes,” said Shaheem Taylor, a lottery marketing outreach coordinator at the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, during a Housing Connect webinar earlier this year. “Regardless of whether you make $10,000, $0, six figures, $50,000 — there are lotteries that are allocated to everyone.”
Read on to understand why some of the city’s affordable housing may appear rather expensive, and what it means for your Housing Connect application:
How the Rent Is Set: Understanding AMI, or Area Median Income
Affordable housing in New York City may be tied to your household’s income, but the measure used to determine an affordable building’s income categories is based on a federally set figure that’s based on rents, not the actual money a household earns.
Confused? Stick with us, because that figure — the area median income, or AMI — is really important to understanding your next application to New York’s housing lottery.
Each year, the federal Department of Housing and Urban Development sets the area median income, or AMI, for the New York City area, which includes the five boroughs as well as Putnam, Rockland, and Westchester counties. The AMI is a federal measure based on rents in the area, not on actual household earnings. Elsewhere, AMI is based on actual incomes, but in our area, HUD considers rent in the calculation because with high housing costs, more people — at higher incomes — would need access to affordable housing.
There is one AMI for the whole city, so the AMI for, say, the Upper East Side or Riverdale is the same for Elmhurst or Brownsville.
Why is the AMI so important? Because when beginning to develop new affordable housing, the city housing agency creates categories of income ranges as a percentage of the AMI, then sets the rents based on them. (Remember, affordable housing means residents spend no more than 30% of their income on housing costs.)
That’s why on Housing Connect, you see listings that say things like, applicants for a certain apartment must not earn more than, let’s say, 60% of the area median income, or 100% of the area median income.
The AMI is the maximum a household is allowed to earn for a given affordable apartment, with rents pegged to be no more than 30% of that number.
So what does that look like? Here’s where the AMI is set in 2026:
- 100% of New York’s AMI was $118,800 for an individual and $169,600 for a family of four.
- 30% of the AMI was $35,640 for an individual and $50,880 for a family of four.
- 130% of the AMI was $154,440 for an individual and $220,480 for a family of four.
If those numbers look high to you — remember, they do not reflect actual incomes in New York City. They reflect market-rate rents in city and nearby counties.
Based on census data, the actual median income for a household in New York City is about $81,000. A family of three with that income would fall somewhere between 50% and 60% of the AMI.
Why Are Some ‘Affordable’ Apartments So Expensive?
Remember how AMI in the New York City area reflects rents rather than actual incomes? The thinking behind that, as HUD sees it, is because rent is so expensive here that more people across a wider range of incomes should be eligible for affordable housing.
But it also can mean that sometimes the affordable housing is not exactly accessible for lower-income New Yorkers — and the prices can rival traditional, market-rate units for potential tenants who have higher incomes.
Chris Walters, a land use policy coordinator at nonprofit Association for Neighborhood and Housing Development, pointed out that as the AMI figures rise each year, so do the rents for affordable apartments.
“As the AMI numbers have increased every year, at the higher end you start to get into rents that border on market-rate in some neighborhoods, or even exceed them,” Walters said.
That means rents go up at both the top income levels and at the bottom, which means the rents can feel out of reach for the lowest-earning households.
Let’s look at some numbers.
Housing Connect advertised a studio for $2,022 in Flatbush — reserved for people making 80% AMI, or between $75,772.00 to $95,040 for an individual. It’s a new building with air conditioning, a dishwasher and in-unit laundry. But on the same block, you could find a studio on the open market listed for $1,875. It’s in a pre-war elevator building and lacks the previous amenities, but there are no income restrictions.
North of there, in Crown Heights, one building on Housing Connect offered two-bedrooms for $4,518 — affordable at 130% of AMI, or for a family of four earning between $162,446 and $220,480. A two-bedroom apartment in the same building that’s not considered affordable is listed on the open market for about $5,000. But a household looking for a two-bedroom just a couple blocks away could find one on the market for $2,750 or $3,300.
Lowest Rents, Biggest Squeeze
Because affordable housing means paying about a third of income towards rent, what that means in practice feels different for different household budgets.
Take a household that makes $100,000 a year. That family would pay about $30,000 annually for rent, with $70,000 left over for other expenses. But if a household makes $45,000 and pays $13,500 annually for rent, that household has just $31,500 left over for all other expenses.
“There’s a big discrepancy between what’s left over for everything else, and that can also make something feel less affordable even if it is ‘affordable,’” said Emily Kurtz, chief housing officer at affordable housing provider RiseBoro Community Partnership.
That math may change, if City Hall under Mayor Zohran Mamdani keeps its promise. His administration in May committed to changing the calculation for rent in affordable housing for New Yorkers at the lowest income levels. For those at 30% of AMI — or $50,880 for a family of four — the rent will be set at no more than a quarter of household income. That’d be around $1,060 per month for that family.
If ‘Affordable’ Apartments Are So Expensive, What’s the Point of Trying To Get One?
Some New Yorkers may see the rents of some lottery units and say, no thanks, that’s not a deal.
But experts point out that affordable apartments are rent stabilized, so while the rent may be expensive in the first year or two, it won’t grow at the same rate as market-rate rents could. Over time, that really adds up.
“The value of having regulated apartments is that the rents stay relatively low as income grows, as other rents grow. But year one, your rent might feel very tight,” Kurtz said.
Also: Rent-stabilized tenants have some of the strongest rights against eviction in the country.
Who Decides On Levels of Affordability and Why?
Developers take multiple factors into consideration as they plan their affordable housing projects. It’s a complicated process because each financing source has different restrictions based on what kind of housing is being developed. Developers can also take advantage of incentives, whether tax abatements or being allowed to build bigger, in exchange for including a certain number of affordable apartments for prescribed income levels
And lots of affordable housing is subsidized, meaning the government throws in taxpayer funding.
“You start to layer, and that’s why affordable housing is so complex, because you’re layering, layering, layering to get as many sources as you can so that you can have very low-income units and workforce housing units,” Kurtz said.
Apartments set at lower rents need more subsidy, and HPD must figure out how to use its money to balance creating as many affordable apartments as possible.
Developers must consider how much it costs not only to build the project, but also to operate and maintain them as costs — like insurance and utilities — rise. Developers must make sure the projects pencil out. In other words, the math needs to math.
Developers also consider the project’s income. The lower the affordability — so AMIs of, say, 30% or 50% instead of 100% or higher — the more limited the rental income a developer can take in.
Taking in more rent means the project can take on more private debt and lean less on public subsidy. And the opposite is true: when a project becomes more affordable to renters it usually needs more public subsidy.
Public subsidies are limited, and require tough choices.
“It’s a public policy decision of how to use subsidy resources and and how to both make those go as far as possible, but also reach the levels of deep affordability that the city clearly needs,” said Patrick Boyle, senior policy director at Enterprise Community Partners. “Reaching lower-income people and making housing affordable to residents takes more subsidy. That’s the trade-off in the calculation.”

https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.title: How Our Newsroom Estimated NYC Housing Lottery Odds
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.author: Kennedy Sessions
https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2026/11/.text:
Over the last few months, The City Reporter reviewed data from the Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s Local Law 217 Report, summarizing housing lottery outcomes from Jan. 1, 2022, through Oct. 31, 2024. Our analysis calculated the approximate odds of the more than 10.9 million applications submitted through the city’s Housing Connect portal.
The report shows outcomes based on household size, income, and race. HPD categorizes applicant numbers by whether they are a city resident, the borough where the applicant lived, and the community board where they resided at the time they applied. It also breaks down the housing lottery stages, including the number of initial applications, selected applications, signed leases, and rejected applications.
HPD said it has redacted the number of approved applications and leases for privacy reasons in cases where fewer than 10 applications have been approved.
To test our methodology, we spoke with an expert who previously worked with HPD data. They confirmed our methodology and agreed that Local Law 217 data provides the best historical basis for analyzing applicants’ odds. In our previous 2020 housing lottery analysis, we analyzed two HPD datasets of affordable housing lotteries and more than 20 million lottery applications. We didn’t use this methodology in this analysis because HPD declined to give us the data, despite multiple requests.
For this analysis, we calculated the win rate by dividing the number of signed leases by the number of applications.
Win Rate = # of Signed Leases / # of Applications
Then, to find the odds rate by community board, we divided the win rate by 1. These numbers are estimated odds per application.
The data only includes the community districts from which an applicant resided at the time of submission — not the community district where the development they applied for is located. The odds map therefore reflects the chances of winning the lottery for residents applying from a particular neighborhood.
Odds = 1 / Win Rate
There are some other important points:
- Each household can make one application to each lottery. Members of the same household cannot make separate, individual applications.
- Area Median Income bands are defined every year by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
- This analysis does not include the various preferences that factor into the housing lottery, including those for people with a disability, municipal workers, and NYCHA residents, among others.
To calculate the number of units available in housing lotteries from July 30, 2020 to November 2, 2026, we used HPD’s database, Advertised Lotteries on Housing Connect. With this dataset, we calculated the number of advertised lotteries based on their designated income band.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ar.title: Arta Moves Beyond Shipping Art, to Helping Collectors Pay for It
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ar.author: Daniel Cassady
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/ar.text:
For years, Arta has helped collectors get art from a gallery or an auction house to their homes. Now, it wants to help them pay for it, too.
The New York–based technology company has launched Arta Pay, a new financing service that allows collectors to buy art, watches, jewelry, and other luxury goods on credit, paying for them over 10 months while sellers receive the full purchase price within days.
The service offers credit lines ranging from $1,000 to more than $100,000, targeting a part of the market that has often fallen between conventional consumer financing and the large art loans offered by private banks.
Here’s how it works: A collector buying a $10,000 painting would put down at least 10 percent, or $1,000, and pay the remaining balance in nine monthly installments. There’s a flat financing charge of 12.5 percent on the amount borrowed, disclosed upfront. In this example, that would add $1,125 to the cost of the painting if the buyer takes the full nine months to repay it.
The gallery, meanwhile, gets its $10,000 within five business days, without having to worry about collecting the remaining payments. Arta takes on the repayment and fraud risk, and charges sellers no processing fees.
“We’ve spent years building the post-purchase technology that powers commerce across art, luxury, and collectibles,” Adam Fields, Arta’s founder and CEO, said. The new service, he added, is designed to make the transactions easier.
Arta has become a familiar name behind the scenes of the art market, providing shipping, insurance, and other logistical services to auction houses, galleries, and online marketplaces. Its clients include Sotheby’s, Bonhams, and Artsy, and the company says it has facilitated the movement of more than $1 billion worth of objects across more than 65 countries.
The move into financing brings Arta into an earlier stage of the transaction, when a collector is deciding whether to buy something in the first place.
For galleries, the attraction is fairly straightforward. Many already allow trusted clients to pay in installments, but doing so can mean waiting months to receive the full price of a work. Arta Pay gives them a way to offer similar flexibility without extending credit themselves.
The service can be used at online checkouts, in person, or through an ordinary invoice, a useful feature in a business where plenty of sales are still negotiated over email, WhatsApp, or a conversation at an art fair. Collectors can also apply for a credit line before deciding what to buy, using it across purchases from different sellers.
Among the first businesses to adopt the service are Rago Wright, the auction house group, and Swiss Watch Expo.
“Our collectors want flexibility in how they buy, and Arta Pay gives them that,” Richard Wright, CEO of Rago Wright, said in a statement. For the auction house, he added, the advantage is offering payment plans without having to manage the financing or assume the risk.
The idea isn’t entirely new. Art Money, another company that allowed collectors to buy art in installments, stopped taking new business in June 2024 after running out of operating capital. Its founder, Paul Becker, is now managing director of Arta Pay, and several former Art Money employees have joined the operation. Fields told ARTnews that the two businesses are separate, but argued that Arta has an advantage in its established technology platform and relationships with major art-market businesses.
That existing network is central to Arta’s plans. Rather than building a financing business from scratch, the company is adding another service to a platform already used by galleries, auction houses, and collectors.
For now, Arta Pay is available to US citizens and residents, although they can use it to buy from participating sellers overseas. Applications take a few minutes, and most applicants receive a decision in real time following a soft credit check. The credit lines are issued by Lead Bank, with Arta handling the service.
The question, of course, is whether giving collectors another way to spread out the cost of buying art will encourage them to buy more of it. For dealers who would rather spend their time selling paintings than chasing payments, the appeal is obvious.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Museu Nacional da Bíblia: Tribunal de Contas do DF mantém suspensa obra orçada em R$ 120 milhões
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Kennedy Cruz
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A construção do Museu Nacional da Bíblia, prevista para o Eixo Monumental, em Brasília, está no centro de questionamentos do Tribunal de Contas do Distrito Federal (TCDF). A Corte decidiu, por unanimidade, manter suspensa a contratação da obra e cobrar explicações do governo sobre três pontos principais: a escolha de um projeto arquitetônico que ficou em segundo lugar em concurso público, o aumento das estimativas de custo e a previsão de construção de um anfiteatro em área próxima ao museu.
A decisão foi tomada na última quarta-feira (11) e também estendeu a proibição de contratação à Secretaria de Obras do Distrito Federal (SODF). Com isso, tanto a pasta quanto a Secretaria de Cultura e Economia Criativa (Secec) ficam impedidas de avançar com a contratação da execução da obra até nova manifestação do Tribunal.
O processo teve origem em questionamentos apresentados pelos deputados distritais Gabriel Magno (PT) e Fábio Felix (Psol), que acionaram o TCDF em 2025. Os parlamentares contestaram a escolha do projeto, a evolução dos custos e as condições previstas para a implantação do equipamento cultural. Na avaliação do Tribunal, os pontos levantados ainda precisam ser esclarecidos pelo governo.
Um dos principais questionamentos envolve a decisão do governo de optar pelo projeto Orla 013, que ficou em segundo lugar no concurso público de arquitetura, em vez do Orla 014, vencedor da seleção. O relator do processo, conselheiro Renato Rainha, apontou contradições nas justificativas apresentadas pela administração.
Isso porque critérios como economicidade, viabilidade e exequibilidade técnico-construtiva já haviam sido considerados pela comissão julgadora durante o concurso. O Tribunal quer que o governo explique por que esses aspectos foram utilizados posteriormente para justificar a escolha de uma proposta diferente daquela que recebeu a primeira colocação.
O TCDF também pediu esclarecimentos sobre alterações de área e volumetria dos projetos e sobre a cessão dos direitos autorais dos arquitetos. A Secec e a Secretaria de Obras terão prazo de 30 dias para apresentar as respostas e os fundamentos que embasaram a decisão.
Estimativas de custo
Outro ponto que motivou a fiscalização foi a diferença entre os valores apresentados ao longo do planejamento do empreendimento. Os projetos participantes do concurso tinham estimativas de custo entre R$ 21,45 milhões e R$ 28,07 milhões.
Em documentos posteriores, a Secretaria de Obras apresentou valores de R$ 119,08 milhões, calculados pelo método do Custo Unitário Básico (CUB), e R$ 122,39 milhões, por estimativa paramétrica. O Tribunal cobra explicações sobre a metodologia utilizada, as mudanças no escopo da obra e os critérios considerados nos cálculos.
A Secec havia informado uma economia estimada de aproximadamente R$ 6,6 milhões com a escolha do projeto Orla 013. O TCDF quer entender como essa justificativa se relaciona com as estimativas apresentadas posteriormente pela Secretaria de Obras.
O documento de análise encaminhado pelo gabinete do deputado Gabriel Magno ressalta que a diferença entre os valores, por si só, não comprova irregularidade financeira. “A diferença entre estimativas não demonstra, isoladamente, sobrepreço ou dano ao erário. Constitui, contudo, matéria de fiscalização quanto ao objeto considerado, à metodologia de cálculo e à motivação da seleção do projeto”, destaca o documento.
Em publicação conjunta nas redes sociais, Gabriel Magno e Fábio Felix criticaram a elevação dos custos e a escolha da proposta que ficou em segundo lugar. “Os indícios são graves: estimativas que começaram em R$ 21 milhões agora ultrapassam R$ 120 milhões! O GDF ainda deu preferência ao projeto que ficou em segundo lugar no concurso público, ignorando o vencedor”, escreveram.
Anfiteatro e regras urbanísticas
Além do projeto do museu, o Tribunal questiona a previsão de construção de um anfiteatro de 1.661 metros quadrados em uma área próxima ao equipamento cultural. A estrutura está associada a um contrato de repasse de R$ 14,29 milhões e, segundo a representação dos parlamentares, não fazia parte do objeto original do concurso de arquitetura.
Um parecer técnico da Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Urbano e Habitação (Seduh), de 2025, apontou possíveis incompatibilidades da estrutura com as regras de ocupação e preservação do Conjunto Urbanístico de Brasília. Entre os problemas identificados estão a possível ocupação de faixa non aedificandi, área em que construções são restritas, e a extrapolação do limite de ocupação do canteiro central do Eixo Monumental.
O parecer também indicou possível incompatibilidade com o Plano de Preservação do Conjunto Urbanístico de Brasília (PPCUB), instituído pela Lei Complementar distrital nº 1.041/2024. Diante dos apontamentos, o TCDF abriu prazo para manifestações da Seduh, do Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan), do Conselho de Planejamento Territorial e Urbano do Distrito Federal (Conplan) e do Conselho de Defesa do Patrimônio Cultural do Distrito Federal (Condepac).
A Secretaria de Obras também deverá esclarecer se o empreendimento é compatível com os instrumentos de planejamento e orçamento público, como a Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA), o Plano Plurianual (PPA), a Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias (LDO) e a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal (LRF).
Deputados cobram explicações
Os parlamentares comemoraram a manutenção da suspensão e afirmaram que continuarão acompanhando o processo. Gabriel Magno classificou a decisão como uma vitória da fiscalização e criticou a mudança na escolha arquitetônica.
“Não é aceitável que o governo realize um concurso, escolha um vencedor e depois decida executar outro projeto sem apresentar justificativas consistentes. Mais grave ainda é ver uma obra inicialmente estimada em pouco mais de R$ 20 milhões aparecer com estimativas superiores a R$ 120 milhões. O dinheiro público precisa ser tratado com seriedade, transparência e responsabilidade”, afirmou o parlamentar.
Fábio Felix também questionou a destinação de recursos para o empreendimento diante das demandas do Distrito Federal. “O Distrito Federal tem prioridades urgentes que precisam ser respeitadas. Não podemos admitir que milhões de reais sejam comprometidos em uma obra cercada de questionamentos técnicos, jurídicos e orçamentários”, destacou.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120391.title: Gaza-Krieg | Andauernder Krieg trotz Waffenruhe
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120391.author: Cyrus Salimi-Asl
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120391.text:
- Politik
- Gaza-Krieg
Andauernder Krieg trotz Waffenruhe
Im Gazastreifen sterben weiter Menschen durch Bomben, und die Behörden lassen benötigte Hilfsgüter nur spärlich hinein. Was macht der »Friedensrat«?
Was im Gazastreifen passiert, interessiert die Weltöffentlichkeit derzeit nur marginal. Die Aufmerksamkeit ist ganz auf den Regierungsbildungsprozess in Israel gerichtet, wo Oppositionsführer Gadi Eisenkot versucht, eine Koalition zu schmieden. Darüber scheinen viele zu vergessen, dass im Gazastreifen noch immer Krieg herrscht. Beinah jeden Tag greift die israelische Armee Ziele an, obwohl seit dem 10. Oktober vergangenen Jahres formal eine Waffenruhe gilt. Die wurde jedoch vor allem von Israel systematisch gebrochen. Dessen Regierung nimmt sich weiter das Recht heraus, nach eigenem Ermessen dieses oder jenes Gebäude zu bombardieren und mit der üblichen Phrase zu rechtfertigen: Der Angriff habe Hamas-Kämpfern gegolten.
Ob das den Tatsachen entspricht, kann in der Regel niemand unabhängig überprüfen. Dazu kommt, dass bei diesen Angriffen regelmäßig »Kollateralschäden« hingenommen werden: unbeteiligte Zivilisten, die sich zufällig in der Nähe aufhielten und mit in den Tod gerissen werden. So sind nach den jüngsten Angaben des Gesundheitsministeriums in Gaza seit Beginn der Waffenruhe mehr als 1600 Menschen getötet worden. Insgesamt wurden nach dem Hamas-Massaker vom 7. Oktober 2023 fast 75.000 Menschen im Gazastreifen durch die israelische Armee getötet. Die Dunkelziffer geht von weit mehr als 100.000 aus, da viele Leichen noch unter den Trümmern begraben liegen. In ganz Gaza soll es geschätzt mindestens 64.000 Witwen und 71.000 Waisenkinder geben.
Am Montag enthüllte die britische Tageszeitung »The Guardian«, dass das israelische Militär 3,5 Millionen Fotos von Palästinensern auf die Cloud-Plattform von Amazon mit dem Ziel der Gesichtserkennung hochgeladen habe. Durchgesickerten Dokumenten zufolge sei dieser Bildbestand zu Beginn der Luftangriffe und Bodenoffensive Israels im Gazastreifen in die Amazon-Cloud übertragen worden.
Den Unterlagen und Gesprächen mit Militärs zufolge hat Israel in den vergangenen Jahren riesige Datenmengen – darunter sensibles nachrichtendienstliches Material sowie Informationen über Palästinenser, die unter Besatzung leben – in die Rechenzentren von Amazon verlagert. Die große Anzahl entspricht praktisch allen in den besetzten Gebieten lebenden Palästinensern über 15 Jahren.
Erst am Sonntag hatte die israelische Armee bei einem erneuten Angriff einen angeblich ranghohen Kommandeur der radikalislamischen Hamas getötet: Samir Abu Junis. Die Ezzedin-Al-Qassam-Brigaden, bewaffneter Arm der Hamas, erklärten daraufhin auf Telegram, Abu Junis sei Opfer eines »feigen Mord-Einsatzes« geworden. Das israelische Militär und der Inlandsgeheimdienst Schin Bet sprachen von einem Angriff auf einen »ranghohen Terroristen des militärischen Flügels der Hamas«. Der Angriff erfolgte nach Angaben aus Sicherheitskreisen in Al-Mawasi westlich von Khan Junis.
Der Sprecher des von der Hamas kontrollierten Zivilschutzes, Mahmud Bassal, sagte der Nachrichtenagentur AFP, seine Behörde habe die Leiche des 53-jährigen Junis in Empfang genommen. Bei dem israelischen Angriff seien zudem zwei Menschen verletzt worden.
Erst vor wenigen Tagen war das Al-Nasser-Krankenhaus angegriffen worden, bei dem nach palästinensischen Angaben mindestens sechs Menschen getötet wurden. Da das humanitäre Völkerrecht Krankenhäuser in besonderer Weise schützt, könnte der Angriff auch als Kriegsverbrechen zu werten sein. Die Hilfsorganisation Ärzte ohne Grenzen macht Israel schwere Vorwürfe: »Nichts rechtfertigt weder rechtlich noch moralisch den Angriff auf und die Zerstörung eines funktionierenden Krankenhauses mit zahlreichen Patienten und Behandelnden wie dem Nasser-Krankenhaus«, heißt es in einer Mitteilung. Das Handeln der israelischen Armee habe weiterhin Tag für Tag verheerende Auswirkungen auf die Zivilbevölkerung.
Da fragt man sich: Was macht eigentlich der von US-Präsident Donald Trump eingesetzte »Friedensrat«, dessen Aufgabe es ist, die Waffenruhe zu begleiten und durchzusetzen sowie den Wiederaufbau anzuleiten? Nur selten macht er von sich reden. Vergangenen Woche hat er sich zumindest zu den Auswirkungen der gravierenden Überflutungen im Gazastreifen geäußert: »Die dringende Bereitstellung und Verteilung von grundlegenden Hilfsgütern – etwa für Notunterkünfte, sanitäre Anlagen, Entwässerung sowie weitere Maßnahmen zur Winterfestmachung – ist entscheidend für den Schutz von Zivilistenleben«, erklärte das »Board of Peace« in einer Stellungnahme.
Doch tatsächlich Einfluss nehmen auf die israelische Seite kann (oder will) der Friedensrat offenbar nicht. Die israelische Cogat-Behörde hält lebensnotwendige Güter und technisches Gerät an den Grenzübergängen zum Gazastreifen zurück, unter anderem Pumpen zum Abpumpen des Wassers aus den überfluteten Zeltstädten. Seinen Verpflichtungen aus dem Waffenstillstandsabkommen kommt die israelische Seite jedenfalls nicht nach, wie die israelische Tageszeitung »Haaretz« belegt. Nach Daten des israelischen Militärs wurde demnach seit März monatlich nur etwa die Hälfte der vereinbarten Menge an humanitären und kommerziellen Gütern in den Gazastreifen gelassen.
Den Daten zufolge gebe es ein zunehmendes Defizit bei Lebensmittellieferungen sowie einen gravierenden Mangel an medizinischem Bedarf, Zelten und Materialien für die Reparatur beschädigter Infrastruktur. Laut dem Waffenstillstandsabkommen sollte Israel pro Monat etwa 18.200 Lastwagen in den Gazastreifen lassen.
Doch wie die Nachrichtenwebseite »Middle East Eye« berichtet, sollen Daten, die die israelische Cogat-Behörde dem von den USA geführten »International Gaza Support Center« übermittelt hat, zeigen, dass Israel im März etwa 4700 Lastwagen in den Gazastreifen ließ, im April 5300 und im Mai mehr als 9600. Im September erreichten die Lieferungen demnach mit mehr als 13.000 einen Höchststand, fielen jedoch im Oktober wieder auf etwas mehr als 6500 ab.
Großbritannien, Italien, Kanada und Australien haben Israel am Sonntag in einer gemeinsamen Erklärung aufgefordert, einen »raschen und ungehinderten« der humanitären Hilfe Zugang zum Gazastreifen zu ermöglichen. Die Lage sei »furchtbar«, heißt es dort, und die jüngsten Regenfälle hätten »noch mehr Leid gebracht«. »Die Menschen im Gazastreifen brauchen dringend Unterkunft und humanitäre Unterstützung«, stellten die vier Länder fest. Doch würden »150.000 Zelte und andere lebenswichtige Hilfe« an der Grenze zum Gazastreifen zurückgehalten. Sie riefen Israel auf, dies noch vor dem Winter zu ändern. Deutschland hat sich dagegen entschlossen, Israel bei der Kontrolle der Hilfslieferungen zu helfen und hat Scanner für Lastwagen zur Verfügung gestellt. Mit Agenturen

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/pi.title: Video Artist Pipilotti Rist Wins MIT’s $100,000 Arts Award
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/pi.author: Alex Greenberger
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/pi.text:
Pipilotti Rist, one of the most widely acclaimed living video artists, has another feather in her cap in the form of next year’s Eugene McDermott Award in the Arts, a prize given out by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology that comes with $100,000 and a residency on campus.
The Swiss artist is known for phantasmagoric installations that have harnessed video technology to explore the human body in all its many forms. Often working with a heavy dose of humor, Rist has thoughtfully used her camera to explore sexuality, sleep states, and the female form.
Today, she is perhaps best known for her 1997 video installation Ever Is Over All, in which a woman walks down a city street and smashes in car windows with flowers. The work was memorably retooled in the visual album for Beyoncé’s Lemonade.
“I am kissing your Institute and your feet,” Rist said in a statement about the MIT award. “I am immensely touched and grateful to have this trust and investment in ideas I’ve yet to conceive. I’m honored to receive an award that has been granted to so many of my heroes, and look forward to collaborating closely with the brilliant minds at MIT.”
Her past achievements include representing Switzerland at the Venice Biennale in 2005 and a retrospective that appeared at New York’s New Museum in 2016. According to the website for Hauser & Wirth, the mega-gallery that represents her alongside New York’s Luhring Augustine, Rist will stage a permanent installation at the long-awaited Guggenheim Abu Dhabi when it opens in December.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Clássicos, biografias, livros sagrados e até álbum de figurinhas da Copa: veja o que Nicolás Maduro lê na prisão
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Leonardo Fernandes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Ao longo da história, lideranças políticas contra-hegemônicas foram submetidas a circunstâncias que as obrigaram a se apartar fisicamente das lutas que compunham. Vladimir Lenin foi ao exílio antes de consolidar a Revolução Bolchevique de 1917, assim como Fidel Castro o fez prévio ao desembarque do navio Granma, dando início à gloriosa revolução cubana. Pepe Mujica passou mais de 14 anos nos calabouços da ditadura uruguaia. Mandela sobreviveu a 27 anos de penúria nas masmorras do apartheid.
Recompor as forças, escrever, elaborar, estudar, se exercitar: quantas coisas uma mente brilhante pode fazer ao ver-se privada de ser livre?
No dia 3 de janeiro de 2026, Nicolás Maduro Moros, presidente da República Bolivariana da Venezuela, foi sequestrado em sua residência, nas imediações do Forte Tiúna, no sul da capital, Caracas, após o governo dos Estados Unidos ordenar um ataque militar que resultou em mais de uma centena de mortos.
Maduro e sua esposa, a deputada Cilia Flores, foram levados ao Distrito Sul de Nova York, onde aguardam julgamento por acusações de vínculo com o narcotráfico e corrupção, das quais alegam inocência. “Sou o presidente da Venezuela e me considero um prisioneiro de guerra”, declarou o chefe de Estado venezuelano durante sua primeira audiência à justiça estadunidense.
Nesses mais de dez meses em que está na prisão, seu filho, que leva o mesmo nome, Nicolás Ernesto, tem tratado de aliviar a solidão do cárcere com chamadas telefônicas diárias e o envio permanente de livros, que já somam mais de 200 exemplares. O Brasil de Fato e o portal argentino El Grito del Sur tiveram acesso com exclusividade à lista completa de obras recebidas por Maduro, que incluem história e pensamento latino-americano, religiões, literatura, filosofia e até um álbum de figurinhas da Copa do Mundo.
Entre os volumes estão textos sobre Simón Bolívar, a biografia do cantor e militante Alí Primera, obras sobre Fidel Castro e compilações sobre a Constituição da Venezuela. A história dos Estados Unidos e de seus líderes também ocupa espaço relevante, com livros sobre Donald Trump, Martin Luther King Jr., os nativos americanos e a história constitucional daquele país.
A religiosidade e o pensamento filosófico aparecem em grande proporção na lista. A coleção reúne desde a Torá e o Talmud até a Bíblia e encíclicas do Papa Francisco. Há também estudos dedicados a figuras como Santo Tomás de Aquino, São Francisco de Assis e escrituras da tradição dos essênios, além de obras sobre o pensamento oriental, como o Tao Te Ching e o Bhagavad Gita.
Na literatura, constam clássicos universais como Dom Quixote, Cem Anos de Solidão, Os Miseráveis e 1984. O acervo aborda ainda discussões contemporâneas sobre tecnologia e economia, incluindo ensaios sobre inteligência artificial, redes de informação, economia global e transição ecológica.
Além dos temas teóricos, o levantamento inclui manuais de saúde, guias de meditação, dicionários de idiomas e livros de calistenia. A lista surpreende ao registrar itens de lazer e artesanato, como tutoriais de crochê e amigurumi, coleções de quadrinhos e livros de passatempos.

Ausstellung würdigt Fotokünstlerin: Selbst knipst die Frau
Die vor 150 Jahren geborene Käthe Buchler verstand sich stets als Profi-Fotografin. Braunschweig widmet ihr nun eine Ausstellung samt Symposion.
Das Jahr 2026 bietet Anlass, einige Jubiläen der Fotografie zu begehen. Vor 200 Jahren kam das Medium auf, in noch experimentellem Stadium: Das älteste bekannte und erhaltene Foto der Welt, der Blick aus einem Fenster seines Hauses in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes, wurde wohl 1826 von Joseph Nicéphore Niépce mit in einer Camera obscura festgehalten. Nicht ganz so alt, dafür exakt datierbar, sind Leben und Werk zweier deutscher Pionier:innen der Fotografie. Sowohl August Sander aus dem Rheinland als auch Käthe Buchler, geboren in Wolfenbüttel, erblickten 1876 das Licht der Welt, also vor 150 Jahren.
Zugegeben: Sander ist die bekanntere Persönlichkeit. Seine in den 1920er Jahren angelegte, 619 Einzelbilder zählende Porträtreihe „Menschen des 20. Jahrhunderts“ lässt einen Fotografen erkennen, der (noch) daran glaubte, dass der Habitus eines Menschen von seinem gesellschaftlichen Status zu zeugen vermag. Sein gestrenger Kölner Notar nebst Windhund, der beleibte Konditor mit dem Kupferkessel oder die Sekretärin beim Westdeutschen Rundfunk von 1931, rauchend und mit modischem Pagenkopf: Sie gehören zum kollektiven Gedächtnis sozialdokumentarischer Fotografie.
Bilder Sanders wurden in die weltweit gezeigte Wanderausstellung „The Family of Man“ aufgenommen, die ab 1955 mehr als zwei Millionen Besucher:innen erreichte. Die Photographische Sammlung, Stiftung Kultur in Köln würdigt derzeit den 1964 verstorbenen „Jahrhundertfotografen“, so der WDR, in einer Ausstellung zum 150. Geburtstag.
Die Ausstellung
Ausstellung „Menschen und Bilder. Käthe Buchler zum 150. Geburtstag“: Museum für Photographie Braunschweig, bis 29. 11.
Podiumsgespräch „Professionalisierung von Fotografinnen“ mit Giulia Cramm und Nathalie Dimic: ebd, 17. 11., 18 Uhr
Tagung „Käthe Buchler – eine Fotografin des frühen 20. Jahrhunderts aus Braunschweig“: 19. + 20. 11., Hochschule für Bildende Künste Braunschweig
Schüler:innenprojekt „Käthe Buchler heute – Aus Abfall wird Kunst“: Braunschweigische Landessparkasse, bis Ende 2026
Derweil widmet sich das Braunschweiger Museum für Photographie Käthe Buchler, nicht zum ersten Mal. Schon 2003 hatte das Haus den Nachlass der 1930 Verstorbenen erhalten: über 1.000 Glasnegative, rund 250 Autochrome (eine Frühform des Farbdias), Alben und Originalabzüge, die den Zweiten Weltkrieg überdauert haben. Für die jetzige Werkschau „Menschen und Bilder“ wurden durch aktuelle Forschungsergebnisse, Sammlungszugänge und Leihgaben neue Aspekte erschlossen. Besonders wichtig ist der Leiterin des Museums, Barbara Hofmann-Johnson, Käthe Buchler als professionell arbeitende Fotografin vorzustellen.
Mehr als eine Industriellengattin
Das ist eine Neubewertung: Früher wurde sie oft als gut betuchte Industriellengattin abgetan, die, auf zweifellos anerkannt hohem Niveau, als Amateurin wirkte. Das entspricht aber weder ihrem selbstbewussten Auftreten noch ihrem Werk: Ein öffentliches Symposion am 19. und 20. November in Braunschweigs Hochschule für Bildende Künste soll diese Herangehensweise an Buchlers Oeuvre vertiefen.
Käthe Buchler, Fotografin, wirbt per Visitenkarte für ihr Atelier
Vertiefte Blicke lohnen auch die bekannten Serien Buchlers, etwa ihre Porträts: Alle Aufnahmen sind sorgfältig arrangiert, mitunter ist ein neutraler Hintergrund aufgespannt. Dieser ist aber keine formatfüllende Illusion, sondern gibt sich als künstlicher – oder künstlerischer – Eingriff zu erkennen. Da lugen dann etwa Kinder um die Ecke. Mit Raffinesse verfasste Buchler auch ein Selbstbildnis, vermutlich zwischen 1901 und 1904: Sie lässt die obere Kante eines hellen Hintergrunds derart schräg durch den Bildaufbau laufen, dass eine Beschneidung kaum möglich gewesen wäre, ohne das Bild zu verstümmeln.
In dieser Form verwendete sie es als Entwurf einer „Carte de Visite“, mit der sie für ihr „Photographisches Atelier“ warb: „Aufträge jeder Art werden prompt und sicher ausgeführt“ oder „Reelle Bedienung, stets durch die Inhaberin selbst“. Ein weiteres Selbstporträt, um 1905, weist sie, mit Balgenkamera, als Fotografin aus. International wahrgenommen wurde auch Buchlers Reihe „Frauen in Männerberufen“ aus dem Ersten Weltkrieg. Zwei Schaffnerinnen, wohl in der Dienstuniform ihrer Kollegen an der Front, drei junge Milchkutscherinnen mit Pferdewagen oder die Verladerin an der Sackkarre wirken wie ein Vorgriff auf August Sanders typologische Porträts.
Sie fotografierte ab 1901
Die Braunschweiger Ausstellung setzt ihnen vier seiner männlichen Werktätigen entgegen: Gasmänner, Berliner Kohlenträger, Geldbriefträger. Käthe Buchler war auch eine versierte Zeichnerin, das beweist ein Skizzenbuch aus familiärer Leihgabe: So präzise wie auf einem Foto hielt sie Eindrücke fest, wohl während ihrer Hochzeitsreise 1895.
Nach der Geburt zweier Kinder begann sie dann 1901 mit der Fotografie, angeregt durch ihren Schwager aus der Voigtländer-Dynastie, Inhaber eines der beiden einst renommierten Kamerawerke in Braunschweig. Ab 1906 belegte sie Kurse an der Photographischen Lehranstalt des Berliner Lette-Vereins, erwarb eine Plattenkamera, richtete eine Dunkelkammer in ihrem Wohnhaus ein. Ab 1913 folgten konzeptionelle Serien, Vorträge und Ausstellungen ihrer Arbeiten, oft in karitativem Kontext.
Gleich mit ihrem Aufkommen um 1907 wandte Buchler auch die Farbfotografie mittels Autochromen an. Ein Motiv wurden Blumenstilleben der Jahreszeiten: technikgestützte Interpretationen des historischen Vanitas-Topos, der an die Vergänglichkeit allen Lebens gemahnen soll. Zu ihrem Geburtstag am 11. Oktober schmückte jüngst ein Rosenbouquet ihre Grabstellen, nachempfunden einem ihrer Stillleben. Und die zwei Torhäuser des Museums für Photographie bilden neuerdings eine würdige Adresse: Käthe-Buchler-Platz.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. Les cookies et technologies similaires que nous utilisons sur Mediapart sont de différentes natures et nous permettent de poursuivre différentes finalités. 
Certains sont nécessaires au fonctionnement du site et de l’application mobile (vous ne pouvez pas les refuser). D’autres sont optionnels mais contribuent à faciliter votre expérience de lecteur ou de lectrice et d’une certaine façon à soutenir Mediapart. Vous pouvez les refuser ou les accepter ci-dessous, selon leurs finalités. 
Acceptez-vous que Mediapart utilise des cookies ou technologies similaires pour les finalités suivantes ? 
Vous pouvez faire votre choix, pour chaque catégorie, en activant ou désactivant le bouton interrupteur.
                    
                            
                                Nécessaires au fonctionnement
du site ou de l’application
                            Connexion des abonné·es, mesure d’audience anonymisée, envoi des notifications push, suivi des pannes, mise en avant de nos services : ces outils sont nécessaires au suivi de l’activité de nos services et à leur bon fonctionnement.
                                    Voici les différents cookies et technologies similaires compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Cookies d’authentification : connexion des abonné·es.
- Batch (uniquement sur l’application) : envoi de notifications push et de messages in-app.
- Affichage de contenus éditoriaux multimédias : vidéos (YouTube, Dailymotion, Vimeo, INA), réseaux sociaux (Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Twitter), documents (Scribd, Document Cloud, Slideshare), sons (SoundCloud, Spotify, Deezer), cartes (Google Maps, Mapbox, CartoDB, uMap), infographies (Highcharts, GitHub, Datawrapper, Flourish, Infogram, ThingLink, jQuery, Google Fonts, Bootstrap), live blogs (24liveblog, CoverItLive), aide à l’intégration de média dans les publications Journal et Club (Embedly).
- Datadog (uniquement sur le site web) : indicateurs techniques et équilibrage de charge.
- Firebase Cloud Messaging (uniquement sur l’application) : nécessaire au fonctionnement des notifications push sur Android.
- Microsoft App Center (uniquement sur l’application) : système de mise à jour et de suivi des pannes de l’application.
- Piano : mesure d’audience anonymisée
- Selligent (uniquement sur le site web) : communication avec l’abonné·e, mise en avant des services, offres et avantages.
- Typeform : questionnaires facultatifs pour recueillir les avis des lecteurs sur nos produits numériques.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Ces outils nous permettent de recueillir des statistiques de fréquentation du site et de l’application mobile pour comprendre les usages, détecter d’éventuels problèmes et optimiser l’ergonomie de nos produits.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Batch (uniquement sur le site web) : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- CrazyEggs (uniquement sur le site web) : analyse de parcours client.
- Nonli (uniquement sur le site web) : permet à notre équipe des réseaux sociaux de publier les contenus Mediapart sur les réseaux sociaux.
- Piano : mesure d’audience reliée à l’identifiant d’abonné·e.
- Qiota (uniquement sur le site web) : gestion du système de datawall.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                            Il n’y a pas de publicité sur Mediapart. Mais nous faisons la promotion de nos contenus et services sur d’autres sites et réseaux sociaux. Pour cela, nous utilisons les technologies mises à disposition par certains acteurs publicitaires.
                                    Voici les outils tiers compris dans cette catégorie :
                                                                                    - Facebook (uniquement sur le site web) : ciblage d’audience sur les réseaux sociaux pour faire la promotion de Mediapart.
                                                    
                                            
                            
                                Gestion de l’accès aux contenus
                            Nous utilisons le service Qiota d’Opper Marketing Suite pour configurer l’activation d’un datawall sur certains de nos contenus (uniquement sur le site web). Ce dispositif destiné aux utilisateur·ices non abonné·es requiert la saisie d’une adresse email pour accéder aux contenus concernés. En fournissant cette information, l’utilisateur consent à sa collecte, son stockage et son utilisation à des fins statistiques. Conformément à la réglementation en vigueur, les utilisateurs disposent d’un droit d’accès, de rectification et de suppression de leurs données, qu’ils peuvent exercer en contactant dpo@opper.io.

Photo Maison Rowena TEFAF Maastricht, the European Fine Art Foundation’s Dutch art fair, has lined up 277 international galleries for its 2027 edition at MECC, a convention center just outside the center of town, and the fair’s longtime home. TEFAF also runs a New York edition, at the Park Avenue Armory, since 2016.) TEFAF is known for its rigorous vetting process, massive floral displays, and high-profile museum buyers, not to mention top-notch examples from 7,000 years’ worth of art history. Dealers at last year’s fair were “more than pleased” with sales and attendance, ARTnews reported. Related Articles Dealers at TEFAF Maastricht Report Robust Sales, Offering Works Ranging from Two Inches to Room-Size Undaunted by Global Unrest, TEFAF Revs Up for Maastricht Edition With a 'Museum For Sale' Newcomers to the 2027 edition’s main section include Galerie AB and Galerie Édouard Ambroselli, (France); Gallery Arte y Ritual (Spain); Galerie Bei Der Albertina (Austria); Butchoff Antiques (UK); Hazlitt (UK and US); Xavier Hufkens (Belgium); Thomsen Gallery and Martos Gallery (US); and Thaddaeus Ropac (UK, France, Austria, Italy, South Korea). The fair will once again include two special sections: Showcase, featuring nine emerging dealers, all showing at TEFAF for the first time, and Focus, dedicated to seven galleries with booths that zero in on a single artist or curatorial concept. Three of this year’s Focus galleries are new to the fair: Daguet-Bresson from France, Edel Assanti from the UK, and Repetto Gallery from Switzerland.
