https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.title: At Sotheby’s $378.7 M. Doubleheader, Buyers Take Risks Again, Even as Bidding Drags
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.author: Daniel Cassady
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/.text:
Sotheby’s kicked off the November marquee sales with a doubleheader on Monday evening that generated $378.7 million across 74 lots. The top-line results look solid, but a sluggish second half seemed to further illustrate the choosy mood among collectors right now.
The nearly three-hour marathon started strong with the dedicated sale from the collection of cable television magnate Ted Baum and interior designer Ruth Baum. It was a white-glove result, with all 24 works sold for a hammer total of $90.9 million. With fees, the sale landed at $110 million, just a shade above the presale high estimate of $109 million.
The Baum sale was a lively affair from the start. After the first lot—Roy Lichtenstein’s 1983 cut-paper work Two Paintings: Sleeping Muse (Study)—sparked a four-minute contest among three specialists and a bidder in the room, CEO Charles Stewart strode over to Gareth Jones, the house’s chief marketing officer, and said of the $3.8 million total, “Well, that’s a good start.” Three lots later, a Lucio Fontana copper canvas with a glorious cut down the middle ignited another bidding war, the bids ricocheting among three bidders in the room. It hammered at $3.5 million, or $4.4 million with fees, well above the $3 million high estimate.
Oliver Barker, chairman of Sotheby’s Europe, handled the proceedings with panache, making even a fairly ordinary stretch of bidding feel brisk. Amid the bidding for Lot 7, Andy Warhol’s 1984 painting The Scream (After Munch), he teased Jacqueline Wachter, chairwoman of private sales, for taking a bit too long with her phone bidder, asking whether she was “doing her shopping or doing her conversions.” Then he quipped to the audience, “Amazon is always open. As is Sotheby’s Dot Com.” It was a little sharp, perhaps, but it got a laugh and helped lighten the mood as the sale began to drag.
The crowded salesroom was a who’s who of the art trade: Dominique Lévy, Brett Gorvy, Amalia Dayan, David Schrader, Emmanuel Di Donna, Christophe Van de Weghe, and Gagosian Art Advisory’s Bernard Lagrange were just a few of the heavies in attendance.
In the end, six works hammered above their estimates and another 10 landed in range, with spirited bidding throughout, both in the room and on the phone. Joan Mitchell’s Green Book of Barbara Guest led the sale at $19.3 million, followed by Mark Rothko’s Untitled at $17.7 million and Ed Ruscha’s Dimple at $11.6 million. The Baums had bought the Mitchell privately in 1986 for just $65,000, making its sale price nearly 300 times what they paid. The Rothko, which they acquired for $115,000 in 1983, brought more than 150 times its purchase price. Not bad for a few decades of collecting. The final lot in the sale, Mario Merz’s neon sculpture Iguana, sold well below its estimate, but that did little to dampen the enthusiasm, as the room erupted in applause.
The Now and Contemporary sale that followed was considerably less celebratory. Of the 53 lots originally offered, three were withdrawn before the sale, and another five went unsold: works by Kerry James Marshall, Ellsworth Kelly, Roy Lichtenstein, and Keith Haring, and, curiously, a Formula One race car. Tom Eddison, head of contemporary art at Sotheby’s London, who took over auctioneering duties for the sale, said the car was a first for the auction house, and it required a lengthy preamble explaining that the sale was subject to the terms of service of RM Sotheby’s, the house’s classic-car affiliate. The car garnered a handful of bids but failed to reach its low estimate before Eddison declared it unsold. It may be some time before Sotheby’s tries that experiment again.
That’s not to say the results for the contemporary sale were lackluster. When all was said and done, the sale garnered a hammer total of $224.8 million. With fees, the total climbed to $268.8 million, within the presale aggregate estimate of $226.2 million to $323 million, and well above the equivalent sale in November 2025, which generated $178.5 million. Of course, we should note that last year’s sale followed the trove of works from the late cosmetics heir Leonard Lauder, which generated an eye-watering $527.5 million. Alas, not every season sees three Klimts hit the block.
Of the 45 lots that sold, a full 14 hammered above their presale estimates, and another 24 landed in range. Still, while there always seemed to be a handful of bidders for each sold lot, with Eddison darting his hands left, right, and center, most works hammered after only a minute or two.
The most protracted bidding wars came somewhat early. A six-minute contest among four specialists for Jeff Koons’s 1991 sculpture Bob-Tail ended with contemporary art specialist Bame Fierro March winning the lot for a hammer price of $9 million. At $10.7 million with fees, that’s good for just over three times the high estimate. (Is Koons’s market trending back up, or do collectors just really like an adorable English sheepdog?) Seven lots later, Agnes Martin’s cream canvas Desert, from the collection of Lenore and Bernard Greenberg, sold after a six-minute duel between contemporary art specialist Alya Sama and Lisa Dennison, chairman of the Americas. Dennison won on a $9.2 million hammer bid, or $11.3 million with fees, comfortably above the $8 million high estimate. And Andy Warhol’s 1964–65 painting Flowers fetched $18.2 million with fees against a $10 million to $15 million estimate.
Mark the Warhol and Koons results as green shoots for a market that’s spent much of the past two years playing it safe. Neither artist has had the easiest time in the secondary market lately, which makes those results particularly interesting. Something to watch going forward, especially for Koons.
After the sale, Dennison pointed to the continued strength of early Martin paintings, which have been outperforming expectations for several seasons.
Art adviser Ed Dolman similarly found the night’s results encouraging. In a text message toward the end of the sale, he said, “The best works always do fine, [but] buyers were taking some risks again.”
Dolman also pointed to the depth of bidding. While 29 of the 45 sold lots in the contemporary sale had guarantees—as did every work in the Baum sale—those guarantors were often outbid on Monday night. Buyers, it seemed, were willing to go a little further.
Not that everything was suddenly flying off the walls. Lichtenstein’s Reflections on ‘Painter and Model,’ the top lot of the contemporary sale at $24.7 million with fees, came in well short of the high end of its $20 million to $30 million estimate. Willem de Kooning’s Water…Soft Banks of a Window (Untitled VIII) brought $20.3 million, just above its $20 million low estimate, while Sam Francis’s Towards Disappearance I made $17.1 million against a $15 million to $20 million estimate.
The buzziest result of the night was no doubt for Yayoi Kusama’s 1960 painting No. 3P.B., which hammered for $12.5 million after 10 bids spread across four minutes. With fees, the result came to $15.1 million, just above the $15 million high estimate, and good for a new record for the artist, who died in August. About 10 lots later, another of her “Infinity Nets” paintings, Infinity Nets (OZEH), sold for a hammer price of $2.5 million, or $3.1 million with fees, just a shade above the $3 million high estimate. That work, a white canvas measuring roughly 6½ by 8½ feet, is far more recent, dating to 2011. And if you missed out on those two Kusamas, have no fear: Another 10 works of hers will hit the block over the rest of marquee week. Five are from her long-running “Infinity Nets” series.
Yet, for all the strong prices, the second half of the contemporary sale was a slog. With Eddison at the rostrum, the pace slowed considerably. Bids were drawn out, pauses stretched on, and even works that eventually fetched impressive prices seemed to take an age to get there. A few market watchers wondered whether such a sluggish tempo might discourage bidders, particularly on works that didn’t have much competition to begin with. It was an odd contrast: a sale that sometimes felt as though it was struggling to find its rhythm, even as buyers were spending millions more than expected.
To Nina Del Rio, an art adviser and auction house veteran, the results looked remarkably strong, particularly given the subdued energy in the second half of the sale. Still, she said, there hasn’t been much evidence of a shift in the market. At least not a fundamental one. Buyers appear to be behaving much as they did in May, when the best works attracted serious money but enthusiasm for younger artists remained muted. A few years ago, the Now sale was where collectors went to get their hands on artists whose waiting lists seemed impossible to crack. That sense of urgency has largely disappeared.
What collectors do seem willing to pay for is scarcity. Del Rio pointed to the modern masterpieces coming up later in the week, the sort of works that rarely appear at auction and may not come around again for decades. Among them is Wednesday’s sale of the Blaquier Collection, a group of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces said to be worth around $450 million, and a $180 million Van Gogh suddenly subject to a last-minute restitution claim.
Dennison warned against reading too much into a single evening. Given the current mood, starting the week with contemporary art rather than a mix of modern and contemporary masterpieces makes it harder to judge the market as a whole. And while works in the $10 million to $20 million range performed well, the sale lacked the $30 million, $40 million, and $50 million trophies that drive enthusiasm across the whole week.
As for that Formula One car, Dennison said the result left her scratching her head. The last bid offered, $3.9 million, was just under the $4 million low estimate. Did the interested buyer really think the $100,000 gap was too wide to bridge?
There is a risk to putting something unexpected into a contemporary art sale. But, as Dennison pointed out, sometimes it works, as when Christie’s sold the Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton “Stan” during its 20th Century Evening Sale in 2020 for $31.8 million, nearly quadruple the high estimate.
Sotheby’s shouldn’t give up on the idea. There’s something appealing about an evening sale that doesn’t draw a firm boundary around paintings and sculptures. Not every experiment works the first time, or even the second. And if the object is truly one-of-a-kind, buyers are ready to shell out the cash.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Brasil gasta R$ 14,5 bilhões por ano com a Lei Antidrogas; apenas 10% vão para medidas socioeducativas
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Luís Indriunas
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Brasil gastou pelo menos R$ 14,5 bilhões com a Lei de Drogas, também chamada de Lei Antidrogas, em 2024. Quase metade (48,9%) desse valor é para repressão (polícia militar e sistema prisional) e apenas 10% para medidas socioeducativas, aponta a pesquisa “Drogas: Quanto Custa Proibir”, do Centro de Estudos de Segurança e Cidadania (CESeC), divulgada nesta terça-feira (17).
O estudo inédito abrange as 27 unidades da federação e instituições federais, analisando a partir da legislação de 2006, cujo objetivo é “articular ações de prevenção do uso indevido, atenção e reinserção social de usuários e dependentes, além da repressão à produção e ao tráfico”, segundo o artigo 1º da Lei nº 11.343.
“Qualquer valor do orçamento público que seja utilizado para produzir insegurança, violência e morte é uma quantia mal gasta. É inadiável reorientar as prioridades orçamentárias diante dos danos causados pela guerra às drogas”, destaca Julita Lemgruber, coordenadora do CESeC.
Com o dinheiro gasto na guerra contra as drogas, poderiam ser construídos quase 6 mil Centros de Atenção Psicossocial Álcool e Drogas (CAPSad). Apesar de os dados já mostrarem um gasto que, em média, representa 7,9% dos orçamentos das unidades da federação. O Paraná lidera, com 11,8% das despesas das instituições do Sistema de Justiça Criminal alocadas à legislação, seguido por Espírito Santo (11,5%) e São Paulo (11,1%). Os menores percentuais gastos com sistema socioeducativo são do Amazonas (2,3%), Minas Gerais (2,6%) e Tocantins (3,0%).
“Passados 20 anos de vigência, a Lei de Drogas brasileira está longe de ter cumprido o objetivo que a justificou. A redação de 2006 prometia diferenciar usuários e traficantes como forma de diminuir o encarceramento. Mas a ausência de um critério objetivo para separar os dois grupos deixou essa distinção a cargo da discricionariedade policial, do Ministério Público e do Judiciário. O resultado foi o oposto do prometido: explosão do encarceramento em massa, sem evidências de ter-se reduzido a oferta de drogas ou o poder das facções”, apontam as conclusões do relatório.
O montante gasto com repressão pode ser ainda maior que os R$ 14,5 bilhões, porque a pesquisa não alcança todas as despesas relacionadas, como os gastos com operações e incursões policiais.
Um estudo de caso conduzido pelo pesquisador Daniel Cerqueira, no Rio de Janeiro, em 2024, mostra que foram realizadas 1.965 operações no estado, mais de cinco por dia, totalizando cerca de R$ 440 milhões em despesas com efetivo policial, helicópteros, blindados, viaturas, munições e outros recursos.
O documento aponta ainda que os gastos apenas com a vigilância de reconhecimento facial são estimados em R$ 3,5 bilhões entre outubro de 2021 e junho de 2026.
Além disso, segundo o CESeC, a guerra contra as drogas também impacta os gastos em outras áreas. O relatório “Tiros no Futuro”, lançado em 2022 pelo mesmo instituto de pesquisa, demonstrou que 74% das escolas cariocas vivenciaram pelo menos um tiroteio em seu entorno em 2019. Outra pesquisa, “Favelas na Mira do Tiro”, estimou um prejuízo anual de R$ 14 milhões para moradores e R$ 2,5 milhões para comerciantes em apenas dois complexos de favelas cariocas.
Além de dimensionar financeiramente os custos, as conclusões da pesquisa indicam para o fracasso da política, iniciada nos Estados Unidos nos anos 1970 e replicada mundo afora. “Um fato é indiscutível: pessoas usam drogas desde tempos imemoriais. Não se conhece história da sociedade humana sem o uso de substâncias psicoativas”, destaca o relatório, que aponta um crescimento do consumo. De 2012 a 2023, o percentual de pessoas que já consumiram substâncias psicoativas ilícitas passou de 10,3% para 18,7% no Brasil, um aumento de 82%.
Por fim, o relatório mostra ainda que o tráfico de drogas, para garantir a lavagem de dinheiro ilegal, se infiltra em outros crimes, como grilagem e garimpo, entre outros.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120392.title: BSW | BSW-Verfassungsbeschwerde: Letztes Wort zu Bundestagswahl?
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120392.author: Wolfgang Hübner
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120392.text:
- Politik
- BSW
BSW-Verfassungsbeschwerde: Letztes Wort zu Bundestagswahl?
Karlsruhe entscheidet über die Forderung nach Neuauszählung der Ergebnisse. Indessen eskaliert im BSW der Streit über das Verhältnis zur AfD.
Für das BSW ist dieser Mittwoch ein wichtiger Tag, wohl einer wichtigsten in der noch kurzen Parteigeschichte: Der Zweite Senat des Bundesverfassungsgerichts veröffentlicht seine Entscheidung über die »Wahlprüfungsbeschwerde im Zusammenhang mit der Auszählung der Stimmzettel und der Feststellung des Zweitstimmenergebnisses der Partei BSW bei der Wahl zum 21. Deutschen Bundestag am 23. Februar 2025«, wie es auf der Internetseite des obersten deutschen Gerichts heißt.
Das BSW, das seit Oktober den Namen der Gründerin Sahra Wagenknecht nicht mehr im Parteititel führt und nun Bündnis für soziale Gerechtigkeit und wirtschaftliche Vernunft heißt, hofft darauf, dass sämtliche Stimmen der letzten Bundestagswahl noch einmal ausgezählt werden. Denn die Partei war laut den Ergebnissen am Wahlabend mit 4,972 Prozent der gültigen Stimmen äußerst knapp an der Fünf-Prozent-Hürde und damit am Einzug in den neuen Bundestag vorbeischrammt.
Nur gut 13.800 Stimmen fehlten bundesweit; so knapp war noch keine Partei bei einer Bundestagswahl gescheitert. Kurz darauf wurden die Stimmen in ausgewählten Wahllokalen noch einmal ausgezählt – dort, wo das BSW auf Unstimmigkeiten hingewiesen hatte. Im Ergebnis der Überprüfung landete das BSW bei 4,981 Prozent; noch immer fehlen demnach 9529 Stimmen.
Im Parlament gescheitert
Darauf wollte das BSW es nicht beruhen lassen und sammelte weiter Hinweise auf Zähl- oder Übermittlungsfehler. In der Partei spricht man von systematischen, strukturellen Fehlern und ist überzeugt, faktisch die Fünf-Prozent-Hürde übersprungen zu haben. »Bei korrekter Auszählung der Bundestagswahl wären wir aller Voraussicht nach in den Bundestag eingezogen«, heißt es etwa im Leitantrag zum BSW-Bundesparteitag Ende November in Dresden.
Doch die Beschwerde beim Wahlprüfungsausschuss des Bundestags wurde abgewiesen; der Ausschuss und auch das Bundestagsplenum sahen es Ende 2025 nicht als erwiesen an, dass das BSW in einem Maß benachteiligt wurde, dass es die Verteilung der Parlamentsmandate verfälscht hätte. Lediglich die AfD-Fraktion unterstützte das Anliegen des BSW. Zuvor hatte schon das Bundesverfassungsgericht eine Organklage des BSW abgewiesen, in der die Partei Benachteiligungen etwa bei der Gestaltung der Wahlzettel geltend gemacht hatte.
Erst nach der Ablehnung durch den Wahlprüfungsausschuss konnte sich das BSW erneut an das Bundesverfassungsgericht wenden, so wollen es die im konkreten Fall zeitraubenden Regeln. Denn immerhin sind nun schon 21 Monate seit der Bundestagswahl vergangen, fast die Hälfte der Wahlperiode.
Die Beschwerde des BSW dreht sich maßgeblich um die Vermutung, dass es in vielen Fällen mit der Kleinpartei Bündnis für Deutschland verwechselt worden sei, die auf den Wahlzetteln direkt unter dem BSW stand. Sollten Wähler die beiden Parteien verwechselt haben, dann war das einfach Pech und ist kein Gegenstand einer Neuauszählung. Anders wäre es, wenn die Wahlkommissionen Stimmen in Größenordnungen nachweislich falsch zugeordnet hätten.
Existenzielle Frage mit weitreichenden Folgen
Ob es dafür ausreichend begründete Hinweise gibt, darüber muss das Bundesverfassungsgericht nun entscheiden. Wobei auch im Falle einer Neuauszählung zunächst nicht klar wäre, ob die fehlenden Stimmen für das BSW wirklich noch zusammenkommen. Für die Partei ist es eine nahezu existenzielle Frage, denn mit einer Bundestagsfraktion von mindestens 35 Abgeordneten wären nicht nur erhebliche politische Möglichkeiten und materielle Ressourcen verbunden, sondern auch eine weitaus stärkere mediale Präsenz. Und ganz und gar nicht zuletzt: Zöge das BSW nachträglich in den Bundestag ein, müssten die anderen Fraktionen je nach ihrer Größe Mandate abgeben. Mit der Folge, dass die schwarz-rote Bundesregierung keine Mehrheit mehr hätte.
Ob Neuwahlen die Folge wären oder sich Schwarz-Rot beispielsweise mit den Grünen arrangieren würde, steht auf einem anderen Blatt. Diese möglichen politischen Folgen, so gravierend sie auch sein mögen, dürfen jedoch die Entscheidung der Verfassungsrichter nicht beeinflussen.
Aufmerksam wurde zur Kenntnis genommen, dass das Bundesverfassungsgericht vor der Entscheidung keine mündliche Verhandlung anberaumt hat, was bei umstrittenen Fragen üblich ist. Die BSW-Führung ahnt angesichts dessen offenbar vor der Bekanntmachung am Buß- und Bettag nichts Gutes. Jedenfalls versuchte die BSW-Spitze noch einmal, etwas Druck zu machen, indem sie dieser Tage erklärte, wenn das Verfassungsgericht gegen eine Neuauszählung der Bundestagswahl entscheide, »würde dies das Vertrauen in Rechtsstaat und Demokratie endgültig zerstören«. Intern wird erwogen, sich im Falle einer Niederlage an den Europäischen Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte zu wenden. Allerdings würde ein solches Verfahren erneut viel Zeit in Anspruch nehmen.
Offener Konflikt im BSW-Führungszirkel
Immerhin ist der Kampf um eine Neuauszählung der Bundestagswahl noch ein gemeinsames Thema wohl aller BSW-Mitglieder. Ansonsten aber nähert sich die Partei vor dem anstehenden Bundesparteitag einer neuen Auseinandersetzung um ihren Kurs. Es geht zum wiederholten Male um das Verhältnis zur AfD, das schon bei den Kontroversen in Landesverbänden wie Thüringen, Sachsen-Anhalt und Brandenburg sowie bei etlichen Rück- und Austritten eine Rolle spielte. Angefeuert wurde der Konflikt zuletzt durch das unverhohlene Kokettieren des Landesverbands Sachsen-Anhalt und dessen Landtagsfraktion mit der AfD und mit rechtspopulistischen und rechtsextremen Medien.
Kamen bisher schon kritische Stimmen aus dem gewerkschaftlichen Spektrum innerhalb des BSW, so hat der Widerspruch gegen die von Wagenknecht abgesegnete AfD-Offenheit und -Kooperation nun auch den Führungszirkel der Partei erreicht. Das BSW solle sich klar von der AfD distanzieren und »eine formelle oder faktische Tolerierung, eine Stützung einer AfD-geführten Regierung und auf Dauer angelegte Absprachen zur Zusammenarbeit« ausschließen, heißt es in einem Antrag an den Dresdner Parteitag, der von vier Vizevorsitzenden und drei weiteren Vorstandsmitgliedern unterschrieben wurde.
In diesem Sinne soll der Leitantrag des Parteitags verändert werden. Die AfD soll demnach ebenso als politischer Gegner betrachtet werden wie »die regierenden Parteien der ›Mitte‹«. Wie diese stehe die AfD – eher noch verstärkt – für Aufrüstung, Sozialabbau und die »Begünstigung der Superreichen«, weshalb sie kein Partner für das BSW sein könne.
Das ist eine deutliche Abgrenzung von Wagenknechts Rhetorik, die AfD und BSW gemeinsam gegen die sogenannten Altparteien stellt. Interessant ist, dass zu den Kritikern frühere Linke-Politiker und BSW-Mitgründer wie Christian Leye, Klaus Ernst, Jessica Tatti und Sevim Dağdelen ebenso gehören wie der Unternehmer Thomas Stanger, der gemeinsam mit seiner Ehefrau bereits mehr als acht Millionen Euro an das BSW spendete.
Protest gegen Schmusekurs mit der AfD
Die beiden Vizevorsitzenden Jessica Tatti und Ralph Suikat verschärften in einem Gastbeitrag auf der Plattform t-online.de noch den Ton. Zwar bezeichnen auch sie die Brandmauer gegen die AfD als falsch, sehen aber den sogenannten Magdeburger Weg des sachsen-anhaltischen BSW als Irrweg. Das BSW sei dort dabei, »sich im Lager der AfD einzusortieren«, schreiben sie, und praktiziere damit »das Lagerdenken der ›Brandmauerparteien‹, nur mit umgekehrtem Vorzeichen«. »Am laufenden Band« würden gezielt Bilder erzeugt, um die Lagerbildung mit der AfD zu inszenieren, »die weit über eine punktuelle inhaltliche Zusammenarbeit hinausgeht«. Wer aber »auf einen Schmusekurs mit der AfD setzt, liefert niemandem einen Grund, zum BSW zu wechseln«. Inhaltliche Unterschiede würden so gut wie nicht aufgemacht, »sondern im Hinterzimmer Gemeinsamkeiten ausgelotet und gemeinsam präsentiert«.
Wagenknecht, die sich ausdrücklich hinter den AfD-freundlichen Kurs des Landesverbands Sachsen-Anhalt und dessen Magdeburger Weg stellt, ließ indessen die von ihr geleitete Grundwertekommission auf die Kritik antworten. Die AfD werde vielfach aus ähnlichen Gründen gewählt wie das BSW, heißt es in einem Statement der Kommission. »Wenn wir uns der Kooperation verweigern, die notwendig ist, um Mehrheiten für sinnvolle Veränderungen zu nutzen, würde das BSW seinem Wählerauftrag nicht gerecht und im Ergebnis noch mehr enttäuschte Wähler an die AfD verlieren.« Mehrheiten sollten bei Sachthemen auch durch gemeinsame Anträge genutzt werden; punktuelle Übereinstimmung bedeute »weder eine gemeinsame politische Grundlage noch eine politische Annäherung«.
Die AfD wird in dem Papier gegen »die von Teilen der veröffentlichten Meinung betriebene Diffamierung der heutigen AfD als ›Nazi-Partei‹« in Schutz genommen, welche nicht zuletzt dazu diene, »die undemokratische Brandmauer zu legitimieren«. Auch jenseits der Entscheidung der Verfassungsrichter in Sachen Bundestagswahl wird der kommende BSW-Parteitag also einiges zu diskutieren haben.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.title: Democrat Mary Peltola closes in on victory in closely watched US Senate race in Alaska – live
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.author: Shrai Popat (now) and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Alaska midterm race could be called on Wednesday as Peltola remains ahead of Republican incumbent
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
The final Senate race of this year’s midterm elections could be resolved tomorrow if Alaska election officials run the state’s ranked choice voting system to determine the result.
With 98% of ballots counted, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is out in front with 49.98% of the vote. By contrast, incumbent Republican senator Dan S Sullivan has a 45.93% share, according to the latest Associated Press figures.
In terms of actual voting numbers, Peltola is ahead by just over 11,000, with 141,637 compared to Sullivan’s 130,162. All eyes will be on Peltola to see if she can keep the pace to achieve 50% of the ballot, two weeks on from the election.
If not, then voters’ second choice votes will be counted. The outcome will determine the final balance of power in the chamber for the next two years, with Democrats already holding a 55-44 majority.
It comes in a turbulent Alaska race, which has seen president Trump demand that Peltola be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. Piling on, Alaska’s Republican governor has since ordered an investigation into Peltola’s campaign.
A New York Times investigation reported that operatives working with Peltola’s campaign helped recruit another Dan Sullivan – Dan J Sullivan – a retired teacher from Petersburg, to split the incumbent’s vote. Peltola and her campaign have denied this.
The ‘other’ Sullivan, who stood as an independent candidate, has only received 4,684 votes – a 1.65% share – and is looking unlikely to be the cause of the Republican senator’s failure should he not retain his seat.
Elsewhere, president Trump has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit, where he is due to meet south east Asian leaders and take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
You can follow that here:
In other developments:
- Donald Trump defended his commerce secretary Howard Lutnick after he came under fire for allegedly slow-walking export restrictions on Nvidia chips to China. This comes after treasury secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week that he has been pushing “for months” to add Megaspeed, the data center company led by an alleged Chinese spy who was reportedly in a relationship with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, to the US trade blacklist.
- Trump blasted the new leadership of CBS News’ 60 Minutes, which was overhauled under the network’s conservative editor-in-chief Bari Weiss. In a social media post, the president was particularly critical of a report on the more than 800 American service members wounded and 23 killed in the war in Iran that 60 Minutes aired on Sunday.
- Trump also said that he would “not mind” seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. The president says the ex-CEO has learned a lesson, and denied that national security has been put at risk.
- The president also continued to shift responsibility to the Biden administration for the nationwide ground stop over the weekend. Trump said that he needed more funding to overhaul the outdated telecommunication system responsible for the disruptions.
- The Trump administration has warned Elizabeth Warren, the senior Democratic senator expected to chair the powerful Senate banking committee, that she could face “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into Donald Trump. The warning mirrors other letters justice department officials have sent to Democratic lawmakers who have indicated they will investigate the Trump administration when the party becomes the majority in Congress next year.
- A federal appeals court heard arguments in Donald Trump’s hush money case, as the president tries to see the case shifted to federal court where he could have it dismissed on grounds of immunity. The hearing concerned a May 2024 ruling that found Trump guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film star Stormy Daniels.

https://taz.de/Ein-Stueck-ueber-den-Blic.title: Ein Stück über den Blick der anderen: Wenn sanfte Elbauen zum wilden Dickicht werden
https://taz.de/Ein-Stueck-ueber-den-Blic.author: Katrin Ullmann
https://taz.de/Ein-Stueck-ueber-den-Blic.text:
Ein Stück über den Blick der anderen: Wenn sanfte Elbauen zum wilden Dickicht werden
Am Hamburger Schauspielhaus geht's in „Weisse Flotte“ um reale Fremdheit und fremde Realitäten. Es basiert auf dem Hörspiel „Die lächerliche Finsternis“.
Ihre eigentliche Mission ist ihnen verloren gegangen. Genauso wie ihr fünfter Mann, der auf einer Elbfahrt verschwand. Genauer: Bei einer Fahrt, bei der sie versuchten, die „ländliche Bevölkerung mit dem migrantischen Mann zu verbinden“.
Jetzt planen sie eine neue. Und zwar im Rangfoyer des Hamburger Schauspielhauses. „Weisse Flotte“ nennen sie ihr Unterfangen, das unter der Leitung der Ensembleschauspielerin Ute Hannig und der Theatermacherin Pia Düsterhus elbaufwärts will, um dort nach dem Vermissten, nach einem gewissen Deutinger zu suchen. An Geesthacht, Lauenburg und Tangermünde vorbei wollen sie bis nach Magdeburg. Denn dort war jener Deutinger zuletzt gesehen worden. Hatte bis dahin, wie seine Kompagnons, etliche grausame, enthemmte Rituale knapp überstanden, war gerettet worden vor wilden Eingeborenen, die oft trunken angefüllt waren mit gegorenem Getreide.
Sie, das sind die vier Übriggebliebenen. Dave Doughman, Ibrahim Kurt, Nikita Petrosian und Shahin Sheikho heißen sie auf dem Programmzettel, im Spiel sind ihre Namen ähnlich klangvoll: Ultimo Michael, Hauptfeldwebel Pellner, Tofdau und Stefan Dorsch. Mit diesen Figurennamen und mit weiten Teilen des aufgeführten Textes nimmt der Abend deutlich Bezug auf Wolfram Lotz’ „Die lächerliche Finsternis“.
Die Unfähigkeit, das Fremde wirklich zu verstehen
Ursprünglich 2013 als Hörspiel geschrieben, machte dieser Text bald im Theater Karriere. Darin erzählt der mehrfach ausgezeichnete Dramatiker – frei nach Joseph Conrad – von einer Reise ins Herz der Finsternis, auch etwa von zwei Bundeswehroffizieren, die durch die Wildnis irren, und außerdem von einem Somalier, dessen heimische Fischgründe von den wohlhabenden Nationen leer gefischt wurden und der darüber zum Piraten geworden ist.
Letztlich erzählt Lotz in seinem Text von unserer Unfähigkeit, das Fremde wirklich verstehen zu können. „Das Gefühl ist ja immer wieder da, dass ich über die Dinge nicht schreiben kann, weil ich sie nicht kenne“, heißt es einmal. Virtuos überwindet Lotz diese Befremdung, indem er sie immer wieder offenlegt, ironisiert und selbst zum Thema macht.
Hannig und Düsterhus fahren mit ihren vier charmanten Darstellern und einigen Passagen aus Lotz’ düsterer Reise gewissermaßen in die Gegenrichtung. Durch die Augen ihrer migrantischen Mannschaft wird an diesem Abend das vermeintlich Vertraute zum Fremden, werden die sanften Elbauen zur undurchdringlichen Sachsen-Anhaltischen Wildnis. Filmaufnahmen von Elbufer und Böschung ziehen über die Wände im Rangfoyer, während migrantische Perspektiven auf ländlich deutsche Horizonte treffen.
Abdriften in die eigenen Geschichten
Als Rahmenhandlung bieten die vier Darsteller einen Vortrag und darin einen Spendenaufruf, der ihre Mission unterstützen soll. Auf einem Flipchart malen sie dafür noch am zu scannenden QR-Code, und immer wieder bedanken sie sich bei ihren Förderern, bei Sponsor*innen und einzelnen Wohltäter*innen wie „Katja aus Eimsbüttel“. Immer mal singen sie auch ein deutsches Volkslied, loben gegenseitig ihre guten Deutschkenntnisse und driften dann regelmäßig ab in die Geschichte und in ihre (eigenen) Geschichten.
Dann sprechen sie in ihrer Muttersprache, erzählen von Herkunft und Kindheit, von Funkenflug und einer tödlichen Markise auf der Terrasse eines ukrainischen Familienhauses. Dann verweben sich wie nebenbei mutmaßlich biografische Katastrophen mit Lotz’ ironischem und zugleich unendlich traurigem Text.
Entstanden im Rahmen von NEW HAMBURG, einem langjährigen Kooperationsprojekt des Deutschen Schauspielhauses mit dem Ev.-Luth. Kirchenkreis Hamburg-Ost sowie der lokalen Kirchengemeinde im und mit dem Stadtteil Veddel, ist „Weisse Flotte“ ein Abend, der gleichermaßen von realer Fremdheit und von fremder Realität erzählt.

https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/des-milliers.title: Des milliers de manifestants à Bruxelles pour dénoncer les conditions d’études
https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/des-milliers.text:
La Belgique emboîte le pas à la France. Ce mardi, plusieurs milliers de personnes ont manifesté à Bruxelles à l’appel des organisations étudiantes dénonçant la dégradation des conditions d’études dans leur pays, sur fond d’économies budgétaires.
Selon l’Agence France-Presse (AFP), le cortège était constitué majoritairement de lycéens et d’étudiants. Ces derniers manifestaient contre le gouvernement fédéral dirigé par le conservateur flamand Bart De Wever.
« On est là pour défendre notre avenir. En Belgique on achète des F-35 pour la Défense et on tape sans cesse dans l’économie non marchande », a déclaré à l’AFP Bastien, futur éducateur spécialisé de 19 ans, en allusion aux restrictions budgétaires visant les secteurs de la santé ou de la culture.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: No Recife (PE), estudantes da UFPE protestam nesta terça-feira (17) contra o projeto de ajuste fiscal do governo Lula
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Na tarde desta sexta-feira (17), estudantes se reúnem na Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE) numa manifestação contra o projeto de lei complementar que trata do “ajuste fiscal” do governo federal (PLP nº 299/2026). Aprovada no Senado no último dia 12, o projeto assinado pelo senador Jaques Wagner (PT) prevê a economia de pelo menos R$ 50 bilhões em 2027, mas com impactos futuros sobre saúde e educação. A “aula pública” convocada pelos estudantes acontece a partir das 16 horas, no jardim externo do Centro de Artes e Comunicação (CAC) da UFPE.
Nas redes sociais, o Diretório Central dos Estudantes (DCE) reclama do nível de influência que o mercado financeiro e seus acionistas conseguem exercer sobre o orçamento público. “O Brasil precisa de investimentos, direitos e desenvolvimento. O mercado não pode estar acima do povo”, diz a nota. “Não podemos aceitar que o orçamento público seja orientado exclusivamente pela lógica do mercado financeiro. (…) Precisamos debater os rumos da economia brasileira e defender um projeto de desenvolvimento que coloque os direitos sociais, a soberania nacional e a qualidade de vida do povo no centro das decisões. (…) O mercado não manda no Brasil”, pontuam os estudantes.
No Senado, os três representantes de Pernambuco — Humberto Costa (PT), Teresa Leitão (PT) e Fernando Dueire (PSD) — seguiram a orientação do governo Lula e votaram a favor do PLP. A previsão é que o PLP seja votado na Câmara Federal nesta quarta-feira (18), um dia após os protestos convocados nacionalmente pela União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE). Entre os cinco deputados federais mais à esquerda da bancada pernambucana — Carlos Veras (PT), Renildo Calheiros (PCdoB), Clodoaldo Magalhães (PV), Maria Arraes (PSB) e Pedro Campos (PSB) —, nenhum sinaliza voto contrário ao ajuste proposto pelo governo Lula.
Entre os parlamentares federais eleitos este ano, mas que só começam a legislar em fevereiro de 2027, três se posicionaram sobre o tema. O crítico mais vocal do reajuste é o deputado federal eleito Jones Manoel (Psol), que tem divulgado vídeos diariamente sobre o tema. “O ajuste fiscal é um erro político do governo. O PLP representa um ataque à saúde, à educação, ao salário mínimo, ao BPC e à previdência. É luta de classes, é conflito redistributivo. É sobre quem vai, a partir do orçamento público, se apropriar da riqueza socialmente produzida”, disse ele num dos vídeos.
A deputada federal eleita Rosa Amorim (PT) também se posicionou nas redes sociais. “Responsabilidade fiscal não pode significar economia feita às custas do povo. O ajuste precisa começar pelos privilégios, pelos super-ricos, pelos bancos e por quem historicamente ganha muito e contribui pouco. O recado das urnas foi claro: o povo precisa estar no centro das decisões do orçamento”. Liana Cirne (PT) falou na tribuna da Câmara de Vereadores contra a pressão do mercado e da imprensa sobre o governo. “Estão confundindo o presidente Lula com o derrotado que fugiu para os Estados Unidos. O presidente Lula não prometeu cortes, muito pelo contrário. A gente não quer corte de gastos”, disparou.
Mas o que diz o projeto de ajuste fiscal?
Um dos pontos que desagradam as organizações da sociedade civil é a mudança nas “receitas vinculadas”: atualmente, há uma exigência de que o governo federal destine para a saúde no mínimo 15% da receita corrente líquida (total de receitas no ano); e para a educação no mínimo 18% da receita líquida de impostos. Se durante o ano o governo obtiver receitas acima do previsto (“receitas extraordinárias”), automaticamente amplia-se também os valores obrigatórios para saúde e educação.
Mas o PLP 299/2026 retira as “receitas extraordinárias” da base de cálculo, de forma que uma ampliação nas receitas ou na arrecadação de impostos passam a ser “sobras” para o pagamento da dívida pública.
O PLP nº 299/2026 também altera o “arcabouço fiscal”, prevendo a limitação do crescimento das despesas em apenas 2% (atualmente o teto é de 2,5%), amplia as possibilidades de contingenciamento de gastos (em caso de frustração de receitas). Se é verdade que o ajuste incomodou setores da sociedade civil, também é verdade que o chamado “mercado financeiro” não está feliz com as medidas. Esperavam uma redução nos gastos sociais.
O principal ponto visto como positivo pelas organizações da sociedade civil é o corte linear de 20% dos benefícios tributários concedidos a grandes empresas, que passam a ter um abatimento menor, mas ainda pagam menos impostos do que prevê a legislação. É isso que a bancada de oposição (notadamente o PL do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro) tem chamado de “aumento de impostos”, mas que na realidade é uma redução no valor dos descontos ainda dados pelo governo.
O PLP também obriga o Congresso Nacional a, dentro de quatro meses, legislar sobre os “supersalários” e os “penduricalhos” dos poderes executivo, legislativo e principalmente do judiciário. A expectativa do governo Lula é que o Congresso garanta uma economia de R$ 2 bilhões ao ano.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120392.title: Vor Koalitionsausschuss | SoVD: Stromsteuersenkung nicht gegen Mütterrente ausspielen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120392.text:
- Politik
- Vor Koalitionsausschuss
SoVD: Stromsteuersenkung nicht gegen Mütterrente ausspielen
Wird die Ausweitung der Mütterrente gekippt, um die versprochene Senkung der Stromsteuer zu bezahlen? Der Sozialverband Deutschland ist dagegen.
Düsseldorf. Der Sozialverband Deutschland (SoVD) hat vor dem Koalitionsausschuss am Dienstag davor gewarnt, eine mögliche Senkung der Stromsteuer und die Mütterrente gegeneinander auszuspielen. »Die versprochene Senkung der Stromsteuer auch für private Haushalte ist angesichts der hohen Lebenshaltungskosten dringend notwendig«, sagte SoVD-Chefin Michaela Engelmeier der »Rheinischen Post«. »Doch zur Gegenfinanzierung ausgerechnet die bereits beschlossene Mütterrente wieder infrage zu stellen, wäre der völlig falsche Weg.«
»Wer Kinder großgezogen hat, verdient Anerkennung, auch in der Rente. Stromsteuer und Mütterrente dürfen nicht gegeneinander ausgespielt werden«, betonte Engelmeier. »Gesamtgesellschaftliche Aufgaben müssen verlässlich aus Steuermitteln finanziert werden und dürfen nicht auf die Beitragszahlenden abgewälzt werden«, fügte sie hinzu. »Soziale Sicherheit darf nicht zum Spielball der Haushaltsverhandlungen werden.«
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) hatte am Montag eine Einigung mit der SPD bei der umstrittenen Senkung der Stromsteuer für den Koalitionsausschuss in Aussicht gestellt. Merz steht unter Druck aus den eigenen Reihen, beim Treffen der Koalitionsspitzen am Dienstagabend die Stromsteuersenkung für Privathaushalte doch noch durchzusetzen. Für die dafür erwarteten Einnahmeausfälle in Höhe von rund fünf Milliarden Euro hatten die Koalitionshaushälter in der vergangenen Woche keine Finanzierung gefunden.
Durch die Mütterrente sollen Erziehungszeiten bei der Rente berücksichtigt werden. Für Erziehungsberechtigte ab 1992 geborener Kinder ist dies bereits der Fall. Die schwarz-rote Koalition hat auf Druck der CSU im vergangenen Jahr die Ausweitung auf Eltern beschlossen, deren Kinder vor 1992 geboren wurden. Dies soll ab dem kommenden Jahr gelten. Einige Abgeordnete der SPD, aber auch aus der Union forderten, das Gesetz rückgängig zu machen, um stattdessen die Senkung der Stromsteuer zu finanzieren. CSU-Chef Markus Söder lehnt das ab. AFP/nd
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.theguardian.com/business/liv.title: China vows to take ‘necessary measures’ against US AI chip restrictions, as investors brace for Nvidia’s results – business live
https://www.theguardian.com/business/liv.author: Graeme Wearden
https://www.theguardian.com/business/liv.text:
China slams new US chip curbs and pledges 'necessary measures'
China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers.
At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson GuoJiakun said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:
“The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s high-tech industries.”
Guo also called the US move a typical example of economic coercion that deviates from the consensus reached by both countries, Reuters reports.
As we blogged yesterday, the US Commerce Department has issued a new rule which limits remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips by companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil.
The new measure closes a loophole which allowed Chinese companies to access cutting-edge US tech by using data centres based in other countries in Asia.
Awkwardly for Beijing, the new “interim final rule” is being imposed just as DonaldTrump prepares to meet China’s president XiJinping later this week in Shenzhen, which is hosting this week’s APEC summit.
Dexter Roberts, a nonresident senior fellow at the AtlanticCouncil’s Global China Hub, says (via Bloomberg):
“This is the worst situation possible for China because the last thing they want to see is any new restrictions on their access to chips.”
“Export controls are what upset them practically more than anything else right now other than maybe Taiwan.”
US government confirms investigation into Megaspeed over Nvidia chip exports
Two US government departments have confirmed they are investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia’s chips to China.
A joint statement issued by the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice explains that Megaspeed has been under investigation since 2024, for “potential export control violations.”
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list, they explain.
And they also state that commerce department agents conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.
The Department of Justice then took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
Tooting their own trumpets, the departments add:
This investigation is the result of the excellent work of the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick and the law enforcement efforts of the Department of Justice under Attorney General Todd Blanche.
That, presumably, is a response to suggestions that Lutnick could be fired following accusations that he had shielded Nvidia from federal oversight, and had failed to blacklist Megaspeed.
Nvidia establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
Nvidia has announced it is creating a new committee to oversee its national security policies, check it is complying with export controls and manage its global trade risk effectively.
The NationalSecurityandExportControlOversightCommittee demonstrates that Nvidia is committed to “the highest standards of governance and oversight,” the company says.
It’s a response to claims that billions of dollars worth of the company’s top AI chips have been redirected to China.
Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia’s board of directors.
“NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security.
As the world’s leading advanced computing company, NVIDIA has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges.
We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation.”
Investors’ euphoria over the AI boom is over, according to the latest survey of fund managers from Bank of America.
BofA’s monthly poll has found that investors have slashed their technology holdings this month. The percentage of investors who were ‘overweight’ on tech stocks fell at the fastest rate since 2006 in November.
The survey also found that 38% of investors predicted that bonds issued by AI hyperscalers are the most likely source of a credit event, followed by private credit with 30%.
BofA investment strategist Michael Hartnett says investors remain bullish on the macro-economic front, with just 3% predicting a recession. They are also optimistic about markets, with cash holdings at an “uber-low 3.6%”.
Newsflash: The European Commission has charged online shopping retailer Temu with failing to tackle the sale of illegal products, my colleague Jennifer Rankin reports.
The EU regulator found that the Chinese online shopping website did not have effective controls to prevent the sale of illegal items, thereby breaching the EU’s Digital Services Act.
Temu has been contacted for comment. The company now has the right to see the charge sheet and mount a defence.
The charges, announced on Tuesday, come after a €200m (£173m) fine on Temu from the EU in May on the grounds of inadequate risk assessment in 2024 to prevent the sale of illegal products and recommender systems that could amplify the promotion of such items.
The latest charges were brought under a different article of the EU’s Digital Services Act, which is intended to protect European internet users from online harms ranging from disinformation to cyberbullying to dangerous goods. They also relate to harms over a longer period, dating since the relevant provisions came into effect in October 2024.
Commission officials said Temu’s “ineffective” controls to stop illegal goods focused on paperwork, rather than products. It also found there were not enough human moderators to manage the huge growth in items listed on the platform. Third-party sellers offering illegal products, EU officials said, faced only weak sanctions from Temu and company systems enabled repeat offenders to sell through other parts of its website.
Temu has 130m users in the EU. If the charges are upheld Temu could be fined 6% of its global annual turnover.
The company said in May it disagreed with the Commission’s decision and saw the €200m fine as disproportionate.
The Commission examined Temu’s risk management systems, rather than specific products. Consumer groups in the EU and UK have previously reported that Temu has offered for sale baby toys presenting choking hazards, jewellery laced with dangerous metals including lead, clothes made with banned chemicals and illegal weapons.
Singapore has said it is carefully studying the new US clampdown on Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres powered by Nvidia chips, in countries including Singapore.
The Singaporean government has said:
“We take our international reputation seriously and do not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities, including export controls.
The scandal “is obviously not a good look for Singapore“, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist with the NationalUniversityofSingapore, told the AFP newswire.
Singapore is also probing what Megaspeed was up to, but Chong said the city-state must strengthen regulatory oversight to avoid the perception of “systemic issues”.
Concerns that the AI boom may slow is pushing down the copper price today.
Copper has fallen to its lowest level in four and a half months, touching $13,144 a metric ton on the LondonMetalExchange this morning.
Copper is heavily used in the AI industry – both to build data centre infrasctructure, and to cool the systems. It is also essential in power networks.
The US president, Donald Trump, has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit,.
After departing from the Boeing 747 gifted to him by Qatar, Trump was greeted by officials and members of the military on the red carpet laid out on the Ninoy Aquino International Airport’s tarmac.
My colleague YohannesLowe is blogging all the key developments:
Demonstrators have also gathered in Manila to protest against Trump:
After a tough day yesterday, when they fell over 4%, Nvidia’s shares on track to dip further.
Nvidia’s shares are down 0.5% in premarket trading, ahead of their latest financial results tonight.
Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at capital,com, says:
Investors are expecting revenue of around $109bn, but the focus will be on data-centre demand, margins, forward guidance and reassurance about the company’s leadership transition.
Strong results could help restore confidence in the AI sector, although even an earnings beat may not be enough if management fails to address concerns about future investment returns. Conversely, disappointing guidance could accelerate the selloff.
European stock markets are down across the board today, after a weak session in the Asia-Pacific.
The pan-European Stoxx600 index is down 0.9%, with losses on the main indices in Frankfurt (-1%), Paris (-1%), Madrid (-0.5%) and Milan (-0.6%) as well as London (-0.8%).
Overnight, South Korea’s Kospi index dropped by another 2.6% as stocks linked to the AI sector continued to be hit.
AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould says:
“Despite its limited exposure to AI, the UK market could not entirely shake off the negative sentiment in markets as tech stocks chalked up further losses,” says
“Asian markets experienced further weakness and London’s contingent of heavyweight resources stocks also came under pressure as commodity prices eased.
“While US futures are pointing to a steady start on Wall Street later, the tone for the remainder of the week will hinge on Nvidia’s earnings update after the bell.
The US has added “another layer of regulatory risk to the global AI trade” by tightening restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI computing through overseas data centres, says CharuChanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.
In a new research note, Chanana explains:
China AI is no longer one trade. Domestic semiconductor suppliers could benefit from the self-sufficiency push, while AI developers face higher costs and potentially slower innovation.
Nvidia and US tech face indirect risks. Nvidia’s reported China revenue may not fully capture demand routed through overseas data centres. The bigger question is how restrictions affect future AI infrastructure orders.
Could regulation become the next big AI risk? Restrictions could eventually extend beyond chips and computing access to Chinese AI models. That could raise costs for businesses using cheaper Chinese models and slow AI adoption — the phase where we expect broader economic value to emerge.
Any set of financial results from Nvidia are important, but there’s particular excitement in the markets today before the chip giant publishes its third-quarter results after Wall Street trading ends tonight.
Nvidia’s Q3 results, and the subsequent conference call with analysts and investors, will be very closely scrutinised given the crisis gripping the company.
Nvidia’s future forecasts will be a key measure of whether the AI industry is growing as rapidly as forecast.
But it will also, surely, be quizzed over the resignation of JensenHuang last week. Will the board confirm that there is no chance of a return for Huang, who quit after reports of extramarital liaisons, including with an alleged Chinese spy, AliceHuang?
Interim CEO ColetteKress could also face questions about reports that $12bn of Nvidia’s chips were directed to companies in China by Megaspeed, AliceHuang’s company.
Kress might also be quizzed about reports that she is concerned about Nvidia’s web of financial support for AI companies….
Investors may also wonder whether the latest clampdown on remote access to AI chips – which have irked China – will hurt Nvidia’s sales.
Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, explains:
The question is, can they calm investors’ nerves about the AI trade? The market expects another monster report. Expectations are for revenue to come in above $109bn for last quarter, a jump of 92% on a YoY basis, earnings per share is expected at $2.47. There is no reason to think that Nvidia will miss these figures, and based on the recent trend of their results, they are likely to post sales figures above expectations.
Although profit margins could dip to 73% from 74%, the company is still likely to report a bullet proof balance sheet, with over $180bn in free cash flow. Nearly all AI companies use Nvidia chips, so the question is: will export restrictions to Asian countries that have acted as conduits to China have a material impact on the company’s revenues going forward?

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/yemen.title: Yemen's government forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab and west coast to defend Aden
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/yemen.author: MEE correspondent
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/yemen.text:
Yemen's government forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab and west coast to defend Aden
Early last month, the chairman of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, announced the launch of Operation Fajr al-Yemen (Dawn of Yemen), aimed at restoring state institutions, retaking the capital, Sanaa, and ending Houthi control.
The announcement came a day after the Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, seized large areas of Taiz governorate and took control of all entrances to Taiz city.
However, no advances have been made on the ground since the operation was announced. Instead, the Houthis have continued to make major gains in both Taiz and Lahij governorates, in Yemen's southwest.
On the west coast, battles were ongoing in Dhubab district, where government forces controlled the Dhubab military airport and surrounding areas. Meanwhile, the Houthis were advancing through the mountains and valleys of Lahij governorate and were on the verge of imposing a siege on military forces along the coast.
On Sunday, 15 November, Yemeni government forces announced the withdrawal of their troops from the Bab al-Mandab area and Dhubab military airport as part of a redeployment aimed at securing the provisional capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
The Houthis advanced into all the areas previously held by government forces on the same day. They are now roughly 70km from Aden's northern entrance, while government forces are regrouping to defend the city.
The latest advance has given the Houthis control of approximately 60km of coastline along the Gulf of Aden, stretching from Bab al-Mandab towards Aden governorate, including the coastal area of Khour Omaira.
Defending Aden
Professor Abdulsattar al-Shamiri, a Yemeni political analyst and CEO of the Johood Center for Studies and Research, said the recent withdrawals should be viewed in the context of battlefield management. He pointed to a failure to close gaps early on, allowing the Houthis to outflank and besiege forces that had advanced towards Dhubab.
“This reflects an inability to manage the battle and control the ground through collective management and coordination among all military units,” Shamiri told Middle East Eye.
'The Houthis may exploit their control over strategic areas to consolidate their influence in Bab al-Mandab while keeping the option of advancing toward Aden open'
- Mansour al-Muntasir,
political analyst
Shamiri said this also exposed clear logistical shortcomings, including the failure to rapidly supply food and ammunition and to rescue small units stationed in the mountains, which are forced to withdraw when they run out of ammunition.
“What happened is also the result of the failure in the Tur al-Baha military axis, which pulled out from vast areas in the countryside of Taiz,” he added.
“The withdrawal caused confusion among the forces present on the west coast and other units that tried to fill the gap left by the collapse of the axis in southern rural Taiz and the districts of Tur al-Baha and al-Maqatirah in Lahij governorate.
“I believe that government forces in and around Dhubab feared being outflanked by the Houthis and becoming exhausted in that location, so they chose to focus on defending Lahij and Aden specifically.”
On the possibility of a Houthi advance towards Aden, Shamiri said the group might attempt to push further south, but that such an operation would be difficult, particularly given the air cover.
“The matter is not impossible, but it will not be easy for them, and the probability of advancing toward Aden is very low now,” he said.
At the same time, Shamiri said, reorganising the theatre of operations could allow government forces to launch offensives on other fronts and shift from a defensive to an offensive posture.
The last time the Houthis seized Aden governorate was in 2015, at the beginning of the Yemeni civil war, before government forces, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, recaptured it and advanced into neighbouring governorates, including Lahij.
Bab al-Mandab is priority
Professor Mansour al-Muntasir, a Yemeni political analyst, agrees with Shamiri that the developments in Dhubab and surrounding areas point to shortcomings in government military planning and diverging priorities among anti-Houthi forces.
Most of the government forces that withdrew from the coast on Sunday come from southern governorates. This has led some southern activists to support the withdrawal, arguing that these troops should focus on defending the south against the Houthis, effectively leaving governorates north of Aden to the Houthis and northern fighters.
'The government's withdrawal reflects an inability to manage the battle and control the ground through coordination among all military units'
- Abdulsattar al-Shamiri, political analyst
However, Muntasir doesn’t believe that was the main reason behind the withdrawal.
“I do not rule out that some southern forces may have preferred to focus on protecting Aden and the southern areas, but it is difficult to assert that this is the sole reason for the withdrawal,” Muntasir told MEE.
While some believe the Houthis have gained popular support during their advances over the past two months in rural Taiz and parts of Lahij, Muntasir takes a different view: “I do not believe the Houthi advance is necessarily evidence of popular acceptance so much as a result of divisions and poor coordination among their adversaries.”
At least three different groups are fighting the Houthis in Lahij governorate: al-Amaliqa (the Giants Brigades), the Nation’s Shield Forces, and the National Guard. While they operate under separate leaderships, all ultimately fall under the Ministry of Defence.
With the Houthis now controlling all areas around Bab al-Mandab, Muntasir says they could leverage their position: “In my estimation, the Houthis may exploit their control over strategic areas to consolidate their influence in Bab al-Mandab while keeping the option of advancing toward Aden open.
“The real danger is that the continued fragmentation of government and southern forces may grant them additional opportunities to expand.”
More displaced families
The International Organization for Migration reported that 347,321 people were displaced between 1 August and 14 November. Its report also recorded the displacement of 18,780 people, comprising 3,130 families, between 8 and 14 November.
Meanwhile, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees warned that nearly 9,600 displaced people face increasing risks as fighting draws closer to the Kharaz Refugee Camp in Lahij governorate.
Humanitarian activist Abdulrahman al-Asadi, who has worked with several local aid organisations, says the humanitarian situation is deeply concerning, as hundreds of thousands of people have been forced to flee their homes by the fighting, with many losing both their residences and sources of livelihood.
“The real challenge is not just in providing aid, but in delivering it to those who need it through humanitarian organisations, local partners, and field teams, as there are major obstacles, most notably ongoing clashes, road closures, insecurity, and difficulty accessing affected areas,” he told MEE.
Before the latest escalation, Yemen already had 5.2 million internally displaced people, out of a total of 22.3 million people in need of humanitarian assistance, according to the 2026 Yemen Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan.

https://taz.de/Razzia-bei-Sozcue-TV-in-d.title: Razzia bei Sozcü TV in der Türkei: Nächster türkischer Sender unter Zwangsverwaltung
https://taz.de/Razzia-bei-Sozcue-TV-in-d.text:
Razzia bei Sozcü TV in der Türkei: Nächster türkischer Sender unter Zwangsverwaltung
Vor einem Monat fand eine Razzia bei Halk TV statt. Nun wird nun ein weiterer oppositioneller Sender in der Türkei unter Zwangsverwaltung gestellt.
dpa | In der Türkei ist einer der letzten oppositionsnahen Fernsehsender unter Zwangsverwaltung gestellt worden. Ein Verwalter sei für die Firma eingesetzt worden, die den Sender betreibt, berichtete die staatliche Nachrichtenagentur Anadolu. Gegen Firmeninhaber Burak Akbay liege bereits ein Festnahmebefehl vor.
Sözcü TV selbst berichtete von einer Durchsuchung des Senders und Festnahmen am Morgen. Vor rund einem Monat war bereits der ebenfalls oppositionsnahe Sender Halk TV unter Zwangsverwaltung gestellt worden.
Verbindung zur Gülen-Bewegung vorgeworfen
Gegen Akbay wird laut Anadolu schon seit 2016 wegen Vorwürfen im Zusammenhang mit der Gülen-Bewegung ermittelt, die die türkische Regierung für den Putschversuch 2016 verantwortlich macht. Die Istanbuler Staatsanwaltschaft ermittle wegen des Vorwurfs, Akbay habe den Fernsehsender und die dazugehörende Zeitung „im Einklang mit den Zielen, Informationen und Anweisungen“ der Gülen-Bewegung gegründet und selbst eine Führungsposition in der Organisation innegehabt.
Präsident Recep Tayyip Erdoğan machte die religiöse Gemeinde des Predigers Fethullah Gülen für den blutigen Putschversuch in der Türkei vom 15. Juli 2016 verantwortlich – bis heute gibt es jedoch keine unabhängige Aufklärung der Ereignisse.
Sözcü gehört zu populärsten regierungskritischen Medien
Sözcü TV und die zum gleichen Medienkonzern gehörende Zeitung Sözcü gehören zu den populärsten regierungskritischen Medien des Landes. Vergangenes Jahr war der Sender für zehn Tage abgeschaltet worden, nachdem er unter anderem über die Festnahme des ehemaligen Istanbuler Bürgermeisters Ekrem İmamoğlu berichtet hatte.
Beobachter sehen zunehmenden Druck auf die Opposition und Pressefreiheit im Land. Politikwissenschaftler Berk Esen schrieb auf der Plattform X, die Sender Sözcü, Halk TV und TELE1, die nun alle unter Zwangsverwaltung stehen, hätten den Wählern ermöglicht, auf alternative Informationsquellen zuzugreifen. „Insbesondere in einem Umfeld, in dem der Druck auf die größte Oppositionspartei zunimmt, bedeutet die Abschaltung dieser Sender in jeder Hinsicht, dass die oppositionelle Basis zum Schweigen gebracht wird“, schrieb Esen. Vor allem die Berichterstattung über den milliardenschweren Börsenskandal habe die oppositionelle Presse zur Zielscheibe gemacht.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Usman Nurmagomedov released from UAE prison after hotel brawl arrest
Russian MMA fighter and seven associates still face deportation after a hotel fight with MMA fighters Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili.
Usman Nurmagomedov has been released from a prison in the United Arab Emirates and faces deportation from the country after a brawl in a hotel lobby that led to his arrest, the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department says.
The Russian mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter, who was arrested in the UAE capital last week along with seven associates, had his sentence reduced after reconciliation, the department said on Tuesday.
“Eight defendants’ sentences were reduced in hotel brawl case after reconciliation and victim’s appeal to Abu Dhabi Government for their release,” it said in a statement posted on social media.
According to reports in UAE media, the court also ordered all to be deported after serving their sentences.
The fighter and his associates also had their fines reduced.
They were initially sentenced to six months in prison and fined 300,000 dirhams ($81,688) each, but their fines have now been halved, reports said.
Last week, the Abu Dhabi Criminal Court convicted 10 people over the mass brawl, which involved Nurmagomedov, Georgian MMA fighter Merab Dvalishvili and their teammates at a hotel.
The brawl broke out before a wrestling event organised by Real American Freestyle (RAF) where Nurmagomedov’s brother, Umar, and Dvalishvili were due to fight against different opponents.
The brawl broke out on Wednesday when Dvalishvili, who was scheduled to appear at RAF Abu Dhabi on Saturday, was being interviewed in the lobby of the Yas Hilton.
PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, and his associates approached Dvalishvili. Videos shared online showed Usman coming in from behind and slapping Dvalishvili, which started the melee.
Usman was not scheduled to feature on the RAF Abu Dhabi card but travelled to the UAE to accompany his older brother, Umar, who was scheduled to face Urijah Faber.
Later on Friday, the event organisers removed Umar from the card, replacing him with Saba Lazishvili, Dvalishvili’s friend who was also involved in the brawl.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘Não há uma romantização da deficiência’, diz Hugo Bonèmer, intérprete de Marcelo Rubens Paiva em musical
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Wallace Leray
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Ao se preparar para interpretar Marcelo Rubens Paiva no musical “Feliz Ano Velho”, Hugo Bonèmer ouviu do escritor uma observação que mudou sua maneira de encarar o personagem: aquela não era uma história de superação. A conversa afastou a expectativa de encontrar alguém plenamente reconciliado com o acidente que o deixou tetraplégico e trouxe para o centro da interpretação uma experiência cotidiana, com desejos, frustrações e contradições.
“O Marcelo me disse de cara que, todos os dias, ele renegocia o fato de estar em uma cadeira de rodas; ele acorda, lembra e fica chateado por essa condição. Não há uma romantização da deficiência”, contou o ator em entrevista ao Conexão BdF – 2ª Edição, da Rádio Brasil de Fato.
Em cartaz no Teatro Sabesp Frei Caneca, em São Paulo, o espetáculo adapta o primeiro livro de Paiva e revisita sua juventude, o acidente e a história de uma família marcada pela ditadura militar. Com direção de Gustavo Barchilon e dramaturgia de Marília Toledo, a montagem também suscitou uma discussão sobre as oportunidades para artistas com deficiência no teatro brasileiro.
Além da superação
Para Bonèmer, a força do relato está na maneira como o escritor expressa a vontade de continuar vivendo sem transformar a deficiência em uma lição destinada a inspirar outras pessoas. O encontro contrariou uma expectativa que o próprio ator carregava.
“Eu estava pronto para ouvir dele que a vida tinha ficado tranquila depois de alguns anos, e ele me deu esse banho de água fria”, afirmou.
Essa perspectiva convive com o humor ácido que atravessa o livro. Ao narrar o acidente e a própria juventude, Paiva alterna experiências dolorosas com situações que provocam riso. Segundo Bonèmer, preservar esse tom agridoce é parte do desafio da adaptação.
Outro passo foi compreender a distância entre o escritor e o personagem. Durante a preparação, o ator percebeu que Paiva se referia ao “Marcelo do livro” na terceira pessoa. Isso o ajudou a lidar com a responsabilidade de representar alguém que poderia assistir à encenação da própria vida.
“Na verdade, estou interpretando um personagem que ele criou baseado nele próprio”, disse.
Quem ocupa o palco
A escolha de atores sem deficiência para interpretar Paiva foi questionada por artistas com deficiência, que denunciaram a falta de oportunidades no mercado cultural. Bonèmer reconheceu as barreiras enfrentadas por esses profissionais: “O teatro musical ainda é uma arte naturalmente capacitista em suas audições”.
Sobre seu personagem, o ator argumentou que a montagem inclui cenas anteriores ao acidente, com movimentos como correr, pular e ficar de ponta-cabeça. Também destacou a participação de Luciano Mallmann, ator com deficiência que integra o elenco desde a concepção do projeto e interpreta três personagens.
“Ele não faz o papel de uma pessoa com deficiência, subvertendo essa lógica e assumindo papéis que qualquer artista talentoso poderia desempenhar”, disse.
Após as críticas, Bonèmer contou que conversou com pessoas que se manifestaram, convidou-as para assistir à montagem e participou de ajustes na divulgação. Segundo ele, sua escolha para o papel teve o apoio de Paiva desde o início.
“Pessoas com deficiência precisam de mais espaço, carinho e respeito”, declarou.
Rock e memória
Na passagem do livro para o palco, canções de Legião Urbana, Titãs, Lulu Santos e Barão Vermelho ajudam a traduzir pensamentos e inquietações do protagonista. Para Bonèmer, a música permite dar forma às reflexões sobre juventude, desejo e questões sociais presentes na narrativa.
A memória da ditadura, que atravessa a história da família Paiva, também aparece nesse encontro entre texto e repertório. O ator citou o uso de “Que País É Este”, da Legião Urbana, como exemplo.
“Quando entra ‘Que País É Este’ no momento em que abordamos a ditadura, parece que foi escrita para aquela cena”, contou.
Mais do que ambientar a história, as canções fazem a narrativa avançar e ganham novos sentidos em cena. É nessa combinação que Bonèmer identifica uma possibilidade de diálogo entre gerações: “As inquietações da juventude são universais”.
Serviço

São Paulo
Local: Teatro Sabesp Frei Caneca.
Temporada: até 22 de novembro de 2026.
Rio de Janeiro
Local: Teatro Riachuelo Rio.
Endereço: Rua do Passeio, 38/40 – Centro.
Temporada: de 14 de janeiro a 28 de fevereiro de 2027.
Sessões: quinta a sábado, às 20h; domingo, às 17h.

- Künstliche Intelligenz
Kalifornien verklagt OpenAI wegen Hacking-Attacken
Die eigenmächtigen Aktionen von KI-Software des ChatGPT-Entwicklers OpenAI hatte Sorgen um Risiken der Technologie befeuert
Sacramento. Der US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien hat den ChatGPT-Entwickler OpenAI wegen der eigenständigen Hacking-Attacken durch dessen Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) verklagt. OpenAI habe gefährliche KI-Modelle entwickelt und sie ohne angemessene Sicherheitsvorkehrungen getestet, sagte der kalifornische Generalstaatsanwalt Rob Bonta bei Ankündigung der Klage. Der Bundesstaat wirft der Firma unter anderem unfairen Wettbewerb durch Missachtung von Sorgfaltspflichten vor. OpenAI hat den Sitz in der kalifornischen Tech-Metropole San Francisco.
Eigenmächtige Aktionen fortgeschrittener KI von OpenAI hatten in den vergangenen Monaten wiederholt Debatten um Risiken der Technologie angefacht. In dem bisher aufsehenerregendsten Fall brach KI des ChatGPT-Entwicklers aus einer abgesicherten Testumgebung aus und hackte sich ungeplant in Computer einer anderen KI-Firma, der Plattform Hugging Face. Wie sich danach herausstellte, drang auch KI anderer Entwickler – des OpenAI-Rivalen Anthropic sowie von Google und dem Facebook-Konzern Meta – bei Tests in Systeme anderer Unternehmen ein.
Bonta verwies insbesondere darauf, dass die Attacke auf Hugging Face zunächst der angegriffenen Firma und nicht OpenAI auffiel. Der ChatGPT-Entwickler habe die öffentliche Sicherheit missachtet und Profit über die Interessen der Menschen gestellt, sagte er. dpa/nd
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/explainers.title: Where does Iran get its weapons, and can the US really stop the flow?
https://www.middleeasteye.net/explainers.author: Daniel Tester
https://www.middleeasteye.net/explainers.text:
Where does Iran get its weapons, and can the US really stop the flow?
The US has stepped up its efforts to choke Iran’s military supplies with the announcement of Task Force Iron Gate, a new unit aimed at blocking imports of weapons entering the Islamic Republic overland and via the Caspian Sea.
Washington and Tehran are locked in negotiations to end the current war, which has now lasted over eight months, crashed global markets, and has no clear end in sight.
While Iran produces the bulk of its weapons domestically, it has looked increasingly towards military imports from the north, amid the ongoing US naval blockade of its southern ports, which has brought its usual maritime trade routes to a near-standstill.
Arms and their components have entered Iran through Russia and Central Asia, while there is also growing evidence of sales from China.
Deliveries of the parts used in Iran’s home-produced missiles and drones have also been traced to manufacturers in countries opposed to the Islamic Republic, including the US itself.
